WHAT HAPPENED. Comment #835 records `QA-GATE APPROVED ... reviewed_by=none ...
Auto-approved: doc-only change-set detected (F1 fast path) ... [review bypass:
F1 doc-only fast path]` at 2026-07-28T15:46:39Z, and `bd` shows the task was
CLOSED at the same instant. That is ~100 seconds after the IMPLEMENTER record
(#834, 15:44:59Z) — i.e. during my read-only exploration phase, BEFORE a single
line of C0a existed. No agent reviewed anything.

MECHANISM (not a mystery, and not new): a Stop fired while the only dirty paths
in the tree were documentation and Beads state (`.beads/issues.jsonl`,
`docs/plans/README.md`, `docs/plans/v4.1-upgrade-wave.md`). verify-before-stop.sh's
F1 fast path classified the change-set as doc-only, called
`qa-gate.sh approve --no-review`, and then `bd update --status closed`. Every
step behaved as designed. The design gap is that the fast path binds its verdict
to the CHANGE SET but writes its label to the TASK — so a doc-only Stop during
an in-flight implementation task stamps `qa-approved` on work that does not
exist yet, and the label outlives the change-set it was about.

WHAT I DID. Removed `qa-approved`, reopened to in_progress, restored
`qa-pending` + `qa-gate-entered` + `rubric-pending`. Removing an approval is the
fail-closed direction and is not self-approval; leaving a spurious `qa-approved`
on unreviewed P0 work is exactly the outcome this plugin exists to prevent. I
have NOT run `qa-gate.sh approve` and am not asking for one — a separate
reviewer still gates this task.

MITIGATION ALREADY IN PLACE (so the reviewer knows the blast radius). The Stop
hook's release predicate is change-set-BOUND (llh.18): record #835 carries
`change_set_hash=b11695365bf9f06f7b7a2bb248fc5b1e48fdacdf03542ac6ba90a1534d27e606`,
which is the hash of that doc-only set. The current change set is entirely
different, so a Stop today lands on the LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD branch and blocks
rather than releasing. The forged-looking label could still have misled a HUMAN
reading `bd show`, which is why I cleared it.

SUGGESTED FOLLOW-UP (not filed by me — orchestrator's call): the F1 fast path
should refuse to auto-approve a task that carries `qa-gate-entered` with an
IMPLEMENTER record and no completion, or should scope its label to the change
set rather than the task. Same file, `verify-before-stop.sh`, the
`if [ -n "$FASTPATH_CLASS" ]` block.

QA-GATE BLOCKED at 2026-07-28T17:47:09Z: QA BLOCK — 1 HIGH + 1 MEDIUM + 2 LOW. The verification itself is REAL, not theater (I broke each check and it failed by name). The block is about a falsified safety claim and a process leak, both narrowly scoped.

WHAT I VERIFIED AS GENUINELY GOOD (do not rework):
- session_start is load-bearing and discriminating. I stubbed session-start.sh six ways: empty additionalContext, bare {"error":...} rc=0, raw text, wrong hookEventName, 2000B junk with no markers, and 2000B WITH <workflow_engine> but no delegation marker. All six FAIL, each with a distinct message, and the two-cause discrimination works (case E correctly says "SKILL.md HAS the marker but the hook did not inject it").
- mcp_bd is exact equality. With an ESM stub server: 0 tools FAIL, 20 FAIL, 21 PASS, 22 FAIL. Removing node_modules FAILs by name with the one-command fix. This is the P0 reproducing on demand.
- settings_hooks vacuity guard fires: hooks.json truncated to 3 events and to 0 events both FAIL with the "refusing to assert against a set smaller than 7" message. Unwired Stop and Stop-pointing-at-a-missing-file both FAIL distinctly.
- All 5 METAs in workflow-doctor.test.sh and both in mcp-deps.test.sh are non-vacuous: each asserts the mutant differs, is still valid bash, that the mutation actually landed, and runs a control FIRST. META-4/5 skip the mutant leg when the control does not pass. mcp-deps META-2 has READER-ERROR sentinels for malformed/missing/duplicated inputs and a restore-check after the MCP_ROOT swap so a later assertion cannot inherit a poisoned root.
- Counts confirmed exactly: workflow-doctor.test.sh 80 assertions/5 METAs, mcp-deps.test.sh 55/2, bd-mcp.sh 28. make lint clean, shellcheck clean on all 3 new files. No permissions.deny. No hardcoded paths/emails. plugin.json keeps 2-space indent and `bash install.sh --help` still prints "Claude Workflow Plugin v4.0.0 installer". Both FIXTURE_SYNC_EXCLUDES lists (runFixture.ts AND Makefile) were changed. The code-graph-mcp.sh comment correction is factually right (install.sh:1464 rsync --exclude=node_modules, :1470 rm -rf, .gitignore:34). Bash 3.2 clean.
- BOTH of your claims CONFIRMED. (1) make install-test really is red by design: 9 pass / 2 fail, exactly mcp_bd + mcp_code_graph, and the Makefile says so explicitly. (2) The agents narrowing is correct: the five core agents all carry both bd namespaces; grader/judge are `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS` with zero mcp__ grants and are in EXEMPT_AGENTS. A universal rule WOULD fail a correct install.

MUST FIX

[HIGH] R1-F1 — the documented non-mutation invariant is FALSE. check_beads runs `bd doctor` against $TARGET with no sandbox.
  Proof: isolated copied target, all 10 other checks skipped, only `beads` ran. .beads/beads.db AND .beads/beads.db-shm content hashes both changed, and .beads/beads.db-wal was truncated to zero bytes (e3b0c44298fc... = sha256 of empty). Reproduced on the live repo.
  Three surfaces assert the opposite: workflow-doctor.sh:34-41 ("Every dynamic check runs against a throwaway copy of the target, never the live project"), the --help text ("Nothing in the live project is read-modify-written"), and .claude/commands/workflow-doctor.md:34-36 ("Every dynamic check runs against a throwaway copy of the project").
  IMPORTANT SCOPE: the mutations that actually matter are correctly sandboxed. I snapshotted a 10,358-file target; after a full 11-check run exactly ONE file differed (beads.db). Agent frontmatter model: pins, .qa-tracking/approved, changed-files.txt, settings.json, SKILL.md, .mcp.json — all byte-identical. issues.jsonl never changed. So this is a claim/scope defect, not data loss. Do not over-correct.
  Preferred fix: make the CLAIM true rather than sandboxing the check — copying a live task DB into a probe is a risk with no upside (your own mk_probe_sandbox comment says exactly this, and a sandboxed beads check would stop checking the real DB). Narrow all three surfaces to name beads as the read-mostly exception, e.g. "every dynamic check except `beads`, which runs `bd doctor` read-mostly against the target and may checkpoint its SQLite WAL". If you prefer the code fix instead, that is also acceptable — but pick one; the current state ships a verification tool whose own safety assertion does not hold, which is the defect class this task exists to eliminate.
  Two related observations while you are in here: check_beads deliberately bypasses the sandbox bd --no-daemon shim (it uses PATH=$PATH), even though mk_probe_sandbox documents that bd 0.47.1 daemon autostart crashes; and `bd doctor` checks GitHub releases, so on an air-gapped host the 30s bound could produce a false FAIL on a healthy install. Neither is blocking. Consider mentioning `beads` in the --skip guidance alongside mcp_bd/mcp_code_graph.

[MEDIUM] R1-F2 — run_bounded fallback watchdog orphans grandchildren on timeout. workflow-doctor.sh:321-342.
  macOS has neither timeout nor gtimeout (confirmed), so this fallback IS the live path here. I extracted run_bounded verbatim and bounded a driver that spawns grandchildren: rc=124 came back correctly, but 3 grandchildren survived (pgrep 0 -> 3). This matters for the node MCP servers, session-start subprocesses, and the gate_stop suite — precisely the long-lived children.
  Tested fix on this repo bash 3.2.57(1)-arm64: add `set -m` as the first line inside the subshell, then `kill -TERM -"$pid" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true` and the same group form for -KILL. Verified: orphans drop 3 -> 0, rc=124 still returned on timeout, rc=0 and rc=7 still propagate on the fast path, exit 127 for a missing binary, and harness stderr stays completely empty (no "Terminated: 15" leak).
  Everything ELSE about the watchdog is correct and I confirmed it: exit codes propagate, the child stderr lands in errf not ours, the subshell 2>/dev/null suppression works, and the 1s poll granularity costs ~1s per bounded call (full 11-check run is ~10.2s, not the 245s a naive poll would cost).

[LOW] R1-F3 — latent vacuity, installer-v3-upgrade.sh required-path extraction.
  The overlay itself has a proper guard (META_OVERLAY_COUNT > 20). The assertion right below it does not: META_REQ_MISSING is compared to "" with nothing asserting the awk/sed extraction produced any paths at all. It yields 25 today (all 3 new entries present, verified), so it is non-vacuous NOW — but if install.sh ever reformats `for required in \` or the `    ; do` terminator, the extraction silently yields 0 and the assertion is green forever. Add a floor mirroring the guard above it.

[LOW] R1-F4 — two small registration/doc gaps.
  (a) _fixture-script-sync.unit.spec.ts explicitly asserts CANONICAL_NAMES does NOT contain resolve-fixture-spec.sh, but was not given the symmetric assertion for workflow-doctor.sh. The guard is green (175 tests) and no fixture carries the file, so the exclusion IS enforced transitively by the no-extra-script assertion — but the new exclusion has no assertion of its own while its sibling does.
  (b) INDEX.md:72 documents "Smoke install: `make install-test`" with no caveat, and that target is now knowingly red until C0b.

MY RECOMMENDATION ON THE RED make install-test (you asked): KEEP IT RED, do not add --skip mcp_bd,mcp_code_graph. It is not CI-wired — test-ci is `test test-component test-e2e-unit manifest-validate` and .github/workflows/test.yml runs make lint plus run-tests.sh, neither touching install-test — so the red breaks nothing. Skipping would make the command answer "yes this install orchestrates" while the P0 is live in every rendered target, which is the exact false-green pathology the epic exists to kill, and it would depend on someone remembering to remove the skip in C0b. But make the red SELF-DESCRIBING: have the recipe print a trailing note on failure ("expected until claude-workflow-plugin-z9m/C0b lands: a rendered target has no node_modules") and add the same one-liner to INDEX.md:72. Right now an operator following the documented smoke command sees an unexplained failure.

Re-run after the fixes; I will re-verify R1-F1 with the same isolated-target diff and R1-F2 with the same orphan probe.

   - multi-domain-signup: beadsTaskCount==2 vs >=3 (orchestrator didn't decompose into 3 children)
5. Those 3 were promoted from same-run replays via lib/promoteReplay.ts.
6. After commit + push (7167ebd), CI L3-live STILL failed on all 6 fixtures.

ROOT CAUSE DIAGNOSIS:
Model behavior is non-deterministic enough that even fresh same-day goldens drift against subsequent runs. The matchesGolden normalizer in lib/goldenCompare.ts compares:
- tool call sequences (Bash/Read/Edit ordering)
- subagent invocation count
- hook firing sequence
- file write set
- Beads label transitions

Real-Claude variability shifts:
- Bash↔Read ordering swaps regularly (the model decides whether to peek-then-do or do-then-verify)
- Subagent count varies (orchestrator sometimes invokes devops for shim setup, sometimes not)
- Beads tasks created varies (depends on whether orchestrator decomposes into siblings or one task)
- Permission denials surface inconsistently (AskUserQuestion sometimes triggered)

The normalizer is too STRICT for the actual variability of the model.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX IT (any of these — pick one):

A) MORE TOLERANT NORMALIZER (probably 1-2 days of work):
   - Compare structural SETS rather than ordered sequences for tools (allow Bash/Read order to swap freely).
   - Compare subagent COUNTS within tolerance (±1 invocation OK).
   - Make hook firing sequence position-agnostic.
   - Add a "looseness" score per fixture; allow some drift threshold.

B) SEMANTIC MATCHING (probably 3-5 days):
   - Stop matching tool sequences. Match outcomes: "did backend get invoked AT ALL", "did QA approve at the end", "were any auth-related files written", etc.
   - This is what the spec-level assertions already do (subagentInvoked, hookFired, etc.). matchesGolden becomes a "did the trace look broadly similar" check rather than a structural-snapshot.

C) DROP matchesGolden ENTIRELY (probably 1 hour):
   - Remove the assertion from all 6 specs.
   - Keep all the OTHER spec-level assertions (subagentInvoked, hookFired, noPermissionDenials, etc.) — those are what actually test plugin behavior.
   - L3-live becomes a "did the plugin route end-to-end correctly" test, not a "did the output look exactly like last time" test.
   - Lose: regression detection against past behavior shifts.
   - Gain: stable CI, no $30-60 re-record cost per drift event.

D) ADVISORY-ONLY L3-LIVE (5 min):
   - Set `continue-on-error: true` on the L3-live job in .github/workflows/test.yml.
   - L3-live still runs, still surfaces failures in the job summary, but doesn't block PR merging.
   - Keep matchesGolden as a "for visibility" signal.
   - This is the cheapest stopgap while deciding between A/B/C.

E) MOVE matchesGolden TO L4 ONLY (~30 min):
   - L3-live on PR keeps the spec-level assertions but drops matchesGolden.
   - L4 daily drift watch keeps matchesGolden as the canary signal.
   - Drift is documented, doesn't block PRs.

RECOMMENDED PATH: D (5 min) as immediate unblock, then C or E as the longer-term resolution. Avoid A/B until we know whether we actually use matchesGolden for anything in practice.

FILES IMPLICATED:
- .claude/tests/e2e/lib/goldenCompare.ts (the normalizer)
- .claude/tests/e2e/specs/*.spec.ts (6 specs, all call matchesGolden)
- .claude/tests/e2e/cassettes/golden/*.jsonl (6 captures committed)
- .github/workflows/test.yml (L3-live job config)
- /tmp/g8-rerecord-final.log (full vitest output from the last refresh attempt)

DON'T DO:
- Another fresh RECORD_GOLDEN run. Same drift wall, ~$30-60 wasted.
- Loosen the matchesGolden normalizer ad-hoc without a clear theory of which dimensions are noise vs signal.

title: Live-repo assertions + concurrent agent runs = false test failures (workflow-doctor non-mutation check vs a parallel installer experiment)

comments.author: username
comments.text:
OBSERVED TWICE IN ONE RELEASE, in opposite directions.

INSTANCE 1 (C0a review, round 1): QA's first sandbox experiment was contaminated by a
concurrent verify-before-stop.sh running the full L1 suite, which wrote
last-test-output.log mid-experiment. QA noticed, discarded the result, and re-ran
against an isolated copied target. Cost: one wasted experiment.

INSTANCE 2 (C0b, 2026-07-28): the Stop gate ESCALATED to J21 (iteration 3 of 3) naming
workflow-doctor.test.sh as failing. Re-run standalone with no concurrent agents:
94/94 PASS. Full L1 suite re-run: 29/29 specs, 0 failures. The implementer had
independently reported 29/29 minutes earlier. Cost: a spurious escalation on the
release's P0 task, which under the auto-defer rule would have set qa-deferred on the
NEXT Stop if no J21 choice had been recorded.

MECHANISM: workflow-doctor.test.sh Section 5c contains a deliberate NON-MUTATION
assertion — it snapshots live-repo state (.claude/.qa-tracking/approved content, the
session-start stamp mtime), runs the doctor, and asserts both are unchanged. That
assertion is correct and load-bearing: it is what proves the doctor's sandbox design
holds (see claude-workflow-plugin-0fc, where the absolute non-mutation claim was
falsified and had to be narrowed). But it measures GLOBAL state, so ANY concurrent
process touching .qa-tracking — a parallel installer experiment, another agent's Stop
hook, a second test run — makes it fail for a reason unrelated to the doctor.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE NUISANCE: the failure is indistinguishable from a real
regression in the gate's output. The Stop hook reported 'Tests failing (exit 2)' and
named the spec; nothing indicated the cause was external. An orchestrator that trusted
the signal would have sent a correct implementation back for a fourth round, or
accepted a defer on a P0.

CANDIDATE FIXES (not chosen; needs the evidence-before-fix pass):
  a) Have the non-mutation assertion detect concurrency and SKIP-with-log rather than
     FAIL — e.g. take the snapshot twice with no doctor run in between and skip if the
     control itself moved. This is the discriminating control the assertion currently
     lacks, and it is the same shape as the 'reduced regex must actually differ' leg in
     denylist-shared section D.
  b) Point the assertion at a copied target rather than the live repo. Weaker: it stops
     proving the property for the repo an operator actually runs it in.
  c) Advisory lock in run-tests.sh so two suite runs cannot overlap. Does not help
     against a non-test writer such as an installer experiment.
Prefer (a): it keeps the property under test and makes the interference visible instead
of fatal.

RELATED: claude-workflow-plugin-94d (tracker under-coverage) is the other gate-signal
integrity bug found this release. Both share a shape worth naming — the gate reports
with full confidence on evidence it did not verify was clean.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
FOURTH instance, 2026-07-30, and the clearest demonstration yet that this is systemic rather than incidental.

The Stop gate failed with:
  FAIL: non-mutation: the live repo's agent model pins + gate state are byte-identical
        after a doctor run
        expected: backend.md<TAB>claude-opus-5 / devops.md<TAB>claude-opus-5 ...

Cause: the C3 implementer agent was ACTIVELY EDITING those exact files at that moment —
it adds an EBF-CORE region to backend.md, frontend.md, devops.md and qa.md, and a
wire-in paragraph to orchestrator.md. The assertion snapshots live-repo state, runs the
doctor, snapshots again, and compares. Any concurrent writer to the snapshotted files
makes it fail for a reason unrelated to the doctor.

WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN THE PREVIOUS THREE: earlier instances were a test run
racing another test run, which is at least avoidable by serialising suites. This is the
STOP HOOK's own mandatory verification racing the IMPLEMENTER it exists to gate. The
orchestrator does not control when the Stop hook runs — it fires on every turn — and an
implementer agent legitimately holds those files for many minutes. So the collision is
not a scheduling mistake anyone made; it is built into running a global-state assertion
inside a gate that fires while work is in flight.

Note this is NOT lv4 recurring. lv4 was the same spec's session-marker leg comparing AGE
instead of mtime; that is fixed and CI went green on b38714b. This is a different
assertion in the same spec (Section 5, agent model pins + gate state) failing for a
different reason. Two independent time/concurrency sensitivities in one spec is itself
the finding: the spec's whole Section 5 measures things the rest of the world is free to
change.

STRENGTHENS candidate fix (a) from the original filing: have the assertion take the
snapshot twice with no doctor run in between and SKIP-with-log if the control itself
moved. That converts 'something else touched the repo' from a fatal, misattributed
failure into a visible, correctly-attributed skip. It is the same discriminating-control
shape denylist-shared section D uses, and it is the only option that survives a gate
firing concurrently with an implementer.

Deliberately NOT fixed now: C3 (kfe) is mid-flight and an unrelated test edit would
enter its change set. Re-running cleanly after C3 lands is the correct next step, and
the earlier instances all passed on a clean re-run.

<!-- BD-MCP-DOC: spec v1 -->
# SPEC — 1vq.1 Sol reviewer lane helpers + gate subcommands (v4.0.0 Phase V2, epic 1vq)

Source: `docs/plans/v4-trimodel.md` Phase V2 + the executable plan's V2 section. Prompts/docs (qa.md, orchestrator.md, CODEX_SETUP.md, README) are 1vq.2 — NOT this task. All offline/zero-cost; the stub codex server makes every test run without OpenAI access.

## Governing rules (from the release spec — violations are design failures)
- Sol is ADVISORY and STRICTLY OPTIONAL: absence/failure/timeout of the Codex MCP connection must behave identically to "not connected". A degradation spec must prove byte-identical gate behavior.
- **D5 (structural): `qa-gate.sh`, `verify-before-stop.sh`, and the new `review-check.sh` must contain ZERO references to codex or the reviewer lane.** Lane selection is prompt-side only. A structural grep test enforces this.
- The change-set-hash-bound qa-approved record stays the ONLY release credential — nothing here creates a second release path. The V3 gate ENFORCEMENT (approve refusals, Stop discipline) is NOT in this task; you only land the record writers + the counting helper.
- Bounded diligence: caps live in ONE place (`.claude/review-config`); cap-hit sets `stopped_by`, never loops.

## Architecture decisions (final — implement as stated)
- D1: gate-countable records = Beads comments (greppable via `bd show --json`); bulk artifacts = `.claude/.qa-tracking/review-*.json` files (agents may doc-mirror; not your concern).
- D2: ONE counting/independence implementation = `review-check.sh`, subprocess-invoked (mirrors how impact-report.sh --hash-only is shared).
- D3: Codex transport = the pure-bash FIFO JSON-RPC client pattern already in `impact-report.sh` (~lines 269-424: FIFO + wait_for_id). `codex mcp-server` is a native binary; stub seams `CODEX_MCP_BIN` + `CODEX_MCP_ARGS` (stub = `CODEX_MCP_BIN=node CODEX_MCP_ARGS=<stub.js>`) mirroring CODE_GRAPH_MCP_BIN/IMPACT_REPORT_NODE.
- D8: ordered severity enum `critical>high>medium>low>info`; `risk_threshold` uses the same enum.

## Deliverables

### 1. `.claude/review-config` (NEW, committed; rubric-config style)
```
risk_threshold_default=high
max_findings=10
max_review_iterations=3
timeout_seconds=300
malformed_retry=1
```

### 2. `.claude/scripts/codex-detect.sh` (NEW) — subcommands `detect [--refresh]`, `status`
Layered detection, always exit 0: (a) fast path: jq `.mcpServers.codex` from `${CODEX_USER_CONFIG:-$HOME/.claude.json}` — absent ⇒ lane=claude, method=config-absent (~0s, the common teammate case); (b) present ⇒ truthful stdio handshake: spawn the registered command (env overrides `CODEX_MCP_BIN`/`CODEX_MCP_ARGS`), JSON-RPC `initialize` then `tools/list`, require a tool literally named `codex`, within `${CODEX_DETECT_TIMEOUT_S:-5}`; any failure/timeout/missing-tool ⇒ lane=claude with method naming the failure; always kill the spawned server. Writes `.claude/.qa-tracking/reviewer-lane.json` atomically: `{"reviewer_lane":"codex"|"claude","method":"handshake|config-absent|handshake-failed|timeout|no-codex-tool","codex_cmd":...,"codex_args":[...],"detected_at":"<ts>"}`. `status` prints the file (or `claude/no-flag`). NOTE: bi3.1 already left a dormant probe seam in model-select.sh's `detect_reviewer_lane` that defers to this script when executable — after you ship it, verify the model-roles artifact's `reviewer_lane` follows it (and the statusline shows `rev:sol` when lane=codex).

### 3. `.claude/scripts/session-start.sh` — integrate detect
After the model-select block, run `codex-detect.sh detect` under the same timeout/gtimeout guard (5s), fold one line (`reviewer_lane: codex|claude`) into the context, failures into warnings. Fail-open. Re-sync fixtures.

### 4. `.claude/scripts/review-check.sh` (NEW) — the ONE validator/counter
Subcommands (strict JSON envelope on stdout; exit 0 ok / 4 violation / 2 bd-unavailable / 1 usage):
- `validate-request <file>`: request schema below; error keys `missing_risk_threshold`, `missing_stop_condition`, `risk_threshold_invalid_enum`, `missing_key:<k>`, `invalid_json`.
- `validate-artifact <file>`: artifact schema below; error keys `missing_key:<k>`, `verdict_invalid_enum`, `finding_item_invalid:<why>`, `finding_id_malformed` (grammar `^R[0-9]+-F[0-9]+$`), `severity_invalid_enum`, `stopped_by_invalid_enum`.
- `gate <task-id> [--comments-json <file>]` (offline L1 seam substituting `bd show --json` output): implement EXACTLY —
```
impl = unique captures /^IMPLEMENTER: role=([a-z]+) / over comments   # may be empty
art  = LAST comment matching /^REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 /                    # none -> exit 4 review_artifact_missing
reviewer = token reviewer=([A-Za-z0-9._-]+); threshold = token risk_threshold=(\w+)
findings = parse token findings=[<id>:<sev>,...]                       # [] => empty
independent = (impl empty) OR (reviewer NOT IN impl)                   # empty set = vacuous pass
open = findings with rank(sev) >= rank(threshold)
       minus ids having a /^RESOLVED <id> / comment containing non-empty fix= AND test= tokens
       minus ids whose LATEST /^ARBITRATION <id> / comment has decision=overrule   # sustain keeps open
!independent -> exit 4 reviewer_not_independent; open>0 -> exit 4 unresolved_findings (+open_finding_ids); else 0
```
Envelope: `{ok, artifact:{...summary...}, reviewer_identity, implementers:[], independent, open_findings, open_finding_ids:[], error_key?, observations}`.

### 5. Request/artifact JSON schemas (files under `.claude/.qa-tracking/`)
- Request `review-request-<sanitized-tid>.json`: `{contract_version:"1", task_id, iteration, risk_threshold*, stop_condition*, change_set_hash, spec, diff, completion_contract, impact_report}` (*mandatory non-empty).
- Artifact `review-artifact-<sanitized-tid>-r<i>.json`: `{contract_version:"1", task_id, reviewer_identity:"sol-codex"|"qa-claude", reviewer_model, reviewed_hash, risk_threshold, stop_condition, verdict:"approve"|"findings", findings:[{id,severity,location,evidence,description}], iterations, stopped_by:"verdict"|"stop_condition"|"cap:max_findings"|"cap:max_review_iterations"|"cap:timeout"}`.

### 6. `.claude/scripts/codex-review.sh` (NEW) — root-invoked Sol driver
`codex-review.sh <task-id> --request <file> --iteration <n>`: validate request (via review-check; fail ⇒ exit 4) → read caps → `--iteration > max_review_iterations` ⇒ exit 6 → resolve server cmd/args from `${CODEX_USER_CONFIG:-$HOME/.claude.json}` (env overrides) → FIFO client: initialize → `tools/call {name:"codex", arguments:{prompt:<envelope>, sandbox:"read-only", cwd:$PROJECT_DIR}}` → overall wall-clock `timeout_seconds` ⇒ kill + exit 5 (no artifact) → extract final text, strip fences, validate as artifact; on invalid, up to `malformed_retry` corrective turns via `tools/call {name:"codex-reply", arguments:{conversationId:<from first result>, prompt:"Validation failed: <error_key>. Emit ONLY the corrected JSON object."}}`; still invalid ⇒ exit 5 → truncate findings to `max_findings` + set `stopped_by=cap:max_findings` when exceeded → FORCE fields: task_id, iterations=<n>, risk_threshold/stop_condition from request, reviewer_identity="sol-codex", reviewer_model from registration/env → write artifact file atomically, echo its path, exit 0. Envelope text: independent ADVISORY reviewer; never approves/labels/modifies; exactly ONE JSON object as final message; blocking bar = risk_threshold; STOP when stop_condition met; at most max_findings findings, most severe first; id grammar R<iteration>-F<n>; then the schema and the full request JSON.
**Schema re-verification (REQUIRED before coding the stub):** codex-cli 0.145.0 is installed on this machine. Probe the REAL server's tool schema offline: run `codex mcp-server` via your own FIFO client (or `printf` a JSON-RPC initialize+tools/list into it) and capture the `codex` tool's inputSchema — the stub must enforce the REAL argument names (prompt/sandbox/cwd may differ; conversationId name for codex-reply likewise). Record what you found in a bd comment. Do NOT invoke the `codex` tool itself (that would hit OpenAI) — tools/list only.

### 7. `qa-gate.sh` — three NEW subcommands (record writers; NO approve/Stop enforcement changes in this task)
- `review-record <tid> [--file <path>]` (mirror grade-record's style byte-for-byte): validate via `review-check.sh validate-artifact` (subprocess — no second validator), then post the comment:
  `REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 iteration=<n> reviewer=<id> model=<m> reviewed_hash=<h> risk_threshold=<sev> verdict=<v> stopped_by=<s> findings=[<id>:<sev>,...] at <ts>: <one-line summary>` (empty ⇒ `findings=[]`). JSON envelope out.
- `resolve-finding <tid> <finding-id> --fix '<ref>' --test '<ref>' '<summary>'`: validate the id exists in the LATEST REVIEW-ARTIFACT comment; empty fix/test ⇒ exit 1; post `RESOLVED <id> at <ts>: fix=<ref> test=<ref> — <summary>`.
- `arbitrate <tid> <finding-id> <overrule|sustain> '<rationale>'`: same id validation; empty rationale ⇒ exit 1; post `ARBITRATION <id> decision=<d> at <ts>: <rationale>`.
Update usage()/header docs. These grammars are LOAD-BEARING V3 contracts — byte-exact as specified.

### 8. Tests (L1 `.claude/scripts/tests/`, L2 `.claude/tests/component/specs/`, META prefix + TEXT anchors)
- L1 `review-check.test.sh`: validate-request rejections (missing risk_threshold / missing stop_condition / bad enum → exact error keys, exit 4); validate-artifact full schema matrix; META: sensitivity (a checker copy with the mandatory-field check stripped must PASS the bad fixture — proving the real check is load-bearing).
- L1 `review-count.test.sh` (via `--comments-json`): below-threshold ignored; RESOLVED lacking test= stays open; ARBITRATION sustain stays open / overrule clears / latest-wins; reviewer==implementer ⇒ exit 4 reviewer_not_independent; empty implementer set ⇒ vacuous independent; **META (plan-mandated): strip an ARBITRATION comment from a good comment-set fixture → the gate-count assertion must flip to unresolved_findings.**
- L2 `codex-detect.sh` spec: fake CODEX_USER_CONFIG absent → claude/config-absent; stub handshake OK → codex; hung stub (never answers) → timeout→claude; crashing stub → handshake-failed→claude; stub advertising NO `codex` tool → no-codex-tool→claude (META); `--refresh` rewrites; reviewer-lane.json feeds model-select artifact + statusline `rev:sol`.
- L2 `codex-review.sh` spec with a RECORDING stub codex MCP server (node script speaking real JSON-RPC over stdio, enforcing the REAL verified inputSchema, logging every request): (a) approve verdict → valid artifact + review-record posts the comment; (b) findings-above-threshold → gate reports open; (c) stub returns max_findings+3 → truncated + `stopped_by=cap:max_findings`; (d) stub sleeps past timeout_seconds (use a tiny cap in the fixture config) → exit 5, no artifact file; (e) prose-then-JSON first reply → corrective codex-reply turn used (stub-recorded); **META (plan-mandated): mutate the recorded artifact's stopped_by from cap:max_findings to verdict → the cap assertion must FAIL.**
- L2 `review-separation-records.sh` (record-writer coverage): review-record/resolve-finding/arbitrate comment grammars byte-exact (grep the posted comments); id-not-found rejections; empty-evidence rejections.
- L2 `reviewer-lane-degradation.sh` (**the degradation proof**): run an identical sequence (seed comments → review-record a qa-claude artifact → review-check gate) in two fixtures — one with reviewer-lane.json=codex + stub server present, one with neither — and diff captured outputs/comments (timestamps normalized): EMPTY. Plus the structural grep: `qa-gate.sh`, `verify-before-stop.sh`, `review-check.sh` contain zero `codex|reviewer.lane|reviewer_lane` matches; **META: inject a codex reference into a copy → structural assertion fails.**

### 9. Fixture sync
All new/modified `.claude/scripts/*.sh` (codex-detect, review-check, codex-review, qa-gate, session-start) byte-synced into the 7 e2e fixtures (manual cp; drift guard will verify). `.claude/review-config` is config — check empirically whether fixtures need it (L2 fixtures symlink scripts and may source the config; seed the fixture lib if the specs need it).

## Constraints
bash 3.2 + jq; stdout contracts + META discipline (LESSONS 3fn, llh.20); comment writers are the ONLY writers of their grammars; qa-gate/verify-before-stop APPROVE/RELEASE LOGIC UNTOUCHED (V3 does enforcement — do not add refusals now); no version bump; no permissions.deny; helpers never invoke the real `codex` TOOL (tools/list handshake only; everything else stubbed); remember helper-rewritten/bash-written files don't enter changed-files.txt (LESSONS bi3.2) — write test fixtures via bash where tracker pollution matters, but your DELIVERABLE scripts via normal Edit/Write so they're gate-tracked.

## Verification before reporting done
All suites green (L1 + L2 + `make lint` + vitest drift guard); the real-schema probe result recorded on the task; JSON manifests parse. F7 contract; llm_observations mandatory.

## REAL codex-cli 0.145.0 schema probe (offline, tools/list ONLY — codex tool NOT invoked)

Probed the installed server via `codex -m gpt-5.6-sol mcp-server` with a FIFO JSON-RPC client: `initialize` + `notifications/initialized` + `tools/list`. serverInfo.version = `0.145.0`. Two tools advertised: `codex`, `codex-reply`.

### `codex` tool inputSchema (VERBATIM key facts)
- `additionalProperties: false` — unknown args are REJECTED. The stub MUST reject them; codex-review.sh MUST send only known props.
- `required: ["prompt"]`.
- Known props: `prompt` (string), `sandbox` (enum: `read-only`|`workspace-write`|`danger-full-access`), `cwd` (string), `model`, `approval-policy` (enum untrusted|on-request|never), `base-instructions`, `compact-prompt`, `config` (object), `developer-instructions`.
- SPEC envelope `{prompt, sandbox:"read-only", cwd}` is FULLY VALID. `read-only` is a real enum member.

### `codex-reply` tool inputSchema
- NO `additionalProperties:false` (extra props tolerated).
- `required: ["prompt"]`.
- `threadId` (string) — CANONICAL. Description: "required, but kept optional for backward compat".
- `conversationId` (string) — **DEPRECATED**: "use threadId instead".
- **DELTA vs SPEC**: SPEC assumed `conversationId`; the REAL preferred field is `threadId`. codex-review.sh will pass `threadId` (primary) and the stub will accept `threadId` (also tolerate `conversationId`).

### tools/call RESULT shape (from openai/codex `codex_mcp_interface.md`, corroborated by web)
```json
{
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Hello from Codex" }],
  "structuredContent": { "threadId": "019bbed6-...", "content": "Hello from Codex" }
}
```
- Final agent message text: `.result.content[].text` (mirrored at `.result.structuredContent.content`).
- Thread id for follow-ups: `.result.structuredContent.threadId` (NOT a top-level `conversationId`; historical issues #3712/#8388/#8580 fixed by PR #18093 which propagates threadId in 0.14x).

### Consequences for codex-review.sh + recording stub
1. Extract final text via `.result.content[] | select(.type=="text") | .text` (fallback `.structuredContent.content`); strip fences; validate as artifact.
2. Extract thread id via `.result.structuredContent.threadId`.
3. Corrective turn: `tools/call {name:"codex-reply", arguments:{threadId:<id>, prompt:"Validation failed: <key>. Emit ONLY the corrected JSON object."}}`.
4. Recording stub enforces: codex requires `prompt`, rejects unknown props (additionalProperties:false semantics), validates `sandbox` enum; returns `{content:[{type:text,text:<artifact>}], structuredContent:{threadId, content}}`; codex-reply requires `prompt` + a thread ref.

codex.js wrapper is a pure passthrough spawn of the native binary (no arg rewriting).

<!-- BD-MCP-META: {"kind":"design-decision","source":"devops-agent"} -->
## Design decisions (post context-gathering, pre-implementation)

**codex-detect.sh no-arg contract**: `detect` and no-arg are aliases — both run full layered detection (config fast-path → 5s stdio handshake requiring a `codex` tool), write reviewer-lane.json atomically, and print ONLY the lane word (`codex`|`claude`) to stdout (diagnostics to stderr). This satisfies bi3.1's dormant `detect_reviewer_lane` seam (model-select.sh:494-512 runs `bash codex-detect.sh` no-arg and uses stdout live) AND session-start's `codex-detect.sh detect` capture. `--refresh` = same (force re-probe). `status` prints the JSON file or `claude/no-flag`.

**Hermeticity fix (necessary)**: On this codex-configured machine, shipping codex-detect.sh makes `detect_reviewer_lane` return codex, which would break existing L2 assertion `specs/model-select.sh` R1 ("artifact reviewer_lane defaults to claude") and slow session-lifecycle by 5s/call. Fix: add `export CODEX_USER_CONFIG=<nonexistent-in-fixture>` to `mk_fixture` (lib/fixture.sh). ## QA findings A + B — both fixed (evidence-before-fix protocol)

### FINDING B (LOW, test integrity) — vacuous D7 negative guard
**Reproduced:** `specs/codex-detect.sh:133` called `assert_not_contains`, defined ONLY in the L1 `model-roles.test.sh` (different tier, never sourced by the L2 runner). **Fix:** added a real `assert_not_contains` to `.claude/tests/component/lib/assert.sh` (mirrors `assert_contains`, inverted: PASS when absent, FAIL+forbidden/haystack message when present; bumps the shared counters so it is COUNTED). Header helper list updated.

**Sensitivity pair added** (the guard would now fail if lane=codex ever collapsed): positive control asserts the SAME all-equal role mapping with `reviewer_lane=claude` DOES render `• model:`, plus a negative that the collapsed render carries no `rev:sol`. So the guard demonstrably discriminates lane=codex from lane=claude. codex-detect spec: 21 → 24 counted assertions.

**Class sweep:** diffed every `assert_*/mk_*/shim_*` identifier called across all L2 specs against the definitions in `lib/` — **no other undefined helper** exists. That was the real risk (one silent no-op implies more).

### FINDING A (MEDIUM latent, vg8) — gate finding-suppression via embedded newline
**Reproduced end-to-end** (newline in `reviewed_hash`): (1) `validate-artifact` ACCEPTED it (exit 0); (2) the one-line record split — line 1 ended at `reviewed_hash=h`, line 2 began `EVIL-SECOND-LINE risk_threshold=high ... findings=[R1-F1:critical]`; (3) `gate` returned `open_findings=0, error_key="", exit 0` — a live **critical** finding silently suppressed.

**Fix, both layers (D5 purity intact — zero codex/lane refs added):**
1. `validate-artifact`: new error key `scalar_contains_control_char:<field>` rejecting newline/CR/tab (jq `[[:cntrl:]]`) in the scalars the record grammar EMBEDS — contract_version, task_id, reviewer_identity, reviewer_model, reviewed_hash, risk_threshold, verdict, stopped_by, `findings[].id`, `findings[].severity`. Runs BEFORE the enum/id-grammar checks so the error key names the real cause.
   *Deliberately PRECISE scope:* the reviewer's free-form prose (`location`/`evidence`/`description`) and the non-embedded `stop_condition` stay multi-line-legal — a blanket ban would reject legitimate Sol output and burn a corrective retry for zero safety gain. L1 pins both directions (multi-line `description`/`evidence` still ACCEPTED).
2. `gate` (defense in depth, TEXT-anchored `MALFORMED-ARTIFACT-GUARD-START/END`): a `^REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 ` line lacking a **well-formed** `findings=[...]` token is now `review_artifact_malformed` (exit 4), never "zero findings". Strengthened beyond the brief to require a CLOSED bracket, because a newline inside a finding id yields `findings=[R1-F1` — a token that is present but unclosed, which a `lacks findings=` check would have missed. This also protects records ALREADY in a Beads DB (layer 1 can't retro-fix those).
3. `qa-gate.sh review-record`: **verified no change needed** — it validates through the review-check subprocess, so it now refuses the exploit artifact (exit 1, `scalar_contains_control_char:reviewed_hash`, **0** comments posted). qa-gate.sh is byte-unchanged, so only review-check.sh needed re-sync.

- L1 `review-check.test.sh` §2b: newline-in-reviewed_hash, CR-in-reviewer_identity, tab-in-reviewer_model, newline-in-finding-id, newline-in-finding-severity → exact error keys; plus two PRECISION cases (multi-line description/evidence still accepted). 30 → **39** assertions.

# SPEC — 1vq.2 V2 Sol reviewer-lane PROMPTS + docs (epic 1vq, Phase V2 second half)

Source: `docs/plans/v4-trimodel.md` Phase V2. The V2 HELPERS shipped in 1vq.1 (qa-approved): `codex-detect.sh`, `.claude/review-config`, `review-check.sh` (validate-request/-artifact/gate), `codex-review.sh` (FIFO driver), and the `qa-gate.sh` record subcommands `review-record`/`resolve-finding`/`arbitrate`. This task WIRES THE PROMPTS to produce the advisory review artifact through those helpers, fixes the grading-packet item-count drift, and writes the operator doc. **This is prompts + docs only — NO code/gate-enforcement changes.** Approve/Stop refusals on reviewer independence + findings are V3 (epic jio); do NOT add them here.

## Scope guardrails (violations = rework)
- ADVISORY ONLY. The review artifact lands in the grading packet as input; it NEVER writes labels or approval records, and the gate does not yet refuse on it. The change-set-hash-bound qa-approved record stays the only release credential.
- Sol is optional: absent/failed/timeout codex → the Claude review path (QA authors the artifact itself) runs the SAME template + artifact schema, so downstream is identical. Both configs already tested green in 1vq.1's degradation spec — don't regress the structural purity (gate scripts stay codex-free).
- Do NOT touch: review-check.sh / codex-review.sh / codex-detect.sh / qa-gate.sh / verify-before-stop.sh logic (all shipped + approved); model-select.sh; the plugin version. You EDIT PROMPTS (qa.md, orchestrator.md, grader.md), docs (AGENTS.md, README, MCP_SERVERS.md), the no-nested-spawn test, and CREATE docs/CODEX_SETUP.md.

## Deliverables

### 1. `.claude/agents/qa.md` — new "Independent review artifact" step (advisory) + packet reconciliation
Add a section (place it as §6-prime, BEFORE the existing §6 rubric-relay, so the review artifact is assembled before the grading packet that carries it):
- After QA's review modules pass, QA assembles a REVIEW REQUEST (the schema shipped in 1vq.1: `.claude/.qa-tracking/review-request-<tid>.json` with contract_version, task_id, iteration, risk_threshold* (default from `.claude/review-config` risk_threshold_default), stop_condition* (QA writes it from the SPEC's acceptance criteria), change_set_hash, spec, diff, completion_contract, impact_report). Validate it with `bash .claude/scripts/review-check.sh validate-request <file>` (reject → fix the missing field).
- Branch on `bash .claude/scripts/codex-detect.sh status` reviewer_lane:
  - **lane=claude** (default / codex absent): QA AUTHORS the artifact itself (`reviewer_identity:"qa-claude"`, reviewer_model = its own pinned model, the shipped artifact schema), then records it via `bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh review-record <tid> --file <artifact>`. Proceed to assemble the grading packet (the artifact is now packet item 8, advisory).
  - **lane=codex**: QA persists the review request (file + optional bd_doc), and RETURNS `qa_status:"needs-review"` with sentinel `REVIEW-RELAY: status=needs-review` in `llm_observations` (mirroring the RUBRIC-RELAY handoff). QA does NOT spawn codex-review (subagents can't spawn/relay to MCP-driving root helpers) and does NOT approve/block on that spawn — the orchestrator relay (deliverable 2) drives Sol, records the artifact, and re-engages QA. On re-engagement the artifact exists; QA folds it into the packet as advisory item 8.
- Make explicit: the artifact is ADVISORY — QA still forms its own verdict; Sol's findings inform, never bind. The reviewer_identity being distinct from the implementer is a V3 gate concern, not a V2 blocker.

### 2. Fix the grading-packet item-count DRIFT (confirmed) + add the advisory artifact as item 8
Current drift: `qa.md:249` says "seven items" and lists item 7 = the mechanical impact report; `docs/AGENTS.md:473` and `:503` say "six items" and omit the impact report. Reconcile to the TRUTH (impact report IS item 7, present since G2.n6d), and add item 8:
- qa.md §6 packet list: keep item 7 (impact report); ADD item **8. Independent review artifact (ADVISORY)** = the latest `review-artifact-<tid>-r<i>.json` / its REVIEW-ARTIFACT comment, labeled advisory ("Sol's or QA-claude's findings; the grader weighs them but they are not binding"). Ensure qa.md's own bd_doc_write packet TEMPLATE (the section that writes sections 1–N) actually emits sections 7 and 8 (the plan flagged the template stopped at 6).
- docs/AGENTS.md:473 + :503: update "six items" → "eight items" and list items 7 (impact report) + 8 (advisory review artifact) in order, matching qa.md.
- grader.md input contract: if it enumerates the packet items, align to eight (seven mandatory + optional advisory 8th); the grader must treat item 8's verdict as advisory, never as a criterion.
- Consistency check: grep the repo for "six items"/"seven items"/"seven-item"/"packet is" and fix EVERY stale count so they all agree (RELEASE_AUDIT/CHANGELOG historical rows excepted — leave those).

### 3. `.claude/agents/orchestrator.md` — §5c "Independent-review relay (REVIEW-RELAY: review-relay)"
Mirror §5a's shape exactly (it's the canonical relay). Place it right after §5a/§5b:
- **Trigger:** QA returns `qa_status:"needs-review"` (sentinel `REVIEW-RELAY: status=needs-review`).
- **Step A:** read caps from `.claude/review-config` and lane from `bash .claude/scripts/codex-detect.sh status`.
- **Step B:** run `bash .claude/scripts/codex-review.sh <tid> --request <review-request file> --iteration <n>` at the ROOT (it drives the codex MCP server; this is why it's a root relay, like the grader).
- **Step C:** on exit 0, record the artifact via `bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh review-record <tid> --file <artifact>`; then re-engage `Task("@qa", ...)` so QA folds it into the packet.
- **Step D failure modes:** exit 5 (timeout/server fail) → record a one-line degradation note on the task and instruct QA to run the CLAUDE lane this round (author the artifact itself); exit 6 (iteration cap) → J21-style escalation, never loop; exit 4 (bad request) → return to QA to fix the request.
- **Cost gate:** codex-review is a PAID external call (meters the operator's OpenAI account) — it is manual/dev-cycle-only and cost-confirmed, exactly like the grader's paid runs. State this in the section.
- **Playwright note** (one paragraph): when the review scope includes frontend changes and the operator has a headless Playwright MCP configured, the reviewer MAY drive it — manual-gated + cost-confirmed; never a required dependency.
- Update "## Plugin scripts (Claude-invoked)" (orchestrator.md:480) to list `codex-detect.sh`, `codex-review.sh`, `review-check.sh`, and the new qa-gate subcommands (review-record/resolve-finding/arbitrate).
- NOTE: arbitration (§5d) and gate ENFORCEMENT are V3 — do NOT add them. This section only drives the ADVISORY artifact.

### 4. `.claude/scripts/tests/no-nested-spawn-instructions.test.sh` — new relay sentinels
Extend the existing sentinel guards (it already checks RUBRIC-RELAY status + grading-relay). ADD: qa.md MUST contain `REVIEW-RELAY: status=needs-review`; orchestrator.md MUST contain `REVIEW-RELAY: review-relay`. Same guard shape; keep the existing no-nested-spawn assertion (the relay must NOT be phrased as a nested spawn). This is the mechanical proof the prompts are wired.

### 5. `docs/CODEX_SETUP.md` — first-class operator doc (verify every command against LIVE docs first)
**Before writing, WebFetch the current OpenAI Codex CLI docs (learn.chatgpt.com / developers.openai.com) to confirm every command — the CLI moves fast; the installed version here is codex-cli 0.145.0.** Cover, in order:
1. What/why: the advisory Sol reviewer lane; absent = zero behavior change (the plugin's own fresh-context Claude review path covers the role).
2. Install the Codex CLI.
3. Both auth paths — ChatGPT-subscription login vs `OPENAI_API_KEY` — and the billing implication of each (Sol reviews meter against the operator's OWN OpenAI account, separate from Anthropic).
4. **User-scope registration only:** `claude mcp add --scope user codex -- codex -m gpt-5.6-sol mcp-server` (verify the flag against live docs; 1vq.1 probed the real server as `codex mcp-server` speaking JSON-RPC, tools `codex`/`codex-reply`, `codex-reply` uses `threadId`). Set reasoning effort to the maximum the CLI accepts via `~/.codex/config.toml` `model_reasoning_effort` (`max` if accepted, else `xhigh`; explicitly NOT "Ultra"/subagent mode — it conflicts with bounded diligence). **Boxed warning: NEVER put the codex entry in the project `.mcp.json`** — teammates without Codex would see a permanently-failed server.
5. Model-pinning guidance: prefer whatever the verified docs offer for tracking the newest model (a default-model config or launch wrapper) over hard-pinning `gpt-5.6-sol`, so day-zero adoption extends to the OpenAI side. Note the operator's current `~/.codex/config.toml` pins an older `gpt-5.2-codex` default — the registration's `-m` overrides per-invocation, but recommend updating the config default.
6. Verification: `/mcp` lists codex connected; workspace trust accepted; then `bash .claude/scripts/codex-detect.sh detect --refresh && bash .claude/scripts/codex-detect.sh status` reports reviewer_lane=codex.
7. Troubleshooting: pending-approval/trust states, handshake timeout, and the graceful-degrade table (any failure → lane=claude, zero behavior change).
8. Optional Playwright note (frontend review UI verification; manual-gated).
9. A banner at the top: Codex-as-MCP-server is experimental/undocumented upstream — re-verify commands against live OpenAI docs when editing this doc.

### 6. README + MCP_SERVERS cross-links (LIGHT — the full tri-model section is V5)
- README: add a short "Optional: external reviewer lane (Sol via Codex)" note under the appropriate section with a link to `docs/CODEX_SETUP.md`, framed as optional/advisory. Do NOT write the full tri-model narrative (that's V5/epic d2j) — one paragraph + link.
- docs/MCP_SERVERS.md: one line noting the OPTIONAL, user-scope, per-operator codex reviewer server (contrast with the two shipped project-scope servers bd/code-graph) + link to CODEX_SETUP.md.

## Fixture sync
qa.md/orchestrator.md/grader.md are agent prompt files — check whether the e2e fixtures carry agent copies that the drift guard tracks (they carried their own agents historically). The no-nested-spawn test is a `.claude/scripts/tests/*.sh` L1 — not a canonical hook script, so likely NOT synced; verify against `_fixture-script-sync.unit.spec.ts` scope empirically. Docs (CODEX_SETUP/AGENTS/README/MCP_SERVERS) are not synced.

## Constraints
Prompts/docs only; advisory-only (no gate enforcement — V3); no arbitration section (V3); no code/version changes; keep gate-script structural purity; the two new REVIEW-RELAY sentinels must be byte-exact so the no-nested-spawn test passes; TEXT-anchored if you add any META; WebFetch-verify all Codex commands before writing CODEX_SETUP.md.

## Verification before done
`bash tests/run-tests.sh`/`make test` green (incl. the extended no-nested-spawn test); `bash .claude/tests/component/run.sh` green (the degradation spec's structural purity must still pass — you touched no gate scripts, so it should); `make lint`; `make check` (AgentLint over the edited agent prompts — no new H/S findings); vitest drift guard; markdown sanity on CODEX_SETUP.md. Report the F7 completion contract; llm_observations mandatory (note anything the live Codex-doc verification changed vs the spec's assumed commands).

## Live Codex-doc verification — deltas vs the SPEC's assumed commands

Verified against: codex-cli 0.145.0 (installed), Claude Code 2.1.220, `learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*` (the `developers.openai.com/codex/*` paths 308-redirect there), and the shipped binary's own model catalog. Every command in CODEX_SETUP.md was EXECUTED on this machine; none of them invokes the `codex` tool, so verification cost $0.

**1. `model_reasoning_effort = "max"` IS accepted — the spec's "max if accepted, else xhigh" resolves to `max`.**
Two independent confirmations: the binary's embedded guidance ("GPT-5.6 supports `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`. If omitted, GPT-5.6 defaults to `medium`.") and the live catalog — `codex debug models` reports gpt-5.6-sol efforts = low, medium, high, xhigh, **max**, ultra, with max = "Maximum reasoning depth for the hardest problems". Doc recommends `max`, `xhigh` documented as the fallback.

**2. DOCS LAG (recorded in the doc).** The PUBLISHED config reference still lists `minimal | low | medium | high | xhigh` for `model_reasoning_effort` and does not mention `max`/`ultra`. The shipped binary accepts both. CODEX_SETUP.md states this explicitly instead of quoting the stale reference — and tells the reader to check `codex debug models` rather than trust either source. Related: `codex login status -c model_reasoning_effort=bogus` does NOT reject the value, so "try it and see" is not a valid verification path; the catalog query is.

**3. `ultra` exists and is exactly what the SPEC told me to avoid — now with a citation.** Catalog: "Maximum reasoning with automatic task delegation"; binary guidance: "Use Ultra reasoning effort for proactive multi-agent behavior". The doc names it and explains why automatic delegation breaks bounded diligence.

**4. SPEC ASSUMPTION SOFTENED: `codex mcp-server` is NOT undocumented upstream.** `learn.chatgpt.com/docs/mcp-server` documents the command, both tools (`codex`, `codex-reply`), `threadId` as the follow-up handle, and the `structuredContent` result shape — and does not label it experimental. The banner is therefore honest rather than wrong: the transport is documented, but (a) Claude-Code-as-the-client is community wiring, not an OpenAI-supported integration, and (b) the surface moves fast enough that the published config reference already lags the binary. Re-verify-on-edit instruction retained.

**5. Auth nuance.** The upstream MCP-server page states it requires an OpenAI API key. In practice ChatGPT-plan login also drives it: this machine reports `Logged in using ChatGPT` and `claude mcp get codex` -> `Status: ✔ Connected` (and 1vq.1's live `rev:sol` ran on that auth). Documented both paths with the billing split (plan credits vs Platform API rates).

**6. NEW, load-bearing, not in the SPEC: user scope is a MECHANICAL requirement, not just etiquette.** `codex-detect.sh` reads `.mcpServers.codex` from the TOP LEVEL of `~/.claude.json`. Verified empirically that `--scope local` writes to `.projects["<abs-path>"].mcpServers` in the same file (3 unrelated projects on this machine carry servers there) and `--scope project` writes the repo `.mcp.json`. The probe sees NEITHER -> `method=config-absent` -> silent Claude lane with no error. So the never-commit warning has two independent reasons, and "registered at the wrong scope" is the FIRST row of the troubleshooting table.

**7. Model-tracking mechanism found + verified (spec asked for "whatever the docs offer").** `codex debug models` renders the catalog with a `priority` preference ordering. Day-zero one-liner, executed: `codex debug models | jq -r '.models | map(select(.visibility=="list")) | sort_by(.priority) | .[0].slug'` -> `gpt-5.6-sol`. Full listing today: sol(1), terra(2), luna(3), gpt-5.5(7), gpt-5.4(16), gpt-5.4-mini(23).

**8. CORRECTION to the SPEC's pinning advice.** The spec preferred a config default over hard-pinning `-m`. But `codex-review.sh` derives the recorded `reviewer_model` from `CODEX_MCP_MODEL` -> a `-m`/`--model` pair in the REGISTERED ARGS -> else the literal string `codex`. Dropping `-m` still runs the config model but degrades the audit trail to `reviewer_model: "codex"`. The doc therefore recommends BOTH: config default (so interactive sessions track it too) AND keep `-m <slug>` in the registration (so the artifact records the real id), with a one-command refresh recipe.

**9. Stale-default trap documented.** The operator's `~/.codex/config.toml` pins `model = "gpt-5.2-codex"` — a slug no longer present in the catalog at all — while the registration's `-m` masks it for MCP runs. Documented generically as a "reconcile both" step. I did NOT modify anything outside the repo.

Doc commands executed successfully during verification: `command -v codex`/`--version`, `codex login status`, `claude mcp get codex`, `codex debug models` (both jq one-liners), `codex-detect.sh detect --refresh` -> `codex`, `codex-detect.sh status | jq -c '{reviewer_lane, method}'` -> `{"reviewer_lane":"codex","method":"handshake"}`. Additionally, the qa.md 6p.1 request-assembly snippet and the 6p.2 artifact schema were run verbatim against the real shipped validators: `validate-request` -> ok, `validate-artifact` -> ok, and a negative control (`stopped_by="bogus"`) -> exit 4 `stopped_by_invalid_enum`. `review-record` was deliberately NOT run against the live task (it would post a fake REVIEW-ARTIFACT comment into this task's audit trail); L1/L2 already cover it.

title: make lint does not cover .claude/tests/component/specs/*.sh — every L2 spec is unlinted by the canonical target
description:
Found during bjx (v4.1 U1). The Makefile lint target enumerates .claude/scripts/*.sh, .claude/scripts/tests/*.sh, install.sh and uninstall.sh — but not .claude/tests/component/specs/*.sh. There are now 38 L2 specs totalling several thousand lines of bash, none of them shellchecked by make lint. Specs written this release were lint-clean only because their authors ran shellcheck manually and said so; nothing enforces it.

Fix is a one-line glob addition, but check first whether the specs pass cleanly as a set — the L2 idiom (pre-sourced lib functions, inherited PASS/FAIL counters, deliberate unquoted heredocs in fixture builders) may need targeted disable directives, and a lint target that everyone learns to ignore is worse than one that is honest about its scope. If the set does not pass cleanly, consider a separate target (lint-specs) wired into test-ci rather than widening lint itself.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
EVIDENCE-BEFORE-FIX: root cause stated with captured observations, before any patch.

REPORTED: two symptoms in projects that curl-installed v4. (1) no workflow at all —
main session does everything, no delegation, no gate. (2) both MCP servers unavailable.
Same v4 orchestrates correctly inside the plugin's own repo.

FINDING: these are TWO bugs, not one. The directive expected a single packaging failure
and said to treat them as one investigation until evidence separates them. Evidence
separated them. Agent registration is ELIMINATED as a cause for either.

=== SYMPTOM 2 — CONFIRMED, single sufficient cause ===
MCP server dependencies are never installed in a target, and the curl path cannot even
copy them:
- install.sh:314-327 — under `curl | bash` the source is `git clone --depth 1`.
  .gitignore:34 is `node_modules/`, so THE CLONE NEVER HAS node_modules TO COPY.
  This makes install.sh:1448's rsync `--exclude=node_modules` and :1454's `rm -rf`
  secondary — fixing only those would not help the curl path at all.
- install.sh:242-289 — prereq gate hard-requires git, jq, bd. `node` is NEVER checked,
  despite "engines": {"node": ">=18.17"} in both server package.json files.
- Reproduced empirically: both launchers are dynamic-import shims
  (bd-mcp/bin/bd-mcp.js:5, code-graph-mcp/bin/code-graph-mcp.js:10) and die with
  ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk' (imported at
  bd-mcp/src/server.js:21-22, code-graph-mcp/src/server.js:23-24).
- Node's ESM resolver walks upward from the importing file, so in a target it finds
  nothing and both servers exit 1 on spawn.
- Explains the works-here/fails-there boundary exactly: this repo has node_modules from
  development (91 / 94 entries).
- Intermittency explained: a target that is itself a Node project with a hoisted
  @modelcontextprotocol/sdk could accidentally resolve, so the bug is not uniform.

Fix is cheap and needs no toolchain: NO native dependencies. sql.js and web-tree-sitter
are pure WASM; zero `hasInstallScript` and zero dev packages in either lockfile; both
package-lock.json files are git-tracked at lockfileVersion 3; the 10 tree-sitter .wasm
grammars already ship git-tracked.

AGGRAVATING: the docs assert the bug is already fixed.
- .claude/mcp/bd-mcp/README.md:30 and code-graph-mcp/README.md:47 both say
  "The plugin installer runs this automatically" — false since the feature shipped.
- install.sh:2126 / install.ps1:2155 advertise "Two MCP servers" in the SUCCESS readout.
- docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md has ZERO occurrences of "MCP".

=== SYMPTOM 1 — mechanism confirmed, trigger needs one observation from the target ===
NOT caused by symptom 2: orchestrator.md:106 and qa.md:188 mandate graceful degradation
when the code-graph tools are absent, and the Beads lifecycle runs through the `bd` CLI
over Bash, not through MCP. So a dead MCP server cannot suppress delegation.

Two candidates remain, both real, both fixed by this epic regardless of which fired:
(4) session-start.sh:21-25 and :27-31 are two hard `exit 1` paths that print a BARE
    {"error": ...} — not a hookSpecificOutput/additionalContext envelope. Claude Code
    therefore receives NO workflow_engine block, NO delegation contract, NO gate
    instructions: the session runs with the plugin installed and the orchestrator
    contract absent, and nothing says so. That is symptom 1's exact shape. Everything
    after :31 is fail-open and the workflow_engine block at :412-422 is unconditional,
    so these are the ONLY two paths that lose the context wholesale. Likeliest trigger
    is PATH divergence: bd resolves in the operator's login shell but not in the
    non-interactive shell Claude Code spawns for hooks.
(5) install.sh:1782-1799 — a mode-2 Update whose target has a pre-existing
    .claude/settings.json that is not exactly one JSON object (empty, JSONC-with-
    comments, or malformed) sets SETTINGS_MERGE_STATUS=failed-untouched and leaves the
    file UNCHANGED => ZERO hooks wired, exit 0. install.sh:1802-1803 (mode 3) skips
    settings.json entirely, same result. The status variable is consumed ONLY inside
    v3_write_report() (:1954, :1964), which runs only under V3_UPGRADE=true — so on a
    plain Update the operator gets one red line mid-scroll and then
    "Installation complete." Contrast .mcp.json's merge failure at :1550-1553, which is
    SAFE: it installs the shipped config rather than leaving the target unwired.

ELIMINATED — agent registration. The copied .claude-plugin/plugin.json IS inert in a
target (no marketplace.json exists anywhere in the repo; install.sh is a pure file copy),
so its mcpServers and "hooks" keys are dead there. BUT .claude/agents/*.md is Claude
Code's own project-agent location and the frontmatter is valid, so agents ARE
discoverable. Namespacing eliminated too: every agent's `tools:` frontmatter carries BOTH
mcp__plugin_claude-workflow_bd and mcp__bd forms.

=== ROOT ENABLER — CONFIRMED, and it is why this shipped three times ===
Every installer assertion is presence or sha256; not one is functional.
- Makefile:228-231 `install-test` is the ENTIRE post-install verification: two `test`
  calls (`test -d .claude`, `test -f plugin.json`).
- installer-mcp-config.sh / installer-manifest-parity.sh / installer-v3-upgrade.sh assert
  file presence and hash parity. The closest to functional is
  installer-v3-upgrade.sh:417, which asserts settings.json gained the SubagentStart hook
  KEY — upgrade path only, presence only, never that the hook runs.
- code-graph-mcp.sh:51-59 SKIPS ITSELF when node_modules is absent, and its comment
  states the OPPOSITE of install.sh's behaviour ("The install.sh path copies node_modules
  along with the rest of the tree when shipping"). That sentence made the self-skip look
  benign. It also boots from $(plugin_root), never from a rendered target, so even
  without the skip it could not have caught this.
- There is no bd-mcp equivalent spec at all, and no doctor/verify/preflight surface
  anywhere in the repo (searched doctor|verify|preflight|self-check).
- docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md:235 row S1 is explicit: boot "verified locally" while the
  rendered-install evidence is presence only.

=== WHAT WOULD FALSIFY / STILL OPEN ===
Which of (4) and (5) actually fired in the reported project. Discriminating commands,
to be run IN the affected target:
  jq -e '.hooks | keys' .claude/settings.json        # errors or <7 keys => (5)
  bash -lc 'command -v bd'; bash -c 'command -v bd'  # differ => (4) PATH divergence
  ls .claude/mcp/bd-mcp/node_modules                 # absent => symptom 2, expected
Both candidates are fixed and both become caught by the new doctor, so the OUTCOME no
longer depends on the answer — but the causal claim does, and it stays open until an
observation from that machine lands here.

title: qa-gate.sh approve does not clear a prior cycle qa-blocked label
description:
Found during athena-hk4 r2 (ENG-2574). Same script family and same defect class as claude-workflow-plugin-jue (enter not clearing qa-approved) and athena-m7l.

SYMPTOM: cmd_approve clears qa-gate-entered, qa-pending and rubric-pending, but NOT a qa-blocked label left by a previous cycle. A task that was blocked and then re-approved ends up carrying BOTH qa-approved and qa-blocked simultaneously — a contradictory state that any label-based reader (a watcher, a dashboard, a human skimming) can resolve either way. QA had to remove it by hand to leave the trail coherent.

Observed live: athena-hk4 showed 'LABELS: backend, devops, frontend, qa-approved, qa-blocked' immediately after approve; a monitor polling labels reported APPROVED off a state that also said BLOCKED.

FIX: cmd_approve should clear qa-blocked as part of the same atomic label transition it already performs. Pair with claude-workflow-plugin-jue — together they are 'the label transitions are not exhaustive across cycles', and the cheapest durable fix is one function that sets the terminal label and clears every other cycle label unconditionally.

BROADER PATTERN (worth fixing at the root): label presence is being used as a verdict signal, so any stale label is a false verdict. Consider having approve/block write the bound change_set_hash to a machine-readable file that readers poll for a CHANGE, rather than asking them to interpret a set of flags.

title: J21 iteration cap counts Stop attempts during long reviews, not defect rounds

comments.author: username
comments.text:
OBSERVED TWICE on claude-workflow-plugin-z9m (C0b), 2026-07-28/29.

The J21 escalation cap fired twice on a task where the code was healthy both times:

INSTANCE 1: a concurrency false-failure (see claude-workflow-plugin-1nz) — the gate
reported workflow-doctor.test.sh failing; standalone it was 94/94 and the full suite
29/29. Escalated on a spurious signal.

INSTANCE 2 (this one): the gate escalated with 'technical checks passed' and skipped
re-running them per the escalation contract. Nothing was failing. The independent
review simply had not returned yet, and each orchestrator Stop while waiting incremented
the counter.

MECHANISM: the iteration counter increments per Stop attempt, and an orchestrator
waiting on a long-running independent review necessarily Stops repeatedly. So the cost
of a THOROUGH review is charged to the same budget as defect rounds. C0b's reviews were
genuinely thorough — round 2 alone ran five mutants of the shipped installer plus a
full E2E preserve/destroy matrix — and that thoroughness is exactly what the escalation
penalised.

WHY IT MATTERS: the auto-defer rule means that if no J21 choice is recorded by the next
Stop, the gate sets qa-deferred. On this task that would have deferred the release's P0
fix while its review was still running and about to pass. The failure mode is silent and
favours haste.

SUGGESTED DIRECTIONS (not chosen; needs a design pass):
  a) Do not increment when the Stop is a pure wait — i.e. when technical checks passed
     AND the change set hash is unchanged since the previous iteration AND a review is
     in flight. That triple is cheap to evaluate and precisely characterises 'nothing
     happened since last time'.
  b) Count REVIEW ROUNDS (block records / review artifacts) rather than Stop attempts.
     Closer to J21's stated intent — 'this task has needed N attempts' — and immune to
     orchestrator polling frequency.
  c) Leave the counter and make the escalation text distinguish 'iterated N times with
     failures' from 'stopped N times, nothing failing', so the operator's J21 choice is
     informed. Cheapest, and it fixes the misleading signal without touching semantics.

Prefer (b) if the design allows: it measures the thing J21 is named for. (a) is a good
interim. Recorded as an observation with two data points rather than a proposal — the
evidence-before-fix pass should confirm the increment site before anything changes.

SYMPTOM: a sweep over targets whose tests read stdin (verify-before-stop.sh / post-edit.sh / qa-gate.sh all do `INPUT=$(cat)`) reports e.g. killed:3 survived:0 generated:56 — only 3-4 of 56 mutants actually run; the rest are silently never processed. The summary looks "clean" (0 survivors) and is dangerously misleading.

ROOT CAUSE: the parser drive loop reads the mutant wire format via `while IFS= read -r line ... done < "$MUTANTS_FILE"` (mutation-sweep.sh ~line 469-502). For each mutant it calls run_mutant, which runs the per-mutant test command in a subshell at ~line 424-427:
    (
        cd "$wt" || exit 1
        CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$wt" timeout_cmd "$MUTANT_TEST_TIMEOUT_S" bash -c "$TEST_CMD"
    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || test_rc=$?
stdin is NOT redirected, so fd0 is inherited from the `while read < mutants.txt` loop. When $TEST_CMD invokes a hook that does `INPUT=$(cat)` (or any bare `cat`/`read`), it consumes the REMAINING lines of mutants.txt. The parser's next `read` then hits EOF and the loop exits — the sweep terminates after only the mutants consumed before the first stdin-reading test.

IMPACT: any sweep whose test-cmd exercises stdin-reading code under-runs catastrophically and reports a falsely-clean survivor set. This silently defeats the whole tier for hook-script targets (the primary use case).

FIX (one line): redirect the per-mutant test invocation's stdin from /dev/null, e.g.
    ) </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 || test_rc=$?
on the subshell at ~line 427. (Equivalent: `exec </dev/null` at the top of the subshell, or read the mutants file on a dedicated fd: `while read -u 9 ...; done 9< "$MUTANTS_FILE"`.)

WORKAROUND used in llh.5 (no production edit): prefixed the --test-cmd string with `exec </dev/null;`. With that prefix the sweep correctly processed all 56 mutants.

SECONDARY (lower severity): `MUTANT_TEST_TIMEOUT_S` (and SWEEP_TIMEOUT_S) are read as `${VAR:-default}` AFTER `. "$CONF"` sources mutation.conf, which sets them as plain assignments — so an env-var override is clobbered by the conf value. An operator passing `MUTANT_TEST_TIMEOUT_S=240` on the command line is silently ignored (stays 60). Consider honoring an env override (source conf with `:-` guards, or let a CLI flag win). Workaround: point MUTATION_CONF at a temp conf copy with the desired timeout.

Discovered-from: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.5 (G2.6ix survivor triage). Run that exposed it: .claude/.mutation-runs/20260613T100354Z (killed:3/56) vs the corrected .claude/.mutation-runs/20260613T102846Z (exec </dev/null + 240s timeout, all mutants processed).

comments.author: username
comments.text:
<!-- BD-MCP-META: {"kind":"qa-note","source":"qa-agent","from_task":"claude-workflow-plugin-llh.5"} -->
## QA triage (from llh.5 gate review) — ledger impact + severity, NOT fixing here

Confirmed REAL by code read + live repro. Both halves reproduce:
- **stdin-drain** at `mutation-sweep.sh:424-427`: the per-mutant subshell runs `timeout_cmd ... bash -c "$TEST_CMD"` with only `>/dev/null 2>&1` (no stdin redirect); the parser loop reads `< "$MUTANTS_FILE"` (line ~502), so fd0 is the mutants file. All three intended sweep targets read stdin via bare `cat` (`verify-before-stop.sh:478`, `post-edit.sh:19`, `qa-gate.sh:1100` `raw=$(cat)`), so a custom test-cmd exercising them drains the mutants file -> early-stop.
- **conf-clobber** at `mutation-sweep.sh:65-71`: `[ -f "$CONF" ] && . "$CONF"` sources `mutation.conf` (plain assignments `MUTANT_TEST_TIMEOUT_S=60` line 41, `SWEEP_TIMEOUT_S=1800` line 47) BEFORE the `${VAR:-default}` lines, so an env override is silently clobbered.

**Live repro this session:** first re-sweep `20260613T100354Z` = generated 56 / killed 3 / survived 0 (early-stop, falsely-clean). I re-ran a scoped vbs sweep with the `exec </dev/null` workaround + temp-conf timeout and it processed past mutant 6 with 0 survivors — workaround confirmed effective.

### LEDGER IMPACT (for G4 / RELEASE_AUDIT.md) — narrower than first feared

365 does **NOT** retroactively invalidate the v3.4.0 C.3 acceptance numbers. I verified the original C.3 run `20260612T063107Z` processed **all 32 mutants** (killed:4 / survived:28; survivors span `verify-before-stop.sh:175..869` + `post-edit.sh:16..120`) — NOT a 3-4 early-stop. Reason: C.3 used the **default** `--test-cmd` (`DEFAULT_TEST_CMD="bash .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh"`, the L1 suite), whose hook invocations pipe their *own* stdin (`echo '{...}' | bash hook`) and never inherit the sweep's fd0. So the CHANGELOG C.3 claim (32/4/28, 27 genuine/1 equivalent) and the calibration precision 0.9412 (computed over a fixed calibration-set, sweep-independent) both stand.

**But** the bug DOES narrow `RELEASE_AUDIT.md` row **R18** (currently PROVEN): the claim "runs them in throwaway git worktrees against the free L1/L2 tiers" holds only for the **default L1** test-cmd. Any **L2-inclusive custom `--test-cmd`** (which the claim implies is supported, and which is the natural way to exercise hook behavior) silently under-runs via this bug and reports a falsely-clean survivor set. Recommendation for G4: **drop R18 from PROVEN to PROVEN-WITH-CAVEAT** with this row cited, and add to this bug's description an explicit statement that it masks sweep coverage for custom (L2-inclusive) test-cmds. The bug currently documents the symptom but not the R18/C.3 relationship.

### Severity

P2 (current) is arguably light given the bug "silently defeats the whole tier for hook-script targets" with a falsely-clean report — the dangerous part is the *silent* under-run, not a loud failure. Consider P1, OR keep P2 but add a loud guard (assert processed==generated, or fail the sweep if survived==0 AND processed<<generated). Left open and unfixed per llh.5 scope; flagging for the G4 owner.
