code_search, code_context, code_index_health (byte-compatible with the
existing code-context-mcp), plus symbol_callers, impact_of, dead_code,
dependency_path (new-stable). Zero native compile.

GRAMMAR PROVENANCE: @vscode/tree-sitter-wasm@0.3.1 (MIT, published
2026-04). Vendored 10 .wasm grammars under grammars/ totalling 9.6 MB:
typescript (^0.23.2), tsx (^0.23.2), javascript (^0.25.0), python
(^0.25.0), go (^0.25.0), rust (vscode-built), java (^0.23.5), ruby
(^0.23.1), php (0.24.2), bash (^0.25.0). Full provenance table in
grammars/MANIFEST.md. We tried tree-sitter-wasms@0.1.13 first but it
ships the legacy 'dylink' custom-section name; web-tree-sitter 0.26
requires 'dylink.0'. The vscode-built grammars use the modern format.

SQLITE CHOICE: sql.js@1.14.1 (wasm). Spec mentioned node:sqlite (Node
22+) as an alternative; we stay on sql.js because the plugin floor is
Node 18.17. Trade-off: sql.js loads the whole DB into memory, but
realistic index sizes are a few MB so this is fine. Documented in
README + db.js header.

LAZY BUILD VERIFIED: server boot ~110ms (no DB read, no parsing); first
tool call triggers ensureIndex which preloads parsers and walks the
project; subsequent calls hit the warm DB in milliseconds.

LANGUAGE COVERAGE (honest, see README matrix):
- ts/tsx/js: defs (functions, classes, methods, types, exports), calls
  (incl. member+new), imports (relative paths resolved to local files
  via common extensions + index files)
- python: defs (def, class, top-level assignments), calls, imports
  (dotted modules resolved to .py / __init__.py)
- go: defs (incl. methods + type specs + consts/vars), calls (incl.
  selector method calls), imports (recorded by name only — module
  resolution not attempted)
- rust: defs (fn, struct, enum, trait, impl, mod, const, static),
  calls (incl. macros), imports (recorded by name only)
- java/ruby/php/bash: per-language def smoke + calls (tree-sitter-ruby
  0.23 removed method_call node — query updated accordingly)

WHAT THE STATIC GRAPH CAN'T SEE (echoed in tool descriptions): dynamic
dispatch, reflection / metaprogramming, macro expansion, renaming
re-exports, external library calls. dead_code carries an extra-loud
caveat block because false positives there are common (barrel
re-exports, externally consumed surface).

SYMBOL_CALLERS PREEXISTING: NO. The .mcp.json
_phase7_codebase_graph_target.tools_to_expose listed symbol_callers
but the current code-context-mcp ships only 3 tools (code_search /
code_context / code_index_health). It is new-stable with this server
and called out in the README.

TESTS:
- node:test suite (3 files, 31 tests, ~1.5s):
  - tests/indexer.test.js: 7 tests (cross-file resolution, incremental
    rebuild fires only on hash change, pruning drops deleted files,
    polyglot smoke for rust/java/ruby/php/bash, CORRUPT_INDEX contract,
    force=true)
  - tests/tools.test.js: 14 tests (all 7 tools incl. seeded transitive
    closure for impact_of, seeded orphan unusedHelper for dead_code,
    middle->deep dependency_path + not_connected branch, healthy/
    unhealthy/uninitialized health, both-seeds-present rejection)
  - tests/server.test.js: 9 protocol-level tests (Zod validation,
    structured error envelopes carry hint+example)
- L2 spec .claude/tests/component/specs/code-graph-mcp.sh: 29
  assertions covering boot, tools/list, health round-trip,
  malformed-args envelope, META-TEST corrupt-index reports unhealthy,
  META-TEST sensitivity (stub the detection branch, assert the
  unhealthy assertion now fails). Uses the rubric-loop.sh awk-stub +
  sentinel anchor-drift-guard pattern. All passing in make test-all
  (20 specs, 388 assertions total).

VERIFICATION RUN (cold-start stdio): initialize -> serverInfo.name=
code-graph-mcp / version=1.0.0; tools/list returns the 7 tools with
inputSchemas; code_search({query:"buildServer"}) returned 3 matches in
~3.3s wall (cold first build of the plugin repo). Subsequent calls are
ms. Pasted in the agent return JSON.

NOT TOUCHED (B.2 follows): .mcp.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json,
code-context-mcp/. The new server is OFF the wire in this task. Gate
not approved; no commit, no push.

KEY DECISIONS:
- Dedupe symbols by (file_id, name, start_line, start_col) in the
  indexer's per-file map, merging is_export when an export_statement
  also captures the inner def. Without this, every exported symbol
  appears twice and the single-candidate resolver refuses to bind any
  edge to it.
- Skip-by-rel-path .claude/.code-graph + .claude/.qa-tracking instead
  of skipping .claude/ wholesale. The plugin's own source lives in
  .claude/, so a wholesale skip would make the server unable to index
  its own home repo (and any user-extended .claude/scripts/ tree).
- Lazy first build is in ensureIndex inside each tool handler — never
  in module init, never at server boot. Boot stays instant.
- File seed for impact_of uses the file's symbols PLUS file_dependents
  (importers). Symbol seed walks transitive callers only. Both seeds
  share the same nodes[] shape; file seed adds the file_dependents
  array.
- Errors carry both hint: and example: in every CodeGraphError. The
  example is a worked valid call so a self-correcting agent can retry
  without a human round-trip.

  are SCENARIO-named, not fixture-named. Verified the mapping from each
  spec's `FIXTURE_PATH = path.resolve(__dirname, "..", "fixtures", "<name>")`:

    rubric-revision-loop   → rubric-revision-loop.spec.ts

  was 1:1; actually 6/7 are — the lone exception is node-react-auth).
  Makefile's own help (line 49) and README docs advertise FIXTURE=node-react-auth,
  so fixture name is the documented interface.

G2 — Failing test (before fix):

  Specs: Total: 1  Passed: 0  Failed: 1
  Assertions: Passed: 1  Failed: 16
  (Failures: every resolver invocation hits "No such file or directory" —
   the helper didn't exist yet, which is the precise failure shape we want
   the test to surface.)

RESOLUTION MECHANISM:
  Added .claude/scripts/resolve-fixture-spec.sh (new helper). It scans
  .claude/tests/e2e/specs/*.spec.ts for a path.resolve(...,"fixtures",
  "<FIXTURE>") reference and prints the matching spec filename. Unknown
  fixture → exit 1 with a listing of available fixtures on stderr. Missing
  arg → exit 2 + usage. Honours CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR for installed-plugin
  scenarios; falls back to script-relative plugin-root derivation. Skips
  underscore-prefixed unit specs (_*.unit.spec.ts) so they can't shadow
  a live spec match.

  Makefile test-live now (a) resolves first, then prompts — so a typoed
  FIXTURE fails fast before the cost preview, (b) shells out to the helper
  per fixture, (c) prints "resolved spec(s) -> <list>" so the user sees
  the resolved targets BEFORE confirming, (d) preserves FIXTURE=required,
  cost-confirmation, multi-fixture FIXTURES=, and CONFIRM=1 behaviour.

  Resolver design rationale documented inline in the script header: the
  alternative — a static dispatch table — would drift the next time
  someone adds a spec, which is the exact regression class we're fixing.
  Scanning the source-of-truth (the spec's own FIXTURE_PATH constant)
  means the resolver stays correct without an extra maintenance burden.

  - issues.jsonl is NOT in .beads/.gitignore, so it gets cleaned.
  - sync_base.jsonl IS in .beads/.gitignore (line 38), so it survives.
  - beads.db is also gitignored — survives — carrying the metadata table's stale hash.

   'To restrict tools, use either the tools field (allowlist) or the
   disallowedTools field (denylist). This example uses tools to exclusively
   allow Read, Grep, Glob, and Bash. The subagent can't edit files, write
   files, or use any MCP tools'. The SDK structurally strips MCP tools from
   the subagent's surface when 'tools:' is an allowlist that omits them.
   Same defect in backend.md, frontend.md, devops.md, orchestrator.md.
   Evidence: cassettes/seed/node-react-auth-2026-06-11T23-34-49-784Z.jsonl —
   declared 7 code-graph tools at root scope, 0 invocations from QA, QA's
   free text 'code-graph MCP unavailable' (false from outside QA, true from
   inside QA's stripped surface).

2. DOC QUOTE ON MCP TOOL NAMES (code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions):
   'mcp__puppeteer matches any tool provided by the puppeteer server'
   'mcp__puppeteer__* wildcard syntax that also matches all tools from the puppeteer server'
   'mcp__puppeteer__puppeteer_navigate matches the puppeteer_navigate tool'
   The same naming registry applies to subagent 'tools:' allowlist entries
   (the docs do not show MCP entries in 'tools:' examples but the canonical
   tool-naming registry is shared across the permission system).
   Plugin-bundled MCP tool form (code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp):
   'mcp__plugin_<plugin-name>_<server-name>__<tool-name>'.

3. FRONTMATTER FORM USED:
   Each non-grader agent's 'tools:' line was extended with four server-level
   grants (the cleanest, resilient-to-new-tools form):
     mcp__plugin_claude-workflow_code-graph  (plugin-load prefix, code-graph)
     mcp__plugin_claude-workflow_bd          (plugin-load prefix, bd)
     mcp__code-graph                         (project-scope prefix, code-graph)
     mcp__bd                                 (project-scope prefix, bd)
   Both prefixes are declared because plugin.json and .mcp.json register the
   servers under different prefixes (plugin-load = full plugin-namespaced;
   project-scope = bare server name). The agent files are bundled by
   plugin.json AND committed to the project tree, so either path can be the
   load path depending on how the user installs the plugin.

4. FAILING TEST EVIDENCE (pre-fix run of the new L1 test):
   Created .claude/scripts/tests/agent-mcp-tools-parity.test.sh — asserts
   for every agent file with a 'tools:' frontmatter line that every

5. FIXES SHIPPED (no commit, no QA approve):

   a. AGENT FRONTMATTER (5 files):
      .claude/agents/qa.md, backend.md, frontend.md, devops.md, orchestrator.md

      Replaced the graceful-degradation prose so an EMPTY index is NOT a
      degradation reason — code_index_health reporting empty/missing means
      'first impact_of call builds the index lazily; PROCEED'. Degrade to
      grep ONLY when the code-graph tools are structurally absent from the
      tool surface (no mcp__*code-graph* entry). Both files updated.

      .claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/node-react-auth/fixture.yaml — re-added the
      invariants block stripped during the live run's restore. Includes
      qa-queried-impact-of as the Phase B regression anchor. The failing
      _invariants.unit.spec.ts:845 test ('real fixture.yaml files parse and
      declare invariants for all 6 fixtures') flips green post-fix.

   d. RESTORE EXCLUSION MECHANISM (.claude/tests/e2e/lib/runFixture.ts):
      Added HARNESS_METADATA_FILES = ['fixture.yaml'] and the
      snapshotHarnessMetadata / restoreHarnessMetadata helpers.
      snapshotFixture now captures fixture.yaml's bytes AT THE TOP OF THE

title: Dirty-on-entry recovery wipes uncommitted fixture.yaml before snapshotHarnessMetadata captures it
description: Cause B from Run 3 forensic. In runFixture.ts the order is: (1) dirty-on-entry check runs 'git reset --hard HEAD && git clean -fd' at lines 811-818; (2) snapshotFixture runs at line 838 which calls snapshotHarnessMetadata. If the fixture's nested-git HEAD does not contain the operator's intended fixture.yaml (e.g. the outer plugin repo updated fixture.yaml in commit 256e0c1 but the fixture's nested git HEAD = 7207544 'auto-init' predates that), the operator's edit appears as uncommitted relative to the nested HEAD. The dirty recovery wipes it, snapshot captures already-wiped bytes, and the end-of-run restore writes the wiped bytes back. Net: fixture.yaml -28 lines vs outer HEAD on disk, satisfiesInvariants() fails with 'no invariants declared'.
notes:
COMPLETED OFFLINE (no paid runs). Evidence-before-fix protocol followed.

=== ROOT CAUSE (verbatim, with citations) ===

In runFixture.ts (pre-fix), the dirty-on-entry self-heal at lines 811-818 ran BEFORE snapshotFixture at line 838. Sequence in run 3 of Phase B:
  1. Fixture's nested git HEAD = 7207544 ('fixture: initial state (auto-init)', Mon May 11 2026) predates the outer plugin repo's invariants commit 256e0c1 (Fri Jun 12 2026).
  2. Outer repo's fixture.yaml has the invariants block; inner repo sees those 28 lines as UNCOMMITTED relative to its own HEAD.
  3. runFixture sees 'git status --porcelain' dirty → fires recovery: 'git reset --hard HEAD && git clean -fd -e node_modules'.
  4. Reset wipes the operator's intended invariants block. clean wipes crash-leftover untracked files.
  5. snapshotFixture(line 838) calls snapshotHarnessMetadata which now reads the POST-RESET (no-invariants) fixture.yaml bytes.
  6. End-of-run restoreHarnessMetadata writes those post-reset bytes back → working tree ends -28 lines vs outer HEAD.
  7. Mid-run, satisfiesInvariants() reads the file at this state → parseInvariantsFromYaml returns 0 → matcher fails with 'no invariants declared in fixture.yaml'.

Empirical verification offline:
  - Pre-restore working tree (manual git checkout -- fixture.yaml at the start of this session): 28-line diff vs HEAD, matching the brief's claim.
  - Test red baseline: vitest specs/_invariants.unit.spec.ts:845 ('real fixture.yaml files parse and declare invariants for all 6 fixtures') failed with 'fixture node-react-auth should declare invariants (post-0.8): expected 0 to be greater than 0' — proving the working tree fixture.yaml had 0 invariants.

=== CAUSE A (Question A) — REBUTTED ===

The brief hypothesised code-graph tools 'vanished' in run 3. FALSE PREMISE — the trace shows 7 code-graph tools declared identically to run 2 (each occurring 3x: top-level toolsAvailable, systemInit.tools, systemInit.raw.tools). pluginErrors=[], systemInit.mcpServers shows plugin:claude-workflow:code-graph status=connected in both runs. The brief author counted the 2x server-name occurrences (server registration scope only) and mistakenly concluded tool-level names also vanished.

The REAL cause-A finding: QA had impact_of available and chose not to call it (model-behaviour gap). Filed as claude-workflow-plugin-366.9, stays OPEN as it needs a paid run to test mitigations.

=== FIX (366.8) ===

Files changed:
  - .claude/tests/e2e/lib/runFixture.ts: extracted dirty-on-entry recovery into exported selfHealOnEntry(fixturePath) which captures snapshotHarnessMetadata BEFORE the git reset+clean and writes it back IMMEDIATELY after. Replaced the inline lines 811-818 with a call to selfHealOnEntry.
  - .claude/tests/e2e/specs/_fixture-restore.unit.spec.ts: added spec 'Run-3 regression: uncommitted fixture.yaml SURVIVES the dirty-on-entry self-heal that precedes snapshotFixture (claude-workflow-plugin-366.8)' — sets up a sandbox with operator's uncommitted invariants edit + crash leftovers + agent mid-crash mutation, calls selfHealOnEntry, asserts (a) fixture.yaml retains operator bytes, (b) crash leftover is cleaned, (c) tracked src.js reverted to HEAD; then runs the full snapshotFixture / mid-run-mutation / restoreFixture round-trip and re-asserts (d) fixture.yaml ends with operator's bytes.
  - .claude/tests/e2e/specs/_phase-b-run3-trace.unit.spec.ts: new anchor pinning run-3 facts (367-line spec).
  - .claude/tests/e2e/cassettes/seed/node-react-auth-2026-06-12T00-50-56-312Z.jsonl: anchored.

## FIX for QA cycle-1 HIGH data-loss finding — ready for re-review

Gate left at `qa-blocked` as instructed. No commit. No approve.

### Independent reproduction first (evidence-before-fix)
Reproduced all three arms myself before touching code, with my own sentinel and probe (trees at `/tmp/my-36z-probe.txt`). Confirmed byte-for-byte:

- **A** v3.5→v4 upgrade: sentinel absent from the ENTIRE tree including the backup; readout printed `docs/HOOKS.md (replaced; yours is in the backup)`.
- **B** mode-2 Update: a backup dir existed but held nothing outside `.claude/`; same false claim.
- **C** fresh install over a pre-existing `docs/HOOKS.md`: overwritten under a bare `OK   HOOKS.md`.

Root cause confirmed at the cited lines. **I also found a fourth leg QA did not cite**: the v2→v3 migration backup (`install.sh`, was CLAUDE.md-only). A v2 tree can own a `docs/HOOKS.md`, and that path sets `UPDATE_MODE=true` then falls through to a fresh install with no verdict walk. Fixed too — the goal was to kill the class, not the three instances.

### Fix approach per arm

**Structural (kills the class).** `$SHIPPED_DOCS` / `$ShippedDocs` hoisted ABOVE every backup leg in both installers, and the backup list is now *derived* from it:
`BACKUP_ROOT_FILES="CLAUDE.md .mcp.json LESSONS.md .worktreeinclude $SHIPPED_DOCS"` (ps1: `@(...) + $ShippedDocs`). One helper — `backup_root_files` / `Copy-RootFiles` — is called from every leg: **4 in bash** (v2, v3, mode 1, mode 2), **3 in ps1** (no v2; it redirects). A future addition to the subset cannot go missing from a backup, because there is no second literal to forget.

**A + B (arms with a backup dir).** Both legs now snapshot root-scope files. The retired hardcoded lists are gone from both files (asserted `== 0`).

**C (fresh path, no plan/no backup dir).** Pre-copy `preserve_pre_existing_doc` / `Save-PreExistingDoc`: exists-AND-differs → operator bytes to `<path>.bak`, named readout line, then copy. Skipped under `VERDICT_MODE` (those paths take a real backup) and `MERGE_MODE` (mode 3 skips existing files). A failed preservation **refuses the copy** — losing the plugin's doc is recoverable from source, losing the operator's is not. An already-identical doc collects no `.bak`.

**Why `.bak` and not `.new`:** the gate messages and the CHANGELOG upgrade note point operators at `docs/HOOKS.md` **by name**, so the shipped doc must win the canonical path. `.new` is the operator-class convention (operator content wins); these are workflow class. `.bak` is the suffix the installer already uses for pre-merge copies, and the generated .gitignore already covers it.

### Layout decision: MIRRORED (as QA recommended)
A root row keeps its relative path; a flat row's relative path IS its basename — so the four pre-U0.8 names land exactly where they always did and only nested rows are new. Rationale: the old "flat" comment was really about `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (which would nest a second `.claude-plugin/` inside a `.claude/` snapshot); flattening `docs/HOOKS.md` to `HOOKS.md` is ambiguous against any root-level `HOOKS.md` and makes the report's `diff -r` advice wrong. Same rule this change set gave the trash, so both destructive paths now agree. **`plugin.json` keeps its flat basename** as the one deliberate exception (flagship 6f depends on it) — pinned so "make it all mirrored" can't silently break 6f.

### Regression tests — CONTRACT, not report string
New **L2 flagship section 11** (+34 assertions), driven by content:
- 11a upgrade arm: operator bytes RECOVERABLE and byte-exact at the mirrored `backup/docs/HOOKS.md`; not flattened; flat entries + plugin.json still flat.
- 11b mode-2 arm: post-install edit recoverable byte-exact in the mode-2 backup.
- 11c fresh arm: `.bak` byte-exact, readout names both the file and where the bytes went; identical-doc case collects no `.bak`.
- 11d META: strips `ROOT-BACKUP-START/END` from a copy → bytes become unrecoverable **while the mutant still prints "yours is in the backup"**, which is precisely why the report string was never a usable oracle.

The checker is a content search (`operator_bytes_recoverable`), so a fix that only reworded the claim leaves these red. Verified: the 10 new assertions were **RED before the fix, GREEN after**.

Sentinels sit **inside** the helper deliberately — wrapping the definition made the strip fail-CLOSED (4 call sites to an undefined function, aborting under `set -e`); a META must leave a runnable installer. Stripped, it degrades to pre-U0.8 behaviour, never a crash. Pinned in 6r.

New **L1 packaging-parity section 6r** (+40) — ps1 textual parity: one helper each, exact call-site counts per leg, derivation-from-`$ShippedDocs`, **definition-order assertions** (list defined above the first leg, or the derivation reads an empty variable and the bug returns with the fix apparently in place), retired lists gone, layout documented in both, plugin.json-flat exception, fail-open strip, and the fresh-guard mirror. **META 21** deletes the ps1 mode-2 call (located by line number, not a brittle indentation pattern) and watches the count assertion fail.

### plugin_json_version (QA's non-blocking item) — fixed properly
QA's premise was slightly off and testing it found the real hazard: the loose `^[[:space:]]*"version"` anchor ignores *inline* nested keys but **does** take a nested own-line `"version"` appearing before the top-level one. Tightened to the top-level indent depth. **META 22** extracts the sed program FROM install.sh (not a retyped copy), proves the shipped anchor returns `9.9.9` on the hostile fixture while the retired one returned `0.0.1`, and pins that a reformat yields EMPTY (→ 6m's executed `--help` check fails loudly) rather than silently wrong.

### Suite totals
- **L1 26/26.** packaging-parity 423 → **469**.
- **L2 36/36, 1471 assertions** (was 1437; +34).
- **L3 offline 437 pass / 5 skipped**; fixture drift guard 175/175.
- `make lint` clean (shellcheck rc=0); `make manifest-validate` OK.
- ps1: 6l ASCII guard clean on both files; brace/paren balance identical to HEAD.

### My own re-run of QA's three arms, post-fix
| arm | operator bytes recovered from | byte-exact |
|---|---|---|
| A upgrade | `.claude-v3-backup-*/docs/HOOKS.md` | YES |
| B mode-2 | `.claude-backup-*/docs/HOOKS.md` | YES |
| C fresh | `docs/HOOKS.md.bak` | YES |

Live file is the shipped copy in every arm; arm C readout: `keep docs/HOOKS.md was already here and differs; your copy saved as docs/HOOKS.md.bak`.

### QA-verified-clean areas — confirmed undisturbed
Refreeze still byte-identical from the tag (117 rows, diff still exactly +1); uninstall.sh/.ps1 unchanged by this fix; gitignore still 9/9 with ps1 line-for-line parity; branding still `v4.0.0` by execution; merge-status four-state untouched.

### New behaviour deltas for QA (beyond cycle 1)
1. Backups now contain root-scope files at mirrored paths — mode 2's backup previously held nothing outside `.claude/`, so its contents grow.
2. Mode 1's `CLAUDE.md`-only copy is superseded by the shared helper (CLAUDE.md is the first list entry — same coverage, one code path).
3. The v2 migration backup now covers root files too (fourth leg, not in QA's report).
4. Fresh install can now emit a `keep ... saved as *.bak` line and leave a `.bak` sidecar in `docs/`.
5. A fresh install REFUSES to overwrite a shipped doc when the `.bak` could not be written (prints `warn`, exits 0, plugin doc not installed at that path).

model-select: switched claude-opus-4-7 -> claude-fable-5
Pin AFTER:  claude-fable-5
```

The notice fires (via _warn — stderr passes through subshells), but the gate at cmd_apply:500 NEVER prevents the rewrite. The pin IS changed.

**Root cause** (file:line evidence):

`.claude/scripts/model-select.sh:491` reads `best=$(pick_best "$models")`. The `$(...)` is a command substitution subshell. Inside pick_best, line 341 does `MANUAL_ADOPT_REQUIRED="$picked_id"`. Bash semantics: variable assignments inside a `$(...)` subshell modify the subshell-local copy only; the parent process's variable is untouched. So when cmd_apply checks `if [ -n "$MANUAL_ADOPT_REQUIRED" ]` at line 500, it always sees the empty string from line 89. The "loud notice + manual /workflow-model adopt" contract documented at lines 49-52 of the file header is bypassed in 100% of unparseable-date cases.

Same subshell pattern at lines 468 (cmd_resolve) and 551 (cmd_status); the impact at those sites is smaller (no rewrite) but the manual-adopt gate is uniformly dead.

**Why the L2 spec missed it**: specs A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, X, Y, Z, W, I cover happy paths + exclusion + cache + sort tie-break + lying picker. ZERO assertions exercise the unparseable-created_at branch. The MANUAL_ADOPT_REQUIRED gate is untested.

**Fix sketch** (two viable approaches):

1. Pass MANUAL_ADOPT_REQUIRED out of pick_best via stdout sentinel. Have pick_best print `MANUAL\t<id>` on the manual-adopt path and `<id>` otherwise; have cmd_apply parse the prefix.
2. Write MANUAL_ADOPT_REQUIRED to a temp file inside pick_best and have callers read it after the substitution. (Less clean — relies on shared filesystem state.)

Approach 1 is cleaner: the sentinel travels via the already-used stdout channel, no shared mutable global needed.

**Required regression tests**:
- L2 spec: unparseable created_at on winner -> apply refuses rewrite (assert pin unchanged); resolve still prints the id with the LOUD notice on stderr; status surfaces "cached best: <id> (manual adopt required)".
- L2 spec META-TEST: strip the gate from cmd_apply, assert the preceding test fails (sensitivity).

**Scope**: Item 1 of hotfix vlp.1 must be re-opened. The other vlp.1 deliverables (created_at sort, exclusion semantics, --refresh, statusline pin, ranking rewrite, docs sweep) are intact and verified.

title: F2/F4/F5/F7/F8 ignore COMMAND_EXCLUSIONS; fault-classes.md claim is false
description:
Phase C.1 mutation generator: only F1, F3, F6 invoke should_skip(), which is the function that enforces COMMAND_EXCLUSIONS. F2 (guard deletion), F4 (variable-default removal), F5 (pipeline-segment drop), F7 (sentinel mutation), and F8 (arithmetic) all read the target file line-by-line WITHOUT checking should_skip. fault-classes.md lines 232-235 claim 'The generator pattern list explicitly skips any line whose first token is in the exclusion set (mutation.conf key command_exclusions).' This is materially false for 5/8 fault classes.

Currently latent — no destructive-command-with-mutatable-shape lines exist in .claude/scripts/*.sh. Becomes exploitable the moment a target with such a line is added or mutated manually.

Mutants apply inside a throwaway worktree (good) but the test command runs with the user's environment (inheriting $HOME, $SAFE_BASE, etc.). A mutant of `rm -rf "${SAFE_BASE:-/tmp/safe}"` becomes `rm -rf "${SAFE_BASE}"` and IF that env var is set to the user's home in the parent shell, the mutant deletes $HOME despite the worktree containment.

Fix: add `should_skip "$line" && continue` to gen_f2, gen_f4, gen_f5, gen_f7, gen_f8 — symmetric with F1/F3/F6. Add an L1 assertion: for each fault class, build a fixture with an rm-shaped trigger line and assert the generator emits zero mutants.

Proof in QA notes:

  PROBE target:
    rm -rf "${HOME:-/}"            (F4 trigger)
    rm -rf "${SAFE_BASE:-/tmp/safe-default-dir}"  (F4 trigger)
    rm -f file | grep foo | wc -l    (F5 trigger)
    rm -rf qa-approved.lock          (F7 trigger)
    rm -f "$((COUNTER + 1)).log"    (F8 trigger)

  Actual generator output:
    F4 emitted 3 mutants (all 'rm -rf ...' lines)
    F5 emitted 1 mutant (drops 'grep foo' segment)
    F7 emitted 1 mutant ('qa-approved' -> 'qa-approve')
    F8 emitted 1 mutant ('+ 1' -> '+ 2')

#!/bin/bash
# workflow-denylist.sh — THE definition of "paths the workflow never treats
# as reviewable work" (claude-workflow-plugin-3mg.1, v4 Phase V4).
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# --------------------
# Three scripts each need the same answer to "is this path reviewable?":
#
#   post-edit.sh           what gets TRACKED into changed-files.txt
#   impact-report.sh       what enters the canonical change set + its HASH
#   verify-before-stop.sh  what the Stop gate treats as needing REVIEW
#
# They each carried their own copy of the regex and the copies DRIFTED:
# only verify-before-stop's knew about `.claude/worktrees/` and the e2e
# fixture-churn alternation. The consequence was not cosmetic — post-edit
# tracked harness-worktree paths that the Stop gate could not see, so those
# paths entered the change-set hash while being invisible to the gate's own
# view of the change set. The hash and the gate disagreed about what "the
# changes" even were.
#
# One definition, three consumers. A change here changes all three at once,
# which is the point — see the HASH MIGRATION note below for the cost.
#
# CONTRACT
# --------
#   WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX   ERE, for `[[ "$p" =~ $WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX ]]`
#   workflow_denylisted <path>
#       exit 0  -> DROP the path (build artifact / workflow-internal churn)
#       exit 1  -> KEEP the path (reviewable work)
#
# Sourcing convention (all three consumers): resolve this file relative to
# ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} of the CONSUMER, never relative to $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.
# A hook script may legitimately run with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR pointing at a
# DIFFERENT checkout than the one the script itself lives in (the primary's
# gate evaluating a worktree); the lib must always be the sibling of the
# script that sources it.
#
# No side effects: this file defines one variable and one function and does
# nothing else. bash 3.2 compatible (no associative arrays, no ${x^^}).
#
# WHAT IS DELIBERATELY *NOT* DENYLISTED
# -------------------------------------
#   CLAUDE.md   behaviour-bearing (session-start injects it) — reviewable.
#   LESSONS.md  audit deliverable — reviewable.
#   HANDOFF.md  audit deliverable — reviewable.
#   .beads/*.jsonl, .claude/.qa-tracking/*
#               NOT denylisted: they stay in the change set / audit trail.
#               verify-before-stop.sh classifies them separately via
#               is_beads_or_gate_path (a change set consisting solely of
#               them is fast-path eligible). Denylisting them would erase
#               them from the hash too, which is not the intent.
# The *.md doc-only fast path (F1) already handles the three .md files above
# when they change alone.
#
# HASH MIGRATION (fail-closed, one landing = one migration)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# change_set_hash is a sha256 over the DENYLIST-FILTERED changed-files list.
# Editing this regex therefore changes the recomputed hash for any change set
# containing a newly-(un)matched path. An approval recorded before the edit no
# longer matches the hash the Stop hook recomputes after it, so the gate emits
# LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD and re-blocks until a fresh `qa-gate.sh enter` +
# re-approve. That is the correct fail-closed direction (a stale approval must
# not release), but it is USER-VISIBLE friction: ship denylist additions in ONE
# landing so in-flight cycles pay the migration exactly once. See CHANGELOG
# and docs/HOOKS.md ("Denylist changes are a hash migration").

# Consolidated regex. Alternation order is cosmetic (ERE alternation is
# unordered for a boolean match); grouped by intent for readability.
#
#   1. build / dependency output directories
#   2. .claude/worktrees/       parallel-agent scratch checkouts. Never a
#                               deliverable; the worktree's own gate reviews
#                               its work in situ.
#   3. e2e fixture churn        .claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/<f>/.claude/{scripts,beads}
#                               and <f>/.beads — rewritten mechanically by the
#                               harness's run-start sync and by the live run's
#                               own bd writes. ANTI-OVERREACH: scoped to those
#                               subtrees only, so a real edit to a fixture's
#                               fixture.yaml / src/ is still reviewable.
#   4. memory files             MEMORY.md (the auto-memory index) and
#                               .claude/memory/. Agent-written recall state,
#                               not deliverables; they must leave the
#                               reviewable set BEFORE F1 doc-only
#                               classification so a memory-only change set is
#                               `empty` (nothing to review) rather than
#                               `doc-only` (auto-approved WITH a gate record).
#   5. lock / map / minified / compiled artifacts
WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX='(^|/)(node_modules|dist|build|coverage|\.git|\.next|\.nuxt|target|__pycache__)/|(^|/)\.claude/worktrees/|(^|/)\.claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/[^/]+/(\.claude/(scripts|beads)|\.beads)/|(^|/)MEMORY\.md$|(^|/)\.claude/memory/|\.(lock|lockb|map|pyc)$|\.min\.(js|css)$|(^|/)(pnpm-lock\.yaml|package-lock\.json|yarn\.lock|bun\.lockb|Cargo\.lock|poetry\.lock|go\.sum)$'

# workflow_denylisted <path> — 0 = drop it, 1 = keep it.
workflow_denylisted() {
    [ -n "${1:-}" ] || return 1
    [[ "$1" =~ $WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX ]]
}

#      WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX + workflow_denylisted, and parses.
#   2. Each of the three consumers SOURCES it, resolved BASH_SOURCE-relative
#      (never $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR-relative: 3mg.2 runs the primary checkout's
#      hook with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR pointing at a worktree).
#   3. No consumer carries a literal `DENYLIST_REGEX='(^...` definition of
#      its own. Assigning FROM the shared variable is the sanctioned form.
#
# META-TEST: a fixture copy of a consumer that re-declares a literal regex
# must FAIL check 3, and one with its source line deleted must FAIL check 2.
# Without those, both checks could be vacuously green.
#
# Exit codes:
#   0  all assertions pass and the META-TESTs flag the broken fixtures
#   1  one or more assertions failed

set -u

PASS=0
FAIL=0
FAILED_TESTS=()

PROJECT_DIR="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd)}"
SCRIPTS_DIR="$PROJECT_DIR/.claude/scripts"
LIB="$SCRIPTS_DIR/workflow-denylist.sh"

# set + its HASH, what the Stop gate treats as needing REVIEW.

assert_eq() {
    local name="$1" expected="$2" actual="$3"
    if [ "$expected" = "$actual" ]; then
        PASS=$((PASS + 1))
        printf '  PASS: %s\n' "$name"
    else
        FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
        FAILED_TESTS+=("$name")
        printf '  FAIL: %s\n    expected: %s\n    actual:   %s\n' \
            "$name" "$expected" "$actual"

# The two checkers. Both take a FILE so the META-TESTs can run them against
# deliberately broken fixture copies — the assertion and its sensitivity
# proof then exercise byte-identical logic.

# check_sources_lib <file> — 0 when the file sources workflow-denylist.sh
# BASH_SOURCE-relative; 1 when it sources it some other way (e.g. anchored on
# $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR); 2 when it does not source it at all; 3 no such file.
#
# Anchoring matters as much as sourcing: a $PROJECT_DIR-relative load reads
# the lib out of whatever checkout the hook was POINTED at rather than the
# one it was INSTALLED in, so a worktree missing the lib would silently
# degrade the primary's gate.
check_sources_lib() {
    local f="$1"
    [ -f "$f" ] || return 3
    grep -qE '(^|[[:space:]])(\.|source)[[:space:]]+"[^"]*/workflow-denylist\.sh"' "$f" || return 2
    grep -qF 'BASH_SOURCE' "$f" || return 1
    # The dir variable feeding the source must be derived from BASH_SOURCE,
    # not from PROJECT_DIR. One line, both tokens.
    grep -qE 'dirname "\$\{BASH_SOURCE\[0\]' "$f" || return 1
    return 0

# denylist-regex definition, 1 when it does.
#
# The signature we forbid is an assignment whose right-hand side is a
# single-quoted ERE starting with the `(^|/)` path anchor every copy of this
# regex has always opened with. `DENYLIST_REGEX="$WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX"`
# (double-quoted, a reference) is the sanctioned form and is NOT matched.
# The lib's own canonical definition is not a consumer and is never passed
# to this checker.
check_no_literal_regex() {
    local f="$1"
    [ -f "$f" ] || return 2
    if grep -qE "^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z0-9_]*DENYLIST_REGEX='\(\^" "$f"; then
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

assert_eq "denylist-lib: .claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh exists (FLAT, syncable)" \
    "yes" "$([ -f "$LIB" ] && echo yes || echo no)"

if [ -f "$LIB" ]; then
    LIB_PARSE=0

    assert_eq "denylist-lib: parses under bash -n" "0" "$LIB_PARSE"

    assert_eq "denylist-lib: defines WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX" "1" \
        "$(grep -cE "^WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX='" "$LIB" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
    assert_eq "denylist-lib: defines workflow_denylisted()" "1" \
        "$(grep -cE '^workflow_denylisted\(\) \{' "$LIB" | tr -d '[:space:]')"

    # No side effects: sourcing the lib must not print, must not exit, and
    # must leave the caller's shell otherwise untouched. Anything else makes
    # it unsafe to load from a hook whose stdout IS the hook envelope.
    LIB_NOISE=$(bash -c ". '$LIB'" 2>&1)
    assert_eq "denylist-lib: sourcing is silent (hook stdout is the JSON envelope)" \
        "" "$LIB_NOISE"

    # And it actually answers: 0 = drop, 1 = keep.
    DL_DROP=$(bash -c ". '$LIB'; workflow_denylisted 'node_modules/x.js' && echo drop || echo keep")
    assert_eq "denylist-lib: workflow_denylisted drops a build path" "drop" "$DL_DROP"
    DL_KEEP=$(bash -c ". '$LIB'; workflow_denylisted 'src/a.ts' && echo drop || echo keep")
    assert_eq "denylist-lib: workflow_denylisted keeps a source path" "keep" "$DL_KEEP"
    # Deliberately NOT denylisted — behaviour-bearing / audit deliverables.
    for keeper in CLAUDE.md LESSONS.md HANDOFF.md; do
        KRC=$(bash -c ". '$LIB'; workflow_denylisted '$keeper' && echo drop || echo keep")
        assert_eq "denylist-lib: $keeper stays reviewable" "keep" "$KRC"
    done
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Assertion 2 + 3: every consumer sources the lib and carries no copy.

for c in $CONSUMERS; do
    f="$SCRIPTS_DIR/$c"
    rc=0
    check_sources_lib "$f" || rc=$?
    assert_eq "denylist-source: $c sources workflow-denylist.sh (BASH_SOURCE-relative)" "0" "$rc"

    rc=0
    check_no_literal_regex "$f" || rc=$?
    assert_eq "denylist-source: $c carries NO literal denylist regex of its own" "0" "$rc"
done

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# META-TEST 1: a consumer copy that re-declares a literal regex must FAIL
# check 3. This is the exact regression the spec exists to stop — someone
# pastes the old one-liner back in "to avoid the dependency".

# Quoted heredoc delimiters throughout: every fixture below is LITERAL shell
# text, never something this spec wants expanded.
META_LITERAL=$(mktemp -t denylist-source-literal.XXXXXX)
cat > "$META_LITERAL" <<'FIXTURE'
#!/bin/bash
_WFDL_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0}")" && pwd)
. "$_WFDL_DIR/workflow-denylist.sh"
# The re-introduced copy. Note this fixture ALSO still sources the lib, which
# is how the drift comes back for real: the source line stays, and the local
# literal quietly wins.
DENYLIST_REGEX='(^|/)(node_modules|dist)/'
FIXTURE

rc_meta=0
check_no_literal_regex "$META_LITERAL" || rc_meta=$?
assert_eq "META: checker flags a consumer that re-declares a literal regex" "1" "$rc_meta"
# ...and note it would have passed the source check, which is exactly why the
# literal-regex check has to exist separately.
rc_meta=0
check_sources_lib "$META_LITERAL" || rc_meta=$?
assert_eq "META: that same copy still passes the source check (checks are independent)" \
    "0" "$rc_meta"
rm -f "$META_LITERAL"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# META-TEST 2: a consumer copy with the source line removed must FAIL check 2.

META_NOSOURCE=$(mktemp -t denylist-source-nosource.XXXXXX)
cat > "$META_NOSOURCE" <<'FIXTURE'
#!/bin/bash
DENYLIST_REGEX="$WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX"
FIXTURE
rc_meta=0
check_sources_lib "$META_NOSOURCE" || rc_meta=$?
assert_eq "META: checker flags a consumer that does not source the lib" "2" "$rc_meta"
rm -f "$META_NOSOURCE"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# META-TEST 3: a consumer that sources the lib but anchors on
# $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR must FAIL check 2 as well. That form looks correct and
# behaves correctly on a single checkout, and breaks precisely in the
# cross-worktree topology 3mg.2 builds on.

META_PROJDIR=$(mktemp -t denylist-source-projdir.XXXXXX)
cat > "$META_PROJDIR" <<'FIXTURE'
#!/bin/bash
PROJECT_DIR="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}"
. "$PROJECT_DIR/.claude/scripts/workflow-denylist.sh"
DENYLIST_REGEX="$WORKFLOW_DENYLIST_REGEX"
FIXTURE
rc_meta=0
check_sources_lib "$META_PROJDIR" || rc_meta=$?
assert_eq "META: checker flags a PROJECT_DIR-anchored source (not BASH_SOURCE-relative)" \
    "1" "$rc_meta"
rm -f "$META_PROJDIR"

# --- Summary -------------------------------------------------------------

if [ "$FAIL" -gt 0 ]; then
    printf '\nFAILED: %d\n' "$FAIL"
    for t in "${FAILED_TESTS[@]}"; do
        printf '  - %s\n' "$t"
    done
    exit 1
fi
printf '\nPASSED: %d assertion(s)\n' "$PASS"
exit 0

LEGACY_BODY=$(cd "$F3" && git status --porcelain | LC_ALL=C sort)
rm -f "$BASE3"
printf '%s\n' "$LEGACY_BODY" > "$LEGACY3"
: > "$TRACK3"
bash "$CT3" clear
assert_eq "gbv2-5.1: a v1 approved-baseline is still honoured when no v2 file exists" \
    "ALLOW" "$(stop_decision "$F3")"
# 5.2 A new pre-dirty file is still NEW relative to the legacy snapshot.
printf 'export const post = 1;\n' > "$F3/src/post-legacy.ts"
: > "$TRACK3"
assert_eq "gbv2-5.2: dirt not in the legacy snapshot still blocks" \
    "block" "$(stop_decision "$F3")"
# 5.3 The first v2 write retires the legacy file.
CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$F3" bash "$QG3" baseline-capture --by test-harness >/dev/null 2>&1
assert_eq "gbv2-5.3: the first v2 write created the v2 file" "yes" \
    "$([ -f "$BASE3" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
assert_eq "gbv2-5.3: ...and deleted the legacy approved-baseline" "no" \
    "$([ -f "$LEGACY3" ] && echo yes || echo no)"

# ===========================================================================
# SECTION 6 — THE `-d .git` FIX, in a real linked worktree.
#
# In a linked worktree `.git` is a FILE containing `gitdir: ...`, so the old
# `[ -d "$PROJECT_DIR/.git" ]` predicate answered NO. Two things silently
# switched off there: the baseline writer (approve wrote nothing) and the Stop
# gate's git-status fallback. With an empty changed-files.txt the gate then
# had NO detector at all — it FAILED OPEN and released unreviewed work, in
# exactly the isolation:"worktree" topology the plugin tells agents to use.
# Both predicates now ask `git rev-parse --git-dir`.
#
# The worktree is created OUTSIDE the fixture on purpose: a checkout under
# `.claude/worktrees/` is denylisted, which would mask the very detection
# this section measures.
# ===========================================================================
WT_PARENT=$(mktemp -d -t gbv2-worktree.XXXXXX)
WT="$WT_PARENT/linked"
WT_OK=1
(cd "$F3" && git worktree add -q "$WT" -b gbv2-linked) >/dev/null 2>&1 || WT_OK=0

if [ "$WT_OK" != "1" ] || [ ! -e "$WT/.git" ]; then
    printf 'SKIPPED: gate-baseline-v2 section 6 (git worktree add unavailable in this environment)\n'
else
    # Give the worktree the hook surface a real checkout has.
    mkdir -p "$WT/.claude/scripts" "$WT/.claude/.qa-tracking"
    for s in "$(plugin_root)"/.claude/scripts/*.sh; do
        [ -f "$s" ] || continue
        ln -sf "$s" "$WT/.claude/scripts/$(basename "$s")"
    done
    fast_stack_stub "$WT"
    BASE_WT="$WT/.claude/.qa-tracking/gate-baseline"
    TRACK_WT="$WT/.claude/.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt"
    : > "$TRACK_WT"

    # 6.1 The precondition that broke the old predicate.
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.1: the linked worktree's .git is a FILE, not a directory" "file" \
        "$([ -d "$WT/.git" ] && echo dir || { [ -f "$WT/.git" ] && echo file || echo missing; })"
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.1: ...so the old \`-d .git\` predicate would have said NO" "no" \
        "$([ -d "$WT/.git" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.1: ...while rev-parse --git-dir says YES" "yes" \
        "$(git -C "$WT" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo yes || echo no)"

    # 6.2 The writer works there now. Pre-fix it took the "no git repo" arm,
    # removed any baseline and returned success — no snapshot, silently.
    printf 'export const w = 1;\n' > "$WT/src/pre.ts"
    CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="$WT" bash "$WT/.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh" \
        baseline-capture --by test-harness >/dev/null 2>&1
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.2: baseline-capture writes a snapshot inside a linked worktree" "yes" \
        "$([ -f "$BASE_WT" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
    assert_contains "gbv2-6.2: the worktree snapshot carries the worktree's dirt" \
        "src/pre.ts" "$(baseline_body "$BASE_WT")"

    # 6.3 With everything baselined the gate releases — no false block.
    : > "$TRACK_WT"
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.3: a fully-baselined worktree releases" "ALLOW" "$(stop_decision "$WT")"

    # 6.4 THE load-bearing assertion. New dirt after the baseline must BLOCK.
    # Pre-fix the fallback never ran in a worktree, so this released: the gate
    # failed OPEN on genuinely unreviewed work.
    printf 'export const unreviewed = 1;\n' > "$WT/src/unreviewed.ts"
    : > "$TRACK_WT"
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.4: unreviewed new work in a linked worktree BLOCKS (was: failed open)" \
        "block" "$(stop_decision "$WT")"
    # Causation, as in 1.4: remove ONLY the unreviewed path; the baselined
    # dirt stays put and the release comes back.
    rm -f "$WT/src/unreviewed.ts"
    : > "$TRACK_WT"
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.4: precondition — the baselined dirt is STILL dirty" \
        "1" "$(dirt_lines "$WT" | grep -c 'src/pre\.ts' | tr -d '[:space:]')"
    assert_eq "gbv2-6.4: removing ONLY the unreviewed path restores the release" \
        "ALLOW" "$(stop_decision "$WT")"

    (cd "$F3" && git worktree remove --force "$WT") >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
rm -rf "$WT_PARENT"

[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]
```

### 5. LESSONS.md
# Lessons ledger

Production lessons learned the hard way. Each entry is a single-sentence
takeaway, traceable to the Beads task(s) that produced it, with the date
it was first recorded.

Add new entries via `.claude/scripts/lessons.sh add '<lesson>' --source <task-id>`
— never hand-edit. The helper deduplicates by normalized text (case- and
whitespace-insensitive), so repeating an existing lesson appends the new
source to that entry rather than creating a duplicate. The only legitimate
hand-edit is pruning entries that are no longer relevant.

The orchestrator reads this file during planning (see `orchestrator.md`),
the grader (Phase A) receives it in the grading packet, and the QA agent
proposes additions at epic close. Treat it as the institutional memory the
plugin runs against, not a static reference doc.

## Lessons

- Parallel agents in the same working tree contaminate each other's branches; concurrent specialists require worktree isolation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Boundary mocks must use the real downstream producer's shape, pinned via a fixture extracted from the producer's spec — never invented. A mock that feeds `body.error` so the test can assert `body.error` is circular and proves nothing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- New agent files must be registered in .claude-plugin/plugin.json agents[] in the same commit that creates them; an unregistered agent is silently invisible to the SDK — no error surfaces. Guard: agents-manifest-parity test. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Subagents cannot spawn other subagents in the Claude Code runtime (docs: sub-agents page — Agent(agent_type) has no effect in subagent definitions). Any agent-spawning step must live at the root conversation level; design multi-agent handoffs as root-orchestrated relays, never nested spawns. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Interface examples must be executed by a test: the Makefile's own usage string (make test-live FIXTURE=node-react-auth) was broken for the one fixture whose spec file is scenario-named — nothing ever ran the documented invocation. Caught only when a paid live run failed fast. Any CLI surface a doc or help text advertises needs an L2 assertion that executes that exact invocation (dry-run mode where the real one costs money). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Prose cues do not reliably drive subagent tool usage: across 4 live runs, QA made zero impact_of calls even when its task prompt contained the exact tool name, alias, target symbols, and invariant name. When a workflow REQUIRES a tool call, make it mechanical (compute it where calls are reliable — e.g. orchestrator at root — and pass results down), don't prompt for it. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n6d --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Rendered fixture installs pin plugin scripts at render time: the fixture's verify-before-stop.sh predated the cue fix by one commit, so a hook-template change never reached the live run. Script-level fixes require re-rendering fixture installs (or a version check at run start) before they affect live validation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.10 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Never run QA review concurrently with a builder in the same working tree: QA attributed the parallel C.2 task's freshly-written files to the C.1 task under review and blocked it for scope creep. Sequence QA after all writers finish, or give builders worktree isolation (orchestrator.md 4b exists for exactly this). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.1 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Manifest-declared assets must be presence-asserted at the install target: install.sh's hardcoded agent list silently dropped grader.md for two releases (v3.2.0-v3.3.0) — every fresh install was missing the rubric loop's grader while the repo's own tests stayed green. Glob-copy from the manifest source of truth and add an installer-spec presence assertion for every plugin.json agents[]/commands[] entry. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Bash functions invoked via $(...) command substitution run in a subshell — any variable they set is lost to the parent. The manual-adopt gate in model-select.sh was dead code for exactly this reason (set at :341, read at :500, never connected). When a helper must signal the caller, encode the signal in its stdout contract (e.g. a MANUAL<tab> prefix) and parse it at every call site; add a META-TEST that strips the parse to prove the gate is load-bearing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-3fn --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- A security hardening that breaks the workflow is worse than the documented residual it closes. Fail-closing prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh on ambiguous identity assumed every specialist carries a probeable identity, but this runtime does not surface subagent_name to PreToolUse hooks — so it denied legitimate specialist Write/Edit (a P0-class regression) to close a P2 Bash-write vector. When a guard depends on an identity signal the runtime may not provide, prefer fail-OPEN plus the structural guard (the orchestrator's omitted Write/Edit tools, which IS airtight) and document the residual; never trade a P2 for a P0. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.19 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Line-number-anchored mutation META-tests are brittle: any comment or line addition above the anchor silently un-lands the NR==<n>/sed -n Np target, turning a load-bearing META into a no-op (or a spurious failure). Anchor mutation METAs to a unique TEXT pattern in the target line, not an absolute line number. (3 instances re-anchored across verify-before-stop/escalation-binding specs this session.) <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.20 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Effort A/B (cnz.2): verdict max — ultracode showed ZERO orchestration interference in a 39-min time-boxed arm (no Workflow-layer engagement, all spawns on-list, plugin flow faithful), contradicting the pre-registered criterion-4-failure expectation; max still wins because ultracode pins the model at its xhigh proxy (below max) with no observed benefit, and criteria 2-3 went unverified under the time-box. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-cnz.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Paid-run cost estimates must be derived from measured token flows, not guessed: the EFFORT-AB-TEST runbook estimated $10-20 for both arms; actual was ~$206 API-equivalent (~$169 arm B full + ~$37 arm A time-boxed) — a 10x error that forced a mid-test re-confirmation gate. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-cnz.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Regional/transient model exclusions in .claude/model-ranking go stale silently: a `!family` line added for a temporary outage keeps masking downstream behavior (here it collapsed the v4 top==opus-class role split onto Opus for six weeks) long after the outage clears. Gate every un-exclusion on FRESH spawn evidence (subagent-spawns.log + effort-ab logs naming the model), not memory, and date the rationale + rollback line in the file. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-bi3.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Files rewritten by a helper (awk/mv, e.g. workflow-model-apply.sh) instead of the Edit/Write tool never land in changed-files.txt, so the QA impact hash and the change-set-bound approval only cover Edit-tracked files. When a task mutates files via a helper, QA must verify those files explicitly via git diff (not rely on the impact report alone). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-bi3.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- MCP registration scope is a mechanical contract, not etiquette: a detection probe reads ONE config path (top-level .mcpServers of ~/.claude.json for user scope), so local/project-scope registrations are silently invisible — verify the probe read path when writing setup docs and make wrong-scope the first troubleshooting row. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Published CLI config references can lag the shipped binary: verify accepted values against the binary own introspection surface (e.g. codex debug models) rather than the docs or trial-and-error, and record the lag in the operator doc so editors re-verify. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Run suites via their canonical make targets: a bare runner invocation (npx vitest run) includes guarded paid live specs whose fail-closed API-key errors masquerade as regressions; the CI-shaped target (make test-e2e-unit) is the comparable baseline. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- When a change adds a second independent gate to a release path, every META that isolates the FIRST gate must be re-seeded to satisfy the new gate so it still fails for its own reason (jio.1 MM18 migration is the template). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.1 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- A deliberate second implementation of a gate predicate (shell counter + TS live invariant) is only a second witness if QA diffs the two rule-by-rule against the writer grammars at their emit sites — the jio.2 parity review caught a greedy-sed vs first-match token-selection divergence (gqp) that every test suite had missed. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- Trace-anchor refreshes that add a skip must be legitimized against the on-disk cassette (jq has(field) on the replay file), not the spec comment — and the pin must assert skipped+pass+exact detail so a future re-record flips loud instead of silently inheriting the skip. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->

# Default rubric (v1)

Applies to every task graded under the rubric-grader QA loop (spec Phase A). Each criterion below is a pass/fail assertion the grader evaluates from the grading packet: `bd show` for the task, the SPEC doc, the diff of the files listed in `.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt`, the F7 completion contract returned by the specialist, and `LESSONS.md`. One-line justification per criterion. No numeric score theater — pass or fail.

The criteria are intentionally short and checkable. Where the criterion needs context (boundary-mock fidelity, F7 fields), the "Evidence that satisfies it" line names the artefact the grader looks at.

## Criteria

### C1. Behavior matches the task description and SPEC.

The shipped diff implements the behavior the task description asks for, and matches the goal + acceptance criteria stated in the attached SPEC doc (read via `bd_doc_read(task_id, name="spec")`). Out-of-scope behavior the SPEC explicitly excludes is NOT in the diff.

Evidence that satisfies it: a 1-2 sentence walk-through that maps every user-visible behavior in the SPEC to a code path in the diff (or to a deliberate, documented deferral in the F7 `decisions` array). A diff that adds plausibly-related behavior the SPEC does not name fails this criterion — that is scope creep.

### C2. Tests added exercise user behavior rather than implementation.

Where the diff introduces new behavior, the diff also introduces tests that assert against the user-visible contract (return shape, side effects, error envelope, accessibility role, status code) rather than against the implementation's private structure (function-name mocking, line-coverage gymnastics, internal control-flow assertions).

Evidence that satisfies it: at least one test in the diff that would still pass if the implementation were rewritten while keeping the user contract identical. A test that asserts only against private symbols, internal call counts, or framework boilerplate fails this criterion.

### C3. The F7 completion contract carries all six fields with substantive `llm_observations`.

The specialist's structured completion payload includes `task_id`, `files_changed`, `tests_added`, `decisions`, `blockers`, and `llm_observations`. `llm_observations` is non-trivial narrative — what surprised the specialist, what was unclear, what they noticed and did not act on. A boilerplate one-liner like "no observations" fails this criterion (principle 9: `llm_observations` is mandatory and substantive).

Evidence that satisfies it: each of the six fields is present and the `llm_observations` paragraph is the kind of thing a human engineer would say at a stand-up.

### C4. No unrelated scope in the diff.

Every file the specialist touched serves the task. Drive-by refactors, formatting churn on untouched lines, and "while I'm here" cleanups that exceed the task brief fail this criterion — they should be filed as paired follow-up Beads tasks instead.

Evidence that satisfies it: the diff's file list maps cleanly to the SPEC's deliverables; any incidental change is either trivial (one-line typo fix) or explicitly justified in the `decisions` array.

### C5. J26 modules relevant to the diff are addressed.

Where the diff touches a domain covered by the J26 security taxonomy (SECRETS, INJECTION, AUTH, CONFIG, DEPS, AI, MOBILE, DATA — see `docs/AGENTS.md`), the diff demonstrates that the relevant modules were considered. Untouched J26 domains are out of scope.

Evidence that satisfies it: the `decisions` array (or the SPEC) names which J26 modules apply, and the diff shows defences in those modules (input validation at the trust boundary, parameterised queries, narrow CORS, audited logging, etc.). A diff that touches user input handling without naming INJECTION fails this criterion.

### C6. Docs updated where behavior changed.

When the diff changes user-visible behavior, the documentation that describes that behavior is updated in the same change. This includes `CHANGELOG.md`, README sections, `docs/*.md`, command help text, and SPEC docs the diff renders out of date.

Evidence that satisfies it: a docs-only file in `files_changed` paired with each behavioral change, or a deliberate `decisions` entry stating why a doc deferral is correct (e.g. an internal refactor that ships without user-visible change). A behavioral change that ships with no doc update and no deferral note fails this criterion.

### C7. Boundary-mock fidelity (LESSONS.md lesson 2).

When the diff introduces or modifies mocks of boundaries the project does not control (third-party HTTP APIs, external SDKs, system calls, message-bus payloads), every such mock derives its shape from a fixture extracted from the real downstream producer's spec (OpenAPI, proto file, SDK source, vendor docs). The fixture's source is cited in a comment, the `decisions` array, or `llm_observations`.

**Automatic needs_revision:** circular pass-through assertions are an immediate fail. A mock that feeds `body.error` so a test can assert `body.error` proves nothing — it tests the test's own setup, not the production behavior. Cite `LESSONS.md` lesson 2 in the justification.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new boundary mock points at a fixture file (`.fixtures/`, `__fixtures__/`, `testdata/`) carrying a snapshot of the producer's payload, and the fixture has a comment naming the source (URL, commit, SDK version). Tests assert against the producer's contract, not against the mock's own input.

# DevOps rubric (v1)

Applied additionally when the task carries the `devops` label. Default criteria still apply; these add domain-specific checks pulled from `.claude/agents/devops.md`. The leverage is default + bugfix — these are the few devops-specific failure modes that recur.

## Criteria

### D1. Scripts are idempotent and re-runnable.

Install, uninstall, hook, and CI scripts in the diff produce the same end state when run twice in a row. A second run of `install.sh` does not double-write hooks, clobber prior settings, or fail because a directory already exists. A migration script that exits non-zero on its second run fails this criterion.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new script uses `mkdir -p`, conditional inserts, and idempotent label operations (`bd label add` returns success if already present); the `decisions` array documents any deliberately non-idempotent step (e.g. a one-shot data migration) and pairs it with a guard (lock file, completion sentinel) so a re-run is detected.

### D2. Graceful degradation on missing optional tools.

When the diff depends on an optional tool (gitleaks, shellcheck, a particular bd version, a specific CI runner image), the missing-tool path is handled: log a structured warning, fall back to a safe default, exit zero where the workflow allows. A hook that exits non-zero because `gitleaks` is not installed fails this criterion — that is not a developer-machine-portable failure mode.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new tool dependency is probed (`command -v tool >/dev/null`); the fallback path is documented in the script comments and tested at L1; the `decisions` array names the dependency and its installation hint.

### D3. No new permission prompts; autonomy preserved.

The diff does not add `permissions.deny` rules to `settings.json`, narrow specialist tool lists below the broad allow set, or introduce any user-facing approval step the plugin previously ran without. Principle 3 of the v3 plan is "full autonomy, no permission prompts" — every deny rule becomes a future approval prompt and breaks the workflow.

Evidence that satisfies it: a diff of `.claude/settings.json` shows only `permissions.allow` expansions, never `deny`; specialist tool frontmatter is unchanged or expanded; the `decisions` array calls out any new tool the broadened allow set covers.

### D4. Secrets and PII stay out of source, logs, and history.

Hardcoded API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, committer emails, and PII are absent from the diff. Logs that the diff adds redact sensitive fields before writing. A commit that introduces an `.env` file with values, a personal email address in a script header, or unredacted PII in a log line fails this criterion (extends C5 / SECRETS + DATA).

Evidence that satisfies it: secrets read from a secret manager or environment variable at runtime; PII fields in new log lines are redacted (`***@`, `user_id=***`); a `gitleaks`-equivalent pass on the diff is clean, and the `decisions` array names the secrets the diff touches.

# SPEC — 3mg.2 V4 pt2: worktree= approval token + bounded Stop-side resolution + scenario-2 fixture (epic 3mg)

Source: `docs/plans/v4-trimodel.md` Phase V4 items 5–7. This is the FINAL V4 landing; after it, epic `3mg` is complete. 3mg.1 already shipped (commit 00ee85a): the shared denylist, gate-baseline v2, the I8 `--git-common-dir` fix, and scenarios 1 (`gate-baseline-v2.sh`) + 3 (`denylist-shared.sh`). **Do NOT re-implement those.** This task adds the cross-checkout approval bridge on top.

## Canonical model (decided, do not relitigate)
Per-worktree tracking, per-worktree hash, per-worktree baseline. Approvals are bridged by a **worktree-annotated approval record** + **bounded read-only resolution in the Stop hook**. KEY discovered constraint, now confirmed LIVE this session: `qa-gate.sh approve` TRUNCATES `changed-files.txt` in its checkout, so a post-approve recompute in that checkout yields the empty-string hash and can never reproduce the approved hash. Therefore resolution MUST be **record-based**: the persisted `.claude/.qa-tracking/impact-report-<tid>.json` SURVIVES approve (approve truncates the tracker, not this file) and carries the approved file list + `change_set_hash`. Read that, do not recompute from the truncated tracker. Hash inputs stay byte-literal (no git normalization).

## Deliverable 1 — approval worktree token (`qa-gate.sh cmd_approve`)
`cmd_approve` currently writes (qa-gate.sh:1149):
`add_comment "$tid" "QA-GATE APPROVED ${hash_field}reviewed_by=$reviewed_by at $ts: $summary$comment_suffix"`
Append a `worktree=<tok>` token AFTER `reviewed_by=$reviewed_by` and BEFORE `at $ts`, on EVERY approve path (normal, F1 fast-path `--no-review`, and the bypass paths — all reach this single add_comment). Final grammar (matches the cross-phase contract):
`QA-GATE APPROVED change_set_hash=<h> reviewed_by=<id> worktree=<tok> at <ts>: <summary>[ [impact-report bypass: …]][ [review bypass: …]]`
- `<tok>` = the approving checkout's absolute toplevel, `%20`-encoded so it is ONE space-terminated token: `git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel` then replace every space with `%20`. If `--show-toplevel` fails (non-git / unresolvable), write `worktree=none` (never omit the token — keep the grammar stable).
- CRITICAL back-compat: the existing v3.5 hash reader `capture("change_set_hash=(?<h>[A-Za-z0-9-]+)")` stops at the space after `<h>`, so it is unaffected — but you MUST add a META-anchored assertion that the old hash regex STILL matches the new record (strip/rename the worktree token region → the compat assertion still passes; the point is the hash capture must never regress). The `reviewed_by=` capture (verify-before-stop matched-record logic) similarly must still work.
- No behavior change when work happens in the primary checkout: `<tok>` is just recorded; resolution (D2) only fires on the hash-mismatch+label-present path that currently blocks.

## Deliverable 2 — Stop-side WORKTREE-RESOLUTION (`verify-before-stop.sh`)
Insert a sentinel-wrapped block `# WORKTREE-RESOLUTION BEGIN` … `# WORKTREE-RESOLUTION END` AFTER `LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD` is set true (near line 1334) and BEFORE the `if [ "$LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD" = "true" ]; then emit_block …` at line 1350. Semantics: when the current checkout's change-set hash matches NO recorded approval (the current LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD block reason), try to resolve the approval against another worktree of the SAME repo before blocking.

```
# only attempt when we actually have a task + the label is present (LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD path)
recorded_hashes = { change_set_hash of every "QA-GATE APPROVED … change_set_hash=<h> …" comment on $CURRENT_TASK }
recorded_token  = worktree= of the LATEST such approval (may be none)
candidates = toplevels from `git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" worktree list --porcelain`   # 'worktree ' lines
             ordered: recorded_token first (if it decodes + is in the list), then the rest;
             SKIP the current checkout (same --show-toplevel); cap 16
for W in candidates:
    j = "$W/.claude/.qa-tracking/impact-report-$CURRENT_TASK.json"      # survives approve
    [ -f "$j" ] || continue
    wh = jq -r '.change_set_hash' "$j"                                   # the approved hash, recorded at approve time in W
    wh ∈ recorded_hashes  || continue                                   # must correspond to a real approval on this task
    # no post-approval drift IN W: its own git status minus its own gate-baseline is empty
    wstatus = git -C "$W" status --porcelain | LC_ALL=C sort
    wbase   = lines-after-'--' of "$W/.claude/.qa-tracking/gate-baseline" | LC_ALL=C sort
    [ -z "$(comm -23 <(printf '%s' "$wstatus") <(printf '%s' "$wbase"))" ] || continue
    # the CURRENT checkout's delta must be a SUBSET of W's approved file set (PR#2 relativization technique):
    approved_files = jq -r '.files[].file' "$j"        # as-tracked paths approved in W
    current_delta  = the reviewable change set in THIS checkout (ALL_CHANGED_FILES already computed above, denylist-filtered)
    every path in current_delta is ∈ approved_files (compare repo-relative; reuse PR#2 relativize helper if needed) || continue
    → RELEASE: echo "{}"; exit 0   (log_sync_error-style note: "Stop released via worktree resolution: approval bound in <W> (hash <wh>)")
# no candidate resolved:
if recorded_token decodes to a path that is NOT in `git worktree list` (worktree deleted):
    → keep LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD block, but set the reason to name the deleted worktree explicitly
      ("approval was bound in worktree <tok> which no longer exists — re-enter + re-review here")
else:
    → fall through to the existing LABEL_WITHOUT_RECORD emit_block; append " (checked N worktree(s))" to the reason
```
- **Record-first, bounded search fallback** (recommended over search-only: O(1) common case, unambiguous). READ-ONLY: per-candidate cost = a couple of file reads + at most ONE `impact-report.sh --hash-only` subshell (only if you choose to verify recompute@W for the non-empty-tracker case — prefer the record's `.change_set_hash` directly and SKIP recompute when W's tracker is empty/post-approve) + one `git status`. NEVER boots the code-graph MCP server. NEVER writes anything.
- Use the 3mg.1 `--git-common-dir` canonicalization to confirm a candidate is the SAME repo (a `git worktree list` entry always is, but guard against a detached/foreign entry).
- FAIL CLOSED: any error (worktree list fails, jq error, unreadable json, ambiguous) → do NOT release; fall through to the block. A resolution must be positively proven, never assumed.
- Do NOT change the same-checkout happy path (matching record → release, already handled above line 1235) or the F1 empty/doc-only fast paths.

## Deliverable 3 — topology validation (item 6, no shipped debug log)
The design assumes a specialist's tool-call hooks fire in the PARENT session with `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<primary>`, while a worktree *session* gets `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<worktree>`. Validate this EMPIRICALLY via the scenario-2 test (D4), which uses a REAL `git worktree add` and drives approve-in-W / Stop-in-primary. Do NOT ship a debug log in post-edit.sh (noise + another fixture sync). Instead: add a short `docs/HOOKS.md` note under the Stop-gate section documenting the verified topology + the WORKTREE-RESOLUTION path and its fail-closed guarantee.

## Deliverable 4 — test `worktree-approval-resolution.sh` (scenario 2 + sentinel META)
NEW L2 `.claude/tests/component/specs/worktree-approval-resolution.sh`, wired into `.claude/tests/component/run.sh`'s `specs/*.sh` enumerator. Use a REAL linked worktree (`git worktree add`), NOT a simulated one — this is also the item-6 empirical probe. bash 3.2 + jq.
- **RELEASE case (the fix):** in a scratch git repo, `git worktree add W`; make a tracked edit in W; `enter`+`approve` in W with `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=$W` (records `worktree=$W` token + persisted `impact-report-<tid>.json` + W gate-baseline). Then run verify-before-stop.sh in the PRIMARY checkout (`CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<primary>`, same task label present, primary's own hash mismatching) → asserts **RELEASE** ({} exit 0) via the resolution. MUST fail on pre-fix code (assert `git show HEAD:.claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh` has no WORKTREE-RESOLUTION sentinel → the release case would block).
- **Negatives (each must BLOCK):** (a) drift-in-W — modify a file in W after approve so W status ⊄ W baseline; (b) deleted-W — `git worktree remove W` (or rm the json) → block naming the recorded token; (c) delta⊄approved — the primary checkout has a reviewable changed file NOT in W's approved file set.

+WTRES_HASH=""
+WTRES_CHECKED=0

+# wtres_decode <token> — the `worktree=` token's path spelling. Mirror of
+# qa-gate.sh approval_worktree_token: %20/%09 first, then %25 back to `%`, so a
+# path that genuinely contains "%20" round-trips instead of decoding to a space.
+wtres_decode() {
+    local t="$1"
+    t="${t//%20/ }"
+    t="${t//%09/	}"
+    t="${t//%25/%}"
+    printf '%s' "$t"
+}
+
+# Per-directory memo for wtres_repo_relative (bash 3.2: no associative arrays).
+_WTRES_MEMO_DIR=""
+_WTRES_MEMO_COMMON=""
+_WTRES_MEMO_PREFIX=""
+
+# wtres_repo_relative <path> <want-common-dir> — print <path>'s REPO-RELATIVE
+# key, i.e. the spelling that identifies the same file in every worktree of the
+# repo whose canonical common-dir is <want-common-dir>. rc 1 + no output when
+# the path cannot be proven to belong to that repo (caller must fail closed).
+#
+# Three input spellings occur in practice:
+#   - absolute, under this checkout       (post-edit records tool_input verbatim)
+#   - absolute, under a SIBLING worktree  (the parent session's hooks record the
+#                                          specialist's worktree path)
+#   - already repo-relative               (the git-status fallback's `${line#???}`)
+# git supplies the mapping (`--show-prefix` + basename) so nothing depends on
+# how a path happened to be spelled (/var vs /private/var on macOS, symlinked
+# project roots, trailing slashes).
+wtres_repo_relative() {
+    local p="$1" want="$2" d b
+    [ -n "$p" ] || return 1
+    [ -n "$want" ] || return 1
+    case "$p" in
+        /*) ;;
+        *) printf '%s' "$p"; return 0 ;;
+    esac
+    d=$(dirname "$p") || return 1
+    b=$(basename "$p") || return 1
+    if [ "$d" != "$_WTRES_MEMO_DIR" ]; then
+        _WTRES_MEMO_DIR="$d"
+        _WTRES_MEMO_COMMON=$(repo_identity "$d")
+        _WTRES_MEMO_PREFIX=$(git -C "$d" rev-parse --show-prefix 2>/dev/null) || _WTRES_MEMO_PREFIX=""
+    fi
+    [ -n "$_WTRES_MEMO_COMMON" ] || return 1
+    [ "$_WTRES_MEMO_COMMON" = "$want" ] || return 1
+    printf '%s%s' "$_WTRES_MEMO_PREFIX" "$b"
+}

+# wtres_no_drift_in <worktree> — 0 when <worktree> has NOTHING dirty beyond its
+# own gate-baseline, i.e. nothing changed there after the approval refreshed it.
+# A missing baseline returns 1: absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.
+wtres_no_drift_in() {
+    local w="$1" raw wstatus wbase leftover cmp_rc=0
+    local v2="$w/.claude/.qa-tracking/gate-baseline"
+    local legacy="$w/.claude/.qa-tracking/approved-baseline"
+    # `git status` is captured on its OWN, not piped straight into sort: a
+    # pipeline's rc is the LAST command's, so `git ... | sort` would report
+    # success for a failed git and hand us an empty status — which reads as
+    # "nothing dirty", i.e. it would fail OPEN on exactly the error case.
+    raw=$(git -C "$w" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null) || return 1
+    wstatus=$(printf '%s' "$raw" | LC_ALL=C sort) || return 1
+    if [ -f "$v2" ]; then
+        wbase=$(awk 'body { print; next } /^--$/ { body = 1 }' "$v2" 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort) || return 1
+    elif [ -f "$legacy" ]; then
+        wbase=$(LC_ALL=C sort "$legacy" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
+    else
+        return 1
+    fi
+    # Same collation on both sides as the writer used (see gate_baseline_entries).
+    # comm's own failure must REFUSE, not read as an empty difference — same
+    # fail-open trap as the pipeline above.
+    leftover=$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "$wstatus") <(printf '%s\n' "$wbase") 2>/dev/null) || cmp_rc=$?
+    [ "$cmp_rc" -eq 0 ] || return 1
+    leftover=$(printf '%s' "$leftover" | grep -v '^$') || leftover=""
+    [ -z "$leftover" ]
+}
+
+# wtres_delta_is_subset <report-json> <want-common-dir> — 0 when EVERY path in
+# this checkout's reviewable change set is in the file set that report approved.
+# Empty on either side returns 1: a vacuous subset proves nothing.
+wtres_delta_is_subset() {
+    local j="$1" want="$2"
+    local approved="" f key n=0
+    while IFS= read -r f; do
+        [ -n "$f" ] || continue
+        # An approved path we cannot map is DROPPED, which shrinks the approved
+        # set — the fail-closed direction.
+        key=$(wtres_repo_relative "$f" "$want") || continue
+        approved="$approved$key
+"
+    done < <(jq -r '(.files // [])[] | .file // empty' "$j" 2>/dev/null)
+    [ -n "$approved" ] || return 1
+    for f in ${ALL_CHANGED_FILES[@]+"${ALL_CHANGED_FILES[@]}"}; do
+        [ -n "$f" ] || continue
+        n=$((n + 1))
+        # A current path we cannot map is UNPROVABLE -> refuse outright.
+        key=$(wtres_repo_relative "$f" "$want") || return 1
+        printf '%s' "$approved" | grep -qxF "$key" || return 1
+    done
+    [ "$n" -gt 0 ]
+}
