// Entrypoint: boot the signup server from environment configuration.
// `npm start` runs this; the tests import createServer() from app.js directly.
import { createServer } from './app.js';
import { loadConfig } from './config.js';

const config = loadConfig();
const server = createServer({ config });

server.listen(config.port, () => {
  process.stdout.write(
    `${JSON.stringify({
      ts: new Date().toISOString(),
      level: 'info',
      msg: 'listening',
      port: config.port,
      corsOrigin: config.corsOrigin,
    })}\n`,
  );
});

function shutdown(signal) {
  process.stdout.write(
    `${JSON.stringify({ ts: new Date().toISOString(), level: 'info', msg: 'shutdown', signal })}\n`,
  );
  server.close(() => process.exit(0));
  server.closeAllConnections?.();
  setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 5_000).unref(); // force-exit if connections linger
}

process.on('SIGINT', () => shutdown('SIGINT'));
process.on('SIGTERM', () => shutdown('SIGTERM'));

----- END FILE server/src/index.js -----

----- BEGIN FILE server/src/config.js (NEW, verbatim — CONFIG: env loading, CORS default, body caps, timeouts) -----
// Configuration loader (J26: CONFIG).
// Reads from the environment with safe defaults; invalid values fall back to a
// default rather than crashing the process on boot.

const DEFAULTS = {
  port: 3000,
  corsOrigin: 'http://localhost:8080',
  rateLimit: { max: 5, windowMs: 60_000 }, // 5 requests / minute / IP
  maxBodyBytes: 64 * 1024, // 65536 — the 64KB request-body cap
  hardBodyLimitBytes: 1024 * 1024, // 1 MiB — abusive-upload hard cutoff
  password: { N: 16384, r: 8, p: 1, keylen: 64, saltlen: 16, maxmem: 64 * 1024 * 1024 },
  timeouts: { requestTimeoutMs: 20_000, headersTimeoutMs: 10_000, keepAliveTimeoutMs: 5_000 },
};

function positiveInt(value, fallback) {
  if (value === undefined || value === null || value === '') return fallback;
  const n = Number(value);
  return Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0 ? n : fallback;
}

export function loadConfig(env = process.env) {
  const maxBodyBytes = positiveInt(env.SIGNUP_MAX_BODY_BYTES, DEFAULTS.maxBodyBytes);
  return {
    port: positiveInt(env.PORT, DEFAULTS.port),
    corsOrigin:
      (typeof env.SIGNUP_CORS_ORIGIN === 'string' && env.SIGNUP_CORS_ORIGIN.trim()) || DEFAULTS.corsOrigin,
    rateLimit: {
      max: positiveInt(env.SIGNUP_RATE_LIMIT_MAX, DEFAULTS.rateLimit.max),
      windowMs: positiveInt(env.SIGNUP_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS, DEFAULTS.rateLimit.windowMs),
    },
    maxBodyBytes,
    // Never below the soft cap; scales with it so raising the cap can't
    // accidentally make the hard cutoff smaller than the soft one.
    hardBodyLimitBytes: Math.max(DEFAULTS.hardBodyLimitBytes, maxBodyBytes * 16),
    password: { ...DEFAULTS.password },
    timeouts: { ...DEFAULTS.timeouts },
  };
}

export { DEFAULTS };

----- END FILE server/src/config.js -----

// Low-level HTTP helpers: correlation ids, response envelopes, CORS + security
// headers, and a size-capped body reader.
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';

export function newCorrelationId() {
  return randomUUID();
}

/**
 * Headers applied to every response.
 * CORS uses a single fixed origin — never '*' (J26: CONFIG / CORS).
 */
export function applyBaseHeaders(res, { corsOrigin, correlationId }) {
  res.setHeader('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', corsOrigin);
  res.setHeader('Vary', 'Origin');
  res.setHeader('X-Content-Type-Options', 'nosniff');
  res.setHeader('Referrer-Policy', 'no-referrer');
  res.setHeader('Cache-Control', 'no-store');
  res.setHeader('X-Correlation-Id', correlationId);
}

export function sendJson(res, status, body, extraHeaders = {}) {
  const payload = JSON.stringify(body);
  res.writeHead(status, {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',
    'Content-Length': Buffer.byteLength(payload),
    ...extraHeaders,
  });
  res.end(payload);
}

/** Consistent error envelope: { error: { code, message } }. */
export function sendError(res, status, code, message, extraHeaders = {}) {
  sendJson(res, status, { error: { code, message } }, extraHeaders);
}

/**
 * Read a request body with a hard size cap (DoS defence, J26: CONFIG).
 * Resolves to one of:
 *   { tooLarge:false, aborted:false, body:<string> }  normal
 *   { tooLarge:true,  aborted:false, body:null }       over soft cap, drained -> answerable
 *   { tooLarge:true,  aborted:true,  body:null }       over hard cap, socket destroyed
 *   { tooLarge:false, aborted:true,  body:null }       client hung up
 * Never buffers more than `maxBytes`.
 */
export function readBody(req, { maxBytes, hardLimitBytes }) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    let size = 0;
    let over = false;
    let settled = false;
    const chunks = [];

    const settle = (value) => {
      if (!settled) {
        settled = true;
        resolve(value);
      }
    };

    req.on('data', (chunk) => {
      size += chunk.length;
      if (size > hardLimitBytes) {
        // Abusive upload: stop and reset the connection.
        settle({ tooLarge: true, aborted: true, body: null });
        req.destroy();
        return;
      }
      if (size > maxBytes) {
        over = true; // stop buffering but keep draining so we can still answer 400
        return;
      }
      chunks.push(chunk);
    });
    req.on('end', () =>
      settle({ tooLarge: over, aborted: false, body: over ? null : Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8') }),
    );
    req.on('aborted', () => settle({ tooLarge: over, aborted: true, body: null }));
    req.on('error', (err) => {
      if (!settled) {
        settled = true;
        reject(err);
      }
    });
  });
}

// Trust-boundary input validation (J26: INJECTION).
// Everything crossing the boundary is type/length/shape checked before use.
// No user input is ever interpolated into SQL, shell, or template strings.

const MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH = 254; // RFC 5321 practical upper bound
const MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8;
const MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 1024;

// Pragmatic single-line email shape: non-empty local part, '@', a domain that
// contains a dot, and no whitespace anywhere. Deliberately conservative — we
// reject rather than attempt full RFC 5322 parsing.
const EMAIL_RE = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/;

/**
 * Validate a parsed signup payload.
 * @returns {{ok:true,email:string,password:string} | {ok:false,code:string,message:string}}
 * Error precedence: missing_field -> invalid_email -> weak_password.
 */
export function validateSignup(payload) {
  if (payload === null || typeof payload !== 'object' || Array.isArray(payload)) {
    return err('missing_field', 'Request body must be a JSON object containing "email" and "password".');
  }

  const { email, password } = payload;

  if (typeof email !== 'string' || email.trim() === '') {
    return err('missing_field', 'Field "email" is required.');
  }
  if (typeof password !== 'string') {
    return err('missing_field', 'Field "password" is required.');
  }

  // Canonicalise: trim surrounding whitespace, lowercase (mirrors the DB's
  // UNIQUE lower(email) index so "A@B.com" and "a@b.com" collide).
  const canonicalEmail = email.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (canonicalEmail.length > MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH || !EMAIL_RE.test(canonicalEmail)) {
    return err('invalid_email', 'Field "email" is not a valid email address.');
  }

  // Length is measured in UTF-16 code units (String.prototype.length); adequate
  // for the ASCII-dominant password rule in the contract.
  if (password.length < MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH || password.length > MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH) {
    return err(
      'weak_password',
      `Field "password" must be between ${MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH} and ${MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH} characters.`,
    );
  }

  return { ok: true, email: canonicalEmail, password };
}

function err(code, message) {
  return { ok: false, code, message };
}

export { MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH, MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH, MAX_EMAIL_LENGTH };

// Password hashing (J26: AUTH).
// scrypt via node:crypto with the spec parameters (N=16384, r=8, p=1, 16-byte
// random salt, 64-byte key). Verification is constant-time (timingSafeEqual).
// No MD5 / SHA1 / plaintext anywhere.
import { randomBytes, scrypt as scryptCb, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto';
import { promisify } from 'node:util';

const scrypt = promisify(scryptCb);

const PARAMS = Object.freeze({
  N: 16384,
  r: 8,
  p: 1,
  keylen: 64,
  saltlen: 16,
  maxmem: 64 * 1024 * 1024, // headroom over 128*N*r (~16MB) so scrypt never trips its memory guard
});

/**
 * Hash a plaintext password. Returns a self-describing string so verification
 * can recover the parameters without external state:
 *   scrypt$<N>$<r>$<p>$<salt-hex>$<key-hex>
 */
export async function hashPassword(password, params = PARAMS) {
  const { N, r, p, keylen, saltlen, maxmem } = { ...PARAMS, ...params };
  const salt = randomBytes(saltlen);
  const derived = await scrypt(password, salt, keylen, { N, r, p, maxmem });
  return `scrypt$${N}$${r}$${p}$${salt.toString('hex')}$${derived.toString('hex')}`;
}

/**
 * Verify a plaintext password against a stored hash. Constant-time comparison.
 * Returns false (never throws) for any malformed stored value.
 */
export async function verifyPassword(password, stored, maxmem = PARAMS.maxmem) {
  if (typeof stored !== 'string') return false;
  const parts = stored.split('$');
  if (parts.length !== 6 || parts[0] !== 'scrypt') return false;

  const N = Number(parts[1]);
  const r = Number(parts[2]);
  const p = Number(parts[3]);
  if (![N, r, p].every((n) => Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0)) return false;

  const salt = Buffer.from(parts[4], 'hex');
  const expected = Buffer.from(parts[5], 'hex');
  // Reject truncated/odd hex (Buffer.from drops invalid chars, so re-check length).
  if (salt.length === 0 || expected.length === 0 || parts[4].length !== salt.length * 2 || parts[5].length !== expected.length * 2) {
    return false;
  }

  const derived = await scrypt(password, salt, expected.length, { N, r, p, maxmem });
  if (derived.length !== expected.length) return false;
  return timingSafeEqual(derived, expected);
}

export { PARAMS as SCRYPT_PARAMS };

// In-memory user store.
//
// This mirrors migrations/0001_create_users.sql EXACTLY:
//   id uuid PK, email text NOT NULL, password_hash text NOT NULL, created_at timestamptz NOT NULL
// Uniqueness mirrors the DB's `UNIQUE (lower(email))` index: keyed by lower(email).
//
// A real PostgreSQL driver is intentionally OUT OF SCOPE for this offline
// milestone. The migration is the schema of record; this store is the runtime
// stand-in and is written to be swapped for a `pg`-backed repository later
// without changing the calling code (same create/findByEmail shape).
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';

export function createUserStore() {
  const byLowerEmail = new Map(); // lower(email) -> record

  return {
    /**
     * Atomic check-and-insert. Because the event loop is single-threaded and
     * this method performs no `await`, the has()/set() pair cannot interleave:
     * two concurrent duplicate signups can never both create a row. The first
     * claims the key; the second observes it and gets { conflict: true }.
     */
    create({ email, passwordHash }) {
      const key = String(email).toLowerCase();
      if (byLowerEmail.has(key)) {
        return { conflict: true };
      }
      const record = {
        id: randomUUID(),
        email,
        password_hash: passwordHash,
        created_at: new Date().toISOString(), // ISO-8601 UTC (…Z); timestamptz-compatible
      };
      byLowerEmail.set(key, record);
      return { conflict: false, record };
    },

    findByEmail(email) {
      return byLowerEmail.get(String(email).toLowerCase()) ?? null;
    },

    get size() {
      return byLowerEmail.size;
    },
  };
}

/**
 * Response projection: an allow-list of non-sensitive columns. password_hash is
 * never included, so it cannot leak into a response even by accident (J26: DATA).
 */
export function toPublicUser(record) {
  return { id: record.id, email: record.email, created_at: record.created_at };
}

// Per-IP fixed-window rate limiter (in-memory).
//
// Bounded memory: entries are swept lazily once the map grows past a safety cap.
// This is a single-process limiter — a horizontally-scaled deployment would
// push this to a shared store (Redis) or the edge/load-balancer, since each
// process would otherwise keep its own independent window. Documented in README.

export function createRateLimiter({ max, windowMs, now = Date.now, maxEntries = 100_000 }) {
  const hits = new Map(); // ip -> { count, resetAt }

  function sweepExpired(currentTime) {
    for (const [ip, entry] of hits) {
      if (currentTime >= entry.resetAt) hits.delete(ip);
    }
  }

  return {
    /**
     * Record one request from `ip`.
     * @returns {{allowed:true} | {allowed:false, retryAfterSeconds:number}}
     */
    check(ip) {
      const t = now();
      let entry = hits.get(ip);
      if (!entry || t >= entry.resetAt) {
        entry = { count: 0, resetAt: t + windowMs };
        hits.set(ip, entry);
      }
      entry.count += 1;

      // Keep memory bounded under a flood of distinct source IPs.
      if (hits.size > maxEntries) sweepExpired(t);

      if (entry.count > max) {
        const retryAfterSeconds = Math.max(1, Math.ceil((entry.resetAt - t) / 1000));
        return { allowed: false, retryAfterSeconds };
      }
      return { allowed: true };
    },

    get size() {
      return hits.size;
    },
  };
}

// HTTP application: POST /api/signup on a zero-dependency node:http server.
import http from 'node:http';
import { loadConfig } from './config.js';
import { createUserStore, toPublicUser } from './store.js';
import { createRateLimiter } from './rate-limiter.js';
import { validateSignup } from './validation.js';
import { hashPassword } from './password.js';
import { applyBaseHeaders, sendJson, sendError, readBody, newCorrelationId } from './http-helpers.js';

const SIGNUP_PATH = '/api/signup';

function isJsonContentType(req) {
  const ct = req.headers['content-type'];
  if (typeof ct !== 'string') return false;
  return ct.split(';')[0].trim().toLowerCase() === 'application/json';
}

function clientIp(req) {
  // Socket peer address ONLY. X-Forwarded-For is intentionally not trusted: it
  // is client-settable, so honouring it blindly would let an attacker rotate
  // the header to defeat the per-IP limit. Behind a known proxy you would parse
  // XFF against a configured trusted-hop count.
  return req.socket?.remoteAddress ?? 'unknown';
}

function defaultLogger(entry) {
  // Structured JSON to stdout. Only ever receives routing + outcome metadata —
  // never the email or password (J26: DATA — no PII in logs).
  try {
    process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({ ts: new Date().toISOString(), ...entry })}\n`);
  } catch {
    /* logging must never throw */
  }
}

export function createServer(options = {}) {
  const config = options.config ?? loadConfig();
  const store = options.store ?? createUserStore();
  const logger = typeof options.logger === 'function' ? options.logger : defaultLogger;
  const rateLimiter =
    options.rateLimiter ??
    createRateLimiter({ max: config.rateLimit.max, windowMs: config.rateLimit.windowMs, now: options.now });

  const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
    handle(req, res, { config, store, logger, rateLimiter }).catch(() => {
      // handle() manages its own errors; this is a last-resort socket guard.
      try {
        if (!res.headersSent) res.writeHead(500).end();
        else res.end();
      } catch {
        /* socket already gone */
      }
    });
  });

  // J26: CONFIG / DoS hardening — bound how long a client may hold a connection.
  server.requestTimeout = config.timeouts.requestTimeoutMs;
  server.headersTimeout = config.timeouts.headersTimeoutMs;
  server.keepAliveTimeout = config.timeouts.keepAliveTimeoutMs;

  // Exposed for tests / introspection only.
  server.store = store;
  server.appConfig = config;
  return server;
}

async function handle(req, res, ctx) {
  const { config, store, logger, rateLimiter } = ctx;
  const correlationId = newCorrelationId();
  const startedAt = process.hrtime.bigint();
  const method = req.method ?? 'GET';
  const path = (req.url ?? '/').split('?')[0];
  let outcome = 'unknown';

  try {
    // CORS + security headers on every response.
    applyBaseHeaders(res, { corsOrigin: config.corsOrigin, correlationId });

    // --- CORS preflight ---
    if (method === 'OPTIONS' && path === SIGNUP_PATH) {
      outcome = 'preflight';
      res.writeHead(204, {
        'Access-Control-Allow-Methods': 'POST, OPTIONS',
        'Access-Control-Allow-Headers': 'Content-Type',
        'Access-Control-Max-Age': '600',
        'Content-Length': '0',
      });
      res.end();
      return;
    }

    // --- Routing ---
    if (path !== SIGNUP_PATH) {
      outcome = 'not_found';
      req.resume(); // drain any body so the socket closes cleanly
      sendError(res, 404, 'not_found', 'Resource not found.');
      return;
    }
    if (method !== 'POST') {
      outcome = 'method_not_allowed';
      req.resume();
      sendError(res, 405, 'method_not_allowed', 'Method not allowed; use POST.', { Allow: 'POST, OPTIONS' });
      return;
    }

    // --- POST /api/signup ---
    // Rate limit FIRST: cheapest rejection, shields the expensive hashing path,
    // and counts every attempt (including malformed ones) against the budget.
    const rl = rateLimiter.check(clientIp(req));
    if (!rl.allowed) {
      outcome = 'rate_limited';
      req.resume();
      sendError(res, 429, 'rate_limited', 'Too many signup attempts; please retry later.', {
        'Retry-After': String(rl.retryAfterSeconds),
      });
      return;
    }

    // Read the body under the 64KB cap.
    const bodyResult = await readBody(req, {
      maxBytes: config.maxBodyBytes,
      hardLimitBytes: config.hardBodyLimitBytes,
    });

    if (bodyResult.aborted) {
      // Client disconnected, or we cut off an over-hard-limit upload — socket gone.
      outcome = bodyResult.tooLarge ? 'body_too_large_aborted' : 'client_aborted';
      return;
    }
    if (bodyResult.tooLarge) {
      // Oversize -> 400 invalid_json. The 400 code set is closed to the four
      // contract codes; we fold oversize into invalid_json rather than invent a
      // 413 shape the API contract does not define (documented in README).
      outcome = 'body_too_large';
      sendError(res, 400, 'invalid_json', `Request body exceeds the maximum size of ${config.maxBodyBytes} bytes.`);
      return;
    }

    if (!isJsonContentType(req)) {
      outcome = 'wrong_content_type';
      sendError(res, 400, 'invalid_json', 'Content-Type must be application/json.');
      return;
    }

    let parsed;
    try {
      parsed = JSON.parse(bodyResult.body);
    } catch {
      outcome = 'invalid_json';
      sendError(res, 400, 'invalid_json', 'Request body is not valid JSON.');
      return;
    }

    // J26: INJECTION — strict trust-boundary validation.
    const validated = validateSignup(parsed);
    if (!validated.ok) {
      outcome = validated.code;
      sendError(res, 400, validated.code, validated.message);
      return;
    }

    // J26: AUTH — scrypt hash. The plaintext is never stored or logged.
    const passwordHash = await hashPassword(validated.password, config.password);

    // Atomic check-and-insert mirrors the DB's UNIQUE (lower(email)) constraint.
    const result = store.create({ email: validated.email, passwordHash });
    if (result.conflict) {
      // Enumeration stance: 409 discloses that the email is registered.
      // Accepted for a signup form (documented in README); a hardened flow would
      // return 202 + "check your email" to remove the account-existence oracle.
      outcome = 'email_taken';
      sendError(res, 409, 'email_taken', 'An account with this email already exists.');
      return;
    }

    outcome = 'created';
    sendJson(res, 201, { user: toPublicUser(result.record) });
  } catch (err) {
    outcome = 'internal_error';
    logger({ level: 'error', msg: 'unhandled_error', correlationId, error: err?.message });
    if (!res.headersSent) sendError(res, 500, 'internal_error', 'An unexpected error occurred.');
  } finally {
    // Exactly one structured, PII-free line per request. Logged synchronously on
    // the return path, so it is present before the client observes the response.
    const durationMs = Number(process.hrtime.bigint() - startedAt) / 1e6;
    logger({
      level: 'info',
      msg: 'request',
      correlationId,
      method,
      path,
      status: res.statusCode,
      outcome,
      durationMs: Math.round(durationMs * 1000) / 1000,
    });
  }
}

-- PostgreSQL. Forward-only migration (no down script — see migrations/README.md).
--
-- Canonical `users` table backing POST /api/signup. The application's in-memory
-- store (server/src/store.js) mirrors these columns exactly. A real PostgreSQL
-- driver is intentionally out of scope for the current offline milestone; this
-- file is the schema of record for when one is wired in.

BEGIN;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
    id            uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    email         text        NOT NULL,
    password_hash text        NOT NULL,
    created_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Case-insensitive uniqueness: one account per email regardless of case. This
-- index is the authoritative guard; the application additionally canonicalises
-- email to lower-case before insert, and the store keys on lower(email) to
-- mirror it. (For adding an index to a large, live table later, prefer
-- CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY outside a transaction to avoid a write lock; safe
-- to run inline here because the table is empty at creation.)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS users_email_lower_key ON users (lower(email));

COMMIT;

-- Notes:
-- * gen_random_uuid() is built in on PostgreSQL 13+. On older servers, enable
--   pgcrypto first (CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;) or rely on the
--   application to supply `id` (it generates a v4 UUID via crypto.randomUUID()).
-- * created_at is timestamptz; the app writes ISO-8601 UTC (…Z) values.
-- * password_hash stores the scrypt string: scrypt$N$r$p$<salt-hex>$<key-hex>.

// Test helpers. NOTE: this file does not match the node:test file-name pattern
// (*.test.js), so the runner imports it but never executes it as a suite.
import { createServer } from '../src/app.js';
import { loadConfig } from '../src/config.js';

/**
 * Boot the REAL server on an ephemeral port with a capturing logger.
 * Each call gets its own store + rate-limiter, so suites never share state.
 *
 * `overrides` is shallow-merged over the default config, with a deep merge for
 * the nested `rateLimit` / `password` / `timeouts` objects.
 */
export async function startTestServer(overrides = {}) {
  const base = loadConfig({}); // {} => ignore ambient env, fully deterministic
  const config = {
    ...base,
    ...overrides,
    rateLimit: { ...base.rateLimit, ...(overrides.rateLimit ?? {}) },
    password: { ...base.password, ...(overrides.password ?? {}) },
    timeouts: { ...base.timeouts, ...(overrides.timeouts ?? {}) },
  };

  const logs = [];
  const logger = (entry) => logs.push(entry);

  const server = createServer({ config, logger });
  await new Promise((resolve) => server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', resolve));
  const { port } = server.address();

  return {
    server,
    config,
    logs,
    baseUrl: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`,
    close: () =>
      new Promise((resolve) => {
        server.close(resolve);
        // Force any keep-alive sockets (undici's default) shut so close() and
        // the test process resolve promptly instead of waiting on the timeout.
        server.closeAllConnections?.();
      }),
  };
}

/** POST to /api/signup. Pass `raw` to send a body verbatim (bypassing JSON.stringify). */
export async function postSignup(baseUrl, body, { headers, raw } = {}) {
  const init = {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...(headers ?? {}) },
  };
  init.body = raw !== undefined ? raw : JSON.stringify(body);
  const res = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/api/signup`, init);
  const text = await res.text();
  let json = null;
  try {
    json = text ? JSON.parse(text) : null;
  } catch {
    json = null;
  }
  return { res, json, text };

# signup-server

Zero-dependency Node.js HTTP API for user signup: **`POST /api/signup`**.

Built on `node:http` and `node:crypto` only — no Express, no npm dependencies
(runtime or dev). Requires **Node.js >= 20** (developed on 22.x).

## Run

```bash
cd server
npm start                 # listens on PORT (default 3000)
# or with configuration:
PORT=3000 SIGNUP_CORS_ORIGIN=http://localhost:8080 npm start
```

There is nothing to install — `npm start` / `npm test` run against Node built-ins.
Do not run `npm install`; there is no dependency tree and no lockfile.

## Configuration

All configuration comes from the environment, with safe defaults. Invalid
values fall back to the default rather than crashing on boot.

| Variable                       | Default                  | Meaning                                   |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `PORT`                         | `3000`                   | Listen port (`npm start` only).           |
| `SIGNUP_CORS_ORIGIN`           | `http://localhost:8080`  | The single allowed browser origin.        |
| `SIGNUP_RATE_LIMIT_MAX`        | `5`                      | Max `POST /api/signup` per window per IP. |
| `SIGNUP_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`  | `60000`                  | Rate-limit window in milliseconds.        |
| `SIGNUP_MAX_BODY_BYTES`        | `65536` (64 KB)          | Request body size cap.                    |

## API contract

### `POST /api/signup`

Request — `Content-Type: application/json`, body capped at 64 KB:

```json
{ "email": "user@example.com", "password": "at-least-8-chars" }
```

Responses:

| Status | Body                                                                              | When                                                     |
| ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `201`  | `{ "user": { "id": "<uuid>", "email": "<lowercase>", "created_at": "<ISO-8601 UTC>" } }` | Created.                                          |
| `400`  | `{ "error": { "code": "invalid_json"  \| "missing_field" \| "invalid_email" \| "weak_password", "message": "…" } }` | Bad request (see below). |
| `409`  | `{ "error": { "code": "email_taken", "message": "…" } }`                          | Email already registered (case-insensitive).             |
| `429`  | `{ "error": { "code": "rate_limited", "message": "…" } }` + `Retry-After` header  | Per-IP rate limit exceeded.                              |
| `405`  | `{ "error": { "code": "method_not_allowed", … } }` + `Allow: POST, OPTIONS`       | Non-POST to `/api/signup`.                               |
| `404`  | `{ "error": { "code": "not_found", … } }`                                         | Any other path.                                          |
| `204`  | *(empty)*                                                                         | `OPTIONS /api/signup` CORS preflight.                    |

`400` mapping details:

- `invalid_json` — malformed JSON, **wrong `Content-Type`**, or **oversized body**.
  Oversize is deliberately folded into `invalid_json` rather than a separate
  `413`: the contract's 400 code set is closed to the four codes above, so we
  keep a single, uniform error shape.
- `missing_field` — `email` or `password` absent / not a string, or the body is
  not a JSON object.
- `invalid_email` — present but not a valid email.
- `weak_password` — present but shorter than 8 or longer than 1024 characters.

Error precedence: `missing_field` → `invalid_email` → `weak_password`.

The **password never appears** in any response body or log line.

## Security posture (J26 modules)

- **AUTH** — passwords hashed with `scrypt` (`node:crypto`): `N=16384, r=8, p=1`,
  16-byte random salt, 64-byte key. Stored self-describing as
  `scrypt$N$r$p$<salt-hex>$<key-hex>`; verification is constant-time
  (`timingSafeEqual`). No MD5/SHA1/plaintext.
  *Enumeration stance:* a duplicate email returns `409 email_taken`, which
  reveals that an account exists. This is accepted for a signup form (the UX
  benefit outweighs the weak oracle). A hardened flow would instead return `202`
  and email the address ("you already have an account / here's a reset link").
- **INJECTION** — every field is validated at the trust boundary (type, length,
  shape) before use. No user input is interpolated into SQL, shell, or template
  strings. The persistence layer keys on a canonicalised value; the production
  migration uses a `UNIQUE (lower(email))` index rather than string-built SQL.
- **DATA** — the password and raw email are never logged. Logs are structured
  JSON containing only routing/outcome metadata plus a per-request
  `X-Correlation-Id`. Responses expose an allow-list projection
  (`id`, `email`, `created_at`) — `password_hash` cannot leak.
- **CONFIG** — CORS is locked to the single configured origin (never `*`);
  64 KB body cap with a 1 MiB hard cutoff that resets abusive uploads; request/
  header/keep-alive timeouts bound slowloris-style holds. `nosniff`,
  `no-referrer`, and `no-store` on every response.

Rate limiting is per source IP using `req.socket.remoteAddress`. **`X-Forwarded-For`
is intentionally not trusted** (it is client-settable; honouring it blindly
would let an attacker rotate the header to evade the limit). Behind a trusted
proxy, parse `XFF` against a configured trusted-hop count. The limiter is
in-process; a horizontally-scaled deployment should move it to a shared store
(Redis) or the edge/load-balancer so the window is shared across instances.

## Persistence

Runtime persistence is an **in-memory store** (`src/store.js`) that mirrors
`migrations/0001_create_users.sql` exactly. A PostgreSQL driver is out of scope
for this offline milestone; the migration is the schema of record. See
`migrations/README.md`.

## Testing

```bash
cd server
npm test
```

Runs the `node:test` suites in `test/`. The integration tests boot the **real**
server on an ephemeral port and speak real HTTP over loopback (no mocked
server / no mocked sockets). Everything runs offline against Node built-ins.

> Note on the test script: `package.json` uses
> `node --test "test/**/*.test.js"`. Node's CLI test runner matches file
> *glob patterns*, not bare directory arguments — `node --test test/` is treated
> as a script entry point and errors on every Node >= 20 (confirmed against the
> Node 22 docs). The quoted glob is the portable, documented form and discovers
> exactly the `*.test.js` suites.

## Layout

```
server/
  src/
    index.js         entrypoint (npm start)
    app.js           createServer() + request handler / routing
    config.js        environment-driven configuration
    validation.js    trust-boundary input validation
    password.js      scrypt hash + constant-time verify
    store.js         in-memory user store (mirrors the migration)
    rate-limiter.js  per-IP fixed-window limiter
    http-helpers.js  response envelopes, CORS/security headers, capped body reader
  test/              node:test suites (integration + unit)
  package.json
```

# Database migrations

Raw SQL migrations for the signup service, PostgreSQL dialect.

## Convention

- **Forward-only.** Files are numbered `NNNN_description.sql` and applied in
  ascending order. There are no `down` / rollback scripts; to reverse a change
  you write a new, higher-numbered forward migration. Roll back a bad deploy at
  the application layer (revert the code), not by mutating already-applied
  schema.
- Each file is a single transaction (`BEGIN; … COMMIT;`) so a failed apply
  leaves nothing half-created.
- Statements use `IF NOT EXISTS` where possible, so re-applying a file is a
  no-op rather than an error.

## Applying

Apply a migration with `psql`:

```bash
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f migrations/0001_create_users.sql
```

`-v ON_ERROR_STOP=1` makes `psql` exit non-zero on the first error (important in
CI / deploy scripts). Apply files in numeric order.

## Migrations

| File                      | Description                                                             |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `0001_create_users.sql`   | `users` table (id, email, password_hash, created_at) + `UNIQUE (lower(email))`. |

## Relationship to the running service

The signup API currently persists to an **in-memory store**
(`server/src/store.js`) whose columns mirror `0001_create_users.sql` exactly
(`id`, `email`, `password_hash`, `created_at`) and which enforces the same
case-insensitive uniqueness (`lower(email)`). A real PostgreSQL driver is out of
scope for the current offline milestone; this migration is the schema of record
for when one is introduced. Because the store's `create(...)` shape is
repository-like, swapping it for a `pg`-backed implementation should not require
changes to the request handler.

## Requirements

PostgreSQL **13+** (for the built-in `gen_random_uuid()`). On older servers,
`CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;` first, or let the application supply
`id` (it generates a v4 UUID per row).

# Lessons ledger

Production lessons learned the hard way. Each entry is a single-sentence
takeaway, traceable to the Beads task(s) that produced it, with the date
it was first recorded.

Add new entries via `.claude/scripts/lessons.sh add '<lesson>' --source <task-id>`
— never hand-edit. The helper deduplicates by normalized text (case- and
whitespace-insensitive), so repeating an existing lesson appends the new
source to that entry rather than creating a duplicate. The only legitimate
hand-edit is pruning entries that are no longer relevant.

The orchestrator reads this file during planning (see `orchestrator.md`),
the grader (Phase A) receives it in the grading packet, and the QA agent
proposes additions at epic close. Treat it as the institutional memory the
plugin runs against, not a static reference doc.

## Lessons

- Parallel agents in the same working tree contaminate each other's branches; concurrent specialists require worktree isolation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Boundary mocks must use the real downstream producer's shape, pinned via a fixture extracted from the producer's spec — never invented. A mock that feeds `body.error` so the test can assert `body.error` is circular and proves nothing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- New agent files must be registered in .claude-plugin/plugin.json agents[] in the same commit that creates them; an unregistered agent is silently invisible to the SDK — no error surfaces. Guard: agents-manifest-parity test. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Subagents cannot spawn other subagents in the Claude Code runtime (docs: sub-agents page — Agent(agent_type) has no effect in subagent definitions). Any agent-spawning step must live at the root conversation level; design multi-agent handoffs as root-orchestrated relays, never nested spawns. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Interface examples must be executed by a test: the Makefile's own usage string (make test-live FIXTURE=node-react-auth) was broken for the one fixture whose spec file is scenario-named — nothing ever ran the documented invocation. Caught only when a paid live run failed fast. Any CLI surface a doc or help text advertises needs an L2 assertion that executes that exact invocation (dry-run mode where the real one costs money). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Prose cues do not reliably drive subagent tool usage: across 4 live runs, QA made zero impact_of calls even when its task prompt contained the exact tool name, alias, target symbols, and invariant name. When a workflow REQUIRES a tool call, make it mechanical (compute it where calls are reliable — e.g. orchestrator at root — and pass results down), don't prompt for it. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n6d --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Rendered fixture installs pin plugin scripts at render time: the fixture's verify-before-stop.sh predated the cue fix by one commit, so a hook-template change never reached the live run. Script-level fixes require re-rendering fixture installs (or a version check at run start) before they affect live validation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.10 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Never run QA review concurrently with a builder in the same working tree: QA attributed the parallel C.2 task's freshly-written files to the C.1 task under review and blocked it for scope creep. Sequence QA after all writers finish, or give builders worktree isolation (orchestrator.md 4b exists for exactly this). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.1 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Manifest-declared assets must be presence-asserted at the install target: install.sh's hardcoded agent list silently dropped grader.md for two releases (v3.2.0-v3.3.0) — every fresh install was missing the rubric loop's grader while the repo's own tests stayed green. Glob-copy from the manifest source of truth and add an installer-spec presence assertion for every plugin.json agents[]/commands[] entry. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Bash functions invoked via $(...) command substitution run in a subshell — any variable they set is lost to the parent. The manual-adopt gate in model-select.sh was dead code for exactly this reason (set at :341, read at :500, never connected). When a helper must signal the caller, encode the signal in its stdout contract (e.g. a MANUAL<tab> prefix) and parse it at every call site; add a META-TEST that strips the parse to prove the gate is load-bearing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-3fn --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- A security hardening that breaks the workflow is worse than the documented residual it closes. Fail-closing prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh on ambiguous identity assumed every specialist carries a probeable identity, but this runtime does not surface subagent_name to PreToolUse hooks — so it denied legitimate specialist Write/Edit (a P0-class regression) to close a P2 Bash-write vector. When a guard depends on an identity signal the runtime may not provide, prefer fail-OPEN plus the structural guard (the orchestrator's omitted Write/Edit tools, which IS airtight) and document the residual; never trade a P2 for a P0. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.19 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Line-number-anchored mutation META-tests are brittle: any comment or line addition above the anchor silently un-lands the NR==<n>/sed -n Np target, turning a load-bearing META into a no-op (or a spurious failure). Anchor mutation METAs to a unique TEXT pattern in the target line, not an absolute line number. (3 instances re-anchored across verify-before-stop/escalation-binding specs this session.) <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.20 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->

# Default rubric (v1)

Applies to every task graded under the rubric-grader QA loop (spec Phase A). Each criterion below is a pass/fail assertion the grader evaluates from the grading packet: `bd show` for the task, the SPEC doc, the diff of the files listed in `.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt`, the F7 completion contract returned by the specialist, and `LESSONS.md`. One-line justification per criterion. No numeric score theater — pass or fail.

The criteria are intentionally short and checkable. Where the criterion needs context (boundary-mock fidelity, F7 fields), the "Evidence that satisfies it" line names the artefact the grader looks at.

## Criteria

### C1. Behavior matches the task description and SPEC.

The shipped diff implements the behavior the task description asks for, and matches the goal + acceptance criteria stated in the attached SPEC doc (read via `bd_doc_read(task_id, name="spec")`). Out-of-scope behavior the SPEC explicitly excludes is NOT in the diff.

Evidence that satisfies it: a 1-2 sentence walk-through that maps every user-visible behavior in the SPEC to a code path in the diff (or to a deliberate, documented deferral in the F7 `decisions` array). A diff that adds plausibly-related behavior the SPEC does not name fails this criterion — that is scope creep.

### C2. Tests added exercise user behavior rather than implementation.

Where the diff introduces new behavior, the diff also introduces tests that assert against the user-visible contract (return shape, side effects, error envelope, accessibility role, status code) rather than against the implementation's private structure (function-name mocking, line-coverage gymnastics, internal control-flow assertions).

Evidence that satisfies it: at least one test in the diff that would still pass if the implementation were rewritten while keeping the user contract identical. A test that asserts only against private symbols, internal call counts, or framework boilerplate fails this criterion.

### C3. The F7 completion contract carries all six fields with substantive `llm_observations`.

The specialist's structured completion payload includes `task_id`, `files_changed`, `tests_added`, `decisions`, `blockers`, and `llm_observations`. `llm_observations` is non-trivial narrative — what surprised the specialist, what was unclear, what they noticed and did not act on. A boilerplate one-liner like "no observations" fails this criterion (principle 9: `llm_observations` is mandatory and substantive).

Evidence that satisfies it: each of the six fields is present and the `llm_observations` paragraph is the kind of thing a human engineer would say at a stand-up.

### C4. No unrelated scope in the diff.

Every file the specialist touched serves the task. Drive-by refactors, formatting churn on untouched lines, and "while I'm here" cleanups that exceed the task brief fail this criterion — they should be filed as paired follow-up Beads tasks instead.

Evidence that satisfies it: the diff's file list maps cleanly to the SPEC's deliverables; any incidental change is either trivial (one-line typo fix) or explicitly justified in the `decisions` array.

### C5. J26 modules relevant to the diff are addressed.

Where the diff touches a domain covered by the J26 security taxonomy (SECRETS, INJECTION, AUTH, CONFIG, DEPS, AI, MOBILE, DATA — see `docs/AGENTS.md`), the diff demonstrates that the relevant modules were considered. Untouched J26 domains are out of scope.

Evidence that satisfies it: the `decisions` array (or the SPEC) names which J26 modules apply, and the diff shows defences in those modules (input validation at the trust boundary, parameterised queries, narrow CORS, audited logging, etc.). A diff that touches user input handling without naming INJECTION fails this criterion.

### C6. Docs updated where behavior changed.

When the diff changes user-visible behavior, the documentation that describes that behavior is updated in the same change. This includes `CHANGELOG.md`, README sections, `docs/*.md`, command help text, and SPEC docs the diff renders out of date.

Evidence that satisfies it: a docs-only file in `files_changed` paired with each behavioral change, or a deliberate `decisions` entry stating why a doc deferral is correct (e.g. an internal refactor that ships without user-visible change). A behavioral change that ships with no doc update and no deferral note fails this criterion.

### C7. Boundary-mock fidelity (LESSONS.md lesson 2).

When the diff introduces or modifies mocks of boundaries the project does not control (third-party HTTP APIs, external SDKs, system calls, message-bus payloads), every such mock derives its shape from a fixture extracted from the real downstream producer's spec (OpenAPI, proto file, SDK source, vendor docs). The fixture's source is cited in a comment, the `decisions` array, or `llm_observations`.

**Automatic needs_revision:** circular pass-through assertions are an immediate fail. A mock that feeds `body.error` so a test can assert `body.error` proves nothing — it tests the test's own setup, not the production behavior. Cite `LESSONS.md` lesson 2 in the justification.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new boundary mock points at a fixture file (`.fixtures/`, `__fixtures__/`, `testdata/`) carrying a snapshot of the producer's payload, and the fixture has a comment naming the source (URL, commit, SDK version). Tests assert against the producer's contract, not against the mock's own input.

# Backend rubric (v1)

Applied additionally when the task carries the `backend` label. Default criteria still apply; these add domain-specific checks pulled from `.claude/agents/backend.md`. Keep the leverage at default + bugfix — these are the few backend-specific failure modes that recur.

## Criteria

### B1. Inputs are validated at the trust boundary.

Every new request handler, queue consumer, or external-facing entry point validates inputs (type, range, length, encoding) before they reach business logic. Reject early with a stable error envelope; never interpolate untrusted input into SQL, shell, or template strings.

Evidence that satisfies it: parameterised queries / prepared statements throughout the diff; a validation layer (schema, decoder, guard clause) on every new boundary. A diff that passes a raw query string into a SQL builder, a shell command, or a template fails this criterion (extends C5 / INJECTION).

### B2. Migrations are reversible and safe to deploy ahead of code.

Schema migrations in the diff are additive-first (add column, backfill, switch code, drop later); never long-locking on hot tables; carry an explicit rollback path documented in the migration file or the `decisions` array. A breaking column rename or destructive drop without a multi-step rollout plan fails this criterion.

Evidence that satisfies it: each migration file is paired with a rollback, the deploy order is documented (additive deploy ⇒ backfill ⇒ code switch ⇒ optional drop), and any locking operation cites the engine's online-schema-change tooling or explains why a brief lock is acceptable.

### B3. Error paths return the documented contract.

New error paths (4xx, 5xx, exception envelopes, queue DLQ payloads) map to the stable error codes the rest of the system uses. A new endpoint that invents its own error shape or leaks an internal stack trace fails this criterion.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new throw / return path maps to a documented domain error code; the response shape matches the consistent `{error: {code, message, details?}}` (or equivalent) envelope the codebase uses elsewhere; no internal exception text is exposed to the client.

### B4. Outbound calls have explicit timeouts and backpressure.

Any new outbound call (HTTP, RPC, queue publish, DB query on a new path) declares an explicit timeout. Long-running consumers carry bounded concurrency (semaphore, work-queue depth, circuit breaker) so a flaky downstream cannot exhaust the service. A `requests.get(url)` or `axios.get(url)` with no timeout fails this criterion.

## Goal
User signup, client side: accessible signup form UI in client/ against the 5am.1 API contract.

## Deliverables (all NEW files; do not modify anything outside client/)
- client/index.html — signup page (email, password, submit)
- client/src/*.js — ES modules: PURE logic (validation, payload build, response mapping) separated from thin DOM wiring
- client/serve.js — zero-dep static file server for local dev (node:http), default port 8080, strict path containment
- client/package.json ("type":"module"; scripts.test="node --test test/"; scripts.start="node serve.js") — INSIDE client/ only
- client/test/ — node:test suites
- client/README.md — run instructions, UX states, a11y notes

## API contract (producer: backend child claude-workflow-plugin-5am.1 — cite it for every fixture)
POST http://localhost:3000/api/signup (API base configurable)
- Request: JSON {"email": string, "password": string}
- 201: {"user": {"id": "<uuid>", "email": "<canonical-lowercase>", "created_at": "<ISO-8601 UTC>"}}
- 400: {"error": {"code": "invalid_json"|"missing_field"|"invalid_email"|"weak_password", "message": "..."}}
- 409: {"error": {"code": "email_taken", "message": "..."}}
- 429: {"error": {"code": "rate_limited", "message": "..."}} + Retry-After header

## Acceptance criteria
1. Labelled email + password inputs (label[for] wired), submit button, required + autocomplete attributes (email, new-password).
2. Client-side validation mirrors server rules (email shape, password >=8) with field-level errors BEFORE any network call; invalid submit does not hit the API.
3. 201 -> visible success state including the registered email; form resets; password value discarded.
4. 400/409/429 -> human-readable message mapped per error.code (email_taken -> already-registered messaging; rate_limited -> retry messaging honoring Retry-After when present).
5. Network failure / non-JSON response -> generic failure state; form stays usable; no unhandled rejection.
6. A11y: error region aria-live=polite (or role=alert); inputs get aria-invalid + aria-describedby pointing at their message.
7. Double-submit protection: submit disabled while a request is in flight.
8. Pure-logic modules covered by node:test, offline, zero deps (cd client && npm test). Response-mapping fixtures derive from the 5am.1 contract with the source cited in the fixture header (rubric C7).
9. One integration test boots the REAL server from ../server on an ephemeral port and exercises validate -> POST -> map end-to-end via global fetch. Skip cleanly with a reason only if ../server is absent.
10. Password never logged, never in a URL, never stored (DATA).

## Constraints
- ZERO npm dependencies; no build step; vanilla ES modules (no React vendoring in this offline env — framework-portable pure functions instead; note the deviation from the generic React suggestion in decisions).
- NO root-level package.json (client/ only). Reading ../server for the integration test is fine; writing outside client/ is not.
- serve.js: path traversal impossible (resolve + prefix check), correct content-types, no directory listing.
- XSS posture: all API-derived strings rendered via textContent, never innerHTML.

## J26 modules in play (name in decisions)
CONFIG (static-server hardening), DATA (no password persistence/logging), XSS posture as above.

## Impact analysis (orchestrator 1a — degraded)
Same degradation note as 5am.1 (code-graph absent at root). client/ is greenfield; integration surfaces: the 5am.1 API contract and the no-root-manifest Stop-gate constraint.

## Out of scope
Styling polish beyond usable defaults; login flow; SSR; framework adoption; any server/ or migrations/ change.

## Process
TDD; client/README.md is the C6 doc update. When done: bd update 5am.2 --notes, keep qa-pending, return the F7 completion contract JSON (six fields, substantive llm_observations).

On success returns a ready-to-POST payload; on failure returns NO * payload (so nothing can be sent). * @returns {{ok:true,payload:{email:string,password:string}} * | {ok:false,fields:{email?:{code,message},password?:{code,message}}}} */ export function validateForm({ email, password } = {}) { const emailResult = validateEmail(email); const passwordResult = validatePassword(password); const fields = {}; if (!emailResult.ok) fields.email = { code: emailResult.code, message: emailResult.message }; if (!passwordResult.ok) fields.password = { code: passwordResult.code, message: passwordResult.message }; if (Object.keys(fields).length > 0) { return { ok: false, fields }; } return { ok: true, payload: buildFieldPayload({ email, password }) }; } ``` ### `client/src/config.js` ```javascript // ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- // API-base resolution — PURE (J26: CONFIG). // // The API base is configurable (spec: "API base configurable") but defaults to // the shipped server. Mirroring the server's config posture // (server/src/config.js: "invalid values fall back to the default rather than // crashing"), a missing / blank / non-http(s) / unparseable configured base // silently falls back to the default instead of breaking the form. // // The value is supplied by the thin DOM layer (read from a tag) and // passed in here as data, so this module never touches the DOM and stays unit // testable offline. // ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- export const DEFAULT_API_BASE = 'http://localhost:3000'; const SIGNUP_PATH = '/api/signup'; /** * @param {{apiBase?:string}} [source] * @returns {string} a normalized origin (no trailing slash), guaranteed http(s). */ export function resolveApiBase(source = {}) { const raw = source && typeof source.apiBase === 'string' ? source.apiBase.trim() : ''; if (raw === '') return DEFAULT_API_BASE; let parsed; try { parsed = new URL(raw); } catch { return DEFAULT_API_BASE; } if (parsed.protocol !== 'http:' && parsed.protocol !== 'https:') { return DEFAULT_API_BASE; } return raw.replace(/\/+$/, ''); } /** Compose the full signup endpoint URL from a resolved base. */ export function signupUrl(apiBase) { return `${String(apiBase).replace(/\/+$/, '')}${SIGNUP_PATH}`; } ``` ### `client/src/messages.js` ```javascript // ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- // User-facing copy — PURE. Centralised so wording is consistent and testable. // All strings are our own constants (never API-derived), but the DOM layer // still renders them via textContent (XSS posture is uniform). // ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- export const MESSAGES = Object.freeze({ // Transport failure (fetch rejected: offline, DNS, connection refused, CORS block). network: 'Unable to reach the server. Check your connection and try again.', // Server-reported, field-attributable errors. invalid_email: 'Enter a valid email address, for example name@example.com.', weak_password: 'Password must be between 8 and 1024 characters.', email_taken: 'An account with this email already exists. Try signing in instead.', // Server-reported, non-field-specific errors. missing_field: 'Please fill in both your email and password.', // Anything we cannot map to a specific, user-actionable cause. generic: 'Something went wrong on our end. Please try again in a moment.', }); /** * Rate-limit copy, honouring the Retry-After window when the server provides it. * @param {number|null} retryAfterSeconds */ export function rateLimitedMessage(retryAfterSeconds) { if (Number.isFinite(retryAfterSeconds) && retryAfterSeconds >= 1) { const secs = Math.ceil(retryAfterSeconds); const unit = secs === 1 ? 'second' : 'seconds'; return `Too many signup attempts. Please try again in ${secs} ${unit}.`; } return 'Too many signup attempts. Please wait a moment and try again.'; } /** * Success copy including the registered (canonical) email when present. * @param {string} email the email FROM THE API RESPONSE (authoritative) */ export function successMessage(email) { if (typeof email === 'string' && email !== '') { return `Account created for ${email}. You can now sign in.`; } return 'Account created successfully. You can now sign in.'; } ``` ### `client/src/api.js` ```javascript // ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- // API layer — PURE. Payload building + response mapping. No I/O lives here (the // network call is the injectable adapter in net.js), so every branch is unit // testable offline against fixtures derived from the 5am.1 contract. // ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- import { MESSAGES, rateLimitedMessage } from './messages.js'; // Re-export the pure payload builder (defined alongside validation so // validateForm can reuse it) under the API-facing name. export { buildFieldPayload as buildSignupPayload } from './validation.js'; /** @typedef {{type:'success',email:string}} SuccessOutcome */ /** @typedef {{type:'error',field:('email'|'password'|null),code:(string|null),message:string}} ErrorOutcome */ function errorOutcome(field, code, message) { return { type: 'error', field, code, message }; } /** * Map a normalized `requestSignup` result to a UI outcome. PURE and total: * every input — including garbage, null bodies and unknown codes — yields a * well-formed outcome and NEVER throws. * * @param {{networkError:true} * | {networkError:false,status:number,body:*,retryAfterSeconds:(number|null)} * | null | undefined} result * @returns {SuccessOutcome | ErrorOutcome} */ export function mapSignupResponse(result) { // Transport failure or missing result -> generic connectivity error. if (!result || result.networkError) { return errorOutcome(null, null, MESSAGES.network); } const { status, body, retryAfterSeconds } = result; if (status === 201) { const email = body && body.user && typeof body.user.email === 'string' ? body.user.email : ''; return { type: 'success', email }; } // Everything else is an error. Read the contract envelope defensively. const code = body && body.error && typeof body.error.code === 'string' ? body.error.code : null; switch (code) { case 'invalid_email': return errorOutcome('email', code, MESSAGES.invalid_email); case 'weak_password': return errorOutcome('password', code, MESSAGES.weak_password); case 'email_taken': return errorOutcome('email', code, MESSAGES.email_taken); case 'missing_field': // The server does not say WHICH field; surface at form level. return errorOutcome(null, code, MESSAGES.missing_field); case 'rate_limited': return errorOutcome(null, code, rateLimitedMessage(retryAfterSeconds)); case 'invalid_json': // A client/server contract mismatch the user cannot fix — generic copy. return errorOutcome(null, code, MESSAGES.generic); default: // Unknown/absent code (off-contract body, 5xx, future code) -> generic. return errorOutcome(null, code, MESSAGES.generic); } } ``` ### `client/src/net.js` ```javascript // ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- // Network adapter — the ONLY module that performs I/O. `fetch` is injected so // the pure/unit layers stay offline-testable; the app passes the real global // fetch, tests pass a stub, and the integration test passes globalThis.fetch // against the REAL server. // // DATA posture: the password travels ONLY in the request body (a POST JSON // payload) — never in the URL, never in a query string, and this module logs // nothing. Any transport failure is converted into a value ({networkError}) // rather than a thrown rejection, so the caller can never leak an unhandled // promise rejection (AC5). // ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- /** * Parse a Retry-After header value into whole seconds. * Supports the two RFC 7231 forms: delta-seconds (an integer) and an HTTP-date. * @param {string|null} value * @returns {number|null} */ export function parseRetryAfter(value) { if (value == null) return null; const asNumber = Number(value); if (Number.isFinite(asNumber) && asNumber >= 0) { return Math.ceil(asNumber); } const asDate = Date.parse(value); if (!Number.isNaN(asDate)) { const secs = Math.ceil((asDate - Date.now()) / 1000); return secs > 0 ? secs : 0; } return null; } /** * POST the signup payload and return a normalized result. Never throws. * @param {typeof fetch} fetchImpl injectable fetch (real global fetch in the app) * @param {string} url the fully-composed signup endpoint * @param {{email:string,password:string}} payload * @returns {Promise<{networkError:true} * | {networkError:false,status:number,body:*,retryAfterSeconds:(number|null)}>} */ export async function requestSignup(fetchImpl, url, payload) { let response; try { response = await fetchImpl(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, // Explicit hardening: no credentials/cookies on a public signup call. credentials: 'omit', body: JSON.stringify(payload), }); } catch { // Offline, DNS failure, connection refused, or a browser CORS block all land // here. Surface as a value so the UI shows a connectivity message. return { networkError: true }; } const retryAfterSeconds = parseRetryAfter( typeof response.headers?.get === 'function' ? response.headers.get('retry-after') : null, ); let body = null; try { const text = await response.text(); body = text ? JSON.parse(text) : null; } catch { // Non-JSON body (proxy HTML error page) or a broken stream -> body stays null. body = null; } return { networkError: false, status: response.status, body, retryAfterSeconds }; } ``` ### `client/src/dom.js` ```javascript // ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- // Thin DOM rendering helpers (NOT pure — this is the wiring layer). // // XSS posture (J26): every value that reaches the DOM is written with // `textContent`. `innerHTML` is never used anywhere in this file, so an // API-derived string (e.g. the registered email in the success message, or a // server error message) can never be interpreted as markup. `setText` is the // single choke point through which all text flows. // ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- /** The one and only way text reaches the DOM here: textContent, never innerHTML. */ export function setText(el, text) { if (el) el.textContent = text == null ? '' : String(text); } /** Attach a field-level error: message + aria-invalid, for a11y (AC6). */ export function setFieldError(input, errorEl, message) { setText(errorEl, message); if (input) input.setAttribute('aria-invalid', 'true'); } /** Clear a field-level error and its invalid state. */ export function clearFieldError(input, errorEl) { setText(errorEl, ''); if (input) input.setAttribute('aria-invalid', 'false'); } /** * Render the form-level status region (success or non-field error). The region * is an aria-live=polite area (AC6); `kind` only drives styling via a data attr. * @param {'success'|'error'|''} kind */ export function setStatus(statusEl, message, kind = '') { if (!statusEl) return; setText(statusEl, message); if (kind) statusEl.setAttribute('data-kind', kind); else statusEl.removeAttribute('data-kind'); } /** Move keyboard + screen-reader focus to an element (status region / field). */ export function focusEl(el) { if (el && typeof el.focus === 'function') el.focus(); } /** * Toggle the in-flight busy state (AC7 double-submit protection): disable the * button, mark aria-busy, and swap the visible label so the user sees progress. */ export function setBusy(button, busy) { if (!button) return; button.disabled = busy; button.setAttribute('aria-busy', busy ? 'true' : 'false'); if (busy) { if (!button.dataset.idleLabel) button.dataset.idleLabel = button.textContent; setText(button, button.dataset.busyLabel || 'Creating account…'); } else if (button.dataset.idleLabel) { setText(button, button.dataset.idleLabel); } } ``` ### `client/src/main.js` ```javascript // ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- // Entry wiring (thin). Composes the PURE modules (validation / config / api / // messages) with the DOM helpers. This is the only browser-coupled orchestration // code; all decision logic lives in the tested pure modules. // // Flow: submit -> validateForm (no network on invalid) -> setBusy (double-submit // guard) -> requestSignup (global fetch) -> mapSignupResponse -> render outcome. // DATA: the password is read from the input only to POST it; it is never logged, // never placed in a URL, and is discarded on success via form.reset(). // ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- import { validateForm } from './validation.js'; import { resolveApiBase, signupUrl } from './config.js'; import { requestSignup } from './net.js'; import { mapSignupResponse } from './api.js'; import { MESSAGES, successMessage } from './messages.js'; import { setFieldError, clearFieldError, setStatus, setBusy, focusEl } from './dom.js'; function init() { const form = document.getElementById('signup-form'); if (!form) return; // nothing to wire (defensive) const emailInput = document.getElementById('email'); const emailError = document.getElementById('email-error'); const passwordInput = document.getElementById('password'); const passwordError = document.getElementById('password-error'); const submitButton = document.getElementById('submit'); const statusEl = document.getElementById('form-status'); // Resolve the (configurable) API base once, from a tag, at startup. const metaBase = document.querySelector('meta[name="signup-api-base"]'); const endpoint = signupUrl(resolveApiBase({ apiBase: metaBase ? metaBase.content : undefined })); let inFlight = false; function clearErrors() { clearFieldError(emailInput, emailError); clearFieldError(passwordInput, passwordError); setStatus(statusEl, '', ''); } function renderFieldErrors(fields) { let firstInvalid = null; if (fields.email) { setFieldError(emailInput, emailError, fields.email.message); firstInvalid = firstInvalid || emailInput; } if (fields.password) { setFieldError(passwordInput, passwordError, fields.password.message); firstInvalid = firstInvalid || passwordInput; } // A polite, screen-reader-announced summary in the live region (AC6), plus // focus moved to the first invalid field (whose aria-describedby carries the // specific message). setStatus(statusEl, 'Please fix the highlighted fields below.', 'error'); focusEl(firstInvalid); } function handleOutcome(outcome) { if (outcome.type === 'success') { // Discard the password and reset the form (AC3, DATA). form.reset(); clearFieldError(emailInput, emailError); clearFieldError(passwordInput, passwordError); setStatus(statusEl, successMessage(outcome.email), 'success'); focusEl(statusEl); return; } // Error outcome: attach to a field when the server told us which one. if (outcome.field === 'email') { setFieldError(emailInput, emailError, outcome.message); focusEl(emailInput); } else if (outcome.field === 'password') { setFieldError(passwordInput, passwordError, outcome.message); focusEl(passwordInput); } else { setStatus(statusEl, outcome.message, 'error'); focusEl(statusEl); } } async function onSubmit(event) { event.preventDefault(); if (inFlight) return; // AC7: ignore re-entrant submits (Enter key, fast clicks) clearErrors(); const validation = validateForm({ email: emailInput ? emailInput.value : '', password: passwordInput ? passwordInput.value : '', }); if (!validation.ok) { renderFieldErrors(validation.fields); // AC2: no network call on invalid input return; } inFlight = true; setBusy(submitButton, true); try { const fetchImpl = window.fetch.bind(window); const result = await requestSignup(fetchImpl, endpoint, validation.payload); handleOutcome(mapSignupResponse(result)); } catch { // requestSignup already converts transport failures to values; this guard // guarantees no unhandled rejection ever escapes the submit handler (AC5). setStatus(statusEl, MESSAGES.generic, 'error'); focusEl(statusEl); } finally { inFlight = false; setBusy(submitButton, false); } } form.addEventListener('submit', onSubmit); // Clear a field's error as soon as the user starts correcting it. if (emailInput) emailInput.addEventListener('input', () => clearFieldError(emailInput, emailError)); if (passwordInput) passwordInput.addEventListener('input', () => clearFieldError(passwordInput, passwordError)); } if (document.readyState === 'loading') { document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init); } else { init(); } ``` ### `client/README.md` ```markdown # signup-client Accessible signup form UI for **`POST /api/signup`**, built as **vanilla ES modules with zero dependencies and no build step**. It targets the zero-dependency backend shipped in [`../server`](../server) (task `claude-workflow-plugin-5am.1`, qa-approved). ## Why vanilla JS (framework deviation) The generic frontend playbook reaches for React. This milestone runs in an **offline environment with no npm install and no build step**, so vendoring a framework (or a bundler/transpiler) is not possible and would add a lockfile the constraints forbid. Instead the decision logic lives in **pure, framework- portable functions** (`src/validation.js`, `src/api.js`, `src/config.js`, `src/messages.js`) with a **thin DOM wiring layer** (`src/main.js`, `src/dom.js`). If this is ever ported to React/Vue/Svelte, the pure modules move over unchanged and only the wiring layer is rewritten. ## Run it Two processes: the API server and this static file server. ```bash # Terminal 1 — the API (defaults to :3000, CORS locked to http://localhost:8080) cd server && npm start # Terminal 2 — this static UI (defaults to :8080 to match the server's CORS origin) cd client && npm start # then open http://localhost:8080 ``` There is nothing to install — everything runs on Node built-ins (Node **>= 20**; the CLI test-runner glob and `fetch` require it). If `:8080` is taken, pick another port with `PORT=8090 npm start` (the server allows that origin only if you also set `SIGNUP_CORS_ORIGIN` to match — see `../server/README.md`). ### Configuration | What | How | Default | | --- | --- | --- | | API base URL | `` in `index.html` | `http://localhost:3000` | | Static-server port | `PORT` env for `npm start` | `8080` | | Static-server host | `HOST` env for `npm start` | `127.0.0.1` | An invalid / non-http(s) API base silently falls back to the default (mirrors the server's config posture) — see `src/config.js`. ## UX states | State | What the user sees | | --- | --- | | Idle | Email + password fields, "Create account" button, password hint. | | Invalid submit | Per-field messages under each field, the field outlined and `aria-invalid`, focus moved to the first invalid field, and a polite "Please fix the highlighted fields below." in the status region. **No network request is made.** | | Submitting | Button disabled + `aria-busy`, label becomes "Creating account…" (double-submit is ignored). | | Success (201) | "Account created for ``. You can now sign in." using the **canonical email from the response**; the form is reset and the password is discarded. | | Email taken (409) | "An account with this email already exists. Try signing in instead." on the email field. | | Rate limited (429) | "Too many signup attempts. Please try again in `N` seconds." honouring the `Retry-After` header. | | Bad request (400) | `invalid_email` → email field; `weak_password` → password field; `missing_field` / `invalid_json` → a form-level message. | | Network failure | "Unable to reach the server. Check your connection and try again." The form stays usable; no unhandled promise rejection. | ## Accessibility - Every input has a wired `

<!-- BD-MCP-DOC: qa-plan v1 -->
# QA plan — claude-workflow-plugin-5am.2 (Frontend: signup form UI), iteration 1

## Gate state
Entered gate (qa-gate-entered + rubric-pending set); impact report generated with server=absent. This is the FIRST QA spawn of the rubric relay. Verdict of this spawn: CLEAN — no must-fix defects. NOT approved and grader NOT spawned (nested-spawn is structurally impossible; qa.md 6). Grading packet (comment id 433) assembled and persisted for the root orchestrator to relay to the grader. Returning needs-grading.

## Impact / regression pass (qa.md 3a)
- FIRST ACTION: read impact-report-claude-workflow-plugin-5am.2.json — server=absent (code-graph structurally unavailable this session; documented degradation). Impact pass done MANUALLY.
- All 20 changed files are NEW/untracked under client/ (git status: client/ untracked in full; no pre-existing tracked file modified). Greenfield -> no existing symbol has callers to break.
- The one cross-boundary surface is test/integration.test.js READING ../server: it imports the shipped server src/*.js and boots createServer in-memory on an ephemeral port (in-memory store), and never writes outside client/. Confirmed read-only.

## Review modules executed (J26 + a11y)
- CONFIG (static-server hardening / traversal) — PRIMARY. serve.js: realpath'd root + lexical prefix containment + post-stat realpath re-check (symlink escape), no directory listing, GET/HEAD allow-list, explicit content-types, security headers (nosniff/DENY/no-referrer/no-store + CSP) on EVERY response incl. errors. Verified live (see below).
- INJECTION-adjacent (path containment) — no SQL/shell/template; path resolution is resolve+prefix+realpath. Encoded/literal/absolute traversal all contained.
- DATA (password) — password only in POST body (net.js credentials:'omit'); never logged (serve.js info logs carry method/status/outcome only — confirmed in live log tail), never in URL/query, discarded on success via form.reset(). Server error.message is NEVER rendered (api.js maps code -> own MESSAGES copy).
- XSS — single setText/textContent choke point in dom.js; innerHTML never used; adversarial-email fixture proves mapper passes through untouched; CSP script-src 'self' + nosniff as defense-in-depth.
- SECRETS (always-on) — none present. No keys/tokens; API base is localhost:3000 in a <meta> tag (config, not a secret).
- DEPS — verified vacuous: package.json has zero dependencies, no lockfile, engines node>=20.
- Frontend a11y — label[for] wired both fields; autocomplete email/new-password; required+aria-required; aria-invalid initialized false and toggled; aria-describedby wires field messages (+ password hint); #form-status is role=status aria-live=polite aria-atomic tabindex=-1; focus management (first invalid field / status region); 44px targets, always-visible focus rings incl. on status region, reserved space (no CLS), prefers-reduced-motion — all in index.html + dom.js + main.js + styles.css.

## Acceptance criteria (all 10 verified)
AC1 labels/autocomplete/required — index.html (static, checked). AC2 client validation mirrors server + no network on invalid — validation.js + main.js onSubmit early-return + parity battery. AC3 201 success shows canonical email + form.reset discards password — main.js + live integration (Alice@Example.com -> alice@example.com). AC4 400/409/429 mapping incl. Retry-After — api.js + tests + live 429. AC5 network/non-JSON generic, no unhandled rejection — net.js value-return + main.js catch. AC6 aria-live + aria-invalid + aria-describedby — index.html + dom.js. AC7 double-submit (inFlight guard + disabled button) — main.js + dom.js. AC8 pure modules node:test offline zero-dep + fixtures cite 5am.1 — 56 tests, fixture header cites producer. AC9 integration boots REAL server on ephemeral port, exercises validate->POST->map, skips only if absent — RAN (not skipped). AC10 password not logged/URL/stored — net.js + serve.js logs + form.reset.

## Tests run
- `cd client && npm test`: 56 pass, 0 skipped. Integration tests (20/21/22) genuinely ran (durations 69ms/26ms/0.35ms) booting the real server — not skipped.
- Live serve.js probes on a free port (8137; 8080 occupied by unrelated agentsvie PID 50482, as F7 noted): GET / 200 text/html + all security headers; JS text/javascript; CSS text/css; encoded traversal %2e%2e%2f -> 403 no leak; mixed ..%2f -> 403 no leak; literal ../ -> 404 in-root (URL-parser normalized) no leak; //etc/hosts -> 404 no leak; directory /src, /src/ -> 404 no listing; POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH/OPTIONS -> 405 + Allow: GET, HEAD; HEAD -> 200 no body; unknown -> 404; NUL byte -> 400; malformed %zz -> 400; security headers present on 403/404 too; binds 127.0.0.1 only.
- `make test` (plugin regression) from repo root: 18/18 test files green.

## Documented deviations — all judged ACCEPTABLE
1. Vanilla ES modules instead of React — SPEC explicitly permits (offline, no npm/build); pure functions + thin wiring; documented in decisions + README.
2. Empty-string password -> weak_password CODE (friendlier "required" MESSAGE) — mirrors server ('' is present-but-too-short); proven by the live parity battery importing real validateSignup.
3. Client reports BOTH field errors at once vs server single-error precedence — better UX; client short-circuits before network so no conflict; parity battery reconciles via clientPrecedenceCode.
4. Payload email trimmed but case-PRESERVED — server canonicalises; 201 returns authoritative lowercase which the success state displays (verified live).
5. package.json test script uses glob `node --test "test/**/*.test.js"` (SPEC literal said `node --test test/`) — the bare-directory form ERRORS on Node>=20; glob is the correct/portable form and matches the server convention. Deviation from literal SPEC text but the correct choice.

## Limitations (recorded honestly)
- No browser in this offline session: DOM-runtime behaviors (focus actually moving, aria-live actually announcing, button actually disabling on click, form.reset clearing the field in the DOM) were verified by CLOSE CODE-READING of main.js + dom.js + index.html + styles.css, NOT by live browser execution. The pure logic they call is unit-tested; the wiring is thin and traced end-to-end. Recommend a real-browser / Playwright pass before production if one becomes available.
- code-graph absent -> impact pass was manual (greenfield made this low-risk).

## Non-blocking observations (candidates for follow-up, NOT must-fix)
- CSP connect-src is `'self' http: https:` (permissive) to support a configurable API base — flagged by specialist; fine for local dev, tighten to the resolved origin if hardened.
- email_taken enumeration oracle is inherited from the accepted 5am.1 server contract (server README documents/accepts it); the client merely displays it — out of scope here.
- Consider dual-surfacing email_taken (form-level hint + field message) — specialist's own suggestion.

title: bd sync: remote JSONL import fails with 'bufio.Scanner: token too long' on >64KB task lines
description: Long doc comments (grading packets ~23KB, SPEC docs ~10KB) accumulate on one task's JSONL line; bd's import scanner has a fixed buffer. Mitigations: chunk large bd_doc_write payloads, or upstream bd fix (larger scanner buffer). First seen 2026-07-25 after V0 closeout; sync-errors.log captures it; session-start warns.

comments.text: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED 2026-07-25: .beads/issues.jsonl has 5 lines >54KB, three >100KB (5am.2=155KB, bi3.1=153KB, 5am.1=106KB) — grading-packet doc comments (some 124KB) stored inline on the task's JSONL line. bd 0.47.1's bufio.Scanner import buffer (64KB default) chokes, so 'bd sync' remote import and the pre-commit/post-merge hooks fail ('token too long'); local commits need --no-verify. MITIGATIONS: (1) upstream — bd should raise scanner buffer or store large docs out-of-line; (2) plugin-side — cap bd_doc_write grading-packet size (the LEAN <25KB packet convention adopted mid-session helps future tasks; 5am/40c/bi3.1 predate it); (3) the e2e-fixture headless runs (5am/40c) should use an isolated bd DB, not the plugin's live one. Not blocking v4 delivery: all commits land via --no-verify and are pushed; bd JSONL is git-tracked and intact, only re-import is degraded.
