# Bugfix overlay (v1)

Applied additionally whenever the task type is `bug` (created with `-t bug` or carrying the `bug` label). Default + the relevant domain rubric still apply; this overlay enforces the evidence-before-fix protocol from spec 0.5. The protocol exists to break symptom-patching chains — speculative fixes stacking into double-digit follow-up PRs for a single issue, none of which can be proved to be the one that worked. Every criterion below is mandatory for bug-typed tasks.

## Criteria

### G1. A failing test demonstrating the root cause exists and predates the fix.

The diff contains a test that fails on the broken commit and passes on the fix commit. The test is committed BEFORE the fix in the commit sequence (or in a single commit if the workflow squashes), so a reviewer can run the test against the parent of the fix and watch it fail.

Evidence that satisfies it: the commit log (or the diff structure) shows the test arriving before the fix; the test is keyed to the user-visible symptom in the bug report, not to an internal symptom the fix happens to flip. A diff where the test and the fix arrive in the same blob with no failing-test evidence fails this criterion. A test that asserts only against the fix's new code path (and would not have been red against the broken version) also fails — it does not demonstrate the root cause.

### G2. A root-cause statement with cited evidence is attached to the Beads task.

The Beads task carries a comment in the shape "X did Y because W; evidence: Z" — with actual evidence: a trace excerpt, a `git bisect` SHA, log lines, a profiler output, a network HAR. A prose hand-wave without a citation fails this criterion. The evidence must name the specific input, code path, or contract that flips behavior.

Evidence that satisfies it: a Beads comment (or a section in `notes`) on the task that cites at least one concrete artefact — file:line of the bad code, a deploy log timestamp, a database row that triggered the failure. "Probably a race condition" with no trace fails.

### G3. The fix rationale contains no speculative language.

The `decisions` array, `llm_observations`, and the Beads notes describe the fix in declarative terms: "the X path now does Y; this makes Z hold because W". Hedging language — "might", "should fix", "probably", "in theory", "I think this works" — fails this criterion. Speculation in the fix description is the strongest signal that the root cause is not understood and the patch is a guess.

Evidence that satisfies it: a reviewer can read the fix rationale and predict, without running the test, whether the patch addresses the documented root cause. If the rationale leaves the reviewer guessing, this criterion fails.

### G4. The fix flips the failing test from G1.

The test added in G1 fails on the pre-fix code and passes on the post-fix code — exactly. A test that was already passing before the fix and continues to pass is not regression coverage; it is a smoke check. The fix must be the change that turns the test from red to green.

Evidence that satisfies it: a side-by-side run against the parent commit and the fix commit shows the same test transitioning from FAIL to PASS. If the test passes on both sides, G4 fails (and likely G1 fails too — the test does not encode the root cause).

approval — the satisfied verdict binds the same change set`, and the durable record carries

a summary that discusses the mechanism will trip it. Cheap mitigation if that ever ships:

**1. Framing lock-in.** In round 2 I tested the `iteration` field across five hostile values
and correctly found each reads unbound *alone*. I framed the field as an **injection** vector
— "can this forge a binding?" — got a safe answer, and closed the line. R2-F3 asks the
opposite direction: "can this make a record *unreadable*, and what does that do to
supersession?" Same input, different question. A safe answer closes an **input**, not a
**field**. That is the real reason a second model caught it; a deliberately re-framed second
pass by the same model would have too.

**2. I should have found `qa.md` 6f myself.** In round 2 I reviewed the approve/rubric
interaction and formed a view on whether the script should refuse, without citing the
document that *governs* whether the script may refuse. The implementer found it and it
decided the question. Reviewing a policy boundary without reading the policy is the error.

title: worktree-sweep: document that --apply deletes IGNORED files with the worktree (and why --ignored is not the fix)
description:
QA finding R1-F1 (medium) from the C1b review. Documentation only — the code is correct.

## What was reproduced

Gate 3 is `git status --porcelain`, which excludes **ignored** files. In an
independent fixture, a worktree whose only extra content was gitignored
(`.env` containing `SECRET=hunter2`, plus `ignored-stuff/cache.bin`) read
CLEAN, passed all six gates, and `--apply` DESTROYED the `.env`.
`git worktree remove` without `--force` does not count ignored files as
making a tree unclean, so nothing downstream stops it.

This is exactly `git worktree remove` semantics and it needs a manual
`--apply`; containment confines it to `.claude/worktrees/<name>`; dry-run is
the default and prints every path first; and committed work always survives
because branches are not deleted. So the behaviour is defensible — what is
missing is that the header comment and `docs/HOOKS.md` describe gate 3 as
"clean = `git status --porcelain` empty (untracked included)", which reads
as "nothing will be lost".

## Why the obvious tightening is NOT the fix

`git status --porcelain --ignored` returns `!! .claude/` even in a correctly
gitignored repo, because gate 6's own evidence file
(`.claude/.qa-tracking/current-task`) is itself ignored. Adding `--ignored`
to gate 3 would make the primary evidence path never yield a removal —
self-defeating. Measured, not assumed.

## Asked for

One sentence in `.claude/scripts/worktree-sweep.sh`'s gate-3 header line and
in the `docs/HOOKS.md` helper-table row: ignored content (`.env`, build
caches) inside a swept worktree is deleted with it, and `--ignored` is
deliberately not used because the gate-6 evidence file is itself ignored.

Optionally also R1-F4 (low): a git-LOCKED worktree that passes all six gates
is printed as REMOVABLE by the dry run, but `--apply` gets a git refusal
(REMOVE-FAILED, rc=1, directory survives — fail-safe). Reading the `locked`
marker from `git worktree list --porcelain` would let the dry run report a
`locked` keeper reason instead of promising a removal git will refuse.

And R1-F5 (info): `SWEEP_ROOT` is only required non-empty and not literally
`/`; it is never checked to be inside `CURRENT_TOP`. `contained_in
"$CURRENT_TOP" "$SWEEP_ROOT"` is one more line of a guard already written.

+#### Worktree-aware gate scoping (Phase V4, epic `3mg`)
+
+The tri-model loop runs implementers and reviewers in parallel worktrees, so
+the gate must evaluate work where it happened. Three production transcript
+scenarios are closed.
+
+- **Approval records name the approving checkout.** `qa-gate.sh approve`
+  appends a `worktree=<tok>` token — the checkout's git toplevel, spaces
+  `%20`-encoded so it stays ONE space-terminated token, `none` off a git
+  checkout (never omitted: a stable grammar is what lets a reader tell "no
+  worktree recorded" from "recorded but unresolvable"). Every approve path
+  reaches the one record writer, including the F1 fast path and both
+  audited bypasses:
+
+  ```
+  QA-GATE APPROVED change_set_hash=<h> reviewed_by=<id> worktree=<tok> at <ts>: <summary>
+  ```
+
+  Token ORDER is the compatibility contract: every addition since llh.18
+  goes AFTER the hash token, space-separated, so the v3.5
+  `change_set_hash` and V3 `reviewed_by` captures extract identical values
+  from the old and new shapes. Pinned by a differential META
+  (`review-separation.test.sh` 4.2b) that strips the `WORKTREE-TOKEN`
+  sentinels from a copy of `qa-gate.sh`, approves with it, and runs BOTH
+  reader expressions over BOTH record shapes plus a renamed token.
+- **The Stop hook resolves cross-worktree approvals**
+  (`WORKTREE-RESOLUTION` in `verify-before-stop.sh`). This closes the
+  deadlock where a review performed in a linked worktree recorded a
+  change-set hash the primary checkout could never reproduce, so its Stop
+  hook reported "qa-approved label present but no change-set-bound
+  approval record matches" forever. Only on the path that already blocks,
+  the hook tries the recorded token first (O(1)), then `git worktree list
+  --porcelain`, skipping the current checkout, capped at 16 candidates. A
+  candidate releases only when ALL of these are positively proven: it is a
+  worktree of this repo (symlink-resolved `--git-common-dir`, never a
+  toplevel string compare); its persisted `impact-report-<tid>.json`
+  carries a `change_set_hash` that a real approval record on the task
+  cites; its own `git status` minus its own `gate-baseline` is empty (no
+  post-approval drift there); every reviewable path in THIS checkout is
+  inside that report's approved file set, compared repo-relative; and the
+  V3 `review-check.sh gate` predicate is still clean (same audited
+  `[review bypass:` escape) — so a finding recorded after the approval
+  re-arms this path too.
+- **Record-based, not recomputed.** `approve` truncates
+  `changed-files.txt` in the approving checkout, so a recompute there
+  returns the sha256 of the empty list — the approved hash is
+  unreproducible even in the worktree that produced it. The resolution
+  therefore reads the persisted impact report, which survives approve. The
+  L2 spec asserts both the truncation and the diverging recompute, so
+  making that truncation conditional fails loudly instead of silently
+  disabling resolution.
+- **Read-only, fail-closed, no MCP boot.** File reads plus `git worktree
+  list` / `git rev-parse` / `git status` / `jq`. Nothing is written
+  anywhere (the spec re-checksums the candidate worktree), and the
+  code-graph MCP server is never booted (asserted with an armed canary
+  that is proved live on an `enter` and silent on every Stop). Any error,
+  unreadable artifact, or ambiguity falls through to the block. A removed
+  worktree is named in the block reason ("bound in worktree `<path>`,
+  which no longer exists"); otherwise the reason gains "(checked N
+  worktree(s))".

+## 🧠 The tri-model workflow
+
+Three classes of agent, three model lanes, one gate. `.claude/model-roles`
+maps each **role** to a selection **strategy**, and `model-select.sh`
+re-resolves every lane at session start — so each class auto-adopts the
+newest model in its own tier without anyone editing a version string.
+
+| Role | Agents | Strategy | Resolves to |
+|------|--------|----------|-------------|
+| `orchestrator` | `orchestrator` | `top` | the resolver's single best pick — the newest, most capable family in your account listing |
+| `implementer` | `backend`, `frontend`, `devops` | `opus-class` | the newest `claude-opus-*` model listed, falling back to `top` when your account lists none |
+| `reviewer` | `qa`, `grader`, `judge` | `top` | the top pick for the fresh-context Claude review path; the optional external lane routes the review turn to Sol via Codex when connected |
+
+The model each lane lands on is **resolver output, not configuration**.
+Read the live mapping with `bash .claude/scripts/model-select.sh roles`
+(prints `role  strategy  resolved-id`), see it in the statusline
+(`orch:… impl:… rev:…`, collapsing to the single-model shape only when all
+three lanes resolved to the same id *and* the reviewer lane is `claude`),
+and override with `/workflow-model`. Setting every role to `top` in
+`.claude/model-roles` reproduces the v3.5 single-model behavior exactly.
+
+### Nobody signs off on their own work
+
+This is a gate rule, not a prompt. The change-set-hash-bound `qa-approved`
+record is the **only** release credential, and since v4.0.0
+`qa-gate.sh approve` refuses (exit 4) unless both hold:
+
+1. the task carries a **review artifact** whose `reviewer_identity` differs
+   from every implementer recorded for that task — `subagent-start.sh`
+   writes `IMPLEMENTER: role=<backend|frontend|devops> task=<id>` at spawn,
+   so identity is captured by the harness, not self-declared; and
+2. **zero findings** at or above the review's `risk_threshold` are still
+   open.
+
+`verify-before-stop.sh` re-runs the *same* predicate before releasing the
+Stop hook, because findings can arrive after an approval and a write-once
+record cannot know about them. Both ends call one counter
+(`review-check.sh gate`) — there is no second implementation of it, and no
+second way to release. A missing or unrunnable counter fails **closed** at
+both ends.
+
+### Arbitration
+
+When the implementing specialist disputes a finding, exactly two things
+clear it and nothing else does:
+
+- **Resolve with evidence** — `qa-gate.sh resolve-finding <tid> <finding-id>
+  --fix '<ref>' --test '<ref>' '<summary>'`. Both refs are mandatory; this
+  is the evidence-before-fix protocol as a record.
+- **Arbitrate** — `qa-gate.sh arbitrate <tid> <finding-id>
+  <overrule|sustain> '<rationale>'`. `overrule` clears the gate count;
+  `sustain` keeps the finding OPEN as the audit record of a dispute that was
+  heard and upheld — which is what makes an overrule mean anything.
+
+Arbitration is the **orchestrator's** job: the reviewer and the author are
+the two parties, so only the third can adjudicate, and the rationale must
+cite both positions.
+
+### The optional Sol lane
+
+The reviewer role runs on the plugin's own fresh-context Claude path by
+default, for free. Install and register the OpenAI Codex CLI at user scope
+and the same artifact comes from Sol instead — a second model family reading
+the same diff. It is strictly optional and purely advisory: it writes no
+labels, records no approval, the review turn is manual and cost-confirmed,
+and it meters your own OpenAI account. With Codex absent, failed, or timed
+out, the workflow is byte-identical (proved by a degradation spec, not
+asserted). Setup, billing, model tracking, and troubleshooting:
+[`docs/CODEX_SETUP.md`](docs/CODEX_SETUP.md).
+
+### Effort policy
+
+Three layers, and none of them is a model-version pin:
+
+- **Floor** — `.claude/settings.json` `effortLevel: "xhigh"`, the highest
+  value that field accepts. Persists across sessions.
+- **Session level** — `.claude/effort-verdict`, currently **`max`**,
+  recorded by the A/B interference test in
+  [`docs/EFFORT-AB-TEST.md`](docs/EFFORT-AB-TEST.md). Launch a working
+  session with `make session`, which reads the first non-comment line of
+  that file and execs `claude --effort <verdict>` (defaulting to `max` when
+  the file is missing or empty).
+- **Ceiling** — every agent's frontmatter `effort: max`, the durable
+  per-agent maximum.
+
+Honest limit: `ultracode` is session-only and its hook-environment proxy is
+`xhigh`, so a session launched at ultracode is indistinguishable from a
+plain xhigh session from inside the plugin. SessionStart therefore *detects
+and warns* when the live effort, the floor, and the verdict disagree —
+detect-and-warn is the ceiling here, and the plugin does not claim to
+enforce the session level.

### 5. LESSONS.md
# Lessons ledger

Production lessons learned the hard way. Each entry is a single-sentence
takeaway, traceable to the Beads task(s) that produced it, with the date
it was first recorded.

Add new entries via `.claude/scripts/lessons.sh add '<lesson>' --source <task-id>`
— never hand-edit. The helper deduplicates by normalized text (case- and
whitespace-insensitive), so repeating an existing lesson appends the new
source to that entry rather than creating a duplicate. The only legitimate
hand-edit is pruning entries that are no longer relevant.

The orchestrator reads this file during planning (see `orchestrator.md`),
the grader (Phase A) receives it in the grading packet, and the QA agent
proposes additions at epic close. Treat it as the institutional memory the
plugin runs against, not a static reference doc.

## Lessons

- Parallel agents in the same working tree contaminate each other's branches; concurrent specialists require worktree isolation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Boundary mocks must use the real downstream producer's shape, pinned via a fixture extracted from the producer's spec — never invented. A mock that feeds `body.error` so the test can assert `body.error` is circular and proves nothing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- New agent files must be registered in .claude-plugin/plugin.json agents[] in the same commit that creates them; an unregistered agent is silently invisible to the SDK — no error surfaces. Guard: agents-manifest-parity test. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Subagents cannot spawn other subagents in the Claude Code runtime (docs: sub-agents page — Agent(agent_type) has no effect in subagent definitions). Any agent-spawning step must live at the root conversation level; design multi-agent handoffs as root-orchestrated relays, never nested spawns. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Interface examples must be executed by a test: the Makefile's own usage string (make test-live FIXTURE=node-react-auth) was broken for the one fixture whose spec file is scenario-named — nothing ever ran the documented invocation. Caught only when a paid live run failed fast. Any CLI surface a doc or help text advertises needs an L2 assertion that executes that exact invocation (dry-run mode where the real one costs money). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Prose cues do not reliably drive subagent tool usage: across 4 live runs, QA made zero impact_of calls even when its task prompt contained the exact tool name, alias, target symbols, and invariant name. When a workflow REQUIRES a tool call, make it mechanical (compute it where calls are reliable — e.g. orchestrator at root — and pass results down), don't prompt for it. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n6d --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Rendered fixture installs pin plugin scripts at render time: the fixture's verify-before-stop.sh predated the cue fix by one commit, so a hook-template change never reached the live run. Script-level fixes require re-rendering fixture installs (or a version check at run start) before they affect live validation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.10 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Never run QA review concurrently with a builder in the same working tree: QA attributed the parallel C.2 task's freshly-written files to the C.1 task under review and blocked it for scope creep. Sequence QA after all writers finish, or give builders worktree isolation (orchestrator.md 4b exists for exactly this). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.1 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Manifest-declared assets must be presence-asserted at the install target: install.sh's hardcoded agent list silently dropped grader.md for two releases (v3.2.0-v3.3.0) — every fresh install was missing the rubric loop's grader while the repo's own tests stayed green. Glob-copy from the manifest source of truth and add an installer-spec presence assertion for every plugin.json agents[]/commands[] entry. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Bash functions invoked via $(...) command substitution run in a subshell — any variable they set is lost to the parent. The manual-adopt gate in model-select.sh was dead code for exactly this reason (set at :341, read at :500, never connected). When a helper must signal the caller, encode the signal in its stdout contract (e.g. a MANUAL<tab> prefix) and parse it at every call site; add a META-TEST that strips the parse to prove the gate is load-bearing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-3fn --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- A security hardening that breaks the workflow is worse than the documented residual it closes. Fail-closing prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh on ambiguous identity assumed every specialist carries a probeable identity, but this runtime does not surface subagent_name to PreToolUse hooks — so it denied legitimate specialist Write/Edit (a P0-class regression) to close a P2 Bash-write vector. When a guard depends on an identity signal the runtime may not provide, prefer fail-OPEN plus the structural guard (the orchestrator's omitted Write/Edit tools, which IS airtight) and document the residual; never trade a P2 for a P0. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.19 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Line-number-anchored mutation META-tests are brittle: any comment or line addition above the anchor silently un-lands the NR==<n>/sed -n Np target, turning a load-bearing META into a no-op (or a spurious failure). Anchor mutation METAs to a unique TEXT pattern in the target line, not an absolute line number. (3 instances re-anchored across verify-before-stop/escalation-binding specs this session.) <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.20 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Effort A/B (cnz.2): verdict max — ultracode showed ZERO orchestration interference in a 39-min time-boxed arm (no Workflow-layer engagement, all spawns on-list, plugin flow faithful), contradicting the pre-registered criterion-4-failure expectation; max still wins because ultracode pins the model at its xhigh proxy (below max) with no observed benefit, and criteria 2-3 went unverified under the time-box. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-cnz.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Paid-run cost estimates must be derived from measured token flows, not guessed: the EFFORT-AB-TEST runbook estimated $10-20 for both arms; actual was ~$206 API-equivalent (~$169 arm B full + ~$37 arm A time-boxed) — a 10x error that forced a mid-test re-confirmation gate. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-cnz.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Regional/transient model exclusions in .claude/model-ranking go stale silently: a `!family` line added for a temporary outage keeps masking downstream behavior (here it collapsed the v4 top==opus-class role split onto Opus for six weeks) long after the outage clears. Gate every un-exclusion on FRESH spawn evidence (subagent-spawns.log + effort-ab logs naming the model), not memory, and date the rationale + rollback line in the file. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-bi3.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Files rewritten by a helper (awk/mv, e.g. workflow-model-apply.sh) instead of the Edit/Write tool never land in changed-files.txt, so the QA impact hash and the change-set-bound approval only cover Edit-tracked files. When a task mutates files via a helper, QA must verify those files explicitly via git diff (not rely on the impact report alone). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-bi3.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- MCP registration scope is a mechanical contract, not etiquette: a detection probe reads ONE config path (top-level .mcpServers of ~/.claude.json for user scope), so local/project-scope registrations are silently invisible — verify the probe read path when writing setup docs and make wrong-scope the first troubleshooting row. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Published CLI config references can lag the shipped binary: verify accepted values against the binary own introspection surface (e.g. codex debug models) rather than the docs or trial-and-error, and record the lag in the operator doc so editors re-verify. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Run suites via their canonical make targets: a bare runner invocation (npx vitest run) includes guarded paid live specs whose fail-closed API-key errors masquerade as regressions; the CI-shaped target (make test-e2e-unit) is the comparable baseline. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- When a change adds a second independent gate to a release path, every META that isolates the FIRST gate must be re-seeded to satisfy the new gate so it still fails for its own reason (jio.1 MM18 migration is the template). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.1 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- A deliberate second implementation of a gate predicate (shell counter + TS live invariant) is only a second witness if QA diffs the two rule-by-rule against the writer grammars at their emit sites — the jio.2 parity review caught a greedy-sed vs first-match token-selection divergence (gqp) that every test suite had missed. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- Trace-anchor refreshes that add a skip must be legitimized against the on-disk cassette (jq has(field) on the replay file), not the spec comment — and the pin must assert skipped+pass+exact detail so a future re-record flips loud instead of silently inheriting the skip. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- State a gate writes for its own bookkeeping can destroy the evidence a later check needs: qa-gate.sh approve truncates changed-files.txt, so re-running impact-report.sh --hash-only in the approving checkout returns the empty-list hash and can never reproduce the approved hash — even there. Any cross-checkout or after-the-fact verification must read the PERSISTED record (impact-report-<tid>.json, which survives approve), never recompute; assert the destruction in the test so making it conditional fails loudly instead of silently disabling the reader. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-3mg.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->

# Default rubric (v1)

Applies to every task graded under the rubric-grader QA loop (spec Phase A). Each criterion below is a pass/fail assertion the grader evaluates from the grading packet: `bd show` for the task, the SPEC doc, the diff of the files listed in `.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt`, the F7 completion contract returned by the specialist, and `LESSONS.md`. One-line justification per criterion. No numeric score theater — pass or fail.

The criteria are intentionally short and checkable. Where the criterion needs context (boundary-mock fidelity, F7 fields), the "Evidence that satisfies it" line names the artefact the grader looks at.

## Criteria

### C1. Behavior matches the task description and SPEC.

The shipped diff implements the behavior the task description asks for, and matches the goal + acceptance criteria stated in the attached SPEC doc (read via `bd_doc_read(task_id, name="spec")`). Out-of-scope behavior the SPEC explicitly excludes is NOT in the diff.

Evidence that satisfies it: a 1-2 sentence walk-through that maps every user-visible behavior in the SPEC to a code path in the diff (or to a deliberate, documented deferral in the F7 `decisions` array). A diff that adds plausibly-related behavior the SPEC does not name fails this criterion — that is scope creep.

### C2. Tests added exercise user behavior rather than implementation.

Where the diff introduces new behavior, the diff also introduces tests that assert against the user-visible contract (return shape, side effects, error envelope, accessibility role, status code) rather than against the implementation's private structure (function-name mocking, line-coverage gymnastics, internal control-flow assertions).

Evidence that satisfies it: at least one test in the diff that would still pass if the implementation were rewritten while keeping the user contract identical. A test that asserts only against private symbols, internal call counts, or framework boilerplate fails this criterion.

### C3. The F7 completion contract carries all six fields with substantive `llm_observations`.

The specialist's structured completion payload includes `task_id`, `files_changed`, `tests_added`, `decisions`, `blockers`, and `llm_observations`. `llm_observations` is non-trivial narrative — what surprised the specialist, what was unclear, what they noticed and did not act on. A boilerplate one-liner like "no observations" fails this criterion (principle 9: `llm_observations` is mandatory and substantive).

Evidence that satisfies it: each of the six fields is present and the `llm_observations` paragraph is the kind of thing a human engineer would say at a stand-up.

### C4. No unrelated scope in the diff.

Every file the specialist touched serves the task. Drive-by refactors, formatting churn on untouched lines, and "while I'm here" cleanups that exceed the task brief fail this criterion — they should be filed as paired follow-up Beads tasks instead.

Evidence that satisfies it: the diff's file list maps cleanly to the SPEC's deliverables; any incidental change is either trivial (one-line typo fix) or explicitly justified in the `decisions` array.

### C5. J26 modules relevant to the diff are addressed.

Where the diff touches a domain covered by the J26 security taxonomy (SECRETS, INJECTION, AUTH, CONFIG, DEPS, AI, MOBILE, DATA — see `docs/AGENTS.md`), the diff demonstrates that the relevant modules were considered. Untouched J26 domains are out of scope.

Evidence that satisfies it: the `decisions` array (or the SPEC) names which J26 modules apply, and the diff shows defences in those modules (input validation at the trust boundary, parameterised queries, narrow CORS, audited logging, etc.). A diff that touches user input handling without naming INJECTION fails this criterion.

### C6. Docs updated where behavior changed.

When the diff changes user-visible behavior, the documentation that describes that behavior is updated in the same change. This includes `CHANGELOG.md`, README sections, `docs/*.md`, command help text, and SPEC docs the diff renders out of date.

Evidence that satisfies it: a docs-only file in `files_changed` paired with each behavioral change, or a deliberate `decisions` entry stating why a doc deferral is correct (e.g. an internal refactor that ships without user-visible change). A behavioral change that ships with no doc update and no deferral note fails this criterion.

### C7. Boundary-mock fidelity (LESSONS.md lesson 2).

When the diff introduces or modifies mocks of boundaries the project does not control (third-party HTTP APIs, external SDKs, system calls, message-bus payloads), every such mock derives its shape from a fixture extracted from the real downstream producer's spec (OpenAPI, proto file, SDK source, vendor docs). The fixture's source is cited in a comment, the `decisions` array, or `llm_observations`.

**Automatic needs_revision:** circular pass-through assertions are an immediate fail. A mock that feeds `body.error` so a test can assert `body.error` proves nothing — it tests the test's own setup, not the production behavior. Cite `LESSONS.md` lesson 2 in the justification.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new boundary mock points at a fixture file (`.fixtures/`, `__fixtures__/`, `testdata/`) carrying a snapshot of the producer's payload, and the fixture has a comment naming the source (URL, commit, SDK version). Tests assert against the producer's contract, not against the mock's own input.

# DevOps rubric (v1)

Applied additionally when the task carries the `devops` label. Default criteria still apply; these add domain-specific checks pulled from `.claude/agents/devops.md`. The leverage is default + bugfix — these are the few devops-specific failure modes that recur.

## Criteria

### D1. Scripts are idempotent and re-runnable.

Install, uninstall, hook, and CI scripts in the diff produce the same end state when run twice in a row. A second run of `install.sh` does not double-write hooks, clobber prior settings, or fail because a directory already exists. A migration script that exits non-zero on its second run fails this criterion.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new script uses `mkdir -p`, conditional inserts, and idempotent label operations (`bd label add` returns success if already present); the `decisions` array documents any deliberately non-idempotent step (e.g. a one-shot data migration) and pairs it with a guard (lock file, completion sentinel) so a re-run is detected.

### D2. Graceful degradation on missing optional tools.

When the diff depends on an optional tool (gitleaks, shellcheck, a particular bd version, a specific CI runner image), the missing-tool path is handled: log a structured warning, fall back to a safe default, exit zero where the workflow allows. A hook that exits non-zero because `gitleaks` is not installed fails this criterion — that is not a developer-machine-portable failure mode.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new tool dependency is probed (`command -v tool >/dev/null`); the fallback path is documented in the script comments and tested at L1; the `decisions` array names the dependency and its installation hint.

### D3. No new permission prompts; autonomy preserved.

The diff does not add `permissions.deny` rules to `settings.json`, narrow specialist tool lists below the broad allow set, or introduce any user-facing approval step the plugin previously ran without. Principle 3 of the v3 plan is "full autonomy, no permission prompts" — every deny rule becomes a future approval prompt and breaks the workflow.

Evidence that satisfies it: a diff of `.claude/settings.json` shows only `permissions.allow` expansions, never `deny`; specialist tool frontmatter is unchanged or expanded; the `decisions` array calls out any new tool the broadened allow set covers.

### D4. Secrets and PII stay out of source, logs, and history.

Hardcoded API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, committer emails, and PII are absent from the diff. Logs that the diff adds redact sensitive fields before writing. A commit that introduces an `.env` file with values, a personal email address in a script header, or unredacted PII in a log line fails this criterion (extends C5 / SECRETS + DATA).

# V5 live-validation results (d2j.2) — 2026-07-26

Both cost-confirmed live validations PASSED. Core claim demonstrated LIVE: **Sol's presence changes review quality but never the release mechanics.**

## Validation (a) — Codex/Sol CONNECTED (real gpt-5.6-sol)
- Subject: a 6-line `count_files(dir)` bash helper with a disputable issue; spec scopes it to visible, space-free internal paths.
- `codex-review.sh` drove the REAL Codex MCP server (gpt-5.6-sol, read-only sandbox, no subagent spawning) → exit 0, valid artifact `reviewer_identity=sol-codex reviewer_model=gpt-5.6-sol verdict=findings`.
- Sol produced a genuine, high-quality finding R1-F1 (medium): `ls | wc -l` undercounts directories with hidden entries (subtler than the planted unquoted-variable issue).
- Gate flow through the REAL scripts: `review-record` → `review-check gate` = BLOCK (`independent:true` [sol-codex ≠ backend implementer], `open_findings:1`, `unresolved_findings`, exit 4) → orchestrator `arbitrate R1-F1 overrule` (interpretive dispute: "entries" scoped to visible per contract) → `review-check gate` = PASS (`open_findings:0`, exit 0).

## Validation (b) — Codex ABSENT (feature-detect → Claude lane)
- `codex-detect` with an empty config → `reviewer_lane=claude` (absence correctly detected).
- Twin subject task d2j.2.1; Claude-lane artifact `reviewer_identity=qa-claude reviewer_model=claude-fable-5`, SAME schema (validate-artifact ok).
- IDENTICAL gate flow: `review-record` → gate BLOCK (`independent:true`, `open_findings:1`, `unresolved_findings`) → `arbitrate overrule` → gate PASS (`open_findings:0`).

## Comparison (the audited claim)
Reviewer identity/model/quality differ (sol-codex/gpt-5.6-sol vs qa-claude/claude-fable-5); the gate DECISIONS are byte-identical: both block on the open at-threshold finding, both release only after arbitration. Confirms the offline `reviewer-lane-degradation.sh` result under REAL conditions.

## IMPORTANT FINDING — Codex model configuration (operator-scope)
The real Sol lane initially FAILED (codex-review exit 5). Root cause, diagnosed via direct JSON-RPC probes:
1. `~/.codex/config.toml` pinned `model = "gpt-5.2-codex"`, which the ChatGPT-account backend REJECTS: `400 invalid_request_error: "The 'gpt-5.2-codex' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."`
2. codex-cli 0.145.0 mcp-server mode does NOT honor the registration's `-m gpt-5.6-sol` flag, nor `-c model=…` override — `config.toml`'s `model` is authoritative.
- FIX APPLIED (reversible; backup at `~/.codex/config.toml.bak-d2j2`): set `model = "gpt-5.6-sol"`. Re-probe resolved to gpt-5.6-sol and succeeded. **codex-review.sh / codex-detect themselves are CORRECT** — transport, `.result.content[].text` extraction, and graceful exit-5 degradation all worked; the failure was purely the operator's model pin. Filed as a follow-up + docs/CODEX_SETUP.md troubleshooting update.

Real Codex/Sol spend was SMALL: a handful of short gpt-5.6-sol calls (connectivity probes + one review of a ~6-line diff), each seconds long, metered to the operator's OpenAI/ChatGPT account. No paid Claude sub-agents were spawned for the validations themselves (the gate flow used the shell scripts directly). Well under the $20–80 estimate.

title: F1 doc-only fast path has an off-repo blast-radius blind spot: docs carrying copy-pasteable commands that write outside the repo auto-approve unreviewed
description:
Systemic gap surfaced by gl6 (v4.1 U1). The F1 doc-only fast path in verify-before-stop.sh auto-approves any change set whose paths are all doc-only (is_doc_only_path matches *.md), on the reasoning that "no reviewable source changed". But a markdown file can carry copy-pasteable shell commands whose blast radius is entirely OUTSIDE the repo — gl6 added a recipe that rewrites the operator global ~/.codex/config.toml, and QA reproduced a HIGH data-loss path in it (unguarded cp + truncate-before-read: 115 bytes -> 22, zero backup) that F1 would have auto-approved unseen. No in-repo test can see that failure class; the orchestrator only caught it by deliberately routing the change past F1.

Options to consider: (a) exempt from F1 any doc whose diff adds fenced shell blocks containing redirects/cp/mv/rm targeting paths outside the repo (grep-level heuristic, fail toward review); (b) maintain a small denylist of operator-facing docs (CODEX_SETUP.md, STAGING_QA.md when it lands, README install sections) that never take the fast path; (c) leave F1 as-is and make it a documented orchestrator responsibility. Evidence: gl6 QA record (HIGH + 2 MEDIUM + 2 LOW, all in commands that write or back up operator config); the lesson "Doc-only is not low-risk" filed from the same cycle.

# Preserved from gl6 (v4.1 U1) — sandboxed operator-config safety harness

Extracts the pin-rewrite function VERBATIM from docs/CODEX_SETUP.md (awk on the fenced block) rather than from a copy that could drift, then runs failure arms in a sandboxed HOME. Old recipe: SAFE=4 UNSAFE=2. Fixed recipe: SAFE=7 UNSAFE=0. Arms: control, dir 500, file 000, dir-ro+file-writable, file 444, no config, no ~/.codex.

Directly reusable for dkp (F1 doc-only blast-radius blind spot) — this is the shape of test that would have caught the HIGH before F1 auto-approved it.

## verify-doc.sh
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Extracts codex_pin_newest VERBATIM from docs/CODEX_SETUP.md and runs it under
# QA's failure arms in a sandboxed HOME. Never touches the real ~/.codex.
set -u
DOC=/Users/edk0/Desktop/projects/claude-workflow-plugin/docs/CODEX_SETUP.md
WORK=/tmp/gl6-harness
PASS=0; FAIL=0

# --- extract the function from the doc, stripping the 3-space code-block indent ---
awk '/^   codex_pin_newest\(\) \{/,/^   \}$/ { sub(/^   /,""); print }' "$DOC" > "$WORK/extracted.sh"
if ! grep -q '^codex_pin_newest() {' "$WORK/extracted.sh"; then
    echo "EXTRACTION FAILED — function not found in doc"; exit 1
fi
echo "--- extracted $(grep -c '' "$WORK/extracted.sh") lines from the doc ---"
bash -n "$WORK/extracted.sh" || { echo "EXTRACTED FUNCTION IS NOT VALID BASH"; exit 1; }
zsh -n "$WORK/extracted.sh" || { echo "EXTRACTED FUNCTION IS NOT VALID ZSH"; exit 1; }
echo "syntax: valid in bash AND zsh"

# --- stub codex: deterministic, offline, no cost ---
mkdir -p "$WORK/stubbin"
cat > "$WORK/stubbin/codex" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
case "$1 $2" in
  "debug models") printf '{"models":[{"slug":"gpt-5.6-sol","visibility":"list","priority":1}]}\n' ;;
  "doctor --json")
      cfg="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/config.toml"
      m=$(grep -m1 '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/.*=[[:space:]]*"\{0,1\}//; s/"$//')
      printf '{"checks":{"config.load":{"details":{"model":"%s"}}}}\n' "${m:-<default>}" ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac
STUB
chmod +x "$WORK/stubbin/codex"
export PATH="$WORK/stubbin:$PATH"

REALISTIC='# my codex config
model = "gpt-5.2-codex"
model_reasoning_effort = "max"
network_access = true

[tools]
web_search = true   # first-party search
view_image = true

[profiles.legacy]
model = "gpt-4.1-old"
'

arm() {  # arm <name> <setup> <expect: intact|rewritten|created|abort>
    local name="$1" setup="$2" expect="$3"
    local SB; SB=$(mktemp -d -t gl6doc.XXXXXX) || return
    local CODEXDIR="$SB/.codex" CFG="$SB/.codex/config.toml"
    mkdir -p "$CODEXDIR"; printf '%s' "$REALISTIC" > "$CFG"
    local before; before=$(cksum < "$CFG" | awk '{print $1}')
    local bb; bb=$(wc -c < "$CFG" | tr -d ' ')

    "$setup" "$CODEXDIR" "$CFG"

    local out rc
    out=$( HOME="$SB" bash -c "source '$WORK/extracted.sh'; codex_pin_newest" 2>&1 ); rc=$?

    chmod u+rwx "$CODEXDIR" 2>/dev/null; chmod u+rw "$CFG" 2>/dev/null
    local ab as baks verdict
    if [ -e "$CFG" ]; then ab=$(wc -c < "$CFG"|tr -d ' '); as=$(cksum < "$CFG"|awk '{print $1}')
    else ab=MISSING; as=MISSING; fi
    baks=$(ls "$CODEXDIR"/config.toml.bak-* 2>/dev/null | grep -c . | tr -d ' ')
    local strays; strays=$(ls "$CODEXDIR"/config.toml.new.* 2>/dev/null | grep -c . | tr -d ' ')

    case "$expect" in
      intact)  [ "$as" = "$before" ] && verdict="SAFE (bytes intact)" || verdict="DATALOSS" ;;
      created) if [ "$ab" = MISSING ]; then verdict="UNSAFE (nothing created)"
               elif [ "$(cat "$CFG")" = 'model = "gpt-5.6-sol"' ]; then verdict="SAFE (fresh pin)"
               else verdict="UNSAFE (unexpected content)"; fi ;;
      abort)   if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then verdict="UNSAFE (proceeded)"
               elif [ -e "$CODEXDIR" ]; then verdict="UNSAFE (created dir)"
               else verdict="SAFE (aborted cleanly)"; fi ;;
      *)       if [ "$ab" = MISSING ]; then verdict="DATALOSS"
               elif ! grep -q '^model = "gpt-5.6-sol"$' "$CFG"; then verdict="DATALOSS (no pin)"
               elif ! diff -q <(printf '%s' "$REALISTIC" | grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=') \
                              <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$CFG") >/dev/null; then
                    verdict="PARTIAL (non-model line moved)"
               else verdict="SAFE (correctly rewritten)"; fi ;;
    esac
    [ "$strays" != 0 ] && verdict="$verdict +STRAY-TEMP"

    printf '%-32s rc=%-3s %4s -> %-8s baks=%-2s %s\n' "$name" "$rc" "$bb" "$ab" "$baks" "$verdict"
    [ -n "$out" ] && printf '%36s%s\n' "" "$(printf '%s' "$out" | tail -1)"
    case "$verdict" in SAFE*) PASS=$((PASS+1));; *) FAIL=$((FAIL+1));; esac
    chmod -R u+rwx "$SB" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$SB"
}

s_control()      { :; }
s_dir_500()      { chmod 500 "$1"; }
s_file_000()     { chmod 000 "$2"; }
s_no_config()    { rm -f "$2"; }
s_no_codexdir()  { rm -rf "$1"; }
s_dir_ro_file_w(){ chmod 555 "$1"; chmod 666 "$2"; }
s_immutable_cfg(){ chmod 444 "$2"; }

echo "==== docs/CODEX_SETUP.md §5 codex_pin_newest, verbatim ===="
arm "control (all writable)"       s_control       rewritten
arm "~/.codex mode 500"            s_dir_500       intact
arm "config mode 000"              s_file_000      intact
arm "dir read-only, file writable" s_dir_ro_file_w intact
arm "config read-only (444)"       s_immutable_cfg rewritten
arm "no config.toml"               s_no_config     created
arm "no ~/.codex at all"           s_no_codexdir   abort
printf -- '---- SAFE=%d  UNSAFE=%d ----\n' "$PASS" "$FAIL"

# --- idempotence + the step-2 verification pair, on a clean sandbox ---
echo
echo "==== idempotence + step-2 verification ===="
SB=$(mktemp -d -t gl6idem.XXXXXX); mkdir -p "$SB/.codex"
printf '%s' "$REALISTIC" > "$SB/.codex/config.toml"
HOME="$SB" bash -c "source '$WORK/extracted.sh'; codex_pin_newest" >/dev/null 2>&1
A=$(cksum < "$SB/.codex/config.toml" | awk '{print $1}')
sleep 1
HOME="$SB" bash -c "source '$WORK/extracted.sh'; codex_pin_newest" >/dev/null 2>&1
B=$(cksum < "$SB/.codex/config.toml" | awk '{print $1}')
[ "$A" = "$B" ] && echo "idempotent: second run byte-identical" || echo "NOT IDEMPOTENT"
echo "resulting config:"; sed 's/^/    /' "$SB/.codex/config.toml"

echo "-- step 2 verification pair against a GOOD config --"
CFG="$SB/.codex/config.toml"; BAK=$(ls -1 "$CFG".bak-* 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
HOME="$SB" codex doctor --json | jq -r '.checks["config.load"].details.model'
if diff <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$BAK") \
        <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$CFG"); then
   echo "    OK: every non-model line survived"; fi

echo "-- step 2 verification pair against a WIPED config (must FAIL loudly) --"
printf 'model = "gpt-5.6-sol"\n' > "$CFG"        # simulate the R1-F1 disaster
echo "    pin check says: $(HOME="$SB" codex doctor --json | jq -r '.checks["config.load"].details.model')"
if diff <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$BAK") \
        <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$CFG") >/dev/null; then
   echo "    diff check: PASSED - BAD, it cannot see the wipe"
else
   echo "    diff check: FAILED as intended - the wipe IS detected"; fi
rm -rf "$SB"
```

## harness.sh
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# gl6 R1-F1 reproduction + regression harness.
# Runs the §5 step-2 recipe under QA's failure arms in a sandboxed CODEX_HOME.
# NEVER touches the real ~/.codex. Arg 1: "old" (current doc text) or "new" (fixed).
#
# Each arm reports: config bytes before -> after, whether a .bak exists, and a
# VERDICT of SAFE (operator bytes intact or correctly rewritten) / DATALOSS.

set -u
VARIANT="${1:-old}"
PASS=0; FAIL=0

REALISTIC_CONFIG='# my codex config
model = "gpt-5.2-codex"
model_reasoning_effort = "max"
network_access = true

[tools]
web_search = true   # first-party search
view_image = true

[profiles.legacy]
model = "gpt-4.1-old"
'

# ---- the recipe under test, OLD (current doc text, lines 279-284) ----
recipe_old() {
    local CFG="$1" NEWEST="$2"
    local BAK="$CFG.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
    cp "$CFG" "$BAK"
    { printf 'model = "%s"\n' "$NEWEST"
      grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$BAK"; } > "$CFG"
}

# ---- the recipe under test, NEW (guarded backup + same-dir temp + atomic mv) ----
recipe_new() {
    local cfg="$1" newest="$2" bak new
    [ -n "$newest" ] || { printf 'could not resolve a slug - aborting\n' >&2; return 1; }
    [ -d "$(dirname "$cfg")" ] || { printf 'no %s - run codex login first\n' "$(dirname "$cfg")" >&2; return 1; }
    if [ -e "$cfg" ]; then
        bak="$cfg.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
        cp -p "$cfg" "$bak" || { printf 'backup failed - aborting, %s untouched\n' "$cfg" >&2; return 1; }
    else
        bak=""
    fi
    new=$(mktemp "$cfg.new.XXXXXX") || { printf 'cannot create temp beside %s - aborting\n' "$cfg" >&2; return 1; }
    { printf 'model = "%s"\n' "$newest"
      [ -n "$bak" ] && grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$bak"
      :; } > "$new" || { rm -f "$new"; printf 'build failed - aborting, %s untouched\n' "$cfg" >&2; return 1; }
    if [ -n "$bak" ]; then
        if ! diff -q <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$bak") \
                     <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$new") >/dev/null; then
            rm -f "$new"; printf 'a non-model line moved - aborting, %s untouched\n' "$cfg" >&2; return 1
        fi
    fi
    mv "$new" "$cfg" || { rm -f "$new"; printf 'install failed - aborting, %s untouched\n' "$cfg" >&2; return 1; }
}

run_recipe() { if [ "$VARIANT" = old ]; then recipe_old "$@"; else recipe_new "$@"; fi; }

# arm <name> <setup-fn> <expectation: intact|rewritten>
arm() {
    local name="$1" setup="$2" expect="$3"
    local SB; SB=$(mktemp -d -t gl6arm.XXXXXX) || return
    local CODEXDIR="$SB/.codex" CFG
    mkdir -p "$CODEXDIR"; CFG="$CODEXDIR/config.toml"
    printf '%s' "$REALISTIC_CONFIG" > "$CFG"
    local before_bytes before_sum
    before_bytes=$(wc -c < "$CFG" | tr -d ' '); before_sum=$(cksum < "$CFG" | awk '{print $1}')

    "$setup" "$CODEXDIR" "$CFG"          # apply the failure condition

    local out rc
    out=$( { run_recipe "$CFG" "gpt-5.6-sol"; } 2>&1 ); rc=$?

    chmod u+rwx "$CODEXDIR" 2>/dev/null; chmod u+rw "$CFG" 2>/dev/null   # regain access to inspect
    local after_bytes after_sum baks verdict
    if [ -e "$CFG" ]; then
        after_bytes=$(wc -c < "$CFG" | tr -d ' '); after_sum=$(cksum < "$CFG" | awk '{print $1}')
    else
        after_bytes=MISSING; after_sum=MISSING
    fi
    baks=$(ls "$CODEXDIR"/config.toml.bak-* 2>/dev/null | grep -c . | tr -d ' ')

    if [ "$expect" = intact ]; then
        if [ "$after_sum" = "$before_sum" ]; then verdict="SAFE (bytes intact)"; else verdict="DATALOSS"; fi
    elif [ "$expect" = created ]; then
        # No config existed. Correct outcome: a fresh file holding just the pin.
        if [ "$after_bytes" = MISSING ]; then verdict="UNSAFE (nothing created)"
        elif [ "$(cat "$CFG")" = 'model = "gpt-5.6-sol"' ]; then verdict="SAFE (fresh pin created)"
        else verdict="UNSAFE (unexpected content)"; fi
    elif [ "$expect" = abort ]; then
        # No ~/.codex. Correct outcome: refuse, create nothing.
        if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then verdict="UNSAFE (proceeded anyway)"
        elif [ -e "$CODEXDIR" ]; then verdict="UNSAFE (created a config dir)"
        else verdict="SAFE (aborted, nothing created)"; fi
    else
        # rewritten: model line must be new AND every non-model line preserved
        if [ "$after_bytes" = MISSING ]; then verdict="DATALOSS"
        elif ! grep -q '^model = "gpt-5.6-sol"$' "$CFG"; then verdict="DATALOSS (no new pin)"
        elif ! diff -q <(printf '%s' "$REALISTIC_CONFIG" | grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=') \
                       <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$CFG") >/dev/null; then
            verdict="PARTIAL (non-model lines changed)"
        else verdict="SAFE (correctly rewritten)"; fi
    fi

    printf '%-34s rc=%-3s %5s -> %-8s baks=%-3s %s\n' \
        "$name" "$rc" "$before_bytes" "$after_bytes" "$baks" "$verdict"
    [ -n "$out" ] && printf '%38s%s\n' "" "msg: $(printf '%s' "$out" | head -1)"
    case "$verdict" in SAFE*) PASS=$((PASS+1));; *) FAIL=$((FAIL+1));; esac
    chmod -R u+rwx "$SB" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$SB"
}

s_control()      { :; }
s_dir_500()      { chmod 500 "$1"; }
s_file_000()     { chmod 000 "$2"; }
s_no_config()    { rm -f "$2"; }
s_no_codexdir()  { rm -rf "$1"; }
s_dir_ro_file_w(){ chmod 555 "$1"; chmod 666 "$2"; }

printf '==== VARIANT: %s ====\n' "$VARIANT"
arm "control (all writable)"        s_control       rewritten
arm "~/.codex mode 500"             s_dir_500       intact
arm "config mode 000"               s_file_000      intact
arm "dir read-only, file writable"  s_dir_ro_file_w intact
arm "no config.toml"                s_no_config     created
arm "no ~/.codex at all"            s_no_codexdir   abort
printf -- '---- %s: SAFE=%d  UNSAFE=%d ----\n' "$VARIANT" "$PASS" "$FAIL"
```

# Preserved from gl6 round 3 — table-driven backup-SELECTION test

Extracts the changed lines VERBATIM from docs/CODEX_SETUP.md (grep -F on shipped text, awk on the function), 8/8 PASS. Covers the class behind 3 of the 4 gl6 findings: backup-glob selection vs listing.

Arms: correct selection against a mixed dated/non-dated set in bash AND zsh; silent-and-empty when only non-dated backups exist (note: 2>/dev/null does NOT suppress a zsh glob failure — zsh fails the glob before ls runs, so the error is the shell's, not ls's); the OLD construct still reproducing the bug as a control; §9 cleanup sparing hand-made backups; guard ordering + hostile-stub behaviour.

Directly reusable for dkp — this is a doc-embedded-command test that no in-repo suite would otherwise run.

## verify-r2.sh
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# R2 verification: (1) the changed §5 step-2 selection line, extracted VERBATIM from
# the doc, under a mixed backup set; (2) the §9 narrowed rm; (3) the reordered guard.
# Sandboxed HOME throughout. Never touches the real ~/.codex.
set -u
DOC=/Users/edk0/Desktop/projects/claude-workflow-plugin/docs/CODEX_SETUP.md
PASS=0; FAIL=0
ck() { if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then printf '  PASS  %s\n' "$1"; PASS=$((PASS+1));
       else printf '  FAIL  %s\n          want=[%s]\n          got =[%s]\n' "$1" "$3" "$2"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); fi; }

# ---------- 1. extract the step-2 BAK selection line verbatim from the doc ----------
SEL=$(grep -F 'BAK=$( { ls -1 "$CFG".bak-[0-9]*; } 2>/dev/null | tail -1 )' "$DOC" | sed 's/^ *//')
[ -n "$SEL" ] || { echo "EXTRACTION FAILED: step-2 selection line not found in doc"; exit 1; }
echo "extracted from doc: $SEL"
echo

echo "==== R2-F1: selection with a mixed backup set (both shells) ===="
for sh in bash zsh; do
  T=$(mktemp -d); CFG="$T/config.toml"; : > "$CFG"
  : > "$CFG.bak-20260726-215700"; : > "$CFG.bak-20260728-010000"
  : > "$CFG.bak-d2j2"; : > "$CFG.bak-old"; : > "$CFG.bak-before-upgrade"
  got=$($sh -c "CFG='$CFG'; $SEL; basename \"\$BAK\"" 2>&1)
  ck "$sh: picks newest DATED backup, not .bak-d2j2/-old/-before-upgrade" \
     "$got" "config.toml.bak-20260728-010000"
  rm -rf "$T"
done

echo
echo "==== R2-F1: silent + empty when only NON-dated backups exist (both shells) ===="
for sh in bash zsh; do
  T=$(mktemp -d); CFG="$T/config.toml"; : > "$CFG"; : > "$CFG.bak-d2j2"
  got=$($sh -c "CFG='$CFG'; $SEL; printf '[%s]' \"\$BAK\"" 2>&1)
  ck "$sh: empty and SILENT (no zsh 'no matches found' leak)" "$got" "[]"
  rm -rf "$T"
done

echo
echo "==== R2-F1: the old construct would have failed these (control) ===="
T=$(mktemp -d); CFG="$T/config.toml"; : > "$CFG"
: > "$CFG.bak-20260728-010000"; : > "$CFG.bak-d2j2"
old=$(bash -c "CFG='$CFG'; BAK=\$(ls -1 \"\$CFG\".bak-* 2>/dev/null | tail -1); basename \"\$BAK\"")
printf '  old construct picked: %s  %s\n' "$old" \
  "$([ "$old" = config.toml.bak-d2j2 ] && echo '<- the bug, still reproduces' || echo '?')"
rm -rf "$T"

# ---------- 2. §9 narrowed rm ----------
echo
echo "==== §9 cleanup deletes only THIS DOC's backups ===="
RM=$(grep -F 'rm -f ~/.codex/config.toml.bak-[0-9]* ~/.codex/config.toml.before-restore' "$DOC")
[ -n "$RM" ] || { echo "  FAIL: narrowed rm line not found in doc"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }
if [ -n "$RM" ]; then
  T=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$T/.codex"
  cd "$T" || exit 1
  : > "$T/.codex/config.toml"
  : > "$T/.codex/config.toml.bak-20260728-010000"
  : > "$T/.codex/config.toml.bak-20260726-215700"
  : > "$T/.codex/config.toml.bak-d2j2"
  : > "$T/.codex/config.toml.bak-my-precious"
  : > "$T/.codex/config.toml.before-restore"
  HOME="$T" bash -c "$RM" 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    /'
  left=$(ls -1 "$T/.codex" | grep -v '^config.toml$' | sort | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ *$//')
  ck "hand-made backups survive; dated ones + before-restore are gone" \
     "$left" "config.toml.bak-d2j2 config.toml.bak-my-precious"
  cd /; rm -rf "$T"
fi

# ---------- 3. the reordered -d guard is reachable ----------
echo
echo "==== reordered guard: fires when ~/.codex is absent, BEFORE any catalog call ===="
D=/tmp/gl6-harness; mkdir -p "$D"
awk '/^   codex_pin_newest\(\) \{/,/^   \}$/ { sub(/^   /,""); print }' "$DOC" > "$D/fn2.sh"
grep -q '^codex_pin_newest() {' "$D/fn2.sh" || { echo "  FAIL: function not extractable"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }
bash -n "$D/fn2.sh" && zsh -n "$D/fn2.sh" && echo "  syntax: valid in bash AND zsh"
# guard must be the FIRST guard, before the `codex debug models` call
gl=$(grep -n '\-d "${cfg%/\*}"' "$D/fn2.sh" | cut -d: -f1)
cl=$(grep -n 'codex debug models' "$D/fn2.sh" | cut -d: -f1)
ck "the -d guard precedes the catalog call (line $gl < $cl)" \
   "$([ "${gl:-999}" -lt "${cl:-0}" ] && echo yes || echo no)" "yes"
# and it actually fires with a stub codex that WOULD have created the dir
mkdir -p "$D/stub2"
cat > "$D/stub2/codex" <<'S'
#!/bin/bash
mkdir -p "${HOME}/.codex"      # hostile stub: creates the dir, as QA believed codex does
[ "$1 $2" = "debug models" ] && printf '{"models":[{"slug":"x","visibility":"list","priority":1}]}\n'
exit 0
S
chmod +x "$D/stub2/codex"
T=$(mktemp -d)   # no .codex inside
out=$(PATH="$D/stub2:$PATH" HOME="$T" bash -c "source '$D/fn2.sh'; codex_pin_newest" 2>&1); rc=$?
ck "guard fires even against a stub that creates ~/.codex (rc=1)" "$rc" "1"
ck "…and creates nothing" "$([ -e "$T/.codex" ] && echo created || echo clean)" "clean"
printf '    msg: %s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$out" | head -1)"
rm -rf "$T"

printf -- '\n==== R2 verification: PASS=%d FAIL=%d ====\n' "$PASS" "$FAIL"
[ "$FAIL" -eq 0 ]
```

# Preserved from gl6 round 4 (Sol's five HIGH findings) — six operator-config failure classes

repro-r3.sh + verify-r3.sh cover, with the OLD constructs retained as live controls (29/29 PASS, controls still reproduce their bugs so the arms are proven sensitive):

1. **glob breadth** — bak-[0-9]* is one digit then ANYTHING; matched bak-20260728-personal and bak-9-keep, both in an irreversible rm kill list.
2. **filter-status propagation** — a trailing `:` made the group exit 0 on a failed grep; process substitutions hide exit status from diff.
3. **mirror-oracle tautology** — with grep stubbed to exit 127, validation compared a 5-line baseline to a 1-line wiped candidate and reported IDENTICAL (would install).
4. **TOML-semantic damage** — a line filter deleted a model= line from inside a triple-quoted block; the mirror said IDENTICAL. Fixed by PREVENTION (refuse + defer to hand edit), since no line-filter oracle can attribute damage inside a multiline string.
5. **partial-write atomicity** — measured, not assumed: macOS cp does NOT truncate up front, but a FIFO short source left the destination holding 7 bytes of partial content while exiting 0. (A 60MB kill test was inconclusive — APFS clones instantly.)
6. **jq null trap** — jq -r returns the 4-character string `null`, which passes -n and would have registered -m null.

Also recorded: `codex --strict-config doctor` is the correct placement (top-level flag; `codex doctor --strict-config` errors with unexpected argument), and a $STAMP variable holding a digit class does NOT glob-expand in zsh.

No in-repo test can currently see any of these six — their blast radius is the operator home directory. This is dkp's core evidence.

## repro-r3.sh
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Reproduction of Sol's five R3 HIGH findings against the CURRENT doc constructs.
# Sandboxed throughout; never touches the real ~/.codex.
set -u
export PATH="/Users/edk0/.nvm/versions/node/v22.21.1/bin:$PATH"
hr() { printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$1"; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- R3-F1
hr 'R3-F1: is `bak-[0-9]*` a "dated-only" pattern? (doc asserts it is)'
T=$(mktemp -d); CFG="$T/config.toml"; : > "$CFG"
: > "$CFG.bak-20260728-010000"          # a real dated backup this doc creates
: > "$CFG.bak-20260728-personal"        # Sol's counterexample 1
: > "$CFG.bak-9-keep"                   # Sol's counterexample 2
: > "$CFG.bak-d2j2"                     # letter-initial (already excluded)
echo "files:"; ls -1 "$T" | grep bak | sed 's/^/    /'
echo "what the doc's [0-9]* glob actually matches:"
for f in "$CFG".bak-[0-9]*; do printf '    %s\n' "$(basename "$f")"; done
picked=$( { ls -1 "$CFG".bak-[0-9]*; } 2>/dev/null | tail -1 )
printf 'selection picks: %s\n' "$(basename "$picked")"
[ "$(basename "$picked")" != "config.toml.bak-20260728-010000" ] \
  && echo "  F1 CONFIRMED (selection): picks a NON-dated file over the dated one" \
  || echo "  selection happened to be right here, but see the match list above"
echo "and the narrowed rm would delete:"
for f in "$CFG".bak-[0-9]*; do printf '    %s\n' "$(basename "$f")"; done
echo "  F1 CONFIRMED (rm): operator files bak-20260728-personal / bak-9-keep are in the kill list"
echo
echo "proposed strict pattern (8 digits - 6 digits, anchored by glob semantics):"
STAMP='[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]'
for f in "$CFG".bak-$STAMP; do printf '    %s\n' "$(basename "$f")"; done
rm -rf "$T"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- R3-F5
hr 'R3-F5: does jq -r emit the literal string "null" for a missing field?'
echo '  empty catalog:'
v=$(printf '{"models":[]}' | jq -r '.models | map(select(.visibility=="list")) | sort_by(.priority) | .[0].slug')
printf '    value=[%s]  length=%s  passes [ -n ]? %s\n' "$v" "${#v}" "$([ -n "$v" ] && echo YES || echo no)"
[ "$v" = "null" ] && echo "    F5 CONFIRMED: 4-char string 'null' passes -n => function would install model = \"null\""
echo '  missing slug key:'
v2=$(printf '{"models":[{"visibility":"list","priority":1}]}' | jq -r '.models | map(select(.visibility=="list")) | sort_by(.priority) | .[0].slug')
printf '    value=[%s]  passes [ -n ]? %s\n' "$v2" "$([ -n "$v2" ] && echo YES || echo no)"
echo '  moved surface (no .models at all):'
v3=$(printf '{"catalog":[]}' | jq -r '.models | map(select(.visibility=="list")) | sort_by(.priority) | .[0].slug' 2>&1 | head -1)
printf '    value=[%s]\n' "$v3"
echo '  with the proposed `// empty`:'
v4=$(printf '{"models":[]}' | jq -r '.models | map(select(.visibility=="list")) | sort_by(.priority) | .[0].slug // empty')
printf '    value=[%s]  passes [ -n ]? %s\n' "$v4" "$([ -n "$v4" ] && echo YES || echo no)"
echo '  and what step 3 would propagate into the registration:'
v5=$(printf '{"checks":{"config.load":{"details":{}}}}' | jq -r '.checks["config.load"].details.model')
printf '    NEWEST=[%s] -> claude mcp add ... -m "%s"\n' "$v5" "$v5"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- R3-F2a
hr 'R3-F2a: does the trailing `:` mask a grep failure in the build group?'
T=$(mktemp -d); B="$T/bak"; N="$T/new"
printf 'model = "old"\nmodel_reasoning_effort = "max"\nnetwork_access = true\n' > "$B"
# simulate grep failing (unreadable input => grep exits 2)
chmod 000 "$B"
{ printf 'model = "%s"\n' "NEW"
  [ -n "$B" ] && grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$B"
  :; } > "$N" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
chmod 644 "$B"
printf '  group exit status: %s  (0 means "build succeeded")\n' "$rc"
printf '  resulting candidate: %s line(s): %s\n' "$(grep -c '' "$N")" "$(tr '\n' '|' < "$N")"
[ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && echo "  F2a CONFIRMED: grep failed, group reported success, candidate is model-line-only"
echo '  without the trailing `:` the status propagates:'
{ printf 'model = "%s"\n' "NEW"; chmod 000 "$B"; grep -v '^x' "$B"; } > "$N" 2>/dev/null; rc2=$?
chmod 644 "$B"; printf '    status=%s\n' "$rc2"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- R3-F2b
hr 'R3-F2b: are process-substitution failures invisible to diff?'
T2=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$T2/fakebin"
# a PATH with no grep at all
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 127\n' > "$T2/fakebin/grep"; chmod +x "$T2/fakebin/grep"
B2="$T2/bak"; N2="$T2/new"
printf 'model = "old"\nmodel_reasoning_effort = "max"\nnetwork_access = true\n[tools]\nweb_search = true\n' > "$B2"
printf 'model = "NEW"\n' > "$N2"     # the WIPED candidate: only the model line
PATH="$T2/fakebin:$PATH" bash -c '
  if diff -q <(grep -v "^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=" "'"$B2"'") \
              <(grep -v "^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=" "'"$N2"'") >/dev/null
  then echo "  validation said: IDENTICAL (would install)"
  else echo "  validation said: DIFFER (would refuse)"; fi'
echo "  baseline has $(grep -c '' "$B2") lines; candidate has $(grep -c '' "$N2") line — they are NOT identical"
echo "  F2b CONFIRMED if the validation said IDENTICAL above: broken grep => false success on a wiped config"
rm -rf "$T2"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- R3-F3
hr 'R3-F3: does the line filter damage a TOML multiline string, undetectably?'
T3=$(mktemp -d); CFG3="$T3/config.toml"
cat > "$CFG3" <<'TOML'
model = "gpt-5.2-codex"
model_reasoning_effort = "max"

[tools]
notes = """
how to pin:
model = "some-slug"
that is the line that matters
"""
web_search = true
TOML
echo "  original parses as valid TOML? (real binary, --strict-config)"
CODEX_HOME="$T3" codex doctor --json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '"    status=\(.checks["config.load"].status) model=\(.checks["config.load"].details.model)"'
NEW3="$T3/new"
{ printf 'model = "gpt-5.6-sol"\n'; grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$CFG3"; } > "$NEW3"
echo "  lines deleted from inside the multiline string:"
diff "$CFG3" "$NEW3" | grep '^<' | sed 's/^/    /'
echo "  does the MIRROR validation notice? (same filter on both sides)"
if diff -q <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$CFG3") \
            <(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*model[[:space:]]*=' "$NEW3") >/dev/null
then echo "    validation said IDENTICAL -> F3 CONFIRMED: string content silently deleted, undetected"
else echo "    validation said DIFFER"; fi
echo "  proposed detector: does the file contain a multiline delimiter?"
grep -q '"""' "$CFG3" && echo '    YES ("""), so the recipe should refuse and defer to a hand edit'
rm -rf "$T3"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- R3-F4
hr 'R3-F4: does a direct `cp` overwrite leave the destination partial on failure?'
T4=$(mktemp -d)
dd if=/dev/urandom of="$T4/src" bs=1m count=60 2>/dev/null
printf 'PRECIOUS ORIGINAL CONFIG\n' > "$T4/dest"
before=$(cksum < "$T4/dest" | awk '{print $1}')
cp "$T4/src" "$T4/dest" & pid=$!
sleep 0.05; kill -9 $pid 2>/dev/null; wait $pid 2>/dev/null
after_bytes=$(wc -c < "$T4/dest" | tr -d ' '); src_bytes=$(wc -c < "$T4/src" | tr -d ' ')
after=$(cksum < "$T4/dest" | awk '{print $1}')
printf '  dest was 24 bytes; src is %s bytes; after killed cp dest is %s bytes\n' "$src_bytes" "$after_bytes"
if [ "$after" != "$before" ] && [ "$after_bytes" != "$src_bytes" ]; then
  echo "  F4 CONFIRMED: destination left PARTIAL — original content gone, copy incomplete"
elif [ "$after" != "$before" ]; then
  echo "  F4 CONFIRMED (weaker): original destroyed (cp completed before the kill)"
else
  echo "  not reproduced this run; cp opens dest O_TRUNC before reading, so partial state is inherent"
fi
echo "  proposed atomic form (temp beside target + mv), same interruption:"
printf 'PRECIOUS ORIGINAL CONFIG\n' > "$T4/dest2"
b2=$(cksum < "$T4/dest2" | awk '{print $1}')
( t=$(mktemp "$T4/dest2.restore.XXXXXX") && cp -p "$T4/src" "$t" && mv "$t" "$T4/dest2" ) & pid=$!
sleep 0.05; kill -9 $pid 2>/dev/null; wait $pid 2>/dev/null
a2=$(cksum < "$T4/dest2" | awk '{print $1}')
[ "$a2" = "$b2" ] && echo "    dest2 INTACT (original preserved; only a stray temp may remain)" \
                  || echo "    dest2 changed — atomic form did not hold"
ls "$T4" | grep -c restore | sed 's/^/    stray temps: /'
rm -rf "$T4"

printf '\n=== reproduction pass complete ===\n'
```

Observed during QA of wg6, unrelated to that change set (neither wg6 nor lv4 touches `.claude/mcp/code-graph-mcp/`).

EVIDENCE
  full L2 run 1  -> Specs: Total 40, Passed 39, Failed 1 (code-graph-mcp.sh)
                    Assertions: Passed 1927, Failed 1
  isolated re-run (`run.sh --filter code-graph-mcp`) -> 29/29, 0 failed
  full L2 run 2  -> Specs: Total 40, Passed 40, Failed 0
                    Assertions: Passed 1928, Failed 0

The failing assertion's text was lost — the run-1 capture was truncated by the reviewer's
own `tail -60`. Re-running the full suite is what produced the green, so the specific leg
is not yet known. Reproducing will require a full run with complete output retained.

HOST CONTEXT: two stale `node ./.claude/mcp/code-graph-mcp/bin/code-graph-mcp.js`
processes were alive at review time, started Sunday ~11PM and Monday ~12AM (days old,
predating the review session), both at ~0.0% CPU. Left running deliberately rather than
perturb the host mid-review, so their contribution is UNCONFIRMED — it is a hypothesis,
not a diagnosis.

WHY IT MATTERS: the spec boots real node MCP servers and asserts a lazy index build
(`code-graph-mcp-2: pre-build health reports status=uninitialized` then `healthy`). Boot
or build timing under 40-spec load is the obvious suspect class. It is fixture-isolated
(`$SAMPLE/.claude/.code-graph/index.db` under `mk_fixture`), so cross-run index state is
NOT the explanation.

COST: a flaky spec turns a full L2 run red for reasons unrelated to whatever diff is under
review, which is exactly the "guard that fails for unrelated reasons gets muted" failure
mode `lv4` documents for the doctor's non-mutation assertion.

SUGGESTED FIRST STEP: run the full suite N times retaining complete output, capture the
failing assertion text, then decide between a boot-readiness wait, a retry, or an explicit
precondition assertion. Do not "fix" it by loosening the assertion.

title: 0.2 Make the QA-gate escalation cap binding
description: Live transcript showed ESCALATION: Iteration 7 (>= 3) still looping with full-suite re-runs. Add escalated state: qa-escalated label + J21 comment at first cap hit, skip-suite while escalated, auto-defer (qa-deferred) on next choiceless Stop, deferred=allow in verify-before-stop, SessionStart surfaces deferred, runner-vs-assertion failure classification. Spec 0.2.
notes:
IN PROGRESS: spec 0.2 implementation landed locally — escalation cap binding now in place. Awaiting QA review.

KEY DELIVERABLES:
- qa-gate.sh gains `choose <approve|continue|tech-debt|defer> <task-id> <note>` subcommand recording a J21 decision (comment + label/counter side effects) — keeps the audit trail thin.
- qa-gate.sh enter clears qa-deferred/qa-escalated + wipes per-iteration cache on every enter so a deferred task naturally resumes normal gating.
- wipe_iteration_state wipes new escalation cache files (last-test-rc, last-failed-checks, last-runner, escalation-posted).
- verify-before-stop.sh: new state machine.
  * Reads qa-deferred → allow Stop (single audited escape valve, principle 6).
  * Reads qa-escalated; at ITER > MAX_ITERATIONS + 1 → auto-defer (qa-deferred label + audit comment + allow).
  * While qa-escalated set, skip suite re-run; reuse cached FAILED_CHECKS + runner.
  * At first cap hit (ITER reaches MAX_ITERATIONS), set qa-escalated + post J21 ESCALATED comment exactly once (idempotent via marker file).
  * Failure classification: classify_test_failure() distinguishes runner (exit 126/127, "command not found", "Cannot find module", testcontainers TypeError, etc.) from assertion. Runner path leads with "Test suite failed to run (environment/runner issue — fix the environment before changing code)".
- session-start.sh: surfaces qa-deferred tasks ABOVE qa-pending with a banner naming the auto-defer flow.

DOCS:
- docs/WORKFLOW.md label table gained qa-escalated, qa-deferred, qa-gate-entered, qa-blocked (full lifecycle).
- docs/HOOKS.md got a new "Escalation State Machine (spec 0.2)" subsection plus updated qa-gate.sh entry mentioning the `choose` subcommand.

TESTS (all green):
- L1: .claude/scripts/tests/qa-gate-choose.test.sh — 30 assertions covering usage errors, all four choose branches, and re-enter clearing qa-deferred/qa-escalated.
- L2: .claude/tests/component/specs/escalation-binding.sh — 42 assertions:
  * Iterations 1-3 invoke the test shim (count climbs to 3) and iter 3 sets qa-escalated + posts one comment.
  * Iter 4 blocks with escalation wording WITHOUT re-running the suite (shim count stays at 3).
  * Iter 5 auto-defers (qa-deferred set, {} envelope, qa-pending preserved).
  * Subsequent Stop with qa-deferred allows immediately.
  * Re-enter clears qa-deferred/qa-escalated and the next Stop re-runs the suite (count to 4).
  * Runner-vs-assertion classification: exit 127 lands on "Test suite failed to run"; exit 1 with assertion output lands on "Tests failing".
  * Counter reset on active-task change: TID2/TID3 hold independent counter files.
  * ACCEPTANCE invariants: suite NOT re-run after cap (npm=3 across iters 4+5) AND qa-deferred recorded by iter 5.
  * META-TEST: mutating bump_iteration to always return 1 makes the cap-assertion fail (qa-escalated never set, npm count exceeds 3).

VERIFICATION:
- make lint  -> clean (shellcheck 0.11.x).
- make test  -> Total: 3 Passed: 3 Failed: 0 (L1).
- make test-all  -> Specs: 17 / Passed: 17 / Failed: 0; Assertions: 295/0.
- L2 escalation-binding.sh standalone summary: Assertions: Passed: 42 Failed: 0.

KEY DECISIONS:
- Auto-defer threshold: ITER > MAX_ITERATIONS + 1 (i.e., ITER >= MAX+2). Iter 3 = cap-hit (block + escalate). Iter 4 = one more escalated Stop (block, no suite re-run). Iter 5 = auto-defer. Matches the prompt's L2 walkthrough exactly.
- The `choose` subcommand is single-shot: approve delegates to cmd_approve, continue resets state, tech-debt calls tech-debt.sh add --bd-task, defer sets qa-deferred. Comments + labels are the record (principle 7).
- Per-task escalation cache files live alongside iteration-count.<task>. Naming: last-test-rc.<task>, last-failed-checks.<task>, last-runner.<task>, escalation-posted.<task> (idempotency marker). All wiped by wipe_iteration_state.
- classify_test_failure() is conservative: only patterns that are unambiguous runner-infra signals classify as runner; everything else stays "assertion" so we never mis-direct an assertion failure to "fix the environment".

FILES CHANGED:
- .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh
- .claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh
- .claude/scripts/session-start.sh
- docs/WORKFLOW.md
- docs/HOOKS.md

FILES CREATED:

- .claude/tests/component/specs/escalation-binding.sh

NEW SUBCOMMANDS:
- qa-gate.sh choose <approve|continue|tech-debt|defer> <task-id> <note> [tech-debt: severity file:line effort]

LLM OBSERVATIONS:
- Spec text was internally inconsistent about auto-defer timing: high-level spec said "one more Stop" (iter 4), but the prompt's L2 walkthrough explicitly assigned iter 4 to "blocks with J21 wording" and iter 5 to "auto-defers". Followed the prompt's explicit walkthrough since it is the testable acceptance — iter 4 provides a warning shot, iter 5 acts.

title: L2 test-lib hygiene: dead net_required_or_skip + node-dependent assertion outside its HAVE_NODE guard (C0c R1-F3/F4)
description:
Two low-severity QA findings from the C0c independent review.

**R1-F3 — dead code in a shared lib.** `net_required_or_skip()` was added to `.claude/tests/component/lib/fixture.sh:143-196` (~30 lines with comments) and has **zero callers** anywhere in the repo; `installer-target-functional.sh` uses only `net_available()`. It is also untested. Either wire it to a spec that needs it, or drop it — a shared-lib function with no caller drifts silently.

**R1-F4 — a node-dependent assertion escapes its guard.** `.claude/tests/component/specs/installer-target-functional.sh:895-896`:

```
assert_eq "installer-target-functional 7g: 9 passed, 0 failed after the METAs" \
    "9 0" "$(jq -r '"\(.passed) \(.failed)"' "$M7G" ...)"
```

sits **outside** the `if [ "$HAVE_NODE" = "yes" ]` guard that correctly wraps the adjacent exit-code assertion at 891-894. `workflow-doctor.sh:658` hard-requires `node` and `npm` for the `deps` check, so on a node-less host `deps` FAILs, the guarded assertion is skipped as designed, and this unguarded one fails with `8 1`. That contradicts the spec's own header promise that "a node-less host still gets the C0c regression coverage".

Not reachable on this machine or in CI (both have node), which is why it passed 40/40 twice.

**Also worth considering (R1-F6, info):** `make lint` covers `.claude/scripts/*.sh`, `.claude/scripts/tests/*.sh`, `.claude/tests/mutation/*.sh` and `.claude/tests/mutation/lib/*.sh` — but **not** `.claude/tests/component/specs/*.sh` or `.claude/tests/component/lib/*.sh`. The new 968-line spec is therefore unlinted by the project's own lint target. Run manually it is clean at `shellcheck -S warning`; `fixture.sh` carries 2 pre-existing SC2164s (identical count in HEAD, not introduced by C0c).
acceptance_criteria:
- `net_required_or_skip` either has a caller and a test, or is removed.
- `installer-target-functional.sh:895-896` is inside the same `HAVE_NODE` guard as 891-894; verified by running the spec with node/npm masked off PATH.
- Optional: `make lint` extended to cover `.claude/tests/component/{specs,lib}/*.sh`.

title: workflow-manifest.sh hardening: mirror install.sh mcp dir-only semantics (R1-F1) + propagate find failures in scans (R1-F2)
description:
Two LOW-severity findings from the independent QA review of U0.1 (REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 r1, reviewer qa-claude, both below the high risk threshold — advisory, non-blocking; recorded on claude-workflow-plugin-gzc).

**R1-F1 — latent mcp surface divergence** (.claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh:306 vs install.sh:538)
`scan_tree workflow ".claude/mcp" ...` walks every regular file under .claude/mcp (node_modules/.tmp pruned), while install.sh iterates only directories (`for mcp_dir in .../*/`). A loose top-level file ever added directly under .claude/mcp/ would be enumerated by generate but never shipped by install.sh, making classify emit a permanent copy-new for a file the installer cannot deliver. Vacuous today: no such file exists in the repo or the v3.5.0 tag (verified during review). Fix direction: scan per-subdirectory of .claude/mcp to mirror the dir-only loop exactly, or add a paired warning comment at BOTH sites (the same-commit pairing discipline the file header already declares). Add an L1 assertion: a loose file at .claude/mcp/top-level.txt in the synthetic tree must NOT appear in generate output (or must, if the installer is changed to ship it — pick one and pin it).

**R1-F2 — find failures invisible in process substitution** (.claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh:249 and :282)
`find ... -print0 2>/dev/null` runs inside `< <(...)`; a find failure (e.g. unreadable subdirectory mid-walk) is discarded — set -e never sees it, and the affected rows are silently omitted. The unreadable-FILE case, by contrast, fails loud with zero stdout and is pinned by L1 Section 4c. This weakens the all-or-nothing manifest contract for pathological inputs only (generate sources are release archives/checkouts; the frozen-table cmp would catch omissions on the shipped surface). Fix direction: propagate find's status via an exit-marker file (e.g. `find ... || : > "$WORK_DIR/find-failed"` then die after the loop when the marker exists), or drop 2>/dev/null and assert stderr-clean in tests. Add an L1 case with an unreadable SUBDIRECTORY (chmod 000 dir, same root-skip probe as Section 4c).

Both fixes must keep the determinism contract (byte-identical output on the happy path) and re-run the frozen-table reproduction check (`git archive v3.5.0 | ... | cmp - manifests/v3.5.0.sha256`) since U0 later specs byte-compare generate output.
acceptance_criteria:
- R1-F1 closed one of two ways, decided and documented: scan mirrors install.sh's dir-only mcp loop (with L1 loose-file assertion), or paired warning comments landed at both sites in the same commit.
- R1-F2: a find failure during scan_flat/scan_tree aborts generate/classify with a named error and ZERO bytes on stdout (same contract as hash failure); L1 unreadable-subdirectory case added with root-skip probe.
- Happy-path output byte-identical to pre-change (frozen v3.5.0 table still cmp-clean against tag regeneration).
- Full make test + make lint green.
