title: write_gate_baseline reports FAILURE and writes no baseline when the working tree is CLEAN (spurious sync-error every session)
description:
Found while writing the U0.6 upgrade-gate-compat L2 spec (claude-workflow-plugin-ehv). REPORTED, NOT FIXED, per evidence-before-fix — the fix is its own reviewed change. NOT a gate-release gap: it fails in the SAFE direction (no baseline == nothing subtracted == every later change reads as new == block). What it costs is a false alarm and one lost cleanup step.

ROOT CAUSE
.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh, write_gate_baseline(). The brace group that composes the baseline file ends with:

    [ -n "$status_out" ] && printf '%s\n' "$status_out"
  } > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || { rm -f "$tmp"; log_sync_error "...could not write $tmp..."; return 1; }

The group's exit status is the status of its LAST command. When `git status --porcelain` is empty (clean tree), `status_out` is empty, `[ -n "" ]` returns 1, `&&` short-circuits, and the group exits 1 — even though every write succeeded. The `||` arm then deletes the just-written tmp file, logs a failure, and returns 1.

REPRODUCTION (deterministic, ~10s)

    cd /tmp && rm -rf gbclean && mkdir gbclean && cd gbclean
    git init -q && git config user.email t@t.t && git config user.name t
    printf 'x\n' > a.txt
    printf '.claude/.qa-tracking/\n.claude/scripts/\n' > .gitignore
    git add -A && git commit -qm base
    mkdir -p .claude/scripts .claude/.qa-tracking
    for s in <plugin>/.claude/scripts/*.sh; do ln -sf "$s" ".claude/scripts/$(basename "$s")"; done
    git status --porcelain | wc -l          # -> 0  (CLEAN)
    CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=$PWD bash .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh baseline-capture --by manual-probe

OBSERVED (clean tree):
  {"ok":false,"subcommand":"baseline-capture","task_id":"","status":"error",
   "observations":"gate-baseline capture failed (captured_by=manual-probe); see sync-errors.log"}
  rc=2 ; .claude/.qa-tracking/gate-baseline does NOT exist
  sync-errors.log: "write_gate_baseline: could not write .../gate-baseline.tmp.<pid> (captured_by=manual-probe)"

CONTROL (same command, ONE dirty entry — remove `.claude/scripts/` from .gitignore so porcelain is 1):
  {"ok":true,...,"status":"captured","observations":"gate-baseline captured_by=manual-probe entries=1 ..."}
  rc=0 ; the file is written.

So the single variable is "is the tree clean".

ALSO REPRODUCED THROUGH THE REAL CALLERS on a v3.5->v4.1 upgraded fixture with a clean tree — session-start and qa-gate enter both hit it:
  [qa-gate]       write_gate_baseline: could not write .../gate-baseline.tmp.73416 (captured_by=session-start)
  [session-start] gate-baseline capture failed; the Stop gate will treat pre-existing git dirt as new work this session
  [qa-gate]       write_gate_baseline: could not write .../gate-baseline.tmp.73615 (captured_by=qa-gate-enter)
  [qa-gate]       enter: gate-baseline capture failed for <tid> (gate still correct; ...)

IMPACT
1. USER-VISIBLE FALSE ALARM. Every session-start on a clean repo writes a sync-errors.log line; the NEXT session-start surfaces it as "Last session's bd sync failed at <ts>" in workflow_warnings. On a repo that is usually clean this fires forever, for nothing.
2. LOST CLEANUP. The `rm -f "$LEGACY_APPROVED_BASELINE"` that retires the v1 approved-baseline is the LAST statement of the function, after the `mv` — so a clean-tree capture never reaches it and a legacy v1 file survives a "first v2 write" that reported success elsewhere.
3. approve on a clean tree logs "gate-baseline refresh failed" and leaves no v2 baseline.
4. Gate DECISIONS unaffected: empty baseline and absent baseline produce identical Stop verdicts.

WHY NO EXISTING TEST CATCHES IT
Every current baseline spec dirties the tree first — gate-baseline-v2.sh §1 seeds 3 pre-dirty files, §6.2 writes src/pre.ts into the worktree before capturing. The clean-tree case is untested.

SUGGESTED FIX SHAPE (for whoever picks this up, NOT applied)
Make the group's last command unconditional, e.g. `printf '%s' "${status_out:+$status_out$NL}"` or move the guarded printf ahead of a trailing `:`. Land it WITH a regression assertion for the clean-tree case (an L1 qa-gate baseline test is the cheapest home) and a META that reverts the guard and watches it fail.

NOTE FOR THE FIXER: .claude/tests/component/specs/upgrade-gate-compat.sh documents this defect in its header and deliberately avoids depending on it (section 5 deletes both baseline files and asserts absence instead of relying on the writer failing; section 6 approves with real dirt on disk so its v2-write assertion measures the writer). Nothing pins the buggy behaviour, so the fix does not have to update that spec.

title: impact_of cue does not reach QA on clean-flow runs: hook template fires only on Stop-recovery; SKILL delegation step and orchestrator QA-prompt composition carry no impact_of instruction; qa.md 3a alone empirically insufficient (4 live runs, 0 calls)
notes:
OPEN.

=== FINDING ===

After 366.9 shipped the impact_of cue to two surfaces (qa.md 3a FIRST-ACTION wording + verify-before-stop.sh Stop-block QA-Task heredoc), live run 4 STILL had 0 impact_of calls. The 366.9 fix is necessary but not sufficient: the cue does not actually reach QA via the channels we assumed in any clean-flow run.

=== EVIDENCE (4 live runs, all 0 calls) ===

- Run 1: cassettes/seed/node-react-auth-2026-06-11T23-34-49-784Z.jsonl (pre-fixes; QA's frontmatter stripped MCP tools entirely — fixed by 366.6).
- Run 2: cassettes/seed/node-react-auth-2026-06-12T00-50-56-312Z.jsonl (post-366.6; tools available but unused; 366.9 traced root-cause to verify-before-stop.sh heredoc).
- Run 3: same run 2 trace re-evaluated offline post-366.8/366.9 (offline only; not a paid run).
- Run 4: cassettes/seed/node-react-auth-2026-06-12T02-18-12-871Z.jsonl (LIVE, ~1376s, ~$5.46; post-366.8 + 366.9, fixture.yaml preserved end-to-end; satisfiesInvariants evaluated LIVE for the first time).

Run-4 cue-channel inspection (anchored in _phase-b-run4-trace.unit.spec.ts):
  - Stop hook fired 4 events: 2 block, 2 allow.
  - Both block reasons start with 'QA approval required (iteration 1, runner=npm, technical checks passed).'
  - Neither block reason contains 'FIRST: for every changed file' or 'impact_of'.
  - The fixture-local script that ran is at .claude/tests/e2e/fixtures/node-react-auth/.claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh — last touched in a8a7bcf 'v3 upgrade + G8 test harness' (predates 8f07ea9 '366.9 cue fix' to the repo's copy). Hooks.json uses CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh, so the fixture-rendered copy is what runs in-fixture.
  - The repo's .claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh DOES have the cue at lines 977-982; the fixture render is the stale copy.

Orchestrator's free composition compensated, somewhat — the first QA Agent invocation prompt (toolu_018kaX5SpZ2NttWtT3X72aCJ) DID contain:
  Section 6: 'Code-graph regression check — use mcp__plugin_claude-workflow_code-graph__impact_of (or the mcp__code-graph__impact_of alias) on the key new/modified symbols (createApp, LoginForm, the new /auth/login handler) so the qa-queried-impact-of invariant is satisfied for this trace.'

This was the most explicit cue we have ever shipped: tool name, alias, and INVARIANT NAME. The model still did not call impact_of. So the open-loop is not 'cue did not reach QA' but 'cue did not move QA' even when on-the-nose. (The second QA spawn — toolu_01R6B2xH139kD5RTUXq49tEo — was an epic-level re-application after the orchestrator prematurely closed the epic; it omitted impact_of entirely from its prompt, which adds a second failure mode.)

The qa.md 3a FIRST ACTION wording is in the QA agent's system prompt for every spawn (it's part of the loaded agent definition, claude-workflow:qa). 4 live runs have now demonstrated it is empirically insufficient on its own.

=== ROOT CAUSE ===

The impact_of cue has three failed delivery channels in a clean-flow run:
  1. Stop-hook QA-Task heredoc (verify-before-stop.sh) — fires ONLY when QA needs to be re-spawned after a Stop block-then-recover cycle; on a clean flow where the orchestrator delegates to QA proactively (no block needed), the heredoc never fires. AND on fixture runs the fixture-local stale render lacks the cue regardless.
  2. SKILL.md / workflow-engine SessionStart injection — does not mention impact_of at all (we checked the SessionStart additionalContext in run-4 — no impact_of reference).
  3. Orchestrator's free-composed QA delegation prompt — depends on the orchestrator model picking up qa.md 3a's FIRST ACTION wording. Run 4 shows this can happen (orchestrator named the tool + invariant) but is unreliable across spawns (second QA spawn omitted it).
  4. qa.md 3a itself — IS in QA's system prompt, but the FIRST ACTION wording lives in section 3a of a long document and is empirically not weighted high enough relative to the per-spawn Task prompt.

=== DESIGN OPTIONS ===

(carried from 366.9 notes, refined with run-4 evidence)

  A. Tighten qa.md 3a further: lead the entire file with a FIRST ACTION call-out block above the frontmatter / above the role description. Mechanical, no new code surface; but 4 live runs say in-agent-system-prompt cues alone are insufficient.

  B. Mid-Task budget assertion: extend verify-before-stop.sh to detect 'QA approved with fileWrites > 0 AND impact_of calls = 0' and emit a soft block (one re-iteration) — turns the cue from prose into a hard requirement enforced by the gate itself. Risk: false-positive when impact_of is genuinely unavailable; mitigated by checking toolsAvailable.

  C. **Mechanical: orchestrator pre-computes impact_of at root and embeds results in the QA delegation packet** — the orchestrator HAS the code-graph tools and is the one composing the Task prompt for QA anyway. Pre-running impact_of on the changed-symbol seed set turns QA's job from 'remember to invoke a tool the model often forgets' to 'verify the impact analysis the orchestrator already produced'. This is the design the orchestrator's role-split should encode (the parallel to orchestrator.md section 5a + qa.md section 6 RUBRIC-RELAY).

  D. SKILL.md injection of impact_of cue at SessionStart — universal across all spawns of all agents, in the always-loaded context. Cheapest broadcast surface. Same in-prompt weight problem as (A) but fires earlier in the context window.

Preferred path: combine (C) + (B). (C) makes the right behaviour the easy one; (B) catches regressions when the orchestrator skips its pre-compute. (A) and (D) alone are insufficient per 4 live runs of evidence.

=== HANDOFF ===

Standalone bug (no parent epic). Carries past Phase B. Future paid run is the only way to verify a fix — see anchor _phase-b-run4-trace.unit.spec.ts for the current-state baseline; flipping the 'impactCalls.length === 0' assertion red is the success signal.

Evidence anchored: _phase-b-run4-trace.unit.spec.ts (10 active assertions, all green on this trace).

title: approve-idempotency.sh can hang when its parent is SIGTERM'd — 4 orphans at 5h/1d10h, stalled L2 ~90s

comments.author: username
comments.text:
THIRD instance of the 'absence of failure is not success' trap this release, and the first one I walked into myself as orchestrator — recording it here because this task is about the same family (a spec that misbehaves under full-suite conditions but not alone).

WHAT HAPPENED (2026-07-29, C0c verification): the full L2 run reported 40 specs / 39 passed / 1 failed, naming code-graph-mcp.sh, 1868 assertions passed and 1 failed. To diagnose I ran the spec DIRECTLY:

    bash .claude/tests/component/specs/code-graph-mcp.sh | grep -iE '^\s*(FAIL|SKIP)'

That printed nothing and exited 0, and I reported it as passing. It was not passing. L2 specs require the runner's pre-sourced lib, so run directly the file died immediately:

    line 38: mk_fixture: command not found
    line 39: COMPONENT_FIXTURE_PATH: unbound variable

Zero assertions ran. No FAIL line existed to grep BECAUSE nothing executed. Exit 0 came from the last command in the pipeline, not from success.

Run correctly through the runner (bash .claude/tests/component/run.sh --filter code-graph-mcp): 29/29 PASS, 0 fail. So the spec is healthy and the full-suite failure was transient.

WHY IT BELONGS ON THIS TASK: the transient failure is most plausibly resource contention during the full suite, and this task tracks approve-idempotency.sh hanging/stalling (~90s observed, 4 orphaned processes at 5h/1d10h). Whatever stalls the suite is a candidate cause for a neighbouring spec's MCP boot or fixture step timing out. Re-running L2 alone to get a trustworthy number.

THE GENERALISABLE POINT, now with three data points this release:
 1. an L2 run killed at a 10-minute cap reported '0 fails' from 38 of 39 specs (C0b);
 2. a summary pipeline over a truncated log reported 'total spec-level fails: 0' (C0b);
 3. this one — a grep for FAIL over a script that never started.
In all three the pass signal was 'I did not see a failure'. The existing lesson says to assert the completeness line (Total: N). That works for the runner. It does NOT cover invoking a spec outside its harness, where the correct control is to assert a POSITIVE result (a PASS count, a __SPEC_SUMMARY__ line) rather than the absence of a negative.

SUGGESTED, cheap and separate from the hang: give L2 specs a guard that fails loudly when sourced without the lib — e.g. an early check for mk_fixture with a one-line 'run me via component/run.sh' message and exit 2. That converts a silent 0 into an unmistakable usage error, and it would have prevented this misreport entirely.

title: install.sh's generated .gitignore lacks .claude/worktrees/ (the repo's own .gitignore has it)
description:
Noticed during C1b (8xv) while tracing how the worktree sweeper's task-evidence gate interacts with the clean-tree gate.

install.sh's GENERATED_GITIGNORE block (install.sh ~:779-833, executed verbatim
by packaging-parity.test.sh) writes:

    .claude/.session-start
    .claude/.qa-tracking/
    .claude/.mutation-runs/
    .claude/.mutation-worktrees/

but NOT `.claude/worktrees/`. The plugin's own .gitignore gained that line in
C1a (wg6) with the rationale "a leftover worktree was invisible to the gate AND
visible in `git status`". A fresh install into a repo with no .gitignore
therefore reproduces exactly the condition wg6 closed here.

Two consequences, both in the parent checkout (never inside a worktree, which
has no .claude/worktrees/ of its own):
 - `git status` in a target project lists every subagent worktree as untracked.
 - The Stop gate's git-status fallback sees them as session dirt (the shared
   denylist does drop the PATHS, so the change-set hash is unaffected).

Fix is one line in the heredoc + the matching line in install.ps1's mirrored
list, and packaging-parity.test.sh compares the two line-for-line, so both must
move together. Out of scope for C1b, which deliberately shipped no installer
change.

```bash
# jq_get <file> <filter> — raw scalar read, "ERR" when jq fails.
jq_get() {
    jq -r "$2" "$1" 2>/dev/null || echo "ERR"
}

# jq_sorted <file> <filter> — canonical compact form of a subtree, for
# deep-equality comparisons.
jq_sorted() {
    jq -S -c "$2" "$1" 2>/dev/null || echo "ERR"
}

# assert_extractable <label> <file> <name> — the four properties that make an
# expression followable from source: both sentinels present exactly once, and
# a non-empty extraction that looks like the merge program.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # literal `$existing`/`$new` are jq bindings being searched for, never shell expansions
assert_extractable() {
    local label="$1" file="$2" name="$3" expr
    assert_eq "$label: '# BEGIN $name' present exactly once" "1" \
        "$(sentinel_line_count "$file" "# BEGIN $name")"
    assert_eq "$label: '# END $name' present exactly once" "1" \
        "$(sentinel_line_count "$file" "# END $name")"
    expr=$(extract_expr "$file" "$name")
    assert_eq "$label: $name extraction is non-empty" "non-empty" \
        "$([ -n "$(printf '%s' "$expr" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ] && echo non-empty || echo EMPTY)"
    assert_eq "$label: $name extraction binds \$existing and \$new" "yes" \
        "$(printf '%s' "$expr" | grep -q '\.\[0\] as \$existing' \
           && printf '%s' "$expr" | grep -q '\.\[1\] as \$new' \
           && echo yes || echo no)"
}

# assert_extractable_scalar <label> <file> <name> <substring> — the same
# sentinel contract for a single-line expression that carries no $existing/$new
# bindings (the R1-F1 validity gate).
assert_extractable_scalar() {
    local label="$1" file="$2" name="$3" needle="$4" expr
    assert_eq "$label: '# BEGIN $name' present exactly once" "1" \
        "$(sentinel_line_count "$file" "# BEGIN $name")"
    assert_eq "$label: '# END $name' present exactly once" "1" \
        "$(sentinel_line_count "$file" "# END $name")"
    expr=$(extract_expr "$file" "$name")
    assert_eq "$label: $name extraction is non-empty" "non-empty" \
        "$([ -n "$(printf '%s' "$expr" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ] && echo non-empty || echo EMPTY)"
    assert_eq "$label: $name extraction carries the slurp-length check" "yes" \
        "$(printf '%s' "$expr" | grep -qF -- "$needle" && echo yes || echo no)"
}

    "$(cmp -s "$WORK/mcp-norm-1.json" "$WORK/mcp-norm-2.json" && echo same || echo different)"

# ===========================================================================
echo ""
echo "=== Section 3b: merge-input validity gate (R1-F1) ==="
# Both merges bind positionally (.[0] existing, .[1] new) after `jq -s`. That
# binding is only sound if EACH input file holds exactly one JSON document.
# `jq empty` — the oracle this gate replaced — exits 0 for an empty file and
# for a multi-document stream, so a two-document target pushed the shipped file
# out to .[2] and produced a config with none of the shipped servers.

VF_SINGLE="$WORK/vf-single.json"
VF_EMPTY="$WORK/vf-empty.json"
VF_BLANK="$WORK/vf-blank.json"
VF_MULTI="$WORK/vf-multi.json"
VF_MALFORMED="$WORK/vf-malformed.json"
VF_ARRAY="$WORK/vf-array.json"
VF_SCALAR="$WORK/vf-scalar.json"

printf '{"mcpServers":{"myserver":{"command":"node"}}}\n' > "$VF_SINGLE"
: > "$VF_EMPTY"
printf '\n   \n' > "$VF_BLANK"
# Two documents: the exact shape that silently demoted the shipped config.
printf '{"mcpServers":{"myserver":{"command":"node"}}}\n{"mcpServers":{"decoy":{"command":"sh"}}}\n' > "$VF_MULTI"
printf '{ "mcpServers": \n' > "$VF_MALFORMED"
printf '[1,2,3]\n' > "$VF_ARRAY"
printf '42\n' > "$VF_SCALAR"

# validator_verdict <expr> <file> — "accepted"/"rejected", running the
# EXTRACTED gate exactly as install.sh's json_single_object() does.
validator_verdict() {
    if jq -s -e "$1" "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo accepted; else echo rejected; fi
}

# retired_oracle_verdict <file> — what the pre-fix `jq empty` check said. Kept
# so the regression is documented mechanically rather than in a comment.
retired_oracle_verdict() {
    if jq empty "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo accepted; else echo rejected; fi
}

assert_eq "gate: a single JSON object is ACCEPTED" "accepted" \
    "$(validator_verdict "$SH_VALID_EXPR" "$VF_SINGLE")"
assert_eq "gate: the real shipped .mcp.json is ACCEPTED" "accepted" \
    "$(validator_verdict "$SH_VALID_EXPR" "$SHIPPED_MCP")"
assert_eq "gate: the real shipped settings.json is ACCEPTED" "accepted" \
    "$(validator_verdict "$SH_VALID_EXPR" "$SHIPPED_SETTINGS")"
assert_eq "gate: an EMPTY file is REJECTED (takes the loud fallback)" "rejected" \
    "$(validator_verdict "$SH_VALID_EXPR" "$VF_EMPTY")"
assert_eq "gate: a whitespace-only file is REJECTED" "rejected" \
    "$(validator_verdict "$SH_VALID_EXPR" "$VF_BLANK")"
assert_eq "gate: a MULTI-DOCUMENT file is REJECTED (takes the loud fallback)" "rejected" \
    "$(validator_verdict "$SH_VALID_EXPR" "$VF_MULTI")"
assert_eq "gate: a malformed file is REJECTED" "rejected" \
    "$(validator_verdict "$SH_VALID_EXPR" "$VF_MALFORMED")"
assert_eq "gate: a top-level ARRAY document is REJECTED (unindexable by the merge)" "rejected" \
    "$(validator_verdict "$SH_VALID_EXPR" "$VF_ARRAY")"
assert_eq "gate: a top-level scalar document is REJECTED" "rejected" \
    "$(validator_verdict "$SH_VALID_EXPR" "$VF_SCALAR")"

# The regression witness: the retired oracle accepted exactly the two shapes

assert_eq "gate: the retired 'jq empty' oracle ACCEPTED an empty file (the R1-F1 defect)" "accepted" \

assert_eq "gate: the retired 'jq empty' oracle ACCEPTED a multi-document file (the R1-F1 defect)" "accepted" \
    "$(retired_oracle_verdict "$VF_MULTI")"

VF_MERGED="$WORK/vf-merged-multidoc.json"
run_merge "$SH_MCP_EXPR" "$VF_MULTI" "$SHIPPED_MCP" "$VF_MERGED" || true
assert_eq "gate: consequence — merging an accepted multi-doc target DROPS shipped bd" "false" \

assert_eq "gate: consequence — it DROPS shipped code-graph too" "false" \
    "$(jq_get "$VF_MERGED" '.mcpServers | has("code-graph")')"
assert_eq "gate: consequence — the target's SECOND document won the \$new binding" "true" \
    "$(jq_get "$VF_MERGED" '.mcpServers | has("decoy")')"

    "$(validator_verdict "$SH_VALID_EXPR" "$VF_MULTI")"

    "$(printf '%s' "$SH_VALID_EXPR" | normalize_expr)" \
    "$(printf '%s' "$PS_VALID_EXPR" | normalize_expr)"

# ===========================================================================

echo "=== Section 4: expression identity, install.sh <-> install.ps1 (bzy #3) ==="

SH_SETTINGS_NORM=$(printf '%s' "$SH_SETTINGS_EXPR" | normalize_expr)
PS_SETTINGS_NORM=$(printf '%s' "$PS_SETTINGS_EXPR" | normalize_expr)

# ===========================================================================
echo ""
echo "=== Section 5: META-TESTs (bzy #4) ==="
# Each META mutates a COPY and asserts the corresponding check above FAILS.
# Without them, a checker that always returns 0 would look identical to a
# passing suite.

# --- META 1: drop the del() call; the retired key must survive ------------
META_EXPR_NO_DEL=$(printf '%s' "$SH_SETTINGS_EXPR" | sed 's/ | del(\.CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL)//')
assert_eq "META 1: the mutation actually changed the expression" "changed" \
    "$([ "$META_EXPR_NO_DEL" != "$SH_SETTINGS_EXPR" ] && echo changed || echo UNCHANGED)"
META_MERGED="$WORK/meta-no-del.json"
META_RC=0
run_merge "$META_EXPR_NO_DEL" "$OLD_LEGACY" "$NEW_SETTINGS" "$META_MERGED" || META_RC=$?
assert_eq "META 1: the mutated expression is still valid jq (exit 0)" "0" "$META_RC"
META_RC=0; check_retired_key_deleted "$META_MERGED" || META_RC=$?
assert_eq "META 1: without del(), the retired-key check FAILS (returns 1)" "1" "$META_RC"
assert_eq "META 1: and the retired key is demonstrably still there" "xhigh" \

assert_eq "META 2: the mutation actually changed the expression" "changed" \

META_PS_EXPR=$(printf '%s' "$PS_SETTINGS_EXPR" | sed 's/\.hooks = \$new\.hooks/.hooks = $existing.hooks/')
assert_eq "META 3: the mutation actually changed the ps1 copy" "changed" \

META_PS_NORM=$(printf '%s' "$META_PS_EXPR" | normalize_expr)
assert_eq "META 3: one drifted token makes the identity check FAIL" "different" \
    "$([ "$SH_SETTINGS_NORM" = "$META_PS_NORM" ] && echo same || echo different)"
# Companion: normalisation alone is not what makes them differ — the
# unmutated ps1 literal still matches after the same normalisation.
assert_eq "META 3 companion: the unmutated ps1 literal still matches" "same" \
    "$([ "$SH_SETTINGS_NORM" = "$PS_SETTINGS_NORM" ] && echo same || echo different)"

# --- META 4: extraction from a file with no sentinels ---------------------
# Proves section 1's fail-loud arm is reachable: a renamed/removed sentinel
# yields an empty extraction and a zero sentinel count, not a silent pass.
META_NO_SENTINEL="$WORK/no-sentinels.sh"
cat > "$META_NO_SENTINEL" <<'FIXTURE'
#!/bin/bash
SETTINGS_MERGE_JQ='
    .[0] as $existing |
    .[1] as $new |
    $existing | .hooks = $new.hooks
'
jq -s "$SETTINGS_MERGE_JQ" a.json b.json
FIXTURE
assert_eq "META 4: a file without sentinels yields an EMPTY extraction" "EMPTY" \
    "$([ -n "$(extract_expr "$META_NO_SENTINEL" "SETTINGS_MERGE_JQ" | tr -d '[:space:]')" ] && echo non-empty || echo EMPTY)"
assert_eq "META 4: and its BEGIN-sentinel count is 0" "0" \
    "$(sentinel_line_count "$META_NO_SENTINEL" "# BEGIN SETTINGS_MERGE_JQ")"

# --- META 5: a duplicated definition is caught ----------------------------
# The drift shape this spec exists to prevent: a second copy pasted back in.
META_DUP="$WORK/duplicated.sh"
{
    cat "$META_NO_SENTINEL"
    printf '# BEGIN SETTINGS_MERGE_JQ\n'
    printf 'SETTINGS_MERGE_JQ_COPY=1\n'
    printf '# END SETTINGS_MERGE_JQ\n'
    printf '# BEGIN SETTINGS_MERGE_JQ\n'
    printf 'SETTINGS_MERGE_JQ_COPY2=1\n'
    printf '# END SETTINGS_MERGE_JQ\n'
} > "$META_DUP"
assert_eq "META 5: two definitions make the exactly-once check FAIL (count 2)" "2" \
    "$(sentinel_line_count "$META_DUP" "# BEGIN SETTINGS_MERGE_JQ")"

# --- META 6 (R1-F1): weaken the gate back to pre-fix semantics -------------
# `length >= 1` is exactly what `jq empty` meant: "at least one document parses".
# Under it the multi-document rejection must FAIL — which is the assertion the
# whole of section 3b rests on.
META_VALID_WEAK=$(printf '%s' "$SH_VALID_EXPR" | sed 's/length == 1/length >= 1/')
assert_eq "META 6: the mutation actually changed the gate expression" "changed" \
    "$([ "$META_VALID_WEAK" != "$SH_VALID_EXPR" ] && echo changed || echo UNCHANGED)"

assert_eq "META 6: with length >= 1 the MULTI-DOC rejection FAILS (accepted again)" "accepted" \
    "$(validator_verdict "$META_VALID_WEAK" "$VF_MULTI")"
# And the object arm is separately load-bearing: drop it and an array passes.

assert_eq "META 6: dropping the object arm actually changed the expression" "changed" \

assert_eq "META 6: without the object arm a top-level ARRAY is accepted again" "accepted" \
    "$(validator_verdict "$META_VALID_NOOBJ" "$VF_ARRAY")"

# The pre-fix shape. Under it an operator's explicit null must be clobbered —
# so the null-preservation assertion FAILS, proving it is not vacuous.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # `$existing` is jq program text inside sed patterns
META_EXPR_TRUTHY=$(printf '%s' "$SH_SETTINGS_EXPR" \
    | sed -e 's/(\$existing | has("effortLevel"))/$existing.effortLevel/' \
          -e 's/(\$existing | has("statusLine"))/$existing.statusLine/')
assert_eq "META 7: the mutation actually changed the expression" "changed" \
    "$([ "$META_EXPR_TRUTHY" != "$SH_SETTINGS_EXPR" ] && echo changed || echo UNCHANGED)"
META_MERGED_3="$WORK/meta-truthiness.json"
META_RC=0

assert_eq "META 7: under truthiness the operator's effortLevel:null is CLOBBERED" '"xhigh"' \
    "$(jq -c '.effortLevel' "$META_MERGED_3" 2>/dev/null)"

assert_eq "META 7: under truthiness the operator's statusLine:false is CLOBBERED (boolean -> shipped object)" "object" \
    "$(jq -r '.statusLine | type' "$META_MERGED_3" 2>/dev/null)"
# The surgical proof: permissions was NOT part of this mutation, so it still
# survives — a blanket breakage would have taken it out too.
assert_eq "META 7: the mutation is surgical — permissions:null still preserved" "null" \
    "$(jq -c '.permissions' "$META_MERGED_3" 2>/dev/null)"

# --- Summary ---------------------------------------------------------------

if [ "$FAIL" -gt 0 ]; then
    printf '\nFAILED: %d\n' "$FAIL"
    for t in "${FAILED_TESTS[@]}"; do

fi
printf '\nPASSED: %d assertion(s)\n' "$PASS"
exit 0
```

```
- Boundary mocks must use the real downstream producer's shape, pinned via a fixture extracted from the producer's spec — never invented. A mock that feeds `body.error` so the test can assert `body.error` is circular and proves nothing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- New agent files must be registered in .claude-plugin/plugin.json agents[] in the same commit that creates them; an unregistered agent is silently invisible to the SDK — no error surfaces. Guard: agents-manifest-parity test. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Subagents cannot spawn other subagents in the Claude Code runtime (docs: sub-agents page — Agent(agent_type) has no effect in subagent definitions). Any agent-spawning step must live at the root conversation level; design multi-agent handoffs as root-orchestrated relays, never nested spawns. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Interface examples must be executed by a test: the Makefile's own usage string (make test-live FIXTURE=node-react-auth) was broken for the one fixture whose spec file is scenario-named — nothing ever ran the documented invocation. Caught only when a paid live run failed fast. Any CLI surface a doc or help text advertises needs an L2 assertion that executes that exact invocation (dry-run mode where the real one costs money). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Prose cues do not reliably drive subagent tool usage: across 4 live runs, QA made zero impact_of calls even when its task prompt contained the exact tool name, alias, target symbols, and invariant name. When a workflow REQUIRES a tool call, make it mechanical (compute it where calls are reliable — e.g. orchestrator at root — and pass results down), don't prompt for it. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n6d --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Rendered fixture installs pin plugin scripts at render time: the fixture's verify-before-stop.sh predated the cue fix by one commit, so a hook-template change never reached the live run. Script-level fixes require re-rendering fixture installs (or a version check at run start) before they affect live validation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.10 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Never run QA review concurrently with a builder in the same working tree: QA attributed the parallel C.2 task's freshly-written files to the C.1 task under review and blocked it for scope creep. Sequence QA after all writers finish, or give builders worktree isolation (orchestrator.md 4b exists for exactly this). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.1 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Manifest-declared assets must be presence-asserted at the install target: install.sh's hardcoded agent list silently dropped grader.md for two releases (v3.2.0-v3.3.0) — every fresh install was missing the rubric loop's grader while the repo's own tests stayed green. Glob-copy from the manifest source of truth and add an installer-spec presence assertion for every plugin.json agents[]/commands[] entry. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Bash functions invoked via $(...) command substitution run in a subshell — any variable they set is lost to the parent. The manual-adopt gate in model-select.sh was dead code for exactly this reason (set at :341, read at :500, never connected). When a helper must signal the caller, encode the signal in its stdout contract (e.g. a MANUAL<tab> prefix) and parse it at every call site; add a META-TEST that strips the parse to prove the gate is load-bearing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-3fn --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- A security hardening that breaks the workflow is worse than the documented residual it closes. Fail-closing prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh on ambiguous identity assumed every specialist carries a probeable identity, but this runtime does not surface subagent_name to PreToolUse hooks — so it denied legitimate specialist Write/Edit (a P0-class regression) to close a P2 Bash-write vector. When a guard depends on an identity signal the runtime may not provide, prefer fail-OPEN plus the structural guard (the orchestrator's omitted Write/Edit tools, which IS airtight) and document the residual; never trade a P2 for a P0. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.19 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Line-number-anchored mutation META-tests are brittle: any comment or line addition above the anchor silently un-lands the NR==<n>/sed -n Np target, turning a load-bearing META into a no-op (or a spurious failure). Anchor mutation METAs to a unique TEXT pattern in the target line, not an absolute line number. (3 instances re-anchored across verify-before-stop/escalation-binding specs this session.) <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.20 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Effort A/B (cnz.2): verdict max — ultracode showed ZERO orchestration interference in a 39-min time-boxed arm (no Workflow-layer engagement, all spawns on-list, plugin flow faithful), contradicting the pre-registered criterion-4-failure expectation; max still wins because ultracode pins the model at its xhigh proxy (below max) with no observed benefit, and criteria 2-3 went unverified under the time-box. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-cnz.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Paid-run cost estimates must be derived from measured token flows, not guessed: the EFFORT-AB-TEST runbook estimated $10-20 for both arms; actual was ~$206 API-equivalent (~$169 arm B full + ~$37 arm A time-boxed) — a 10x error that forced a mid-test re-confirmation gate. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-cnz.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Regional/transient model exclusions in .claude/model-ranking go stale silently: a `!family` line added for a temporary outage keeps masking downstream behavior (here it collapsed the v4 top==opus-class role split onto Opus for six weeks) long after the outage clears. Gate every un-exclusion on FRESH spawn evidence (subagent-spawns.log + effort-ab logs naming the model), not memory, and date the rationale + rollback line in the file. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-bi3.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Files rewritten by a helper (awk/mv, e.g. workflow-model-apply.sh) instead of the Edit/Write tool never land in changed-files.txt, so the QA impact hash and the change-set-bound approval only cover Edit-tracked files. When a task mutates files via a helper, QA must verify those files explicitly via git diff (not rely on the impact report alone). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-bi3.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- MCP registration scope is a mechanical contract, not etiquette: a detection probe reads ONE config path (top-level .mcpServers of ~/.claude.json for user scope), so local/project-scope registrations are silently invisible — verify the probe read path when writing setup docs and make wrong-scope the first troubleshooting row. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Published CLI config references can lag the shipped binary: verify accepted values against the binary own introspection surface (e.g. codex debug models) rather than the docs or trial-and-error, and record the lag in the operator doc so editors re-verify. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Run suites via their canonical make targets: a bare runner invocation (npx vitest run) includes guarded paid live specs whose fail-closed API-key errors masquerade as regressions; the CI-shaped target (make test-e2e-unit) is the comparable baseline. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- When a change adds a second independent gate to a release path, every META that isolates the FIRST gate must be re-seeded to satisfy the new gate so it still fails for its own reason (jio.1 MM18 migration is the template). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.1 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- A deliberate second implementation of a gate predicate (shell counter + TS live invariant) is only a second witness if QA diffs the two rule-by-rule against the writer grammars at their emit sites — the jio.2 parity review caught a greedy-sed vs first-match token-selection divergence (gqp) that every test suite had missed. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- Trace-anchor refreshes that add a skip must be legitimized against the on-disk cassette (jq has(field) on the replay file), not the spec comment — and the pin must assert skipped+pass+exact detail so a future re-record flips loud instead of silently inheriting the skip. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- State a gate writes for its own bookkeeping can destroy the evidence a later check needs: qa-gate.sh approve truncates changed-files.txt, so re-running impact-report.sh --hash-only in the approving checkout returns the empty-list hash and can never reproduce the approved hash — even there. Any cross-checkout or after-the-fact verification must read the PERSISTED record (impact-report-<tid>.json, which survives approve), never recompute; assert the destruction in the test so making it conditional fails loudly instead of silently disabling the reader. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-3mg.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- The two-file awk join idiom NR==FNR is true for every record of the SECOND file when the first file contributes zero records — an empty first input silently swallows the entire join; load the lookup file in BEGIN via getline and add a structural row-count self-check instead. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-gzc --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
```

# Default rubric (v1)

Applies to every task graded under the rubric-grader QA loop (spec Phase A). Each criterion below is a pass/fail assertion the grader evaluates from the grading packet: `bd show` for the task, the SPEC doc, the diff of the files listed in `.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt`, the F7 completion contract returned by the specialist, and `LESSONS.md`. One-line justification per criterion. No numeric score theater — pass or fail.

The criteria are intentionally short and checkable. Where the criterion needs context (boundary-mock fidelity, F7 fields), the "Evidence that satisfies it" line names the artefact the grader looks at.

## Criteria

### C1. Behavior matches the task description and SPEC.

The shipped diff implements the behavior the task description asks for, and matches the goal + acceptance criteria stated in the attached SPEC doc (read via `bd_doc_read(task_id, name="spec")`). Out-of-scope behavior the SPEC explicitly excludes is NOT in the diff.

Evidence that satisfies it: a 1-2 sentence walk-through that maps every user-visible behavior in the SPEC to a code path in the diff (or to a deliberate, documented deferral in the F7 `decisions` array). A diff that adds plausibly-related behavior the SPEC does not name fails this criterion — that is scope creep.

### C2. Tests added exercise user behavior rather than implementation.

Where the diff introduces new behavior, the diff also introduces tests that assert against the user-visible contract (return shape, side effects, error envelope, accessibility role, status code) rather than against the implementation's private structure (function-name mocking, line-coverage gymnastics, internal control-flow assertions).

Evidence that satisfies it: at least one test in the diff that would still pass if the implementation were rewritten while keeping the user contract identical. A test that asserts only against private symbols, internal call counts, or framework boilerplate fails this criterion.

### C3. The F7 completion contract carries all six fields with substantive `llm_observations`.

The specialist's structured completion payload includes `task_id`, `files_changed`, `tests_added`, `decisions`, `blockers`, and `llm_observations`. `llm_observations` is non-trivial narrative — what surprised the specialist, what was unclear, what they noticed and did not act on. A boilerplate one-liner like "no observations" fails this criterion (principle 9: `llm_observations` is mandatory and substantive).

Evidence that satisfies it: each of the six fields is present and the `llm_observations` paragraph is the kind of thing a human engineer would say at a stand-up.

### C4. No unrelated scope in the diff.

Every file the specialist touched serves the task. Drive-by refactors, formatting churn on untouched lines, and "while I'm here" cleanups that exceed the task brief fail this criterion — they should be filed as paired follow-up Beads tasks instead.

Evidence that satisfies it: the diff's file list maps cleanly to the SPEC's deliverables; any incidental change is either trivial (one-line typo fix) or explicitly justified in the `decisions` array.

### C5. J26 modules relevant to the diff are addressed.

Where the diff touches a domain covered by the J26 security taxonomy (SECRETS, INJECTION, AUTH, CONFIG, DEPS, AI, MOBILE, DATA — see `docs/AGENTS.md`), the diff demonstrates that the relevant modules were considered. Untouched J26 domains are out of scope.

Evidence that satisfies it: the `decisions` array (or the SPEC) names which J26 modules apply, and the diff shows defences in those modules (input validation at the trust boundary, parameterised queries, narrow CORS, audited logging, etc.). A diff that touches user input handling without naming INJECTION fails this criterion.

### C6. Docs updated where behavior changed.

When the diff changes user-visible behavior, the documentation that describes that behavior is updated in the same change. This includes `CHANGELOG.md`, README sections, `docs/*.md`, command help text, and SPEC docs the diff renders out of date.

Evidence that satisfies it: a docs-only file in `files_changed` paired with each behavioral change, or a deliberate `decisions` entry stating why a doc deferral is correct (e.g. an internal refactor that ships without user-visible change). A behavioral change that ships with no doc update and no deferral note fails this criterion.

### C7. Boundary-mock fidelity (LESSONS.md lesson 2).

When the diff introduces or modifies mocks of boundaries the project does not control (third-party HTTP APIs, external SDKs, system calls, message-bus payloads), every such mock derives its shape from a fixture extracted from the real downstream producer's spec (OpenAPI, proto file, SDK source, vendor docs). The fixture's source is cited in a comment, the `decisions` array, or `llm_observations`.

**Automatic needs_revision:** circular pass-through assertions are an immediate fail. A mock that feeds `body.error` so a test can assert `body.error` proves nothing — it tests the test's own setup, not the production behavior. Cite `LESSONS.md` lesson 2 in the justification.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new boundary mock points at a fixture file (`.fixtures/`, `__fixtures__/`, `testdata/`) carrying a snapshot of the producer's payload, and the fixture has a comment naming the source (URL, commit, SDK version). Tests assert against the producer's contract, not against the mock's own input.

# DevOps rubric (v1)

Applied additionally when the task carries the `devops` label. Default criteria still apply; these add domain-specific checks pulled from `.claude/agents/devops.md`. The leverage is default + bugfix — these are the few devops-specific failure modes that recur.

## Criteria

### D1. Scripts are idempotent and re-runnable.

Install, uninstall, hook, and CI scripts in the diff produce the same end state when run twice in a row. A second run of `install.sh` does not double-write hooks, clobber prior settings, or fail because a directory already exists. A migration script that exits non-zero on its second run fails this criterion.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new script uses `mkdir -p`, conditional inserts, and idempotent label operations (`bd label add` returns success if already present); the `decisions` array documents any deliberately non-idempotent step (e.g. a one-shot data migration) and pairs it with a guard (lock file, completion sentinel) so a re-run is detected.

### D2. Graceful degradation on missing optional tools.

When the diff depends on an optional tool (gitleaks, shellcheck, a particular bd version, a specific CI runner image), the missing-tool path is handled: log a structured warning, fall back to a safe default, exit zero where the workflow allows. A hook that exits non-zero because `gitleaks` is not installed fails this criterion — that is not a developer-machine-portable failure mode.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new tool dependency is probed (`command -v tool >/dev/null`); the fallback path is documented in the script comments and tested at L1; the `decisions` array names the dependency and its installation hint.

### D3. No new permission prompts; autonomy preserved.

The diff does not add `permissions.deny` rules to `settings.json`, narrow specialist tool lists below the broad allow set, or introduce any user-facing approval step the plugin previously ran without. Principle 3 of the v3 plan is "full autonomy, no permission prompts" — every deny rule becomes a future approval prompt and breaks the workflow.

Evidence that satisfies it: a diff of `.claude/settings.json` shows only `permissions.allow` expansions, never `deny`; specialist tool frontmatter is unchanged or expanded; the `decisions` array calls out any new tool the broadened allow set covers.

### D4. Secrets and PII stay out of source, logs, and history.

Hardcoded API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, committer emails, and PII are absent from the diff. Logs that the diff adds redact sensitive fields before writing. A commit that introduces an `.env` file with values, a personal email address in a script header, or unredacted PII in a log line fails this criterion (extends C5 / SECRETS + DATA).

Evidence that satisfies it: secrets read from a secret manager or environment variable at runtime; PII fields in new log lines are redacted (`***@`, `user_id=***`); a `gitleaks`-equivalent pass on the diff is clean, and the `decisions` array names the secrets the diff touches.

## U0.4 implementation complete — ready for review (no commit, no gate action)

### Gap reproduced first (evidence before fix)

Fresh v4 install to a mktemp dir, appended a sentinel to `.claude/rubrics/default.md`, re-ran `install.sh --mode=2`: sentinel count `0` (clobbered) and a `.claude-backup-*` dir created on a no-op run. Both are fixed and both are now regression-asserted.

### install.sh — what landed

1. **One verdict walk, two old-table sources.** `V3_PLAN/V3_OLD_TABLE/V3_PRESERVED_FILES/V3_REPLACED_FILES/v3_verdict/v3_count/v3_place_file` renamed to `PLAN_FILE/PLAN_OLD_TABLE/PRESERVED_FILES/REPLACED_FILES/plan_verdict/plan_count/place_by_verdict` (installer-internal only; no external references existed). New `build_plan <old-table>` is the single classify call site, used by the v3 flow (frozen `manifests/v<release>.sha256`) and by mode 2 (the target's own install-manifest body). `copy_file` now gates on `VERDICT_MODE` instead of `V3_UPGRADE`; the v3 flow sets `VERDICT_MODE=true` after a successful classify, so its behaviour is byte-identical (§1-§7 green, unchanged).
2. **Mode-2 UPDATE is verdict-driven** when `$TARGET/.claude/install-manifest` parses: `install_manifest_old_table` validates header (`# claude-workflow-plugin <ver>`) + ≥1 row of the generator's grammar (`path TAB class TAB 64-hex`; `length($3)==64` rather than a `{64}` interval — BSD awk), strips the header into a temp old-table, and exports `INSTALLED_MANIFEST_VERSION`. Globals not stdout: a `$(...)` form would lose both assignments to the subshell (LESSONS.md 2026-06-12). Verdicts route through the same `place_by_verdict`: preserve-custom → `.new` + readout line, replace-custom → copy + warn + named in readout, merge → the existing jq merges (UPDATE_MODE), copy-new/replace-stock → copy, skip-current → skip.
3. **Legacy fallback is exact.** Absent / header-only / foreign-header / garbage-body manifest → plain-copy Update as before, with a one-line note that this run writes the manifest the next one will use. Probed all four: identical legacy outcome (clobber + backup) in every case. Classify failure with a valid manifest → same fallback, different note, backup still taken.
4. **No-change probe (mode 2 only).** Skips backup creation when: VERDICT_MODE on AND manifest version == source version AND plan has ≥1 row AND zero write verdicts (copy-new/replace-stock/replace-custom/preserve-custom). Prints `already at <version>; no file changes — skipping backup`. Merges and the install-manifest rewrite still run. Mode 1 keeps its unconditional backup (explicit destructive reinstall — documented in a comment at the mode-1 arm); mode 3 untouched.
5. **`plan_row_count` ≥1 guard** added during self-review: with an EMPTY plan every path falls to `place_by_verdict`'s unknown-verdict arm and gets COPIED, so an empty plan must not read as "no work". Proven out-of-band: forcing an empty plan yields 0 skip-lines, 1 backup, 47 "not in the shipped manifest" notes — loud, and snapshotted.
6. **Two sentinel pairs** for the L2 METAs: `# NOCHANGE-PROBE-START/END` (fail-safe default `UPDATE_SKIP_BACKUP=false` inside; the META rewrites that one line to force the probe TRUE) and `# UPDATE-VERDICT-START/END` (deleting it degrades to the legacy path, never the reverse).
7. **R1-F1 comment fix** on `detect_v3_install` signal (b): real coverage is an unreadable/hand-edited version field; a deleted manifest routes to the v2 flow via pre-existing v2 signal 2 for as long as `hooks.json` survives, so (b) sees a deleted manifest only when hooks.json is gone too — with an explicit "do not delete v2 signal 2 on the strength of this branch".
8. **Usage text**: mode-2 description documents the new behaviour; `Cannot be combined with --upgrade.` reflowed onto one line (it was wrapped mid-phrase, so no grep-level doc assertion could see it).

### Tests

- **L2 §8 (+43 asserts, 61 → 104):** 8a idempotency on the pristine upgraded tree (11) — exit 0, classified-against-install-manifest line, skip-backup line, 0 `.claude-backup-*`, still exactly 1 `.claude-v3-backup-*`, v3 flow not re-entered, every workflow-class hash unchanged (manifest-generated, guarded >90 rows), no `.new` anywhere, manifest still rewritten. 8b re-customize regression on the §5 tree (12) — new sentinel survives, old one too, `.new` == shipped bytes, no `.new.new`, exactly one `.new` under rubrics/, probe declined, backup created and holding the operator's bytes, readout names the `.new`. 8c METAs (20, 11 META-named) — `git archive HEAD` source tree + one fresh v4 fixture cloned three ways; CONTROL (real installer) preserves AND backs up; mutant 1 (probe forced true, anchored inside the sentinels, exactly one `< / >` pair) → 0 backups, preservation unaffected; mutant 2 (verdict block deleted) → rubric clobbered, no `.new`, no classify line, backup still taken.
- **§8 uses `--mode=2`** (documented in the section header): on a v4 target the mode prompt is reachable and reads from `/dev/tty` whenever one is openable, so a bare re-run would block on a dev machine while passing in CI. Same branch the non-interactive default picks.
- **8a runs on the pristine fixture T2, not T** (documented): preserve-custom IS a write verdict, and T carries two preserved customizations from §4, so a re-run there legitimately writes and legitimately backs up — that case is 8b. T2 is where "nothing to do" is literally true.
- **L1 `installer-flags.test.sh` (47 asserts):** `--help`/`-h` exit 0 + both flags + both exclusivity sentences + never reaches prereqs; `--mode=9`/`--mode=abc` exit 1 with the value and the accepted set named, before prereqs; positive controls (`--mode=2`, `--mode=`, `--upgrade` alone) fall through; exclusivity for `--upgrade --mode=2`, `--mode=2 --upgrade`, `--upgrade --mode 3` (space form); ordering proof — with a bd-less PATH the refusal still fires, does NOT print "Checking prerequisites" and does NOT blame the missing tool, with a CONTROL run on the same PATH proving that PATH is genuinely prereq-hostile; no refused invocation creates anything in the target. META: exclusivity block sed-deleted (anchored on the block's own `if`/`fi`) → runs to completion against a minimal synthetic source + fake-bd and exits 0, not 1; control with the unmutated installer on the identical setup still exits 1 and installs nothing. Fall-through cases use a reduced PATH deliberately: under the real PATH an accepted invocation performs a full 376-file install with a real `bd init` (found and fixed while writing the spec).
- **Out-of-band SUT mutation sensitivity (all restored, `cmp` verified):** (A) probe can never fire → 8a's skip-line + no-backup assertions FAIL; (B) `UPDATE-VERDICT` block deleted from the real install.sh → 8b's re-clobber assertions + 8a's classify line FAIL (9 total); (C) exclusivity block deleted → 12 L1 assertions FAIL including both ordering arms.
- **Suites:** L1 26/26 files green (47 new asserts). L2 34 specs / **1115** assertions green (was 34/1072); `installer-mcp-config.sh` 24/24 untouched-green; the extended spec runs green in isolation (104/104, 12.8s vs 6.3s). L3 offline unit tier 437 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed — including the 175-test fixture-script-sync drift guard, so no `make sync-fixtures` needed (nothing flat under `.claude/scripts/` was touched; `scripts/tests/` is not synced). `make lint` exit 0, `shellcheck install.sh` and the new L1 spec both silent.
- **Functional probe outside the suites:** fresh v4 install → immediate re-run prints `note already at 4.0.0; no file changes — skipping backup`, 0 backup dirs, manifest rewritten; customize a rubric → re-run preserves the sentinel, writes `.new` byte-equal to shipped, creates exactly 1 `.claude-backup-*` holding the operator's version, no skip-line. Also probed the full verdict matrix through mode 2 (replace-stock via a v3.5-era file recorded in the manifest, replace-custom on a workflow file, preserve-custom on `model-ranking`): 119 skip-current / 1 / 1 / 1 / 2 merge, each landing correctly. Mode 1 (unconditional backup, flat overwrite, no `.new`) and mode 3 (skips existing, no backup) confirmed unchanged.

### Hand-off notes

- **U0.7 (ps1 mirror)** must mirror: `install_manifest_old_table` + `build_plan` + the `VERDICT_MODE` gate on the Update path, the no-change probe (mode 2 only, same readout string), the `plan_row_count` guard, and BOTH sentinel pairs if the ps1 is to carry equivalent METAs. The manifest it writes must stay LF-only: a CRLF body fails the row-grammar check and silently degrades a Windows Update to plain copies (safe direction, but a real behaviour difference), and the §6g byte-compare already requires LF.
- **Deliberately out of scope (candidates for U0.5/U0.6):** the v3 flow still picks its old table from `manifests/v<release>.sha256` only. On a v4→v4 `--upgrade` it would be strictly more accurate to prefer the target's install-manifest (today that path treats everything changed since v3.5 as customized — the documented "noisy but lossless" probe-F behaviour). Also unchanged: the v2 flow's plain copies (a v4 tree that loses `plugin.json` routes there via v2 signal 2 and gets a full backup + flat overwrite).
- Mode 2 now costs one classify pass (~124 source + target hashes) per Update. That is what buys per-file preservation; it is skipped entirely when no manifest is present.

```diff
#!/bin/bash
# installer-flags.test.sh — L1 spec for install.sh's ARGUMENT CONTRACT
# (v4.1 Phase U0 / claude-workflow-plugin-pnf, closing x15 review finding
# R1-F4: the exclusivity exit was verified by hand and by nothing else).
#
# WHAT THIS PROTECTS
# ------------------
# `--upgrade` and `--mode` answer the same question by different mechanisms:
# --upgrade owns the whole decision (timestamped backup, per-file hash
# classification, verdict-driven writes) while --mode picks one flat behaviour
# for an existing .claude/. Letting one silently win would make the DESTRUCTIVE
# choice unpredictable — an operator who typed both would have no way to know
# whether their tree was about to be classified or clobbered. The installer
# refuses instead, and that refusal is what this spec pins.
#
# ORDERING IS PART OF THE CONTRACT. Argument validation runs BEFORE the
# prerequisite checks, so a wrong invocation is reported as a wrong invocation
# even on a machine with no git / jq / bd installed. If the checks ever migrate
# below the prereq block, an operator on a fresh machine would be told to
# install Beads when their real problem is two conflicting flags. Section 3
# runs the installer with a PATH that cannot see bd, and section 3's control
# proves that PATH really is prereq-hostile — otherwise "still exits 1" would
# be satisfied by a run that failed for the wrong reason.
#
# ASSERTION ANCHORING: every check is anchored to TEXT (a flag name, a message
# fragment, an exit code) and never to a line number.
#
# SECTIONS
#   0. Preflight: the script exists and parses.
#   1. --help: exit 0, both flags documented, exclusivity documented.
#   2. --mode validation: the enum is enforced, and a VALID mode is let past
#      (so section 2 cannot pass by rejecting everything).
#   3. Exclusivity: both flag orders and the `--mode <n>` spelling, with and
#      without bd on PATH, plus the ordering proof.
#   4. META-TEST: a copy with the exclusivity block deleted stops exiting 1.
#
# Exit codes:
#   0  all assertions pass
#   1  one or more assertions failed

set -u

PASS=0
FAIL=0
FAILED_TESTS=()

PROJECT_DIR="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd)}"
INSTALL_SH="$PROJECT_DIR/install.sh"

# A PATH with the system directories only. Beads installs to ~/.local/bin or
# /usr/local/bin (and jq to /usr/local/bin or /opt/homebrew/bin), so this is
# reliably prereq-hostile — but section 3 verifies that rather than assuming it.
MINIMAL_PATH="/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin"

WORK=$(mktemp -d -t installer-flags-test.XXXXXX)
# Invoked indirectly, by the EXIT trap immediately below.
# shellcheck disable=SC2329
cleanup() { rm -rf "$WORK" 2>/dev/null || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

assert_eq() {
    local name="$1" expected="$2" actual="$3"
    if [ "$expected" = "$actual" ]; then
        PASS=$((PASS + 1))
        printf '  PASS: %s\n' "$name"
    else
        FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
        FAILED_TESTS+=("$name")
        printf '  FAIL: %s\n    expected: %s\n    actual:   %s\n' \
            "$name" "$expected" "$actual"
    fi
}

# contains <haystack> <needle> -> yes/no. Fixed-string, so message fragments
# can be pasted verbatim without escaping.
contains() {
    if printf '%s' "$1" | grep -qF -- "$2"; then printf 'yes'; else printf 'no'; fi
}

# --- run helpers -------------------------------------------------------------
# Every invocation in this file goes through run_installer, so the section-4
# mutant can never differ from the subject by HOW it was run — only by what it
# contains. stdin is /dev/null throughout: the mode prompt and the git-init
# prompt both fall through to /dev/tty when one is openable, and a test that
# blocks on a developer's terminal is worse than no test.
#
# Output is captured combined (the refusal goes to stderr, the usage text to
# stdout) and the exit code lands in $RUN_RC.
RUN_OUT=""
RUN_RC=0
run_installer() {
    local script="$1"
    shift
    RUN_OUT=$(bash "$script" "$@" </dev/null 2>&1)
    RUN_RC=$?
    return 0
}

# Same, with PATH reduced to the system directories. `env` is what applies the
# new PATH to the command lookup for bash itself; passing the running bash by
# absolute path keeps the SUT on the same interpreter as the rest of the suite.
#
# EVERY invocation that is EXPECTED TO FALL THROUGH argument validation uses
# this form, and that is load-bearing rather than tidy: under the caller's real
# PATH an accepted invocation runs a COMPLETE INSTALL — 376 files, a real
# `bd init`, and a `git init` inside the fixture. An argument-contract spec has
# no business doing that, so the reduced PATH is what turns "the parser
# accepted this" into a two-second assertion that stops at the prereq block.
BASH_BIN="${BASH:-$(command -v bash)}"
run_installer_minimal_path() {
    local script="$1"
    shift
    RUN_OUT=$(env PATH="$MINIMAL_PATH" "$BASH_BIN" "$script" "$@" </dev/null 2>&1)
    RUN_RC=$?
    return 0
}

# Is the reduced PATH actually prereq-hostile? Beads installs to ~/.local/bin
# or /usr/local/bin, so normally yes — but a machine with bd in /usr/bin would
# let a fall-through run install for real, so the fall-through assertions are
# skipped there rather than silently doing something expensive.
#
# Probed through `env` + `sh -c` rather than a PATH assignment in a subshell:
# same answer, and it keeps the lookup in the same shape the runs below use.
if env PATH="$MINIMAL_PATH" sh -c 'command -v bd >/dev/null 2>&1'; then
    BD_HIDDEN=no
else
    BD_HIDDEN=yes
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "=== Section 0: the script under test ==="

assert_eq "install.sh exists at the repo root" \
    "yes" "$([ -f "$INSTALL_SH" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
if [ ! -f "$INSTALL_SH" ]; then
    printf '\nFAILED: %d (installer missing; remaining sections cannot run)\n' "$FAIL"
    exit 1
fi
assert_eq "install.sh parses under bash -n" "0" \
    "$(bash -n "$INSTALL_SH" 2>/dev/null && echo 0 || echo 1)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo ""
echo "=== Section 1: --help ==="

run_installer "$INSTALL_SH" --help
assert_eq "--help exits 0" "0" "$RUN_RC"
assert_eq "--help documents --upgrade" "yes" "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "--upgrade")"
assert_eq "--help documents --mode" "yes" "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "--mode")"
# The refusal is only defensible if the usage text says the two cannot be
# combined; an operator should not have to discover that by being refused.
assert_eq "--help states --mode cannot be combined with --upgrade" \
    "yes" "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "Cannot be combined with --upgrade")"
assert_eq "--help states --upgrade cannot be combined with --mode" \
    "yes" "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "Cannot be combined with --mode")"
assert_eq "--help lists all three mode values" "yes" \
    "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "--mode=<1|2|3>")"
# -h is the same door.
run_installer "$INSTALL_SH" -h
assert_eq "-h exits 0 as well" "0" "$RUN_RC"
assert_eq "-h prints the same usage block" "yes" \
    "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "Claude Workflow Plugin v3 installer")"
# Printing usage must not be a side-effecting run.
assert_eq "--help never reaches the prerequisite checks" "no" \
    "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "Checking prerequisites")"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo ""
echo "=== Section 2: --mode value validation ==="

TARGET_A="$WORK/target-a"
mkdir -p "$TARGET_A"

run_installer "$INSTALL_SH" --mode=9 "$TARGET_A"
assert_eq "--mode=9 exits 1" "1" "$RUN_RC"
assert_eq "--mode=9 names the offending value" "yes" "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "'9'")"
assert_eq "--mode=9 names the accepted values" "yes" \
    "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "expected 1, 2, or 3")"
assert_eq "--mode=9 is rejected before the prerequisite checks" "no" \
    "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "Checking prerequisites")"

run_installer "$INSTALL_SH" --mode=abc "$TARGET_A"
assert_eq "--mode=abc exits 1" "1" "$RUN_RC"

# Positive controls. Without these, section 2 would pass just as well against
# an installer that rejected every --mode value it was ever given. Both are
# expected to fall THROUGH validation, so both run on the reduced PATH.
if [ "$BD_HIDDEN" != "yes" ]; then
    echo "  SKIPPED: bd resolves under $MINIMAL_PATH; a fall-through run here would install for real"
else
    # An empty value is indistinguishable from "no override" by design (the
    # variable is tested with -n), so this must NOT be a hard error. Pinned so
    # the check is not "tightened" into rejecting a form the parser treats as
    # unset.
    run_installer_minimal_path "$INSTALL_SH" --mode= "$TARGET_A"
    assert_eq "--mode= (empty) is not a validation error; it falls through" "yes" \
        "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "Checking prerequisites")"

    run_installer_minimal_path "$INSTALL_SH" --mode=2 "$TARGET_A"
    assert_eq "--mode=2 is accepted by the parser (no invalid-value message)" "no" \
        "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "Invalid --mode value")"
    assert_eq "--mode=2 proceeds to the prerequisite checks" "yes" \
        "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "Checking prerequisites")"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

echo "=== Section 3: --upgrade / --mode exclusivity ==="

EXCLUSIVITY_MSG="cannot be combined"

run_installer "$INSTALL_SH" --upgrade --mode=2 "$TARGET_A"
assert_eq "--upgrade --mode=2 exits 1" "1" "$RUN_RC"
assert_eq "--upgrade --mode=2 explains the refusal" "yes" \
    "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "$EXCLUSIVITY_MSG")"
assert_eq "--upgrade --mode=2 names the mode the operator passed" "yes" \
    "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "--mode=2 cannot be combined")"
assert_eq "--upgrade --mode=2 tells the operator what to do instead" "yes" \
    "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "Pass exactly one of them")"

# Reverse order: the parser must not be order-sensitive.
run_installer "$INSTALL_SH" --mode=2 --upgrade "$TARGET_A"
assert_eq "--mode=2 --upgrade exits 1 (reverse order)" "1" "$RUN_RC"
assert_eq "--mode=2 --upgrade explains the refusal (reverse order)" "yes" \
    "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "$EXCLUSIVITY_MSG")"

# The space-separated spelling goes through a different parser arm
# (`--mode` + $2) and must land in the same place.
run_installer "$INSTALL_SH" --upgrade --mode 3 "$TARGET_A"
assert_eq "--upgrade --mode 3 (space form) exits 1" "1" "$RUN_RC"
assert_eq "--upgrade --mode 3 (space form) explains the refusal" "yes" \
    "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "$EXCLUSIVITY_MSG")"

# --- ordering: the refusal precedes the prerequisite checks -----------------
if [ "$BD_HIDDEN" != "yes" ]; then
    echo "  SKIPPED: bd resolves under $MINIMAL_PATH; cannot stage a bd-less run here"
else
    # Neither flag on its own is refused — otherwise the assertions above would
    # be satisfied by an installer that refused everything. Falls through, so
    # the reduced PATH again.
    run_installer_minimal_path "$INSTALL_SH" --upgrade "$TARGET_A"
    assert_eq "--upgrade alone is not refused" "no" \
        "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "$EXCLUSIVITY_MSG")"


    # Control: the SAME reduced PATH, without conflicting flags, must fail in
    # the prerequisite block. This is what makes the assertion below mean
    # "validation ran first" instead of "something exited 1".
    run_installer_minimal_path "$INSTALL_SH" "$TARGET_A"
    assert_eq "control: with a prereq-hostile PATH a plain run exits 1" "1" "$RUN_RC"
    assert_eq "control: ...and it got there through the prerequisite checks" "yes" \
        "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "Checking prerequisites")"
    assert_eq "control: ...reporting a missing REQUIRED tool" "yes" \
        "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "REQUIRED")"

    run_installer_minimal_path "$INSTALL_SH" --upgrade --mode=2 "$TARGET_A"
    assert_eq "exclusivity still exits 1 with bd absent from PATH" "1" "$RUN_RC"
    assert_eq "exclusivity still explains the refusal with bd absent" "yes" \
        "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "$EXCLUSIVITY_MSG")"
    # The proof: the same PATH that stopped the control at the prereq block
    # never got there at all this time.
    assert_eq "exclusivity is reported BEFORE the prerequisite checks" "no" \
        "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "Checking prerequisites")"
    assert_eq "exclusivity does not blame the missing tool" "no" \
        "$(contains "$RUN_OUT" "Beads (bd) not found")"
fi

# The target must be untouched by any refused invocation: a run that exits on
# an argument error has no business creating .claude/.
assert_eq "no refused invocation created anything in the target" "0" \
    "$(find "$TARGET_A" -mindepth 1 2>/dev/null | grep -c . | tr -d ' \n')"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo ""
echo "=== Section 4: META-TEST (the exclusivity check can actually fail) ==="

# Delete the exclusivity block from a COPY, anchored on the block's own `if`
# line and its closing column-0 `fi`. Anchoring on real code rather than a
# comment is deliberate: if the condition is ever reworded the sed matches
# nothing, the "copy differs" assertion below fails, and the META is repaired
# rather than silently rotting into a no-op.
MUTANT="$WORK/install-no-exclusivity.sh"
# shellcheck disable=SC2016  # sed script: the $VAR text is the installer's own source, not an expansion
sed '/^if \[ "\$FORCE_UPGRADE" = true \] && \[ -n "\$INSTALL_MODE_OVERRIDE" \]; then$/,/^fi$/d' \
    "$INSTALL_SH" > "$MUTANT"
assert_eq "META: the mutated copy really differs from install.sh" "1" \
    "$(cmp -s "$MUTANT" "$INSTALL_SH" && echo 0 || echo 1)"
assert_eq "META: the mutated copy is shorter (the block was removed)" "1" \
    "$([ "$(wc -l < "$MUTANT")" -lt "$(wc -l < "$INSTALL_SH")" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
assert_eq "META: the mutated copy is still syntactically valid bash" "0" \
    "$(bash -n "$MUTANT" 2>/dev/null && echo 0 || echo 1)"
assert_eq "META: the mutated copy no longer carries the refusal message" "no" \
    "$(contains "$(cat "$MUTANT")" "$EXCLUSIVITY_MSG")"

# The mutant has to run to completion to show the exit code FLIP, and a
# completed run needs a plugin source: install.sh treats its own directory as
# the source when that directory looks like a checkout, and otherwise CLONES
# FROM THE NETWORK — which a unit test must never do. So the mutant is dropped
# into a minimal synthetic source carrying exactly the files install.sh
# requires, plus the real manifest generator so the install-manifest write is
# the real one. Nothing here touches the repo tree.
SYNTH="$WORK/synthetic-source"
mkdir -p "$SYNTH/.claude/agents" "$SYNTH/.claude/scripts" "$SYNTH/.claude/hooks" \
    "$SYNTH/.claude/commands" "$SYNTH/.claude/skills/workflow-engine" \
    "$SYNTH/.claude-plugin" "$SYNTH/bin"
for agent in orchestrator qa backend frontend devops; do
    printf -- '---\nmodel: test\n---\nsynthetic %s agent\n' "$agent" \
        > "$SYNTH/.claude/agents/$agent.md"
done
for helper in session-start intent-router post-edit verify-before-stop session-end \
    qa-gate review-check impact-report current-task prevent-orchestrator-edits; do
    printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' > "$SYNTH/.claude/scripts/$helper.sh"
done
cp "$PROJECT_DIR/.claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh" "$SYNTH/.claude/scripts/" 2>/dev/null || \
    printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 1\n' > "$SYNTH/.claude/scripts/workflow-manifest.sh"
printf '{"hooks":{}}\n'            > "$SYNTH/.claude/hooks/hooks.json"
printf 'synthetic skill\n'         > "$SYNTH/.claude/skills/workflow-engine/SKILL.md"
printf 'synthetic command\n'       > "$SYNTH/.claude/commands/workflow-model.md"
printf '{"env":{}}\n'              > "$SYNTH/.claude/settings.json"
printf '{"name":"synthetic","version":"9.9.9-test"}\n' > "$SYNTH/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"

# fake-bd: the whole `bd` surface install.sh touches (--version, init, hooks,
# doctor). `doctor` must never print the string 'error' — install.sh greps for
# it case-insensitively.
cat > "$SYNTH/bin/bd" <<'FAKE_BD'
#!/bin/bash
case "${1:-}" in
    --version|-v|version) printf 'bd 0.99.0 (fake-bd for installer-flags)\n' ;;
    doctor)               printf 'fake-bd: all checks passed\n' ;;
    *)                    printf 'fake-bd: ok (%s)\n' "${1:-}" ;;
esac
exit 0
FAKE_BD
chmod +x "$SYNTH/bin/bd"

MUTANT_TARGET="$WORK/mutant-target"
mkdir -p "$MUTANT_TARGET"
(
    cd "$MUTANT_TARGET" || exit 1
    git init -q >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    git -c user.email=test@example.com -c user.name=test \
        commit --allow-empty -q -m "baseline" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
)

if ! command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "  SKIPPED: git unavailable; cannot run the mutant to completion"
else
    cp "$MUTANT" "$SYNTH/install.sh"
    MUTANT_OUT=$(env PATH="$SYNTH/bin:$PATH" "$BASH_BIN" "$SYNTH/install.sh" \
        --upgrade --mode=2 "$MUTANT_TARGET" </dev/null 2>&1)
    MUTANT_RC=$?
    if [ "$MUTANT_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
        printf '  diagnostic: mutant exited %s; tail of output:\n' "$MUTANT_RC"
        printf '%s\n' "$MUTANT_OUT" | tail -8 | sed 's/^/    /'
    fi
    # THE FLIP: install.sh exits 1 on these exact arguments (section 3);
    # without the exclusivity block the same arguments are accepted and the
    # install proceeds. An exit code of 1 here would mean section 3's
    # assertion was passing for some reason other than the check.
    assert_eq "META: without the exclusivity block, --upgrade --mode=2 no longer exits 1" \
        "no" "$([ "$MUTANT_RC" -eq 1 ] && echo yes || echo no)"
    assert_eq "META: the mutant accepts the conflicting flags and completes" \
        "0" "$MUTANT_RC"
    assert_eq "META: the mutant prints no refusal" "no" \
        "$(contains "$MUTANT_OUT" "$EXCLUSIVITY_MSG")"
    # It really installed — so the flip is "ran to completion", not "died
    # somewhere else quietly".
    assert_eq "META: the mutant went on to install into the target" "yes" \
        "$([ -f "$MUTANT_TARGET/.claude-plugin/plugin.json" ] && echo yes || echo no)"

    # And the control: the REAL installer, same arguments, same synthetic
    # source, same fake bd — still refuses.
    cp "$INSTALL_SH" "$SYNTH/install.sh"
    CONTROL_TARGET="$WORK/control-target"
    mkdir -p "$CONTROL_TARGET"
    CONTROL_OUT=$(env PATH="$SYNTH/bin:$PATH" "$BASH_BIN" "$SYNTH/install.sh" \
        --upgrade --mode=2 "$CONTROL_TARGET" </dev/null 2>&1)
    CONTROL_RC=$?
    assert_eq "META control: the unmutated installer still exits 1 on the same run" \
        "1" "$CONTROL_RC"
    assert_eq "META control: ...refusing for the documented reason" "yes" \
        "$(contains "$CONTROL_OUT" "$EXCLUSIVITY_MSG")"
    assert_eq "META control: ...and installs nothing" "0" \
        "$(find "$CONTROL_TARGET" -mindepth 1 2>/dev/null | grep -c . | tr -d ' \n')"
fi

# --- Summary ---------------------------------------------------------------

if [ "$FAIL" -gt 0 ]; then
    printf '\nFAILED: %d\n' "$FAIL"
    for t in "${FAILED_TESTS[@]}"; do
        printf '  - %s\n' "$t"
    done
    exit 1
fi
printf '\nPASSED: %d assertion(s)\n' "$PASS"
exit 0
```
