### 5. LESSONS.md
# Lessons ledger

Production lessons learned the hard way. Each entry is a single-sentence
takeaway, traceable to the Beads task(s) that produced it, with the date
it was first recorded.

Add new entries via `.claude/scripts/lessons.sh add '<lesson>' --source <task-id>`
— never hand-edit. The helper deduplicates by normalized text (case- and
whitespace-insensitive), so repeating an existing lesson appends the new
source to that entry rather than creating a duplicate. The only legitimate
hand-edit is pruning entries that are no longer relevant.

The orchestrator reads this file during planning (see `orchestrator.md`),
the grader (Phase A) receives it in the grading packet, and the QA agent
proposes additions at epic close. Treat it as the institutional memory the
plugin runs against, not a static reference doc.

## Lessons

- Parallel agents in the same working tree contaminate each other's branches; concurrent specialists require worktree isolation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Boundary mocks must use the real downstream producer's shape, pinned via a fixture extracted from the producer's spec — never invented. A mock that feeds `body.error` so the test can assert `body.error` is circular and proves nothing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-e0d.7 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- New agent files must be registered in .claude-plugin/plugin.json agents[] in the same commit that creates them; an unregistered agent is silently invisible to the SDK — no error surfaces. Guard: agents-manifest-parity test. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Subagents cannot spawn other subagents in the Claude Code runtime (docs: sub-agents page — Agent(agent_type) has no effect in subagent definitions). Any agent-spawning step must live at the root conversation level; design multi-agent handoffs as root-orchestrated relays, never nested spawns. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-l1r.5 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Interface examples must be executed by a test: the Makefile's own usage string (make test-live FIXTURE=node-react-auth) was broken for the one fixture whose spec file is scenario-named — nothing ever ran the documented invocation. Caught only when a paid live run failed fast. Any CLI surface a doc or help text advertises needs an L2 assertion that executes that exact invocation (dry-run mode where the real one costs money). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-11 -->
- Prose cues do not reliably drive subagent tool usage: across 4 live runs, QA made zero impact_of calls even when its task prompt contained the exact tool name, alias, target symbols, and invariant name. When a workflow REQUIRES a tool call, make it mechanical (compute it where calls are reliable — e.g. orchestrator at root — and pass results down), don't prompt for it. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n6d --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Rendered fixture installs pin plugin scripts at render time: the fixture's verify-before-stop.sh predated the cue fix by one commit, so a hook-template change never reached the live run. Script-level fixes require re-rendering fixture installs (or a version check at run start) before they affect live validation. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-366.10 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Never run QA review concurrently with a builder in the same working tree: QA attributed the parallel C.2 task's freshly-written files to the C.1 task under review and blocked it for scope creep. Sequence QA after all writers finish, or give builders worktree isolation (orchestrator.md 4b exists for exactly this). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.1 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Manifest-declared assets must be presence-asserted at the install target: install.sh's hardcoded agent list silently dropped grader.md for two releases (v3.2.0-v3.3.0) — every fresh install was missing the rubric loop's grader while the repo's own tests stayed green. Glob-copy from the manifest source of truth and add an installer-spec presence assertion for every plugin.json agents[]/commands[] entry. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-n45.4 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- Bash functions invoked via $(...) command substitution run in a subshell — any variable they set is lost to the parent. The manual-adopt gate in model-select.sh was dead code for exactly this reason (set at :341, read at :500, never connected). When a helper must signal the caller, encode the signal in its stdout contract (e.g. a MANUAL<tab> prefix) and parse it at every call site; add a META-TEST that strips the parse to prove the gate is load-bearing. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-3fn --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-12 -->
- A security hardening that breaks the workflow is worse than the documented residual it closes. Fail-closing prevent-orchestrator-edits.sh on ambiguous identity assumed every specialist carries a probeable identity, but this runtime does not surface subagent_name to PreToolUse hooks — so it denied legitimate specialist Write/Edit (a P0-class regression) to close a P2 Bash-write vector. When a guard depends on an identity signal the runtime may not provide, prefer fail-OPEN plus the structural guard (the orchestrator's omitted Write/Edit tools, which IS airtight) and document the residual; never trade a P2 for a P0. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.19 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Line-number-anchored mutation META-tests are brittle: any comment or line addition above the anchor silently un-lands the NR==<n>/sed -n Np target, turning a load-bearing META into a no-op (or a spurious failure). Anchor mutation METAs to a unique TEXT pattern in the target line, not an absolute line number. (3 instances re-anchored across verify-before-stop/escalation-binding specs this session.) <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-llh.20 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-06-13 -->
- Effort A/B (cnz.2): verdict max — ultracode showed ZERO orchestration interference in a 39-min time-boxed arm (no Workflow-layer engagement, all spawns on-list, plugin flow faithful), contradicting the pre-registered criterion-4-failure expectation; max still wins because ultracode pins the model at its xhigh proxy (below max) with no observed benefit, and criteria 2-3 went unverified under the time-box. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-cnz.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Paid-run cost estimates must be derived from measured token flows, not guessed: the EFFORT-AB-TEST runbook estimated $10-20 for both arms; actual was ~$206 API-equivalent (~$169 arm B full + ~$37 arm A time-boxed) — a 10x error that forced a mid-test re-confirmation gate. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-cnz.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Regional/transient model exclusions in .claude/model-ranking go stale silently: a `!family` line added for a temporary outage keeps masking downstream behavior (here it collapsed the v4 top==opus-class role split onto Opus for six weeks) long after the outage clears. Gate every un-exclusion on FRESH spawn evidence (subagent-spawns.log + effort-ab logs naming the model), not memory, and date the rationale + rollback line in the file. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-bi3.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Files rewritten by a helper (awk/mv, e.g. workflow-model-apply.sh) instead of the Edit/Write tool never land in changed-files.txt, so the QA impact hash and the change-set-bound approval only cover Edit-tracked files. When a task mutates files via a helper, QA must verify those files explicitly via git diff (not rely on the impact report alone). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-bi3.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- MCP registration scope is a mechanical contract, not etiquette: a detection probe reads ONE config path (top-level .mcpServers of ~/.claude.json for user scope), so local/project-scope registrations are silently invisible — verify the probe read path when writing setup docs and make wrong-scope the first troubleshooting row. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Published CLI config references can lag the shipped binary: verify accepted values against the binary own introspection surface (e.g. codex debug models) rather than the docs or trial-and-error, and record the lag in the operator doc so editors re-verify. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- Run suites via their canonical make targets: a bare runner invocation (npx vitest run) includes guarded paid live specs whose fail-closed API-key errors masquerade as regressions; the CI-shaped target (make test-e2e-unit) is the comparable baseline. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-1vq.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-25 -->
- When a change adds a second independent gate to a release path, every META that isolates the FIRST gate must be re-seeded to satisfy the new gate so it still fails for its own reason (jio.1 MM18 migration is the template). <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.1 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- A deliberate second implementation of a gate predicate (shell counter + TS live invariant) is only a second witness if QA diffs the two rule-by-rule against the writer grammars at their emit sites — the jio.2 parity review caught a greedy-sed vs first-match token-selection divergence (gqp) that every test suite had missed. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- Trace-anchor refreshes that add a skip must be legitimized against the on-disk cassette (jq has(field) on the replay file), not the spec comment — and the pin must assert skipped+pass+exact detail so a future re-record flips loud instead of silently inheriting the skip. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-jio.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- State a gate writes for its own bookkeeping can destroy the evidence a later check needs: qa-gate.sh approve truncates changed-files.txt, so re-running impact-report.sh --hash-only in the approving checkout returns the empty-list hash and can never reproduce the approved hash — even there. Any cross-checkout or after-the-fact verification must read the PERSISTED record (impact-report-<tid>.json, which survives approve), never recompute; assert the destruction in the test so making it conditional fails loudly instead of silently disabling the reader. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-3mg.2 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- The two-file awk join idiom NR==FNR is true for every record of the SECOND file when the first file contributes zero records — an empty first input silently swallows the entire join; load the lookup file in BEGIN via getline and add a structural row-count self-check instead. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-gzc --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- jq empty is not a merge-input validity oracle — it accepts empty files and multi-document streams; any jq -s merge that indexes .[0]/.[1] positionally must gate its inputs on "length == 1 and (.[0] | type == \"object\")" or the second document of a corrupted input silently binds as the other merge side. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-p5n --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- Add-if-absent config clauses must key on presence (has("key")), never value truthiness — an operator-owned key holding an explicit null or false is still operator-owned, and truthiness guards silently clobber it on upgrade. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-p5n --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- When a reviewer finding names one call site, sweep every sibling call site with the same shape before resolving — the p5n settings merge carried the identical positional-binding hole the finding named for .mcp.json, and the sweep (J27 step 6) is what made the resolution complete rather than symptomatic. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-p5n --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-26 -->
- When adding a new rung to a detection ladder, probe every input class the EARLIER rungs already claim — an earlier detector can shadow the new rung for inputs its comment says it covers (v2 signal 2 vs detect_v3 signal (b) on deleted-manifest trees), leaving documented coverage dead on arrival. <!-- sources: claude-workflow-plugin-x15 --> <!-- recorded: 2026-07-27 -->

### 6. Rubric(s)
--- .claude/rubrics/default.md ---
---
version: 1
name: default
---

# Default rubric (v1)

Applies to every task graded under the rubric-grader QA loop (spec Phase A). Each criterion below is a pass/fail assertion the grader evaluates from the grading packet: `bd show` for the task, the SPEC doc, the diff of the files listed in `.qa-tracking/changed-files.txt`, the F7 completion contract returned by the specialist, and `LESSONS.md`. One-line justification per criterion. No numeric score theater — pass or fail.

The criteria are intentionally short and checkable. Where the criterion needs context (boundary-mock fidelity, F7 fields), the "Evidence that satisfies it" line names the artefact the grader looks at.

## Criteria

### C1. Behavior matches the task description and SPEC.

The shipped diff implements the behavior the task description asks for, and matches the goal + acceptance criteria stated in the attached SPEC doc (read via `bd_doc_read(task_id, name="spec")`). Out-of-scope behavior the SPEC explicitly excludes is NOT in the diff.

Evidence that satisfies it: a 1-2 sentence walk-through that maps every user-visible behavior in the SPEC to a code path in the diff (or to a deliberate, documented deferral in the F7 `decisions` array). A diff that adds plausibly-related behavior the SPEC does not name fails this criterion — that is scope creep.

### C2. Tests added exercise user behavior rather than implementation.

Where the diff introduces new behavior, the diff also introduces tests that assert against the user-visible contract (return shape, side effects, error envelope, accessibility role, status code) rather than against the implementation's private structure (function-name mocking, line-coverage gymnastics, internal control-flow assertions).

Evidence that satisfies it: at least one test in the diff that would still pass if the implementation were rewritten while keeping the user contract identical. A test that asserts only against private symbols, internal call counts, or framework boilerplate fails this criterion.

### C3. The F7 completion contract carries all six fields with substantive `llm_observations`.

The specialist's structured completion payload includes `task_id`, `files_changed`, `tests_added`, `decisions`, `blockers`, and `llm_observations`. `llm_observations` is non-trivial narrative — what surprised the specialist, what was unclear, what they noticed and did not act on. A boilerplate one-liner like "no observations" fails this criterion (principle 9: `llm_observations` is mandatory and substantive).

Evidence that satisfies it: each of the six fields is present and the `llm_observations` paragraph is the kind of thing a human engineer would say at a stand-up.

### C4. No unrelated scope in the diff.

Every file the specialist touched serves the task. Drive-by refactors, formatting churn on untouched lines, and "while I'm here" cleanups that exceed the task brief fail this criterion — they should be filed as paired follow-up Beads tasks instead.

Evidence that satisfies it: the diff's file list maps cleanly to the SPEC's deliverables; any incidental change is either trivial (one-line typo fix) or explicitly justified in the `decisions` array.

### C5. J26 modules relevant to the diff are addressed.

Where the diff touches a domain covered by the J26 security taxonomy (SECRETS, INJECTION, AUTH, CONFIG, DEPS, AI, MOBILE, DATA — see `docs/AGENTS.md`), the diff demonstrates that the relevant modules were considered. Untouched J26 domains are out of scope.

Evidence that satisfies it: the `decisions` array (or the SPEC) names which J26 modules apply, and the diff shows defences in those modules (input validation at the trust boundary, parameterised queries, narrow CORS, audited logging, etc.). A diff that touches user input handling without naming INJECTION fails this criterion.

### C6. Docs updated where behavior changed.

When the diff changes user-visible behavior, the documentation that describes that behavior is updated in the same change. This includes `CHANGELOG.md`, README sections, `docs/*.md`, command help text, and SPEC docs the diff renders out of date.

Evidence that satisfies it: a docs-only file in `files_changed` paired with each behavioral change, or a deliberate `decisions` entry stating why a doc deferral is correct (e.g. an internal refactor that ships without user-visible change). A behavioral change that ships with no doc update and no deferral note fails this criterion.

### C7. Boundary-mock fidelity (LESSONS.md lesson 2).

When the diff introduces or modifies mocks of boundaries the project does not control (third-party HTTP APIs, external SDKs, system calls, message-bus payloads), every such mock derives its shape from a fixture extracted from the real downstream producer's spec (OpenAPI, proto file, SDK source, vendor docs). The fixture's source is cited in a comment, the `decisions` array, or `llm_observations`.

**Automatic needs_revision:** circular pass-through assertions are an immediate fail. A mock that feeds `body.error` so a test can assert `body.error` proves nothing — it tests the test's own setup, not the production behavior. Cite `LESSONS.md` lesson 2 in the justification.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new boundary mock points at a fixture file (`.fixtures/`, `__fixtures__/`, `testdata/`) carrying a snapshot of the producer's payload, and the fixture has a comment naming the source (URL, commit, SDK version). Tests assert against the producer's contract, not against the mock's own input.

# DevOps rubric (v1)

Applied additionally when the task carries the `devops` label. Default criteria still apply; these add domain-specific checks pulled from `.claude/agents/devops.md`. The leverage is default + bugfix — these are the few devops-specific failure modes that recur.

## Criteria

### D1. Scripts are idempotent and re-runnable.

Install, uninstall, hook, and CI scripts in the diff produce the same end state when run twice in a row. A second run of `install.sh` does not double-write hooks, clobber prior settings, or fail because a directory already exists. A migration script that exits non-zero on its second run fails this criterion.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new script uses `mkdir -p`, conditional inserts, and idempotent label operations (`bd label add` returns success if already present); the `decisions` array documents any deliberately non-idempotent step (e.g. a one-shot data migration) and pairs it with a guard (lock file, completion sentinel) so a re-run is detected.

### D2. Graceful degradation on missing optional tools.

When the diff depends on an optional tool (gitleaks, shellcheck, a particular bd version, a specific CI runner image), the missing-tool path is handled: log a structured warning, fall back to a safe default, exit zero where the workflow allows. A hook that exits non-zero because `gitleaks` is not installed fails this criterion — that is not a developer-machine-portable failure mode.

Evidence that satisfies it: every new tool dependency is probed (`command -v tool >/dev/null`); the fallback path is documented in the script comments and tested at L1; the `decisions` array names the dependency and its installation hint.

### D3. No new permission prompts; autonomy preserved.

The diff does not add `permissions.deny` rules to `settings.json`, narrow specialist tool lists below the broad allow set, or introduce any user-facing approval step the plugin previously ran without. Principle 3 of the v3 plan is "full autonomy, no permission prompts" — every deny rule becomes a future approval prompt and breaks the workflow.

Evidence that satisfies it: a diff of `.claude/settings.json` shows only `permissions.allow` expansions, never `deny`; specialist tool frontmatter is unchanged or expanded; the `decisions` array calls out any new tool the broadened allow set covers.

### D4. Secrets and PII stay out of source, logs, and history.

Hardcoded API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, committer emails, and PII are absent from the diff. Logs that the diff adds redact sensitive fields before writing. A commit that introduces an `.env` file with values, a personal email address in a script header, or unredacted PII in a log line fails this criterion (extends C5 / SECRETS + DATA).

Evidence that satisfies it: secrets read from a secret manager or environment variable at runtime; PII fields in new log lines are redacted (`***@`, `user_id=***`); a `gitleaks`-equivalent pass on the diff is clean, and the `decisions` array names the secrets the diff touches.

### 7. Mechanical impact report (G2.n6d)
Trimmed to headlines + file-level dependents (the full per-symbol node dump is at .claude/.qa-tracking/impact-report-claude-workflow-plugin-pnf.json; it contains only self-relation nodes for the two test files and zero callers/dependents for install.sh — an entry script). change_set_hash re-verified fresh at artifact-authoring time (matches the review request and the recorded artifact).

title: Bug: signup route returns 404 instead of 500 when the data-access layer throws a falsy value
description:
Discovered during QA of 40c.1 via independent fault-injection probing (7 error shapes fuzzed through the 500 path).

ROOT CAUSE: server/src/routes/signup.js outer catch does 'return next(err)'. When the store (or any downstream) throws a FALSY value (null/undefined/0/''/false), Express treats next(falsy) as next() — i.e. 'continue routing' — so the request SKIPS the central error handler in app.js and falls through to the catch-all 404 (not_found) instead of the intended 500 (internal_error).

REACHABILITY: NOT reachable today. The in-memory store throws only EmailTakenError; validateSignup guarantees password is a string before hashPassword (so its TypeError cannot fire); and node-postgres rejects with Error objects. This is a defense-in-depth gap in the 'every unexpected failure funnels to a leak-free 500' invariant, most relevant when the Postgres-backed store lands (claude-workflow-plugin-5x8).

IMPACT: LOW. No information disclosure — the 404 body is a static structured envelope with no internals/stack/secret (fuzz-verified). Only the status code and error code are 'wrong' (404 not_found vs 500 internal_error).

FIX (one line): normalize non-Error throws in the route's outer catch, e.g. 'return next(err instanceof Error ? err : new Error("non-error thrown in signup"));'. Add a regression test that injects a falsy throw from store.insert and asserts 500 + internal_error. Best handled alongside 5x8.

design:
## Scope decision (recorded 2026-07-30, task claude-workflow-plugin-kfe)

REDUCED from the original plan's five vendored skills to ONE vendored skill
plus a practice harvest. This decision previously lived only in the untracked
`docs/plans/v4.1-upgrade-wave.md`; that loss mode is one of this release's own
recorded lessons, so it is recorded here as the durable record.

### What is vendored

`brainstorming` ONLY, from `obra/superpowers` at pin
`3dcbd5c4b48e02263fbf4a3c01e3fe4f81d584d9` (MIT, Copyright (c) 2025 Jesse
Vincent). Lands at `.claude/vendor/superpowers/brainstorming/SKILL.md` with a
sibling `MANIFEST.md` and verbatim `LICENSE.upstream`.

### What is NOT vendored, and why

`writing-plans`, `test-driven-development`, `receiving-code-review`,
`systematic-debugging` are HARVESTED as practices into surfaces that already
exist, not vendored as files. The goal is that the plugin carries the best
practice from each source without importing five layers of ceremony. Each of
those four skills duplicates machinery the gates already enforce (TDD ->
`backend.md` TDD workflow + the Stop-hook test gate; receiving-code-review ->
the 5c/5d review relay and arbitration; systematic-debugging -> the
evidence-before-fix protocol; writing-plans -> orchestrator SS2/SS4a Beads
decomposition and the SPEC doc), and importing them wholesale would ship a
second, competing execution model alongside the plugin's own.

`systematic-debugging` specifically is MERGED into the existing
evidence-before-fix protocol rather than added beside it: one authoritative
debugging protocol, evidence-before-fix winning every conflict, with a
delimited byte-identical EBF-CORE region across the four carriers
(`qa.md`, `backend.md`, `frontend.md`, `devops.md`).

### Reference docs, NOT registered skills

The vendored tree lives under `.claude/vendor/`, not `.claude/skills/`.
Explicit `Read .claude/vendor/.../SKILL.md` instructions in agent prompts load
it exactly where it is wired; skill registration would surface it session-wide,
need frontmatter rewrites plus manifest entries plus a parity test, and would
not reach subagent prompts anyway. It also preserves "everything under
`.claude/skills/` is registered" as an exact invariant, and keeps
`platform-audit.test.sh`'s agents+commands+the-one-SKILL scan honest — a
registered second skill would silently escape that scan.

`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` `skills[]` therefore stays length 1, and that is
an assertion in `.claude/scripts/tests/vendored-skills.test.sh`.

### Do NOT install upstream from the marketplace

Upstream registers all 14 skills session-wide; 13 of them encode a competing
execution/approval model (user-approval gates, self-directed commits,
specialist-spawns-specialist relays that `no-nested-spawn-instructions.test.sh`
and the depth-1 spawn pin forbid).

### Also in scope for the epic

- Root `LICENSE` (MIT, holder `preql-data` per `plugin.json`'s author) —
  `plugin.json:12` declares MIT with no backing file today.
- `THIRD_PARTY.md` — two-row pointer table (tree-sitter grammars, brainstorming).
- `wearclair-module` from the original request stays unidentified: SKIPPED,
  recorded in the harvest table.

title: F1 doc-only fast path binds its verdict to the CHANGE SET but writes qa-approved to the TASK — mid-implementation doc-only Stop stamps approval on work that does not exist

comments.author: username
comments.text:
REPRODUCED LIVE on claude-workflow-plugin-0fc during this release, 2026-07-28.

TIMELINE (from 0fc's own comment stream):
  15:44:00Z  QA-GATE: entered
  15:44:59Z  IMPLEMENTER: role=devops
  15:46:39Z  QA-GATE APPROVED change_set_hash=b1169536... reviewed_by=none
             'Auto-approved: doc-only change-set detected (F1 fast path) —
             no reviewable source changed.' [review bypass: F1 doc-only fast path]
             ...and bd shows the task CLOSED at the same instant.

At 15:46:39Z the implementer was still in read-only exploration. workflow-doctor.sh
did not exist. The only dirty paths were docs and .beads, so F1 classified the change
set correctly — and then wrote its label to the TASK.

THE DEFECT, stated precisely: F1's verdict is a statement about a CHANGE SET ('no
reviewable source changed'). Its label is a statement about a TASK ('this task's work
is approved'). Those are not the same proposition. Any doc-only Stop that happens while
a task is open — mid-implementation, during exploration, during a docs commit in an
adjacent session — converts the first into the second.

WHY THE BLAST RADIUS IS SMALL TODAY, AND WHY THAT IS LUCK: the change-set-bound release
predicate (llh.18 / v4) means the NEXT Stop recomputes a different hash, finds no bound
record, and re-arms. So the damage is a misleading 'bd show' and a closed task, not an
unreviewed release. The gate held for the wrong reason — it held because the approval
went stale, not because it was never granted.

CONTRIBUTING: F1 auto-approves only WITH an active task. That coupling is what puts the
label on a task at all. Compare claude-workflow-plugin-prm/dkp: the SAME coupling in the
other direction hard-blocks task-less plan-mode sessions. One mechanism, two opposite
failures — approves what it should not, blocks what it should not.

CANDIDATE FIXES (not yet chosen — needs the evidence-before-fix pass):
  a) F1 records its verdict WITHOUT the qa-approved label when the task carries an
     IMPLEMENTER record and no completion contract. Narrowest.
  b) F1 scopes its label to the change set it actually judged — i.e. it may only
     approve a task whose recorded change set is the doc-only one.
  c) F1 refuses to auto-approve any task in status=in_progress with an IMPLEMENTER
     record, and says so in the block reason.
Prefer (b) if it can be made to hold: it makes the label mean what the verdict means.

NOT FIXED IN v4.1 — filed rather than folded in, because it is not this release's
subject and the change-set binding contains it. Whoever takes it: the reproduction is
free, just enter a gate on a task and touch only a .md file.

comments.text:
SECOND CONSEQUENCE, observed 2026-07-28 immediately after the first.

The spurious F1 approve does not only mislabel the task — it also CLEARS THE
current-task POINTER, because `qa-gate.sh approve` truncates changed-files.txt and
clears current-task as part of its normal post-approval cleanup.

Observed: after the implementer removed the qa-approved label and reopened 0fc, the
next Stop hook reported 'No active Beads task detected' over a 15-file change set,
and `current-task.sh get` returned empty. The orchestrator had explicitly set that
pointer before delegating.

So one doc-only Stop mid-implementation produces THREE effects, none of them intended:
  1. qa-approved stamped on a task whose work does not exist
  2. the task closed
  3. the active-task pointer cleared, so the NEXT Stop cannot even identify the task
     it should be gating and falls through to the task-less hard block

Effect 3 is what makes this user-visible rather than merely untidy: recovery requires
re-running current-task.sh set, which is not mentioned in any block reason. A reader
who hits this sees 'No active Beads task detected' and has no way to know a fast path
silently unset it.

This strengthens the case for candidate fix (b) — scope F1's label AND its cleanup to
the change set it actually judged. A verdict about a doc-only change set has no business
clearing the implementation tracker for an unrelated in-flight task.

title: worktree-sweep.test.sh A4: broaden the structural deletion ban beyond `rm` (find -delete and rmdir currently evade it)
description:
QA finding R1-F3 (low) from the C1b review. Regression-guard gap, not a live
defect — the shipped `worktree-sweep.sh` contains zero occurrences of
`-delete` / `rmdir` / `unlink` / `shred`.

## What was reproduced

`A4: zero 'rm' against ANY candidate/path variable` bans `rm` only:

    grep -cE '(^|[^[:alnum:]_])rm[[:space:]]'

Injecting `find "$SWEEP_CANON" -mindepth 1 -delete` into the removal path of
a sandbox copy leaves **all 34 L1 assertions PASSING**. Same for
`rmdir "$SWEEP_CANON"`. (A first attempt looked like it failed, but only
because the injected trailing comment contained the word "rm" — trailing
comments survive A4's whole-line comment strip. Re-run clean without it.)

No behavioural assertion catches these either: on a candidate that already
passed every gate, `find -delete` produces the same observable as
`git worktree remove` (directory gone), so L2's 7.x assertions stay green.

## Why it matters

Section A's header states the case for the text check: "A behavioural spec
can only prove this for the inputs it happens to try; the text check covers
every future edit at once." It covers `rm`-shaped future edits. For the one
script in the plugin that can delete an operator's working tree, the ban
should name the primitive class.

## Asked for

Broaden A4's pattern to something like `rm|rmdir|unlink|shred|-delete`
(keeping A6 for `--force`), and soften the header claim to match what the
assertion actually enforces. Add the two injections above to the sensitivity
list so the guard is shown to discriminate.

title: Bug: review-check gate suppressed by embedded newline in a REVIEW-ARTIFACT header field
description:
Discovered during QA of 1vq.1. LATENT (no live release path in V2: the gate predicate is not yet wired to any release credential; the change-set-hash-bound qa-approved record remains the only release path). Track for V3 before review-check.sh gate is wired into enforcement.

QA demonstrated end-to-end: a REVIEW-ARTIFACT whose reviewed_hash string value contains an embedded newline, plus a real critical finding, is (1) accepted by review-check.sh validate-artifact exit 0 (spec-faithful: the specified error-key list is closed with no control-char check); (2) embedded verbatim by qa-gate.sh review-record into the single-line comment grammar; (3) truncated by the gate, which reads only the first line of each comment (jq split on newline, index 0). The risk_threshold and findings tokens fall onto line 2 and are dropped, so the gate reports open_findings=0 and exits 0 (PASS) despite a real blocking finding. Line 1 still begins with the REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 prefix so it is matched as the findings-less artifact.

Root cause: gate correctness rests on the documented single-line-record invariant, but the record writer (the only writer of the grammar) does not enforce it and validate-artifact does not reject control chars in the scalar header fields (reviewer_identity, reviewer_model, reviewed_hash, iteration).

Mitigation (why medium/latent, not high/live): the attacker-influenced finding text (location/evidence/description) is correctly kept OUT of the comment; only the grammar-checked finding id (^R[0-9]+-F[0-9]+$) and enum severity reach the record. Exploit needs control of a header field, which in the sol-codex path comes from the advisory, independence-gated model and in the qa-claude path from QA itself.

Suggested fix: validate-artifact rejects control chars (newline/CR/tab) in scalar string fields; and/or the gate treats a matched REVIEW-ARTIFACT line that lacks a findings= token as malformed rather than as zero-findings.
close_reason: Fixed in-loop under 1vq.1: review-check.sh validate-artifact rejects control chars in the 10 grammar-embedded scalars (scalar_contains_control_char), and gate treats a REVIEW-ARTIFACT line without a closed findings=[...] bracket as review_artifact_malformed (not zero-findings). L1 + META coverage; exploit closed end-to-end.

title: Bug: bd-github-link.sh idempotency grep cannot find existing comment due to bold markdown mismatch
description: post_link_comment() in bd-github-link.sh writes a comment body of 'bd-link: tracked as **`<tid>`** (...)' (line 221, includes `**` bold markers) but the idempotency grep (line 234) looks for 'bd-link: tracked as `<tid>`' (NO bold markers). Because grep -F is fixed-string and the literal contains `**` between 'as ' and '`<tid>`', the grep never matches. Result: duplicate comments WILL be posted on every close — idempotency is broken. Reproduce: post a comment via the script, then run it again with the same task. Both runs will call gh comment. SUGGESTED FIX: change the grep pattern on line 234 to 'bd-link: tracked as **`<tid>`**' (match the actual body shape) OR change the body shape on line 221 to NOT use bold markers. Either keeps idempotency. SEVERITY: HIGH — duplicates pollute issue threads.
notes: FIXED: removed the bold markdown markers around the backtick-wrapped tid in gh_link_comment_body() (line 221, was 'tracked as **`tid`**', now 'tracked as `tid`'). The grep -F idempotency pattern in post_link_comment() (line 240, unchanged) now byte-aligns with the body. Added a comment block above gh_link_comment_body explaining the byte-alignment requirement so future edits can't drift again. Verified by 2 assertions in .claude/scripts/tests/bd-github-link.test.sh Section 3, including a stateful gh stub that proves '3 close fires => exactly 1 post'.

## Reproduction

Fresh tempdir, plugin scripts symlinked, cache absent.

**Faked listing** (`bin/curl` shim returns):
```json
{"data":[
  {"id":"claude-opus-4-7","max_input_tokens":200000,"created_at":"2026-05-01T00:00:00Z","capabilities":{}},
  {"id":"claude-fable-5","max_input_tokens":1000000,"created_at":"2026-05-15T00:00:00Z","capabilities":{}},
  {"id":"claude-zenith-6","max_input_tokens":1000000,"created_at":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z","capabilities":{}}
]}
```

**Ranking** (default plugin ranking, fable > mythos > opus > sonnet > haiku):

**Expected (new contract)**: resolver picks `claude-zenith-6` — newest by `created_at`.

**Actual (current code)**:
```
model-select: unknown family/families in listing (add to .../model-ranking if newer): claude-zenith
claude-fable-5	cache
```

After `apply`:
```

```

Final orchestrator pin: `claude-fable-5`. `claude-zenith-6` was silently excluded — the resolver only warned and proceeded with the first non-empty family bucket (`claude-fable`).

## Root cause statement (J19, evidence-backed)

The root cause is **family-gated selection** in `.claude/scripts/model-select.sh:251-271`. The jq filter at line 262 (`map(select(.id | startswith($fam + "-")))`) drops any model whose id does not start with a configured family prefix; the first non-empty family bucket wins. Evidence:

- file:line — `.claude/scripts/model-select.sh:251-271` (`pick_best` body).
- documented as designed — `.claude/model-ranking:4-7` header: "groups results by these prefixes, picks the highest version within the highest-ranked family the account has access to".
- contributing — sort is version-tuple, not `created_at`. `created_at` is projected at line 152 but never used downstream (lines 263-267).
- contributing — 1-hour cache TTL at line 43 with no `--refresh` flag.
- NOT broken — `workflow-model-apply.sh` rewrites all 7 agent pins correctly; it's just never invoked because the resolver short-circuits at line 434-437 with "no change".

## Fix plan (binding decisions from plan)

1. Ranking → exclusion-only (`!prefix` lines drop matching families). Tertiary tie-break uses ranking-file position. Header rewritten.
2. Sort: `created_at` DESC → `max_input_tokens` DESC → ranking position.
3. Unparseable recency → loud SessionStart notice + `/workflow-model <id>` adopt; never silent auto-adopt.
4. `--refresh` flag bypasses cache.
5. Statusline appends pin (read from orchestrator.md frontmatter, no network).

The fix must flip the new failing tests (specs X, Y, Z, W, and flipped C/H) from red to green. Captured pre-fix failure: see comment `failing-test-evidence` once the L2 spec is updated.

comments.author: username
comments.text:
R3-F1 (medium), found by QA at C0b approval, 2026-07-29. PROVEN BY MUTATION.

mcp-deps-preserve.test.sh executes mcp_deps_install only. It never calls
mcp_server_has_deps, mcp_servers_runnable, or the tail block. Literal reintroduction of
the old predicate IS caught (1 packaging-parity assertion each for the [ -d ] and
reclaim mutants) — but that pins SPELLING, not semantics.

The demonstrating mutant: change -maxdepth 3 to -maxdepth 1 inside mcp_server_has_deps.
It keeps every grepped literal, so packaging-parity passes 623/0 AND mcp-deps-preserve
passes 49/0 — while producing a real, inverse, operator-facing false claim. Against a
target with 3,371 files and 92 package.json whose servers demonstrably boot, it printed
'NOT RUNNABLE YET' and 'has no dependencies installed; this server cannot boot' for
both servers. Depth 1 misses scoped packages (@scope/pkg/package.json is at depth 3).

FIX: add a behavioural section to mcp-deps-preserve.test.sh that SOURCES
mcp_server_has_deps from the shipped install.sh (the file already does this extraction
for the four preserve functions — reuse that machinery) and runs it against three
fixtures: (a) a real tree with pkg/package.json, (b) a scoped-only tree with
@scope/pkg/package.json to pin the depth, (c) a 94-empty-directory husk. Add a META
mutating -maxdepth 3 -> 1 and assert fixture (b) flips.

WHY QA DID NOT WRITE IT: authoring an untested change to the implementer's spec at
approval time is the same shape that produced the husk defect (fixing F1 introduced
it), and it would have invalidated the 1,648/49/623 counts the approval cites. Correct
call — recording it here so the reasoning is not lost.

Context: the husk predicate exists because [ -d node_modules ] answers TRUE for a tree
a failed npm ci left as 94 empty directories. Both arms of that failure exit 3, so no
exit code discriminates — this defect family lives entirely in the readout, which is
why a behavioural test on the predicate is worth more than its severity suggests.

title: Bug: uninstall root-scope traversal guard is lexical only — a symlinked parent dir escapes it
description:
Found during QA of U0.5 (claude-workflow-plugin-56r). NOT a blocker for U0.5 — see
the severity reasoning below and the `qa-plan` doc on 56r.

## What

`manifest_root_rows()` in `uninstall.sh` (the awk filter, currently lines 151-165)
drops manifest rows that are absolute or contain a `..` segment:

```awk
if ($1 !~ /^\.claude\// && $1 !~ /^\.claude-plugin\// &&
    $1 !~ /^\// && $1 !~ /(^|\/)\.\.(\/|$)/) {
    rows[++n] = $1 "\t" $3
}
```

That check is purely LEXICAL. A row naming a path under a **symlinked directory**
passes it, and both `[ -f "$TARGET/$rel" ]` and `hash_of` follow symlinks — so a
hash match puts the resolved (outside) file into `TO_REMOVE`, and the `mv` loop
relocates a file from outside the project into the in-project trash dir.

## Reproduction (verified)

```bash
mkdir -p "$W/outside/dirB" "$W/tB/.claude"
printf 'outside victim\n' > "$W/outside/dirB/victimB.txt"
ln -s "$W/outside/dirB" "$W/tB/data"          # symlinked parent INSIDE the target
{ printf '# claude-workflow-plugin 4.0.0\n'
  printf 'data/victimB.txt\toperator\t%s\n' "$(shasum -a 256 "$W/outside/dirB/victimB.txt" | awk '{print $1}')"
} > "$W/tB/.claude/install-manifest"
printf 'y\n' | bash uninstall.sh "$W/tB"
```

Observed: rc=0; readout lists `data/victimB.txt (unmodified since install)`;
`$W/outside/dirB/victimB.txt` is GONE from its original path and now sits in
`$W/tB/.claude-uninstall-trash-*/victimB.txt`.

## Why this is a real gap and not out of scope

The file header states the invariant it is aiming at — "a manifest row that
escaped the target would move a file from outside the project" — and the L2
spec's §9a header frames the guard as covering what "a CORRUPTED or hand-edited
manifest does to a script that calls `mv`". A symlinked parent is exactly that
scenario, so the guard is incomplete against its own stated contract.

## Why it did NOT block U0.5 (severity: medium, threshold was high)

- Unreachable from any installer-produced manifest. Verified against a freshly
  generated manifest: root scope is exactly three FLAT files, and ZERO rows
  outside `.claude*` contain a `/`. The required row shape does not exist.
- Hash-gated: the attacker must already know the victim's exact bytes, so there
  is no disclosure primitive — only relocation of already-known content.
- The path is printed in the pre-confirmation listing, and the operator must
  answer `y`.
- It is a `mv` into an in-project trash directory, not a delete — recoverable.
- Not a regression: before U0.5 the uninstaller never touched root files at all.
  U0.5 is still a large net safety improvement (it stops leaking three files on
  every uninstall).

## Suggested fix

Cheapest and exact against the shipped surface: also require the root-scope path
to be FLAT, since root scope is flat by construction —

```awk
$1 !~ /\//
```

added to the same condition. If subdirectory root rows are ever wanted instead,
use a physical-containment check (resolve the row's parent with `cd ... && pwd -P`
and require the result to be inside `$(cd "$TARGET" && pwd -P)`), and/or reject a
candidate whose parent chain contains a symlink.

Extend `installer-manifest-parity.sh` §9a with a third victim: a symlinked parent
directory inside the target pointing outside, with the victim's REAL hash (the
existing two rows already establish the control/legitimate-row pattern to copy).

## Sequencing

Deliberately filed rather than fixed inside U0.5 so that the hardening lands
**together with U0.7's `uninstall.ps1` mirror**. U0.7 already has to mirror the
root-scope walk into PowerShell; patching bash now and PowerShell later is how the
two scripts drift out of sync. Do this one in the same change as the ps1 mirror,
with the same rule in both.
acceptance_criteria:
- A manifest row whose parent directory is a symlink pointing outside the target
  is dropped before `mv`; the outside file is untouched and the row is not named
  in the readout.
- A legitimate flat root row in the same manifest is STILL consumed (proves the
  manifest was parsed and the new rule, not wholesale rejection, did the work).
- `installer-manifest-parity.sh` §9a covers the symlinked-parent case, and
  stripping the new rule from `uninstall.sh` flips exactly that assertion.
- The same rule is present in `uninstall.ps1` (U0.7 mirror), not just the bash
  script.
- Legacy behaviour (no manifest / foreign header) remains byte-faithful.
close_reason: Fixed in U0.7 (m7e): physical parent containment (pwd -P / reparse-point walk) in BOTH uninstall scripts; QA repro is now the L2 §9a regression (victim untouched, refusal named in a separate Refused block — AC1 deviation reconciled on-task); §9c META strips the containment block and watches the escape return. 32/32 adversarial probes; no-drift on legacy arms.

<!-- BD-MCP-META: {"kind":"fix-reference","source":"devops-agent","fixed_in":"claude-workflow-plugin-m7e"} -->
FIX LANDED (uncommitted, awaiting QA) in claude-workflow-plugin-m7e — do not close until QA verifies.

**Reproduced first, exactly as filed**: rc=0, readout `data/victimB.txt (unmodified since install)`, `$W/outside/dirB/` left EMPTY, victim in the in-project trash.

**Fix (both scripts, one rule)** — physical containment of the row's PARENT directory, not the cheaper flat-only rule:
- `uninstall.sh`: `TARGET_PHYS=$(cd "$TARGET" && pwd -P)` + `row_contained()` (`cd $(dirname ...) && pwd -P`, must equal `$TARGET_PHYS` or sit under it), wrapped in `WN4-CONTAINMENT-START/END`. Applied AFTER the `[ -f ]` test so absent rows stay silent. 87 insertions, 0 deletions — no existing line modified.
- `uninstall.ps1`: same rule as a reparse-point walk down the row's directory chain + a resolved-prefix comparison against the target, same sentinels. The component walk is load-bearing: `Resolve-Path` / `GetFullPath` do NOT follow links on Windows PowerShell 5.1, so a prefix comparison alone would wave the symlinked row straight through. (AC4 satisfied; pinned textually by packaging-parity.test.sh section 6k, since nothing can execute PowerShell on the CI/dev lane.)

**Why not the suggested `$1 !~ /\//` flat rule**: `workflow-manifest.sh` already documents a shipped-`docs/` subset arriving in a later phase; a flat-only rule would silently stop consuming those rows the release they appear. Verified the containment rule still consumes a legitimate nested row (`docs/sub/guide.md` with real directories).

**AC status**
- AC1 (row dropped before `mv`, outside file untouched): YES — victim file and content intact, nothing named `symlink-victim.txt` in the trash. DEVIATION on the "not named in the readout" clause: the row is NOT named in the "will be moved" list (what the AC protects), but IS named in a separate `Refused (the install manifest names a path outside this project):` block before the y/n and in a post-move `note`. A row that resolves outside the project is the corrupted-manifest case; dropping it silently inside a destructive op is how it goes unnoticed. The m7e brief asks for "refused with a note" explicitly. 9a asserts BOTH directions.
- AC2 (a legitimate flat row is still consumed): YES — `.mcp.json` still reaches the trash in the same run.
- AC3 (§9a covers it; stripping the rule flips exactly that assertion): YES — 9a extended with a third victim carrying its REAL hash, plus a new **9c META** that deletes the sentinel block from a COPY of uninstall.sh and asserts the outside file IS moved again and the mutant still calls it "unmodified since install". installer-manifest-parity: 98 -> 115 assertions, 0 fail.
- AC4 (same rule in uninstall.ps1): YES, see above.
- AC5 (legacy behaviour byte-faithful): YES — hardened vs `git show HEAD:uninstall.sh` on both the no-manifest and the usable-manifest arms produced **byte-identical readouts and identical resulting trees**.

Also probed: parent symlink pointing INSIDE the target -> still consumed; TARGET itself reached through a symlinked path -> flat rows still consumed; no-sha256-tool arm unchanged (note printed, root files left, zero refusal noise).

## U0.3 implementation complete — ready for review (no commit, no gate action)

**Files touched (3):**
- `install.sh` (M) — v3-upgrade flow core
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` (M) — l2-component checkout gains `fetch-depth: 0` (tags for the new spec); only that job's checkout touched
- `.claude/tests/component/specs/installer-v3-upgrade.sh` (NEW) — flagship L2, 61 assertions, 3 META-TEST-named

`git status --short`: `M .beads/issues.jsonl`, `M .github/workflows/test.yml`, `M install.sh`, `?? .claude/tests/component/specs/installer-v3-upgrade.sh` — nothing else.

### install.sh — what landed

1. **`detect_v3_install()`** — (a) `$TARGET/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` version matching `3.*` (primary, sufficient); (b) version empty/unreadable AND both v4 markers absent (`scripts/review-check.sh`, `model-roles`) AND `.claude/` is a real install (v2-signal-3 stub guard). Never fires on a fresh target (verified). Sets `V3_DETECTED_VERSION` / `V3_SIGNALS` BEFORE any copy overwrites plugin.json.
2. **Flags** — `--upgrade` + `--mode` = red error + exit 1 (both documented in `print_usage`). Ladder: forced -> v2 signals ⇒ v2; else target plugin.json exists ⇒ v3; else legacy v2-force. Auto -> v2 ⇒ v2; else v3 ⇒ v3; else the untouched mode prompt/default.
3. **V3 flow** — backup FIRST (`cp -R "$TARGET/.claude/."`, dotfile-inclusive; FATAL on failure since it is the only copy of replaced files) + root files (CLAUDE.md, .mcp.json, LESSONS.md, .worktreeinclude, plugin.json flat as `plugin.json`); then `classify` into a temp plan TSV; `UPDATE_MODE=true` so the U0.2 merges run.
4. **Verdict-driven writes** — routed through `copy_file` -> `v3_place_file` so every existing copy loop (and every future one) inherits the behavior from ONE decision point. `merge`/`copy-new`/`replace-stock` -> copy; `skip-current` -> skip; `replace-custom` -> copy + warn-list; `preserve-custom` -> write `<path>.new`, operator file untouched, preserved-list. plugin.json always copied (version marker). Verdict lookup is `awk` field-1 equality over the TSV (bash 3.2; exact match — paths are full of regex metacharacters — and awk exits 0 on no-match so no `|| true` under `set -e`).
5. **Directory units** — `.claude/mcp/` and `.claude/tests/mutation/` stay rsync-wholesale; their verdicts are deliberately NOT consulted (documented at both blocks + in the readout). Sound because both trees are 100% `workflow` class, so rsync's outcome matches every verdict they can produce.
6. **`install-manifest`** — written on EVERY path (fresh, modes 1/2/3, v2, v3): `# claude-workflow-plugin <source version>` + the generated source TSV verbatim. No timestamp/hostname/path — U0.4/U0.5 compare bytes.
7. **Readout** — plain text (same bytes to stdout and to `$V3_BACKUP_DIR/upgrade-report.txt`), versions read dynamically from both plugin.json files, per-verdict counts + total, merged lines, explicit preserved(.new) and replaced lists, backup path, ACTION REQUIRED (re-block on OPEN tasks -> CHANGELOG "UPGRADE NOTE — one-time hash migration"; review/merge/delete each *.new). Replaces the generic tail for v3 only; fresh/mode readout untouched (rebrand = U0.8).
8. **Dotfile-blind backup fixed in all three places** — v2 backup and mode-1/2 backups moved from `cp -r dir/*` to `cp -R dir/.`. Verified: a mode-2 backup now contains `.qa-tracking/`.

### Verification

- L1: 25/25 specs green. L2: 34 specs / 1072 assertions green (was 33/1011; +1 spec, +61 assertions). installer-mcp-config.sh untouched-green. L3 offline unit tier: 437 passed / 0 failed (no e2e fixture drift — no `.claude/scripts/` file was touched, so no `make sync-fixtures` needed). `make lint` clean; `shellcheck install.sh` clean.
- **SUT mutation sensitivity (out-of-band, restored):** (A) revert the v3 backup to `cp -r dir/*` -> 6f dotfile assertion FAILS; (B) make `.new` unconditional on skip-current -> 7a META-TEST FAILS; (C) skip copying grader.md in the agents loop -> 6a parity FAILS with `\.claude/agents/grader.md (hash differs)` (the exact historical failure mode); (D) bogus tag + `CI=true` -> spec FAILS, `CI` unset -> SKIPPED + spec passes.
- **Manual edge cases:** fresh install (no detection, manifest written, no v3 backup); second run on the now-v4 target (no v3 detection -> mode-2 default, exactly ONE `.claude-v3-backup-*`, no duplicate); `--upgrade` forced on a v4.0.0 target (runs the flow, all skip-current); corrupt plugin.json on a v3.5 tree (signal b fires, readout reads "an unidentified v3.x install -> v4.0.0"); v2 layout still routes to the v2 flow with its own readout; target missing `.mcp.json`/`settings.json` (installed as shipped, report says so); plugin.json v3 with `.claude/` deleted (119 copy-new, backup still made).

### Hand-off notes for later U0 sub-tasks

- **U0.7 (ps1 port):** mirror `detect_v3_install`, the ladder, the flag exclusivity, `v3_place_file`, the install-manifest writer and the report. The old-table lookup already honours `manifests/v<version>.sha256`, so freezing a v4.0.0 table later needs no installer edit.
- **U0.8 (gitignore heal):** `.claude-v3-backup-*/` (and the pre-existing `.claude-backup-*/`, `.claude-v2-backup-*/`, plus `*.bak` and `*.new`) are untracked noise in `git status` right after an upgrade — they belong in the seeded .gitignore.
- **U0.4 (idempotency):** a SECOND run on the upgraded tree now takes the mode-2 default (v4 target, detect_v3 correctly declines). Mode 2 still plain-copies operator files, so it re-clobbers a customized rubric — that gap is U0.4/U0.6 scope, not U0.3.
- The v3 flow refuses (exit 1, after the backup, pointing at `--mode=2`) when `workflow-manifest.sh` or the frozen table is missing from the source tree: no silent degrade to "overwrite everything".

+# installer-v3-upgrade.sh - L2 component spec for the v3.5 -> v4 in-place
+# upgrade path (v4.1 Phase U0 / claude-workflow-plugin-x15).
+#
+# WHAT THIS PROVES
+# ----------------
+# The plugin's installer history is the reason this spec exists: it silently
+# dropped .claude/agents/grader.md for two releases while every test stayed
+# green (LESSONS.md, 2026-06-12). "Installs cleanly" now has to mean fresh
+# installs AND in-place upgrades, proven by an executed test rather than by
+# inspection — so this spec builds a GENUINE v3.5 install (from the v3.5.0 git
+# tag, using v3.5.0's OWN installer), seeds the customizations a real operator
+# would have, runs the shipped installer with NO FLAGS, and asserts the end
+# state file by file.
+#
+# Auto-detection is deliberately part of the subject: the upgrade run passes no
+# --upgrade and no --mode. If detect_v3_install() ever stops firing, section 5
+# fails rather than quietly taking the flat mode-2 path.
+#
+# DELIBERATE DEVIATION: NO bd_required_or_skip
+# --------------------------------------------
+# Every other bd-touching spec in this tier calls `bd_required_or_skip`, which
+# exits 0 with a SKIPPED line when the real Beads CLI is absent — and CI sets
+# BD_SHIM_ONLY=1 precisely because there is no public bd installer to curl.
+# This spec would therefore NEVER RUN in CI, which is the one place the upgrade
+# path most needs a guard. install.sh only ever asks bd for four things
+# (`--version`, `init`, `hooks install`, `doctor`) and ignores everything but
+# the version string and a case-insensitive 'error' grep of doctor's output, so
+# a stub is a complete stand-in. We write a fake-bd into a bin dir prepended to
+# PATH and run for real, in CI and on dev machines alike. mk_fixture is skipped
+# for the same reason (it builds a wrapper around the REAL bd); the fixture
+# cleanup array from lib/fixture.sh is still used for teardown.
+#

+#   1. Tag gate            — v3.5.0 must be reachable; hard FAIL in CI (the CI
+#                            checkout carries fetch-depth: 0 for exactly this),

+#   2. Frozen-table integrity — manifests/v3.5.0.sha256 is byte-identical to a
+#                            manifest regenerated from the tag tree.
+#   3. Genuine v3.5 fixture — v3.5.0's own installer, v3.5 markers present, v4

+#   4. Operator customizations — CLAUDE.md, LESSONS.md, settings env key,
+#                            rubric rule, an .mcp.json server, a gate record
+#                            under the dotfile-only .qa-tracking/.
+#   5. The upgrade under test — no flags; readout assertions.
+#   6. Post-state          — parity, preservation, merges, backup, manifest.
+#   7. META-TESTs          — a second fixture proves the preservation is

+        ;;
+    *)
+        printf 'fake-bd: ok (%s)\n' "${1:-}"
+        ;;
+esac
+exit 0
+FAKE_BD
+chmod +x "$FAKE_BIN/bd"
+export PATH="$FAKE_BIN:$PATH"
+
+# --- helpers ----------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# seed_v35_install <dir> — a genuine v3.5 install: git-init <dir>, then run
+# v3.5.0's OWN installer into it. Returns the installer's exit code.
+seed_v35_install() {
+    local dir="$1"
+    mkdir -p "$dir"
+    (
+        cd "$dir" || exit 1
+        git init -q >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+        # An empty commit keeps any `git rev-parse HEAD` consumer happy and
+        # stops the installer's "Initialize git repository?" prompt path.
+        git -c user.email=test@example.com -c user.name=test \
+            commit --allow-empty -q -m "v3.5 baseline" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+    )
+    bash "$SRC35/install.sh" --mode=1 "$dir" </dev/null \
+        >"$WORK/$(basename "$dir")-install-v35.log" 2>&1
+}
+
+# run_upgrade <dir> <logfile> — the shipped installer, NO FLAGS. Auto-detection
+# is part of what is under test, so nothing is passed that could bypass it.
+run_upgrade() {
+    bash "$PLUGIN_ROOT/install.sh" "$1" </dev/null >"$2" 2>&1
+}
+
+# backup_count_of <target> — how many .claude-v3-backup-* dirs exist.
+backup_count_of() {
+    find "$1" -maxdepth 1 -type d -name '.claude-v3-backup-*' 2>/dev/null \
+        | grep -c . | tr -d ' \n'
+}
+
+# backup_dir_of <target> — the (first) .claude-v3-backup-* dir, or "".
+backup_dir_of() {
+    find "$1" -maxdepth 1 -type d -name '.claude-v3-backup-*' 2>/dev/null \
+        | sort | head -1
+}
+
+# CHECKER (shared with the section 7 META): the backup carries the gate record
+# that lives under the DOTFILE directory .claude/.qa-tracking/. This is the one
+# assertion that would have caught the `cp -r dir/*` glob, which silently omits
+# dotfiles — the whole gate history of a live install.
+#   0 = present, 1 = absent
+backup_has_seeded_record() {
+    [ -f "$1/.qa-tracking/seeded-record.txt" ]
+}
+
+# CHECKER (shared with the section 7 META): the operator's file was preserved
+# and the shipped version written alongside as <path>.new.
+#   0 = the .new file exists, 1 = it does not
+preserved_new_exists() {
+    [ -f "$1/$2.new" ]
+}
+
+# yesno <command...> — "yes" when the command succeeds, "no" when it does not.
+# Keeps boolean assertions readable in assert_eq's expected/actual output.
+#
+# The wrapped command's own output is discarded, and that is load-bearing: this
+# is called inside $( ), so a command that PRINTS as well as returning a status
+# (git rev-parse echoes the sha) would otherwise prepend its stdout to the
+# yes/no and every such assertion would silently compare against garbage.
+yesno() {
+    if "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf 'yes'; else printf 'no'; fi
+}
+
+# ===========================================================================
+# Section 1: tag gate
+# ===========================================================================
+# The fixture is built from the real v3.5.0 tag, so the tag has to be there.
+# In CI that is guaranteed (the l2-component checkout sets fetch-depth: 0 for
+# this spec); a silent skip in CI would let the whole upgrade path rot
+# unnoticed, which is the regression this gate prevents. Locally — shallow
+# clone, worktree without tags — we skip with a log instead of failing a dev's
+# suite for an environment reason.
+TAG_PRESENT=$(yesno git -C "$PLUGIN_ROOT" rev-parse -q --verify "$TAG^{commit}")
+if [ "$TAG_PRESENT" != "yes" ]; then
+    if [ "${CI:-}" = "true" ]; then
+        assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 1: $TAG tag reachable (CI must fetch tags)" \
+            "yes" "$TAG_PRESENT"
+        printf '  diagnostic: git -C %s rev-parse %s^{commit} failed.\n' "$PLUGIN_ROOT" "$TAG"
+        printf '  diagnostic: the l2-component job needs actions/checkout with fetch-depth: 0.\n'
+        exit 1
+    fi
+    printf 'SKIPPED: %s tag unavailable (shallow clone or tagless worktree)\n' "$TAG"
+    exit 0
+fi
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 1: $TAG tag reachable" "yes" "$TAG_PRESENT"
+
+# ===========================================================================
+# Section 2: frozen-table integrity
+# ===========================================================================
+# manifests/v3.5.0.sha256 is the table the upgrade uses to tell "operator never
+# touched this stock file" from "operator edited it". If it drifts from the
+# actual v3.5.0 tree, every verdict downstream is wrong — stock files start
+# looking customized and vice versa. Byte comparison, no tolerance.
+SRC35="$WORK/src35"
+mkdir -p "$SRC35"
+ARCHIVE_RC=0
+( set -o pipefail; git -C "$PLUGIN_ROOT" archive "$TAG" | tar -x -C "$SRC35" ) \
+    || ARCHIVE_RC=$?
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 2: git archive $TAG extracts cleanly" "0" "$ARCHIVE_RC"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 2: extracted tag tree carries its own install.sh" \
+    "yes" "$(yesno test -f "$SRC35/install.sh")"
+
+GEN35_RC=0
+bash "$MANIFEST_TOOL" generate "$SRC35" > "$WORK/gen35.tsv" 2>"$WORK/gen35.err" \
+    || GEN35_RC=$?
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 2: workflow-manifest.sh generate on the tag tree exits 0" \
+    "0" "$GEN35_RC"
+TABLE_CMP_RC=0
+cmp -s "$WORK/gen35.tsv" "$FROZEN_TABLE" || TABLE_CMP_RC=$?
+if [ "$TABLE_CMP_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
+    printf '  diagnostic: first differing rows (regenerated vs frozen):\n'
+    diff "$WORK/gen35.tsv" "$FROZEN_TABLE" 2>/dev/null | head -10 | sed 's/^/    /'
+fi
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 2: manifests/v3.5.0.sha256 is byte-identical to the regenerated tag manifest" \
+    "0" "$TABLE_CMP_RC"
+
+# ===========================================================================
+# Section 3: genuine v3.5 fixture
+# ===========================================================================
+# Built by v3.5.0's OWN installer, not by hand and not by the current one: a
+# hand-rolled "v3.5-shaped" tree would let a detection or hash bug pass because
+# the fixture was built to match the code under test.
+T="$WORK/target"
+V35_RC=0
+seed_v35_install "$T" || V35_RC=$?
+if [ "$V35_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
+    printf '  diagnostic: v3.5.0 installer exited %s; tail of log:\n' "$V35_RC"
+    tail -15 "$WORK/target-install-v35.log" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/    /'
+fi
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 3: v3.5.0's own installer exits 0 with fake-bd on PATH" \
+    "0" "$V35_RC"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 3: fixture manifest declares version 3.5.0" \
+    "3.5.0" "$(jq -r '.version // empty' "$T/.claude-plugin/plugin.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 3: fixture carries the v3.5 marker .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh" \
+    "yes" "$(yesno test -f "$T/.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh")"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 3: fixture lacks the v4 marker .claude/scripts/review-check.sh" \
+    "no" "$(yesno test -e "$T/.claude/scripts/review-check.sh")"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 3: fixture lacks the v4 marker .claude/model-roles" \
+    "no" "$(yesno test -e "$T/.claude/model-roles")"
+
+# ===========================================================================
+# Section 4: seed operator customizations
+# ===========================================================================
+# Six operator-owned edits, one per mechanism the upgrade must respect:
+#   CLAUDE.md              never touched (not in the shipped surface at all)
+#   LESSONS.md             operator class -> preserve + .new
+#   .claude/settings.json  merged class  -> key-wise jq merge
+#   .claude/rubrics/*.md   operator class -> preserve + .new
+#   .mcp.json              merged class  -> key-wise jq merge
+#   .claude/.qa-tracking/  dotfile directory -> must reach the backup
+printf '\n<!-- %s -->\n' "$CLAUDE_SENTINEL" >> "$T/CLAUDE.md"
+printf '\n- %s: never trust an unproven upgrade path.\n' "$LESSON_SENTINEL" >> "$T/LESSONS.md"
+printf '\n- %s: rollback must be demonstrated, not asserted.\n' "$RUBRIC_SENTINEL" \
+    >> "$T/.claude/rubrics/default.md"
+jq '.env.OPERATOR_KEY = "op-1"' "$T/.claude/settings.json" > "$WORK/settings.seeded.json" \
+    && cp "$WORK/settings.seeded.json" "$T/.claude/settings.json"
+jq --argjson srv "$OPERATOR_SERVER_JSON" '.mcpServers["operator-thing"] = $srv' \
+    "$T/.mcp.json" > "$WORK/mcp.seeded.json" \
+    && cp "$WORK/mcp.seeded.json" "$T/.mcp.json"
+mkdir -p "$T/.claude/.qa-tracking"
+printf 'seeded gate record (pre-upgrade)\n' > "$T/.claude/.qa-tracking/seeded-record.txt"
+
+# Pre-conditions. Without these, a silently-failed seed would make the
+# section 6 preservation assertions pass for the wrong reason.
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 4: seeded settings.json carries env.OPERATOR_KEY pre-upgrade" \
+    "op-1" "$(jq -r '.env.OPERATOR_KEY // empty' "$T/.claude/settings.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 4: seeded .mcp.json carries the operator server pre-upgrade" \
+    "$(printf '%s' "$OPERATOR_SERVER_JSON" | jq -cS .)" \
+    "$(jq -cS '.mcpServers["operator-thing"]' "$T/.mcp.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 4: seeded rubric carries the operator rule pre-upgrade" \
+    "$RUBRIC_SENTINEL" "$(cat "$T/.claude/rubrics/default.md")"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 4: seeded gate record exists under the dotfile .qa-tracking/" \
+    "yes" "$(yesno test -f "$T/.claude/.qa-tracking/seeded-record.txt")"
+
+# Pre-upgrade bytes we compare against later.
+PRE_QA_GATE="$WORK/pre-qa-gate.sh"
+cp "$T/.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh" "$PRE_QA_GATE"
+
+# ===========================================================================
+# Section 5: the upgrade under test
+# ===========================================================================
+UPGRADE_LOG_FILE="$WORK/upgrade.log"
+UPGRADE_RC=0
+run_upgrade "$T" "$UPGRADE_LOG_FILE" || UPGRADE_RC=$?
+if [ "$UPGRADE_RC" -ne 0 ]; then
+    printf '  diagnostic: upgrade exited %s; tail of log:\n' "$UPGRADE_RC"
+    tail -25 "$UPGRADE_LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^/    /'
+fi
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 5: install.sh with NO flags exits 0 on a v3.5 target" \
+    "0" "$UPGRADE_RC"
+
+UPGRADE_LOG=$(cat "$UPGRADE_LOG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
+BACKUP_DIR=$(backup_dir_of "$T")
+SOURCE_VERSION=$(jq -r '.version // empty' "$PLUGIN_ROOT/.claude-plugin/plugin.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
+
+# Auto-detection, not a flag, chose this path.
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 5: readout reports auto-detection of the v3.5.0 install" \
+    "Detected v3.5.0 plugin installation" "$UPGRADE_LOG"
+# Both versions come from the two plugin.json files; neither is hardcoded in
+# the installer, so this line also pins that they are read dynamically.
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 5: readout names both versions on one upgrade line" \
+    "Upgrade complete: v3.5.0 -> v$SOURCE_VERSION" "$UPGRADE_LOG"
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 5: readout uses the word preserved" \
+    "preserved" "$UPGRADE_LOG"
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 5: readout mentions the .new convention" \
+    ".new" "$UPGRADE_LOG"
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 5: readout names the backup directory" \
+    "$BACKUP_DIR" "$UPGRADE_LOG"
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 5: readout points at the CHANGELOG hash-migration note" \
+    "UPGRADE NOTE" "$UPGRADE_LOG"
+# The v3 readout REPLACES the generic tail rather than printing alongside it.
+assert_not_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 5: v3 readout replaces the generic completion tail" \
+    "Installation complete." "$UPGRADE_LOG"
+
+# ===========================================================================
+# Section 6: post-state
+# ===========================================================================
+
+# --- 6a. packaging parity: every workflow-class file landed, byte-exact -----
+# Driven from the generator, not from a hand-written list: that is what makes
+# the grader.md class of failure (a shipped file the installer forgot)
+# structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely.
+SRC_MANIFEST="$WORK/source-manifest.tsv"
+TGT_MANIFEST="$WORK/target-manifest.tsv"
+SRC_GEN_RC=0
+bash "$MANIFEST_TOOL" generate "$PLUGIN_ROOT" > "$SRC_MANIFEST" 2>/dev/null || SRC_GEN_RC=$?
+TGT_GEN_RC=0
+bash "$MANIFEST_TOOL" generate "$T" > "$TGT_MANIFEST" 2>/dev/null || TGT_GEN_RC=$?
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6a: generate on the plugin source exits 0" "0" "$SRC_GEN_RC"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6a: generate on the upgraded target exits 0" "0" "$TGT_GEN_RC"
+
+# Guard against a vacuous parity pass: an empty or truncated source manifest
+# would make the comparison below trivially true.
+SRC_WORKFLOW_ROWS=$(awk -F'\t' '$2 == "workflow"' "$SRC_MANIFEST" 2>/dev/null | grep -c . | tr -d ' \n')
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6a: source manifest lists a plausible number of workflow files (>90)" \
+    "yes" "$(yesno test "${SRC_WORKFLOW_ROWS:-0}" -gt 90)"
+
+# The target manifest is loaded in BEGIN via getline rather than with the
+# NR == FNR two-file idiom: NR == FNR is true for every record of the second
+# file when the first contributed none, so an empty target manifest would make
+# awk skip the whole comparison and report perfect parity.
+PARITY_BAD=$(awk -F'\t' -v tgtf="$TGT_MANIFEST" '
+    BEGIN {
+        while ((getline line < tgtf) > 0) {
+            n = split(line, f, "\t")
+            if (n >= 3 && f[1] != "") { tgt[f[1]] = f[3] }
+        }
+        close(tgtf)
+    }
+    $2 == "workflow" {
+        if (!($1 in tgt))          { print $1 " (absent)" }
+        else if (tgt[$1] != $3)    { print $1 " (hash differs)" }
+    }
+' "$SRC_MANIFEST" | sort | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ *$//')
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6a: every workflow-class file hash-matches in the upgraded target" \
+    "" "$PARITY_BAD"
+
+# --- 6b. operator rubric preserved, shipped version alongside ---------------
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 6b: the operator's rubric rule survived the upgrade" \
+    "$RUBRIC_SENTINEL" "$(cat "$T/.claude/rubrics/default.md" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6b: .claude/rubrics/default.md.new was written alongside" \
+    "yes" "$(yesno preserved_new_exists "$T" ".claude/rubrics/default.md")"
+RUBRIC_NEW_CMP_RC=0
+cmp -s "$T/.claude/rubrics/default.md.new" "$PLUGIN_ROOT/.claude/rubrics/default.md" \
+    || RUBRIC_NEW_CMP_RC=$?
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6b: default.md.new is byte-identical to the shipped rubric" \
+    "0" "$RUBRIC_NEW_CMP_RC"
+
+# --- 6c. root-level operator content survived ------------------------------
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 6c: the CLAUDE.md sentinel survived (never in the shipped surface)" \
+    "$CLAUDE_SENTINEL" "$(cat "$T/CLAUDE.md" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 6c: the LESSONS.md sentinel survived" \
+    "$LESSON_SENTINEL" "$(cat "$T/LESSONS.md" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6c: LESSONS.md.new carries the shipped ledger alongside" \
+    "yes" "$(yesno preserved_new_exists "$T" "LESSONS.md")"
+
+# --- 6d. settings.json merged key-wise -------------------------------------
+# The operator key survives, the retired env pin is deleted (union alone can
+# only ADD keys, so its removal is the one thing that proves the del ran), and
+# the workflow-owned hook block was replaced wholesale.
+POST_SETTINGS=$(cat "$T/.claude/settings.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "{}")
+assert_json_field "installer-v3-upgrade 6d: settings.json still carries env.OPERATOR_KEY" \
+    "$POST_SETTINGS" '.env.OPERATOR_KEY' "op-1"
+assert_json_field "installer-v3-upgrade 6d: settings.json no longer carries env.CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL" \
+    "$POST_SETTINGS" 'if (.env // {} | has("CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL")) then "yes" else "no" end' "no"
+assert_json_field "installer-v3-upgrade 6d: settings.json gained the v4 SubagentStart hook" \
+    "$POST_SETTINGS" 'if (.hooks // {} | has("SubagentStart")) then "yes" else "no" end' "yes"
+assert_json_field "installer-v3-upgrade 6d: settings.json carries a top-level effortLevel" \
+    "$POST_SETTINGS" 'if has("effortLevel") then "yes" else "no" end' "yes"
+assert_json_field "installer-v3-upgrade 6d: settings.json carries a top-level statusLine" \
+    "$POST_SETTINGS" 'if has("statusLine") then "yes" else "no" end' "yes"
+
+# --- 6e. .mcp.json merged key-wise -----------------------------------------
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6e: the operator's MCP server survived verbatim" \
+    "$(printf '%s' "$OPERATOR_SERVER_JSON" | jq -cS .)" \
+    "$(jq -cS '.mcpServers["operator-thing"]' "$T/.mcp.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 6e: shipped bd server uses the \${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.} form" \
+    '${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}' "$(jq -r '.mcpServers.bd.args[0] // empty' "$T/.mcp.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 6e: shipped code-graph server uses the \${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.} form" \
+    '${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}' "$(jq -r '.mcpServers["code-graph"].args[0] // empty' "$T/.mcp.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6e: the retired code-context server is absent" \
+    "no" "$(jq -r 'if (.mcpServers // {} | has("code-context")) then "yes" else "no" end' "$T/.mcp.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "err")"
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 6e: the readout names the operator server carrying a bare variable" \
+    "operator-thing" "$UPGRADE_LOG"
+
+# --- 6f. the backup ---------------------------------------------------------
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6f: exactly one .claude-v3-backup-* directory exists" \
+    "1" "$(backup_count_of "$T")"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6f: the backup carries .qa-tracking/seeded-record.txt (dotfile-inclusive copy)" \
+    "yes" "$(yesno backup_has_seeded_record "$BACKUP_DIR")"
+# The backup must hold the PRE-upgrade bytes, and those bytes must actually
+# differ from the post-upgrade file — otherwise "the backup matches" would be
+# satisfied by an upgrade that changed nothing.
+POST_QA_GATE_DIFFERS_RC=0
+cmp -s "$PRE_QA_GATE" "$T/.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh" || POST_QA_GATE_DIFFERS_RC=$?
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6f: qa-gate.sh actually changed in the upgrade" \
+    "yes" "$(yesno test "$POST_QA_GATE_DIFFERS_RC" -ne 0)"
+BACKUP_QA_GATE_CMP_RC=0
+cmp -s "$BACKUP_DIR/scripts/qa-gate.sh" "$PRE_QA_GATE" || BACKUP_QA_GATE_CMP_RC=$?
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6f: the backup's qa-gate.sh is the pre-upgrade file byte-for-byte" \
+    "0" "$BACKUP_QA_GATE_CMP_RC"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6f: the backup carries the pre-upgrade plugin.json as plugin.json" \
+    "3.5.0" "$(jq -r '.version // empty' "$BACKUP_DIR/plugin.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
+
+# --- 6g. install-manifest ---------------------------------------------------
+INSTALL_MANIFEST="$T/.claude/install-manifest"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6g: .claude/install-manifest was written" \
+    "yes" "$(yesno test -f "$INSTALL_MANIFEST")"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6g: install-manifest header names the installed version" \
+    "# claude-workflow-plugin $SOURCE_VERSION" \
+    "$(head -1 "$INSTALL_MANIFEST" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
+MANIFEST_BODY_CMP_RC=0
+tail -n +2 "$INSTALL_MANIFEST" 2>/dev/null | cmp -s - "$SRC_MANIFEST" || MANIFEST_BODY_CMP_RC=$?
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6g: install-manifest body byte-equals the generated source manifest" \
+    "0" "$MANIFEST_BODY_CMP_RC"
+
+# --- 6h. the saved report ---------------------------------------------------
+REPORT="$BACKUP_DIR/upgrade-report.txt"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 6h: upgrade-report.txt was saved into the backup" \
+    "yes" "$(yesno test -f "$REPORT")"
+REPORT_TEXT=$(cat "$REPORT" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 6h: the saved report names the preserved rubric" \
+    ".claude/rubrics/default.md" "$REPORT_TEXT"
+assert_contains "installer-v3-upgrade 6h: the saved report carries the same upgrade line" \
+    "Upgrade complete: v3.5.0 -> v$SOURCE_VERSION" "$REPORT_TEXT"
+
+# ===========================================================================
+# Section 7: META-TESTs
+# ===========================================================================
+
+# --- META (a): preservation is DETECTOR-driven, not unconditional ----------
+# A second genuine v3.5 fixture with the rubric left ALONE. If the installer
+# wrote a .new file for every operator-class file regardless of customization,
+# section 6b would pass for the wrong reason and operators would get spurious
+# .new litter on every upgrade. On this fixture the section 6b assertions MUST

+T2="$WORK/target-pristine"
+V35_RC_2=0
+seed_v35_install "$T2" || V35_RC_2=$?
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 7a: second v3.5 fixture installs cleanly" "0" "$V35_RC_2"
+UPGRADE_RC_2=0
+run_upgrade "$T2" "$WORK/upgrade2.log" || UPGRADE_RC_2=$?
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 7a: second fixture upgrades cleanly" "0" "$UPGRADE_RC_2"
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 7a META-TEST: no default.md.new when the rubric was never customized" \
+    "no" "$(yesno preserved_new_exists "$T2" ".claude/rubrics/default.md")"
+PRISTINE_RUBRIC_CMP_RC=0
+cmp -s "$T2/.claude/rubrics/default.md" "$PLUGIN_ROOT/.claude/rubrics/default.md" \
+    || PRISTINE_RUBRIC_CMP_RC=$?
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 7a META-TEST: an uncustomized rubric matches the shipped bytes after upgrade" \
+    "0" "$PRISTINE_RUBRIC_CMP_RC"
+
+# --- META (b): the backup checker can FAIL --------------------------------
+# A third genuine v3.5 fixture whose .qa-tracking/ is seeded and then DELETED
+# before the upgrade. backup_has_seeded_record — the identical function section
+# 6f asserts on — must report absent here. Without this, a checker that always
+# returned 0 would satisfy 6f and the dotfile-copy fix would be untested.
+T3="$WORK/target-nodotfiles"
+V35_RC_3=0
+seed_v35_install "$T3" || V35_RC_3=$?
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 7b: third v3.5 fixture installs cleanly" "0" "$V35_RC_3"
+mkdir -p "$T3/.claude/.qa-tracking"
+printf 'seeded then removed\n' > "$T3/.claude/.qa-tracking/seeded-record.txt"
+rm -rf "$T3/.claude/.qa-tracking"
+UPGRADE_RC_3=0
+run_upgrade "$T3" "$WORK/upgrade3.log" || UPGRADE_RC_3=$?
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 7b: third fixture upgrades cleanly" "0" "$UPGRADE_RC_3"
+BACKUP_DIR_3=$(backup_dir_of "$T3")
+assert_eq "installer-v3-upgrade 7b: third fixture produced a backup directory" \
